## Context

Test creation calibration today has no signal for "did we add tests for new intent items?" Test-writing sub-agents can produce many tests that pass review but do not cover newly-introduced SC/DoD/AC entries — and the failure is invisible until production. Today there is no per-PR or per-epic metric that distinguishes "suite grew because behavior was added" from "suite grew due to test inflation." Users affected: DSO maintainer, sprint orchestrators, test-writing sub-agents, code-reviewer-test-quality, completion-verifier, and downstream calibration consumers (411b-a047 mutation infrastructure once brainstormed, 69e8-af39 feedback loop). After this epic ships, when a sprint agent closes a story that has an SC with no test_artifact registered in the manifest, the completion-verifier emits a non-empty "Intent Allocation Findings" section naming the uncovered SC — where today closure is silent.

This epic delivers the first version of suite-growth metrics: (a) manifest-claim breadth + (a+) header-vs-source import check, both implemented as deterministic scripts. Stronger signals (intent-anchored line coverage, manifest-claim depth) are deferred to fb3e-b01b at P4 until the simpler signals' real-world catch rate is known.
## Success Criteria

SC1: plugins/dso/docs/contracts/intent-coverage-findings.md published with a jsonschema. Seven finding types: intent_with_no_test, test_artifact_missing_on_disk, test_artifact_fails, header_source_mismatch, dynamic_import_inconclusive (fail-open, warn), source_files_unresolved (warn; both manifest entry's source_files field AND parent ticket file_impact absent/empty), file_impact_likely_stale (warn; source_files resolved from file_impact but referenced files don't exist on disk). Severities: warn (default), block (reserved for intent_with_no_test at closure-time only). contract_version=1. Each consumer validates incoming findings JSON against the published jsonschema before processing.

SC2: plugins/dso/scripts/intent-coverage-check.sh implements (a) — manifest-claim breadth. Reads the 94ed manifest via intent-allocation-read.sh. For each end-state intent_id: (i) entry presence in the merged manifest; (ii) test_artifact.path realpath() normalization THEN file existence on disk; (iii) test pass/fail. Pre-commit invocation runs ONLY steps (i)+(ii) — fast checks. Test-pass validation step (iii) runs in CI workflow OR at closure-time on ticket-transition — NOT on every commit, eliminating pre-commit latency. Findings written to file via `--output-file` flag (ARG_MAX-safe; not passed as command-line argument or env var). Exit codes: 0 = no findings; 1 = warn-only; 2 = at least one block-mode finding.

SC3: plugins/dso/scripts/intent-header-source-check.sh implements (a+) — header-vs-source import check. ONLY applies to test files that have an intent-claim header per d566-afa6 Rule 6; files without a header are skipped (header presence is d566's reviewer concern, not 7f42's). For each test file with a header: (i) extract intent_id; (ii) resolve source_files via manifest entry's source_files field if present → else parent ticket's file_impact array → else emit source_files_unresolved (warn, fail-open; skip check for that intent); when file_impact is used, additionally check disk presence of each referenced file and emit file_impact_likely_stale (warn) for missing entries; (iii) parse the test file with sg (ast-grep); when sg unavailable OR no parser for the test language, emit dynamic_import_inconclusive (warn, fail-open) — NO grep fallback (grep fallback produces false positives); (iv) emit header_source_mismatch when test file contains no reference to any source_files entry. Dynamic-import patterns detected for fail-open: Python importlib.import_module with variable arg; JavaScript eval/Function/dynamic require with computed string; Ruby send/public_send. Findings written via `--output-file` (ARG_MAX-safe).
SC4: Multi-surface consumption — three consumers, one published contract:

- (a) plugins/dso/hooks/pre-commit-intent-coverage-gate.sh invokes only the FAST checks (file existence + header parsing). NO test-runner invocation in pre-commit. Block-mode reserved for intent_with_no_test at closure-time only, detected via ticket-transition hook.

- (b) 94ed-f55c's manifest-aware default validator (already registered with a03c-d55e's pluggable end-state-item-validator hook) ingests the findings JSON. ALL seven finding types (intent_with_no_test, test_artifact_missing_on_disk, test_artifact_fails, header_source_mismatch, dynamic_import_inconclusive, source_files_unresolved, file_impact_likely_stale) are explicitly enumerated as a contract requirement for 94ed's validator output mapping — the validator must register each type for rendering in the completion-verifier "Intent Allocation Findings" section.

- (c) .github/workflows/intent-coverage.yml invokes both scripts AND the (a)-step-iii test-pass validation step at CI time. Posts findings as PR comment via upsert-by-marker pattern: finds prior bot comment by the stable marker `COVERAGE_FINDINGS_<epic-id>` and edits it in place; if absent, posts new. One comment per PR, never a thread. Fallback when comment-write is unavailable (e.g., fork PRs with read-only GITHUB_TOKEN): write findings to the GHA job summary so the signal is not silently dropped.
SC5: Multi-language synthetic end-to-end test covering nine fixture scenarios:
- (a) HAPPY PATH: Python + bash test fixtures with valid intent-claim headers and manifest entries pointing at them. Both scripts return zero findings.

- (b) INTENT_WITH_NO_TEST: fixture epic with 2 SCs, only one has a manifest entry. intent-coverage-check.sh surfaces intent_with_no_test for the uncovered SC. completion-verifier dispatch produces a non-empty "Intent Allocation Findings" section naming it.

- (c) HEADER_SOURCE_MISMATCH: fixture Python test + fixture bash test both with valid intent-claim headers but no source-file symbol references. intent-header-source-check.sh surfaces header_source_mismatch for each.

- (d) SOURCE_FILES_UNRESOLVED: intent_id whose manifest entry has no source_files field AND whose parent ticket file_impact is empty. intent-header-source-check.sh surfaces source_files_unresolved (warn, fail-open) and skips the (a+) check for that intent.

- (e) FILE_IMPACT_LIKELY_STALE: parent ticket file_impact references a path that doesn't exist on disk. intent-header-source-check.sh surfaces file_impact_likely_stale (warn) but still attempts source-symbol matching against the surviving file_impact entries.
- (f) DEFERRED_TEST OVERRIDE: manifest entry with deferred_test: true set. Closure attempt on the parent ticket does NOT block on intent_with_no_test for that intent.

- (g) MISSING_SG: simulate sg absence on the runtime PATH. intent-header-source-check.sh emits dynamic_import_inconclusive (warn) for all test files; NO grep fallback is executed; pre-commit does NOT block.

- (h) BACKWARD_COMPAT_94ED_LEGACY: manifest entry without source_files field AND without deferred_test field (pre-extension legacy schema). Scripts handle gracefully: source_files resolution falls back to parent ticket file_impact; absent deferred_test treated as false. Verifies the additive 94ed schema extension preserves backward compatibility for existing consumers.

SC6: Dynamic-import fail-open verification per language. Python importlib.import_module with variable arg; JavaScript eval/Function/dynamic require with computed string; Ruby send/public_send. Each emits dynamic_import_inconclusive (warn); pre-commit does NOT block; completion-verifier surfaces as informational finding (not blocking closure).
## Approach
Four sequential phases, each independently mergeable:
- Phase 1: SC1 (findings jsonschema contract) + SC2 (intent-coverage-check.sh; manifest-claim breadth check).
- Phase 2: SC3 (intent-header-source-check.sh; header-vs-source via sg) + SC6 (dynamic-import fail-open pattern detection per language).
- Phase 3: SC4 (multi-surface wiring — fast-only pre-commit hook, 94ed validator finding-type mapping, CI workflow upsert-by-marker with GHA-summary fallback).
- Phase 4: SC5 (nine-scenario multi-language synthetic end-to-end test).

7f42's sg usage is internal to intent-header-source-check.sh; this epic does not introduce a shared AST contract. If a Polyglot Test Gate epic later requires polyglot AST traversal, it will own that capability independently. The two epics' sg invocations are not coupled.
## Scenario Analysis (Blue Team surviving)

- Stale file_impact arrays produce false-positive header_source_mismatch (high/correctness): partially mitigated by SC1's new file_impact_likely_stale finding type — staleness is surfaced as warn rather than masquerading as a genuine mismatch.

- Tautological import satisfies (a+) symbol-reference check despite zero behavioral catch power (high/correctness): accepted as known by-design residual; reserved for 411b-a047's mutation-kill verification.
- ARG_MAX exceeded for large epics' findings JSON (high/runtime): mitigated by SC2/SC3's --output-file flag — findings written to disk, not passed via shell arg or env var.

- CI findings comment on fork PRs triggers no-permission error (low/deployment): mitigated by SC4(c)'s GHA-summary fallback — signal survives even when comment-write is unavailable; documented as a known limitation pending fork-PR security work.
## Out of Scope

- Intent-anchored line coverage and manifest-claim depth metrics: deferred to fb3e-b01b at P4. Stronger signals require polyglot per-test line-coverage infrastructure (coverage.py + bashcov + istanbul/nyc) and per-test attribution storage; the ROI on those vs 411b-a047's mutation-kill is poor.
- Behavioral adequacy of imports: a test that imports a source module but doesn't actually exercise the SC behavior satisfies (a+). Reserved for 411b-a047's mutation-kill verification.
- Polyglot Test Gate AST traversal patterns: 7f42 does not introduce a shared sg invocation contract. Polyglot Test Gate (if pursued) owns its own AST traversal.
- Fork-PR-friendly findings posting: deferred to CI security work; SC4(c)'s GHA-summary fallback is the interim signal.
## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation, 2026-05-16)
### State Lifecycle Owner Block (Probe-3 remediation)
| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |

| `source_files` (94ed manifest entry field) | Planner-agent during `/dso:implementation-plan` when filling 94ed manifest | Re-runs of `/dso:implementation-plan` on revised SCs | SC3 `intent-header-source-check.sh`; 94ed's manifest-aware validator | Implicit with manifest entry — when the intent_id is removed (SC removed from epic) |

| `deferred_test` (94ed manifest entry field, bool) | Planner-agent or operator during `/dso:implementation-plan` when test is intentionally deferred | Operator flips to `false` once the deferred test is registered | SC4(a) pre-commit gate; closure-time block-check | Implicit with manifest entry; operator may zero out the override post-registration |

| `COVERAGE_FINDINGS_<epic-id>` PR-comment marker | SC4(c) `intent-coverage.yml` first run on a PR posts the comment with this marker | Subsequent runs upsert-by-marker (find + edit in place) | The upsert workflow itself reads its own marker to find prior comment | N/A — scoped per-PR; PR closure implicitly retires its comment thread (GitHub does not require active cleanup). The marker is a discriminator within a single PR's comment list, NOT a global registry. |

| `contract_version=1` (published JSON schema) | SC1 publishes `contract_version=1` in the schema | Breaking changes bump to `contract_version=2` with formal versioned migration | Each consumer validates incoming findings JSON against the schema before processing | Persistent — version field lives with the schema; older versions deprecated through formal version bump, not deletion |
Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):
- `grep -nE 'source_files|deferred_test' plugins/dso/docs/contracts/intent-allocation-manifest.md` shows both fields documented in the 94ed manifest schema.
- `grep -n 'COVERAGE_FINDINGS_' plugins/dso/workflows/intent-coverage.yml` (or `.github/workflows/`) confirms marker construction.
- `grep -n 'contract_version' plugins/dso/docs/contracts/intent-coverage-findings.md` confirms field publication.
Closes the audit's named gaps: PR-comment marker RETIRE = scoped per-PR (PR closure implicit cleanup); `deferred_test` RETIRE = operator flips or implicit with manifest entry removal.
### External-dependency verification (Probe-6 remediation, 2026-05-18 follow-up)

The original 2026-05-16 remediation pass deferred probe 6 because the audit's suggestion was framed as an External Dependencies block gating closure on external state. Reframing: the in-session sprint environment has `gh` CLI access, which makes GitHub PR-comment and GHA-summary state directly verifiable. Adding the in-session checks here:
| Resource | In-session verification command | Expected |

| Upsert-by-marker PR comment posts successfully | After SC4(c) workflow runs on a sprint PR: `gh api /repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues/<pr>/comments --jq '[.[] \| select(.body \| contains("COVERAGE_FINDINGS_"))] \| length'` | ≥1 |
| Upsert-by-marker idempotency | Re-run intent-coverage.yml on the same PR; count remains the same (no thread; second run edits in place) | Same count, second run logs show `edit` action |
| GHA-summary fallback works on fork PRs | Fork-PR fixture: `gh run view <run-id> --log \| grep -c "COVERAGE_FINDINGS_"` | ≥1 (summary contains marker even when comment-write unavailable) |

| Schema contract version validates | `python3 -c "import json,jsonschema; jsonschema.validate(json.load(open('plugins/dso/docs/contracts/intent-coverage-findings.md.schema')), {'\$schema':'http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#'})"` | Returns 0 |

Verification is in-session: gh CLI is available in the sprint environment, fork-PR fixture is created during sprint dogfooding, and the schema artifact ships in-tree. Converts the prose-only external-dependency concern into a structured contract surface.
## Dependencies

- a03c-d55e (Closure Checks schema migration) — required. Findings reference end-state SC/DoD/AC items separated from Closure Checks by a03c's schema cleavage; surfaced via a03c's pluggable end-state-item-validator hook.

- 94ed-f55c (Plan-time intent allocation manifest) — required. SC2's check consumes the manifest via intent-allocation-read.sh; SC3's source_files resolution prefers the manifest entry's source_files field; SC4(b) hooks into 94ed's manifest-aware default validator.
- d566-afa6 (Generation-time prevention) — required. SC3 parses test-file intent-claim headers per d566-afa6 Rule 6.
### Coordination with 94ed-f55c
Additive 94ed manifest schema extension required:
- New optional field per manifest entry: `source_files: [array of source file paths]`. When present, used preferentially over parent ticket file_impact for SC3's source-symbol resolution.
- New optional field per manifest entry: `deferred_test: bool` (default false). When true, suppresses intent_with_no_test at closure-time block evaluation (SC2 step iii).

Both extensions are additive and non-breaking for forward-compat-preserving consumers (94ed's spec explicitly requires unknown-field passthrough). Coordination via ticket comment on 94ed-f55c-51f5-45f6 referencing this epic and the two new fields.

- Scenario analysis (Step 3): triggered (SCs >= 5); 15 red-team scenarios; 4 surviving after blue-team filter (all addressed via additional spec mitigations).

2. Establish a .test-index authoring style guide: no broad directory wildcards without justification, to prevent a single entry from inflating required test sets for all commits in a directory.
Deferred pending style guide definition. See bug a1c9-a4b7 for full incident context.

**What**: Write failing integration tests for the perceptual diff validation pipeline: Figma PNG export, Playwright screenshot capture, pixelmatch comparison, threshold gating, and graceful degradation.

content.text: ## Description
**What**: Extend `post-all.sh` hook to extract per-turn token counts from the Claude Code hook payload and write them to an active ticket via `ticket-edit.sh --tokens_measured=`.

**Why**: Without automatic extraction, every agent and skill would need to manually emit token counts, which they will not do reliably. The hook runs on every tool call completion and can accumulate per-session token deltas.
**Scope**:
- IN: Parse `post-all.sh` hook payload for token count fields (input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_creation_tokens).
- IN: Active-ticket detection — read a session-local file (e.g. `/tmp/dso-active-ticket-<pid>`) or env var that skills set when beginning work on a specific ticket.
- IN: Accumulate tokens for the session and write periodically (every N tool calls or at session end) to the active ticket.
- OUT: Retroactive token attribution for past sessions.
- OUT: Planning-vs-execution separation — planning skills emit tokens_estimated in their own story.
## Done Definitions
- When this story is complete, a sprint session with an active ticket accumulates `tokens_measured` on that ticket visible via `ticket show`.
← Satisfies: "Measure execution token use on the worked ticket"
- When this story is complete, closing the active ticket stops accumulation for that ticket and resumes if a new active ticket is declared.
← Satisfies: "Measure execution token use on the worked ticket"
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic.
## Considerations
- [Reliability] Hook failure must not block tool use — fail-open if token extraction errors.
- [Performance] Write frequency balance — too frequent writes bloat the event log.
## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

`plugins/dso/agents/second-source-verifier.md` is a fully-built audit agent that confirms three mechanisms were actually used during each story closure: (1) typed-enum verifier P1 field, (2) deterministic narrative renderer (`render-closure-narrative.sh`), (3) story-handoff gate (`check-story-handoff.sh`). PR-G/H/I (Week 3 audit remediation) updated `AGENTS.md` to remove the vague "in-progress epic for full wire-up" annotation and replaced it with a concrete deferred-decision list. This ticket tracks resolving that deferred decision.
## Prerequisites (must be satisfied before wiring)

2. **Decision: advisory-vs-blocking verdict semantics** — when second-source-verifier returns `SECOND_SOURCE_VERDICT: FAIL`, does the sprint closure flow halt (blocking) or just log the finding (advisory)? content.text: ## Story S2: Per-session isolation via session-start hook + session_id sanitization + CI fallback
### Description

**What**: Extend the DSO session-start hook to capture the Claude Code `session_id` from hook input, sanitize to `[a-f0-9-]+` (non-conforming inputs are hashed into a conforming key), and write `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dso-test-run/.current-session`. `test-run.sh` reads this file to scope all state under `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dso-test-run/<session_id>/`. When `.current-session` is missing, the launcher falls back to `$GITHUB_RUN_ID` → `$CI_JOB_ID` → `sha256(cwd)[:16]` in that precedence order. Never uses a silent shared default.

**Why**: Cross-session concurrency (two Claude sessions running tests simultaneously in different worktrees or the same worktree) requires per-session state keying. CI runs are not Claude sessions and need a deterministic fallback.
**Scope**:
- IN: session-start hook update, session_id sanitizer, `.current-session` marker, per-session state dir layout, CI fallback chain
- OUT: same-session duplicate-launch guard (S3), cleanup of orphaned state dirs (operational — not in this epic)
### Done Definitions
- When this story is complete, session-start hook writes the sanitized session_id to `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dso-test-run/.current-session`
← Satisfies: "session-start hook captures the Claude Code session_id, sanitizes to [a-f0-9-]+, and writes ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dso-test-run/.current-session"
- When this story is complete, two Claude sessions with different session_ids invoke `test-run start` simultaneously without shared-state collision (state dirs are distinct)
← Satisfies: "Two Claude sessions running in different worktrees (or the same worktree) can invoke test-run start simultaneously without any shared-state collision"
- When this story is complete, a CI run (no `.current-session` present) derives a session key from `$GITHUB_RUN_ID`, `$CI_JOB_ID`, or `sha256(cwd)` in that precedence order

← Satisfies: "When .current-session is missing (CI runs, session-start hook failed to fire, upgraded plugin with stale hooks), the launcher falls back to a deterministic key derived from $GITHUB_RUN_ID, $CI_JOB_ID, or a cwd-hash in that precedence order — never silently using a shared default"
- When this story is complete, a session_id containing `/`, `..`, or whitespace is rejected-and-hashed rather than used directly in a path
← Satisfies: "sanitizes it to [a-f0-9-]+ (rejecting any input containing /, .., whitespace, or path-traversal sequences — fall back to a hash of the raw session_id when the input is non-conforming)"
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic
### Considerations
- [Security] path-traversal sanitization is a security-relevant boundary — verify with adversarial inputs in unit tests
- [Reliability] session-start hook registration must survive plugin upgrades; if hook fails to fire, the CI fallback chain keeps the launcher functional
## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

content.text: ## Continuous Monitoring and Observability

Deploying code is only half the battle; knowing how it behaves in the wild is the other. Observability involves instrumenting systems with logs, metrics, and traces to understand their internal states.
**The Impact:** It drastically reduces Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR) by allowing teams to pinpoint and fix the root cause of production failures quickly.
## Scope

Integrate observability considerations into the preplanning and implementation-plan workflows so that logging, metrics, and tracing are planned and implemented as first-class concerns alongside feature code — not bolted on after deployment. Preplanning should generate stories that include observability requirements, and implementation-plan should produce tasks that cover instrumentation alongside functional implementation.

content.text: Integrate mandatory security declarations into brainstorm, preplanning, and implementation-plan so security concerns are addressed at planning time — not discovered at code review.
## Mandatory Declarations
Every planning workflow must verify the following security declarations exist before implementation begins:
### 1. Endpoint Access Level Declaration
Every endpoint must explicitly declare its access level: **public**, **authenticated**, or **internal**. Ambiguity (not intentional public) is a planning failure, not a code review finding.
- **Where enforced:** Implementation-plan task generation — every task creating an API endpoint must include an access_level field in its acceptance criteria
- **Preplanning check:** Security reviewer flags stories involving new endpoints without access classification
### 2. PII Encryption-at-Rest Plan
Every data field touching PII must have an encryption-at-rest plan before implementation.
- **Where enforced:** Brainstorm — during gap analysis, any epic involving user data collection must identify PII fields and their encryption strategy
- **Implementation-plan check:** Tasks creating database models or data stores with PII fields must include encryption acceptance criteria
- **What to declare:** Field name, PII category (name, SSN, DOB, address, etc.), encryption method (column-level, volume-level, application-level), key management approach
### 3. External Integration Threat Model
Every external integration must have a threat model entry before implementation.
- **Where enforced:** Brainstorm — during the scrutiny pipeline, any epic involving external APIs, third-party services, or data exchange must produce a threat model entry
- **What to declare:** Integration name, data exchanged, trust boundary, authentication method, failure mode (fail-open vs fail-closed), data residency implications
### 4. Agent/Sub-Agent Permission Scope
Every agent or sub-agent must have a declared permission scope.
- **Where enforced:** Implementation-plan — tasks dispatching sub-agents must declare permitted tools, file access scope, and network access
- **Preplanning check:** Stories involving multi-agent orchestration must include permission boundaries in done definitions
- **What to declare:** Permitted tools list, file/directory access scope, network access (none/internal/external), credential access (none/scoped/inherited)
### 5. User Input Validation Strategy
Every user input path must identify its validation strategy before implementation.
- **Where enforced:** Implementation-plan — tasks accepting user input must declare validation approach in acceptance criteria

- **What to declare:** Input type, validation method (allowlist/denylist/regex/schema), server-side enforcement (mandatory), max length, encoding/escaping strategy for output contexts (HTML, SQL, shell, etc.)
## Integration Approach
### Brainstorm
- Gap analysis phase should check for PII fields and external integrations in the epic scope
- Scrutiny pipeline should flag epics touching user data or external services that lack security declarations
- Success criteria should include security declarations when applicable
### Preplanning
- Security concern area scan (Phase C) should verify each story has the required declarations based on its scope
- Stories without required declarations should be flagged as incomplete
### Implementation-Plan
- Task acceptance criteria library should include composable security declaration blocks
- The 5 parallel reviewers should include a check: "Does every task with [endpoint/PII/integration/agent/input] have the corresponding security declaration?"
- Tasks missing declarations should fail the plan review gate
## Government Context
These declarations map to federal compliance requirements:
- Access levels → NIST 800-53 AC (Access Control) family
- PII encryption → NIST 800-53 SC-28 (Protection of Information at Rest), NIST 800-122
- Threat models → NIST 800-53 RA-3 (Risk Assessment), FedRAMP requirements
- Permission scopes → NIST 800-53 AC-6 (Least Privilege)
- Input validation → NIST 800-53 SI-10 (Information Input Validation), OWASP Top 10

content.text: ## Context

Placeholder epic capturing the research baseline for considering idempotent task semantics in `/dso:implementation-plan` output. The reference pattern (from `navapbc/bao-nguyen-agent-skills` and similar projects): every task an agent emits checks for existing state before performing the action — grep Gemfile before appending; check generator already-run before invoking; collision-detect before scaffolding. Currently DSO's planning skills emit tasks that describe desired state without idempotency guards; the implementer (human or sub-agent) is responsible for state-checks at run time.
This epic is NOT yet brainstormed; it is a durable capture of research so the work can be picked up in a future `/dso:brainstorm` session without re-doing the survey.
## Research baseline (2026-05-08, dispatched as part of Epic B brainstorm)

Surveyed 15 popular agentic / AI-assisted code-generation projects: Cline, Roo Code, Cursor (Composer), Continue.dev, Aider, GitHub Copilot Workspace, SWE-agent, OpenHands/OpenDevin, Devin/Cognition, Goose (Block), Cody (Sourcegraph), Augment Code, smol-developer, MetaGPT, CrewAI, plus LangGraph as orchestration framework reference.

Adoption strength: **weak-to-moderate** (high confidence). Idempotent task semantics as an explicit, default-enforced design principle is rare across the surveyed tools. The dominant pattern: file-write tools overwrite freely; user approval (or git-revert recovery) is the guard, not pre-write state checks. Diff-based editing reduces blast radius but doesn't enforce existence checks.

Strongest exception: LangGraph's persistence/checkpointing layer prevents re-execution of completed workflow tasks (workflow-level idempotency). LangGraph docs *recommend* idempotency at the task level but do not enforce it.

`bao-nguyen-agent-skills` is one of the few projects where the pattern is enforced explicitly at the workflow-as-skill scale — every skill grep-checks Gemfile before appending, checks for existing files before generator invocation, etc. It is a small public collection (4 skills), not a widely-adopted framework.
## Pain-point evidence (real and growing)
- GitHub Copilot Agent double-edit bug: "Agent will edit a file twice, fixing the issue twice, often making worse code" — vscode-copilot-release#9439

- "LLM agents retry tool calls 15-30% of the time due to timeouts, validation errors, or model uncertainty. Without idempotency, a simple retry could corrupt a file, duplicate a transaction, or crash a workflow." — fast.io/resources/ai-agent-idempotent-operations/
- Armin Ronacher's "chaos monkey" principle: tools must be "protected against an LLM chaos monkey using them completely wrong." — lucumr.pocoo.org/2025/6/12/agentic-coding/
- Anthropic engineering on long-running agents: state-verification-before-action via progress notes + git log review. — anthropic.com/engineering/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents
## Open questions for future brainstorm

- Where does the idempotency guard live: in the task TEXT emitted by `/dso:implementation-plan` (a guard clause like "skip if Gemfile already contains gem X"), or in the TOOL LAYER (a file-write wrapper that checks before acting), or at the WORKFLOW LAYER (LangGraph-style checkpoint)? These have very different implementation costs and failure modes.
- False-skip rate: how often would an idempotency guard incorrectly conclude "already done" and skip a legitimately-needed update?
- Sub-agent compliance reliability: do DSO's sub-agents reliably honor guard clause language, or treat it as advisory like LangGraph does?
- Specific semantics of "idempotent" for our purposes: workflow-level, task-level, or operation-level?
- Pilot scope: which task type to pilot the pattern on first (e.g., "add dependency to manifest file") before universalizing?
- Interaction with DSO's testing_mode discipline: how does idempotency-by-default coexist with RED test gating?
## References
- `navapbc/bao-nguyen-agent-skills` — small public skill collection where the pattern is enforced explicitly
- LangGraph "Don't Run It Twice" — dev.to/ajay_gupta_60a0393643f3e9/dont-run-it-twice-mastering-idempotency-in-production-langgraph-agents-2gmp
- LangGraph durable-execution docs — docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/durable-execution
- AI Agent Idempotent Operations Guide — fast.io/resources/ai-agent-idempotent-operations/
- Armin Ronacher "Agentic Coding Recommendations" — lucumr.pocoo.org/2025/6/12/agentic-coding/
- Anthropic "Effective Harnesses for Long-Running Agents" — anthropic.com/engineering/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents
- This baseline was dispatched during Epic B (Strata SDK planning context) brainstorming on 2026-05-08; full sub-agent report lives in this session's transcript.
## Status
Captured for future brainstorming. Do NOT plan or implement until `/dso:brainstorm <epic-id>` has been run interactively. Tagged `scrutiny:pending`.

content.text: ## Incident Overview

During sprint d076-d35e-55db-4843 (the epic that *shipped* the per-branch CI review architecture), the orchestrator used \`DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=0\` to commit sub-agent work directly to the session branch instead of dispatching agents into per-story sub-branches. As a result, 22 commits with DSO-Story trailers landed on the session branch without ever creating sub-branch PRs.

The shipped architecture detected this correctly — \`verify-session-provenance.sh\` marks those commits as un-provenanced, and \`ci.yml\`'s narrow integration review unions un-provenanced SHAs into the LLM review scope. So the entire sprint output ended up routed through a single integration review on PR #140. The LLM reviewer hit a ~1095-line diff and produced cycle-3 findings that included 4/4 critical false positives ("file X does not exist" hallucinations against files that demonstrably do exist).
## Reproduce / Conditions
1. \`/dso:sprint <epic>\` runs in ci-pr mode
2. Sub-agents work in worktree-isolated environments but commit directly to the session branch using \`DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=0\` (escape hatch documented in CLAUDE.md)
3. Story sub-branches are never created
4. Sprint completes; \`merge-to-main.sh\` opens session->main PR
5. CI runs \`per-branch-review.yml\` (per-story review) on the WHOLE diff because the session branch is effectively the story branch
6. LLM review produces unreliable findings on the oversized diff
## Gap
There is no recovery mechanism to retroactively split bypassed commits into per-story sub-branch PRs after the fact. The shipped architecture *detects* the bypass but cannot *remediate* it.
## Proposed Mechanism
\`plugins/dso/scripts/redistribute-session-commits.sh\`:
- Input: \`--epic <epic-id>\` and optional \`--dry-run\`
- Walks \`git log main..session-HEAD\`, extracts \`DSO-Story:\` trailers
- Groups commits by story-id (auto), surfaces untagged commits for user classification (interactive)
- Preserves merge commits (they represent integration history)
- For each story-id: creates \`story/<epic-id>/<story-id>\` from main, cherry-picks the commits in order, pushes, opens PR with \`base=<session-branch>\`
- Result: per-story PRs each trigger per-branch-review.yml on scoped diffs; the session->main PR's narrow integration review shrinks to only true cross-branch concerns
## Related
- Sprint epic d076-d35e-55db-4843 (closed) shipped detect/route mechanism
- Companion bug: governance for the DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=0 escape hatch (separate ticket)

## Context

After a Strata project is scaffolded — by Epic A1's `create-dso-app.sh` or by manual `nava-platform`/`gem "strata"` adoption — `/dso:onboarding` is unaware of Strata. It writes generic `commands.*` keys that silently shadow Strata's Make targets (the friction the CI/CD audit flagged), misses well-documented Strata footguns (e.g., `ActionController::API` load-time crash, Case→Form FK violation), and never tells users about `nava-platform app update` as the canonical upgrade path. This epic adds Strata-awareness to the consolidated `/dso:onboarding` (per 136b-6758) via a sibling detector script, a `prompts/strata/` topic-prompt directory loaded surgically by phase mechanism, and ONE Socratic-confirmation dialog turn (non-tech UX = one yes/edit/no click). Detection feeds A0's namespaced array; config writes consume A1's shared `strata-config-defaults.conf` (drift prevention).
## In Scope

- New `plugins/dso/scripts/detect-strata.sh` (sibling to `detect-stack.sh`). Scans for `.template-*/<file>.yml` markers at PROJECT root (per A1's spike); reads `_src_path` to sub-classify (`framework:strata-rails` / `framework:strata-nextjs` / `framework:strata-flask` / `infra:strata`); reads `_commit` for upgrade-lifecycle context. Gemfile fallback uses canonical fingerprint `gem ['"]strata['"].*github:\s*['"]navapbc/strata-sdk-rails['"]` (NOT bare `gem "strata"`). Emits namespaced tags into A0's `stack` array per the v2 schema. Writes structured detection-facts artifact at `${WORKFLOW_PLUGIN_ARTIFACTS_DIR}/strata-detection.env` (KEY=VALUE: STRATA_TEMPLATE_KIND, STRATA_COMMIT_PIN, STRATA_SRC_PATH, STRATA_DETECTION_SOURCE in {marker, gemfile-fallback}). YAML field values written via `printf '%s=%q\n'` (bash-quoted) to prevent injection. `mkdir -p "$WORKFLOW_PLUGIN_ARTIFACTS_DIR"` before write. Multiline-aware Gemfile scan via awk (handles continuation patterns). Glob `**/.template-*/[a-z][a-z0-9-_]*.yml` supports monorepos. Reusable by Epic B's planning skills.
- New directory `plugins/dso/skills/onboarding/prompts/strata/`:
- `README.md`: index documenting which sub-file the architect-foundation/dialogue phases load at which step; tags each sub-file silent vs. dialog

- `config-writes.md` (silent): sources A1's `plugins/dso/scripts/lib/strata-config-defaults.conf` (ships in plugin filesystem); writes `commands.*` keys per detected `STRATA_TEMPLATE_KIND`. Multi-template projects: union per A0's multi-valued schema. Append via normalize-then-write helper (split on `;`, dedupe, rejoin) to prevent semicolon corruption

- `arch-enforcement.md` (silent): appends Rails-Strata footguns from shared defaults to `.claude/ARCH_ENFORCEMENT.md` if `framework:strata-rails` is in stack array. Footgun idempotency keys on stable HTML-comment markers (e.g., `<!-- strata-footgun:rails:no-action-controller-api -->`), NOT raw rule text. Semantic overlap check before append: grep for keywords like `ActionController::API`, `belongs_to :case`; if found, emit `[A2 WARN] potential conflict: existing rule may overlap with Strata footgun '<title>'; review ARCH_ENFORCEMENT.md` and skip that footgun

- `posture-dialog.md` (dialog): one Socratic turn presenting STRATA_DETECTION_SOURCE, detected template(s), `_commit` pin(s), `_src_path`(s), and the upgrade hint as the dialog's pre-filled default. Four responses: `yes` / `edit` / `not Strata` / `[I no longer use Strata]`. `not Strata` cleanup removes Strata tags from in-memory stack array; comment in project-understanding.md notes "User declined Strata configuration on YYYY-MM-DD". Non-interactive context (no TTY): default to `yes` (proceed with detected defaults) with audit log; documented in README.md. Strata-removal 4th response (`[I no longer use Strata]`) removes Posture section + footguns + Strata commands.* values

- `posture-writer.md` (silent, runs after posture-dialog approval): atomic write via mktemp + mv -f. Writes approved `## Strata Posture` section to `project-understanding.md`. Idempotent (replaces existing section if present; otherwise appends)

- The relevant 136b-6758 phase files (architect-foundation, dialogue) gain phase-conditional Reads of these sub-files when `platform:strata` in stack array. Sequencing: config-writes during config emission step; arch-enforcement during enforcement scaffolding step; posture-dialog during dialogue/confirmation step; posture-writer after posture-dialog approval.

- `detect-strata.sh` wired into A0's detector-orchestration so its output unions into the unified `stack` array (NOT a separate config key). Documented in A0's `DETECTION-SCHEMA.md` as a worked example of "adding a sibling detector".

- New `--no-strata` flag for graceful skip on older plugin versions (when `prompts/strata/` subdirectory missing); explicit error if missing without flag: `[A2] requires prompts/strata/ from plugin v<min>+; update plugin or pass --no-strata`. Documented one-liner migration: `bash plugins/dso/scripts/detect-strata.sh && /dso:onboarding --resume=strata-only` re-runs detection + four sub-files without re-running other phases. STRATA_SKIP signal: `--no-strata` writes `strata.skip=true` to dso-config.conf; sprint/brainstorm/preplanning check this key for graceful degradation.
- Pre-commit hook `check-no-stack-case.sh` self-exclusion list covers the hook's own source, the synthetic-detector fixture, the schema doc's anti-pattern section.

- `dso:completion-verifier` validation on Strata-detected runs: (a) `commands.*` matches `strata-config-defaults.conf` for the detected variant, (b) all 5 Rails-Strata footguns present when `framework:strata-rails`, (c) `## Strata Posture` exists in `project-understanding.md`.
- Behavioral tests:

- `tests/scripts/test-detect-strata-fixtures.sh` against 7 fixtures (rails-with-marker, nextjs-with-marker, flask-with-marker, infra-with-marker, manual-gemfile-only, no-strata, multi-template-rails-and-infra)
- `tests/scripts/test-onboarding-strata-idempotency.sh` — fresh-from-A1 fixture: zero diffs in `commands.*`, `ARCH_ENFORCEMENT.md`, `## Strata Posture`

- `tests/scripts/test-onboarding-strata-fresh-detection.sh` — manual-adoption fixture (Gemfile fingerprint match, no markers): asserts Gemfile-fallback fires, posture-dialog notes detection-source, post-`yes` writes land

- Behavioral tests cover: not-Strata cleanup (asserts tags removed from stack array after dialog), non-interactive default (asserts dialog auto-yes when no TTY), version-skew error path (asserts clear error message + `--no-strata` skip works)
## Out of Scope
- Layer 4 microservice detection (Epic C — d08f-03d7-a148-43d0)
- Strata SDK planning context for brainstorm/preplanning/implementation-plan (Epic B)
- Sample-feature scaffolding
- NextJS/Flask-specific footguns (v1 Rails-only; SDK is Rails-only)
- Multi-template disambiguation dialog (A0's multi-valued `commands.*` handles natively)
- Mixed Strata-and-non-Strata polyglot (single-Strata-template-per-project for v1)
- Modifications to 136b-6758's phase mechanism — A2 consumes the mechanism as documented
## Success Criteria

1. Detection emits correct namespaced tags + facts artifact across 7 enumerated fixtures: (1) rails-with-marker (fresh A1 scaffold); (2) nextjs-with-marker; (3) flask-with-marker; (4) infra-only-with-marker; (5) manual-gemfile-only (Gemfile fingerprint match, no markers); (6) no-strata (negative case); (7) multi-template (Rails+infra). Each golden-master asserts emitted stack-array additions AND `strata-detection.env` contents. Malformed-marker case asserts non-zero exit + clear stderr naming the file.

2. Fresh-from-A1 idempotency: `/dso:onboarding` on A1-scaffolded project produces ZERO file diffs in `commands.*`, `ARCH_ENFORCEMENT.md`, `## Strata Posture`. Posture dialog presents detected facts; `yes` completes phase with no content changes. Confirmation receipt printed: "Strata detected — configured commands.* (test_runner=make test, lint=make lint-ci, ...), added 5 footguns to ARCH_ENFORCEMENT.md, wrote ## Strata Posture to project-understanding.md. No further Strata questions." Verified by behavioral test asserting (a) zero diffs (b) dialog-turn count = 1 (c) receipt content present.

3. Manual-adoption Gemfile-fallback: fixture with multiline-aware Gemfile fingerprint match and no markers triggers fallback. Two assertions: (a) `dso-config.conf` contains correct `commands.*` key-value pairs (unit assertion); (b) `validate.sh --ci` invokes the correct command string when run on the fixture (integration assertion).

4. Phase wiring + completion-verifier: `prompts/strata/README.md` documents sub-file/phase/step mapping; phase files Read sub-files at documented steps; `dso:completion-verifier` confirms (a) `commands.*` matches shared-defaults file, (b) all 5 footguns present (when Rails-Strata), (c) `## Strata Posture` exists. Behavioral tests cover not-Strata cleanup, non-interactive auto-yes, version-skew `--no-strata` skip, strata-removal 4th dialog response.
5. No Strata writes on non-Strata projects: `/dso:onboarding` on a non-Strata fixture produces zero `prompts/strata/*` Reads, zero Strata-specific writes, no Strata mention in any artifact.

6. Reviewer enforcement loop verified: A behavioral test submits a diff containing an `ActionController::API` subclass to a Strata-configured Rails project fixture; the code-reviewer agent returns at least one finding that references the ARCH_ENFORCEMENT.md footgun by keyword (e.g., contains `ActionController::API` or the footgun title). Test fails if findings list is empty OR if no finding references the footgun.
## Scenario Analysis

13 surviving scenarios from red/blue team filter (10 filtered). Mitigations folded into Robustness contract: silent-exit detection failures (explicit error + non-zero exit), ARTIFACTS_DIR creation (mkdir -p before write), multiline Gemfile (awk), not-Strata cleanup (tag removal from stack array), atomic writes (mktemp + mv), semicolon-corruption (normalize-then-write helper), monorepo (glob support), non-interactive default (auto-yes with audit log), KEY=VALUE injection (bash-quoted printf), posture-writer atomicity (mktemp + mv), version-skew (`--no-strata` flag + clear error), footgun text drift (HTML-comment markers as idempotency keys), footgun semantic overlap (warn rather than blind-append).
## Approach

Layered detection (sibling `detect-strata.sh` to existing `detect-stack.sh`, output unioned into A0's array) plus tiered prompt sub-files in `prompts/strata/` directory loaded surgically by phase mechanism. Single Socratic dialog turn for posture confirmation; rest is silent application. Sources A1's shared defaults file for drift prevention. Robustness mitigations across 13 surviving scenarios.
## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation, 2026-05-18)
### Self-use SC (Probe-1 remediation)

The 8623 sprint exercises the new strata detection + Socratic-confirmed posture + silent config flow on a fixture project (or on this DSO repo) during sprint execution. At least one full strata-aware onboarding run produces a populated `## Strata Posture` section in `project-understanding.md` AND writes the strata-detection.env keys.
Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):
- A test fixture project (or self-application against this repo) is onboarded via `/dso:onboarding`; the resulting `project-understanding.md` contains a non-empty `## Strata Posture` section.
- `cat strata-detection.env | grep -cE '^STRATA_(TEMPLATE_KIND|COMMIT_PIN|SRC_PATH|DETECTION_SOURCE)='` returns 4 (all keys populated).
- The detect-strata.sh script's Socratic-confirm step is exercised (transcript shows the dialog OR `--non-interactive` mode is used with the result recorded).
### State Lifecycle Owner Block (Probe-3 remediation)
| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |

| `strata.skip` (dso-config.conf) | `/dso:onboarding` writes false at project setup; operator can flip true to disable | Operator edit | detect-strata.sh; brainstorm/preplanning/impl-plan strata gates | N/A — persistent per-project |

| `STRATA_TEMPLATE_KIND` (strata-detection.env) | detect-strata.sh writes after detection + Socratic confirm | Re-detection on stack change; manual re-run of detect-strata.sh | Brainstorm, preplanning, impl-plan strata-aware gates; create-dso-app.sh | Implicit with `strata.skip=true` flip OR project teardown |
| `STRATA_COMMIT_PIN` | Same | Operator updates when pinning to a new strata template version | Strata-aware planning; create-dso-app.sh | Same |
| `STRATA_SRC_PATH` | Same | Re-detection | Same | Same |
| `STRATA_DETECTION_SOURCE` (enum: auto, socratic, manual) | Same | Same | Audit/observability: which detection mode was used | Same |

| HTML-comment footgun markers in ARCH_ENFORCEMENT.md | Sprint writes during epic ship | Stable (no in-place mutation) | Reviewer + agent guards | Removed only by explicit reviewer decision when the footgun no longer applies (manual edit) |

| `## Strata Posture` section in project-understanding.md | /dso:onboarding writes at first strata-aware run | Re-onboarding rewrites the section (preserving prior content under "Previous detections" subheading if value changes) | Future planning runs read for context | Persistent project artifact; cleaned up only at project teardown |
Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):
- `grep -E '^strata\.skip=' .claude/dso-config.conf` shows the key with documented default.
- `cat strata-detection.env` shows all four env keys populated (or `strata.skip=true` is set, suppressing strata gates entirely).
- `grep -c '## Strata Posture' project-understanding.md` returns 1 in a strata-aware project.
## Dependencies
All three blocking dependencies are in-flight epics in this same brainstorm session, not pre-existing infrastructure. A2 enters sprint only after all three are merged to main:
- A0 (188c-47e4-5abe-4b9c — namespaced array schema): `stack=` namespaced array; multi-valued `commands.*` semicolon-delimited; `DETECTION-SCHEMA.md` axis enum
- 136b-6758 (consolidated onboarding with prompts/<topic>.md mechanism): `phases/<phase>.md` orchestrators + `prompts/<topic>/` Read mechanism
- A1 (d765-a3b6-84bd-4816 — create-dso-app.sh rewrite): `plugins/dso/scripts/lib/strata-config-defaults.conf` (in-plugin filesystem, ALWAYS available regardless of host setup path)

content.text: As an implementation-plan agent running in a partially-deployed environment, I can rely on ref-library-loader.sh to degrade gracefully when dso ref-query or confluence-fetch.sh is absent.
Done definitions:
- Startup check for `command -v dso ref-query` that explicitly verifies subcommand registration (not just dso binary presence); absent → stderr warning, URL-only mode
- Startup check for `command -v confluence-fetch.sh`; absent → stderr warning, corpus-only mode
- Missing `confluence.base_url` in dso-config.conf → configuration error at startup, URL fetch path aborts, corpus-only mode with clear stderr error
- BOTH unavailable → stderr warning, tasks generated without citations, no error
- Story ba7d-729d's "both-unavailable" and guard-related sub-tests continue to pass after implementation
- Unit tests cover each degradation mode
Considerations:
- [Reliability] Subcommand-registration check is stricter than `command -v dso` — test both binary-absent and subcommand-absent paths
- [Maintainability] Centralize fallback logic in one function
- [Maintainability] Subcommand-registration check must suppress/separate its own stderr from the startup warning channel so unrelated dso init warnings are not confused with "ref-query unavailable"

## Context

Sprint orchestrators today cannot reliably determine which files a task will touch before dispatching agents — file impact data is stored as free-text markdown embedded in ticket comments or descriptions, parsed ad-hoc by 4 scripts (sprint-next-batch.sh, sprint-drift-check.sh, sprint-review-scope-check.sh, enrich-file-impact.sh). Each script reimplements its own markdown parser, producing inconsistent extraction results that cause agent conflicts and missed drift detection. This epic gives orchestrators a structured, queryable file impact field so conflict detection and drift checks operate on authoritative data rather than best-effort text extraction. When the ticket system is eventually extracted into an MCP server, file impact will be a structured, queryable field — not a convention buried in free text.
## Success Criteria

- A FILE_IMPACT event type is supported by the ticket system: ticket-lib.sh write_commit_event() accepts FILE_IMPACT in its event type enum, and ticket-reducer.py compiles FILE_IMPACT events into a structured file_impact field in the ticket's compiled state — containing an array of {path, reason} objects with latest-wins semantics

- ticket set-file-impact <id> <json> stores structured file impact data as a FILE_IMPACT event; ticket get-file-impact <id> returns the structured array; ticket show <id> includes the file_impact field in its output

- The Jira outbound bridge surfaces file impact in Jira using two mechanisms: (a) a Jira issue property (key: dso.file_impact, set via direct REST API PUT to /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/properties/dso.file_impact using AcliClient._direct_rest_put() — a new method justified by spike confirming ACLI has no properties subcommand) for machine-readable storage, and (b) a single formatted comment (deduped by UUID marker via the existing comment dedup mechanism and .jira-comment-map) for human visibility. The inbound bridge ignores the dso.file_impact property (properties live outside fields.*) and deduplicates the outbound comment via the existing dedup map. Bridge auth: if API token, no scope change required; if OAuth 2.0, confirm write:jira-work scope is present

- bridge-outbound.py process_outbound() handles FILE_IMPACT events explicitly — they do not fall through silently. When issue property PUT fails, a BRIDGE_ALERT event is written with reason FILE_IMPACT_SYNC_FAILED; when comment add fails, a distinct BRIDGE_ALERT event is written with reason FILE_IMPACT_COMMENT_SYNC_FAILED; no transactional rollback across the two channels

- enrich-file-impact.sh is refactored: LLM generation (Haiku API call) stays in the workflow layer; storage changes from ticket comment to ticket set-file-impact. sprint-drift-check.sh and sprint-review-scope-check.sh are also refactored to use ticket get-file-impact instead of ad-hoc markdown parsing — all four ad-hoc parsers migrate to the structured API. Markdown parsers preserved as SECONDARY fallback for tickets pre-migration
## Dependencies

- Epic A1 (2c28-e5b9 — Ticket System Core Query Layer): partial — sprint-next-batch.sh integration via ticket next-batch needs A1's subcommand. All other SCs in this epic are unblocked. Stories covering sprint-next-batch.sh integration should be sequenced after A1 delivers ticket next-batch.
## Approach

FILE_IMPACT event type follows the existing event pattern (JSON file in ticket directory, atomic commit via flock). Jira bridge uses a new _direct_rest_put() method on AcliClient — AcliClient already stores credentials on self with a comment noting they're available for direct REST calls; _direct_rest_put() contains the ACLI-only pattern break cleanly with unit tests mocking the PUT and asserting credential header injection. Permissions: Browse projects + Edit issues (same auth bridge already has with API tokens).
## Research Findings

- Jira REST API: `PUT /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/properties/{propertyKey}` is the canonical mechanism for structured machine-readable metadata that should NOT appear in fields.* (issue properties live outside the field schema and are ignored by the inbound bridge correctly)

- ACLI limitation confirmed via spike: ACLI has no `properties` subcommand — justifies the _direct_rest_put() pattern break; method reuses same credential mechanism (_build_env) as existing ACLI subprocess calls for credential continuity
- Permissions: `write:jira-work` scope (OAuth 2.0) or standard API token with Browse projects + Edit issues — same scope existing bridge already has; no new scope request required
- UUID-marker dedup: existing .jira-comment-map mechanism handles comment deduplication; new FILE_IMPACT comment uses a new UUID marker category

- Migration pattern: update-artifacts.sh supports versioned migrations via stamp files; file-impact-v1 stamp records {version, migrated_at, tickets_processed, tickets_skipped} for idempotency and audit
- Reducer semantics: latest-wins is the chosen pattern for current-state fields (file impact describes what a ticket's current scope is, not its history)
## Scenario Analysis

- Jira property PUT succeeds but comment add fails (medium, integration): distinct BRIDGE_ALERT reason FILE_IMPACT_COMMENT_SYNC_FAILED for comment-channel failure; no transactional rollback across channels — property succeeds, comment retries on next sync

- Inbound bridge re-reads dso.file_impact property and tries to write back (high, sync loop): inbound ignores the property explicitly; FILE_IMPACT events originate from DSO only — Jira is a one-way surface
- Migration re-runs and duplicates events (high, correctness): stamp file with file-impact-v1 key prevents re-run; idempotency test case in migration test suite
- Migration parses malformed markdown and creates corrupt events (medium, correctness): unparseable entries logged to stderr with ticket ID and skipped; original markdown preserved for manual triage

- Latest-wins reducer semantics clobber earlier FILE_IMPACT events (medium, design): explicit latest-wins is the chosen semantic — documented in SC1 and reducer tests; intentional because file impact is current-state, not historical

- _direct_rest_put() bypasses ACLI's retry/rate-limit handling (medium, reliability): method inherits credential mechanism but not retry logic — basic retry with exponential backoff added in the method; documented limitation

- bridge-outbound FILE_IMPACT branch silently falls through when event handler missing (high, integration): explicit enum check in dispatcher; unknown event types emit BRIDGE_ALERT UNKNOWN_EVENT_TYPE rather than silent drop
### Planning Intelligence Log
- **Web research (Step 2.6)**: triggered

- Bright-line conditions that fired: external integration (Jira REST API `/rest/api/3/issue/{key}/properties/{propertyKey}` endpoint, AcliClient pattern break), novel architectural pattern (FILE_IMPACT event type + latest-wins reducer semantics for structured current-state fields)
- **Scenario analysis (Step 2.75)**: triggered
- Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 7
- **Practitioner-requested additional cycles**: none
- **Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0)**: not triggered
- **Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5)**: triggered — ACLI properties-subcommand spike confirmed absence, justifying _direct_rest_put() pattern break
- **LLM-instruction signal (Step 5)**: not triggered — this epic is data schema + bridge integration; no LLM-facing instruction changes
- **Scale context (Step 0)**: small scale (default) — per-ticket file-impact storage; write volume bounded by ticket edit frequency; not volume-sensitive
## Closure Checks

- update-artifacts.sh is extended with a data migration phase: the first registered migration scans all tickets for ## File Impact patterns in COMMENT event bodies and description text, extracts file paths, and writes corresponding FILE_IMPACT events. Success: all tickets with parseable patterns have a FILE_IMPACT event; unparseable tickets logged to stderr with ticket ID and skipped; re-running on migrated tickets is a no-op (stamp prevents re-run, keyed by migration ID file-impact-v1). Stamp records {version, migrated_at, tickets_processed, tickets_skipped}. Test suite includes well-formed fixture, malformed fixture, and idempotency case

**What**: Sprint Phase I self-use verification for epic c2cc-e3c4 SC-7. During the c2cc sprint itself, confirm the directory-size advisory hook is wired, executable via the session-start dispatcher, and that at least one session-start event has triggered it with one of: (a) a no-issues confirmation logged, or (b) at least one advisory ticket auto-filed with the canonical `directory-size-advisory` tag.

**Why**: Self-use Probe-1 means we dogfood the hook on this very sprint — not a follow-on sprint. SC-7 verification record evidence in the epic verification manifest so the completion-verifier can read it.
**Scope**:

- IN: Phase I verification at sprint wrap, after task 1706-b0cb has merged; must run from the live sprint session so the dispatcher has actually fired the hook; evidence captured in epic verification manifest
- OUT: Implementation of the hook itself (already owned by b026-bc46 / 3dcc-9f35 / bc70-c09b); changing the verification commands in SC-7
## Acceptance Criteria
- Hook executability verified: `test -x plugins/dso/hooks/dispatchers/session-start.sh` returns 0 AND the dispatcher sources `hook_directory_size_monitor` (grep confirms the source line)
- At least one session-start event during the c2cc sprint has invoked the directory-size monitor — confirmed via session log entry, hook stdout capture, or dispatcher trace

- Either (a) the hook emitted its no-issues confirmation line (captured verbatim in the verification manifest), OR (b) `.claude/scripts/dso ticket list --has-tag=directory-size-advisory --format=llm` returns ≥ 1 ticket
- Verification evidence (executability check output, session log excerpt, ticket-list output) appended to the epic's verification manifest under a `self-use-probe-1` section
- If neither (a) nor (b) is observed, task fails — does NOT pass by asserting the hook 'would have' fired

content.text: ## Description

**What**: /dso:preplanning conditional load gated by epic's strata:scoped tag (tag-scoped read bound to specific epic-id, NOT global). When gated open, Reads concepts.md + decomposition.md + guidance/preplanning.md at appropriate phases (~120 lines). Read-after-write fence: preplanning's first action verifies tag present with retry; on retry-exhaustion emits named error `[B] strata:scoped tag not present on <epic-id>; retry brainstorm`.
**Why**: Preplanning consumes the tag set by brainstorm; tag-scoped read ensures multi-epic sessions don't bleed Strata loads across non-Strata epics.
**Scope**:
- IN: Phase-conditional Reads; tag-scoped epic-id check; retry-with-escalation; named error on absence.
- OUT: Brainstorm tag-set logic (S4); implementation-plan loads (S6).
## Done Definitions
- When complete, on Strata epic with strata:scoped tag, preplanning Reads concepts + decomposition + preplanning-guidance ← Satisfies: SC2
- When complete, on Strata project + epic WITHOUT tag, preplanning Reads zero SDK files (tag-scoped) ← Satisfies: SC2, behavioral guarantee tag-scoped-read
- When complete, on strata.skip=true, preplanning Reads zero SDK files regardless of tag ← Satisfies: SC2
- When complete, preplanning's first action verifies tag with retry; retry-exhaustion emits the named error ← Satisfies: SC3, behavioral guarantee cross-skill-consistency
- When complete, unit tests written and passing for each path
## Considerations
- [Reliability] Tag scope is epic-id specific; never global
- [Reliability] Retry budget bounded (e.g., 3 attempts) before escalation
## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

## Context

Ruby and JavaScript/TypeScript projects using the DSO test gate today receive no signal from record-test-status.sh and record-test-exemption.sh because both scripts hardcode python3 -m pytest — RSpec and Jest tests are silently skipped. reinstall-hooks.sh also hard-fails on missing pyproject.toml, preventing hook installation on non-Python projects. This epic introduces a commands.test_runner config key so the test gate pipeline is stack-agnostic. This is Epic A in the polyglot hardening sequence — kudos polyglot triggers (01f5-28c1, T9) and polyglot lint/format gates (3818-310d) both depend on this epic's commands.test_runner and onboarding contract.
## Success Criteria

- commands.test_runner config key defined and documented in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md; onboarding auto-detects stack (Jest for Node/JS, RSpec for Ruby, pytest for Python) and writes the key during setup
- record-test-status.sh routes .rb, .js, .ts files to commands.test_runner instead of hardcoded python3/pytest
- record-test-exemption.sh uses commands.test_runner instead of hardcoded python3 -m pytest "$NODE_ID"
- reinstall-hooks.sh removes the hard-fail on missing pyproject.toml; installs hooks on any supported stack (pyproject.toml OR Gemfile OR package.json present)

- commands.test_file_runner (optional companion key) defined and documented in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md for per-file test execution (accepts a `{file}` placeholder that the gate substitutes with the target test file path); when unset the per-file gate falls back to commands.test_runner with the file appended as a positional argument. Enables the background-execution primitive epic to drive per-file gating without hardcoding language-specific invocations.
## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation, 2026-05-18)
### Self-use SC (Probe-1 remediation)

The 87e9 sprint exercises the new `commands.test_runner` + `commands.test_file_runner` keys on the DSO repo itself (DSO is Python, so the keys take Python-runner values during this sprint), AND a multi-stack fixture project is exercised end-to-end to prove the polyglot path.
Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):
- `grep -E '^commands\.test_runner=' .claude/dso-config.conf` shows the Python runner value populated for the DSO repo.
- A pre-commit run during the 87e9 sprint executes the test gate via the new key resolution path; transcript shows the configured runner invoked (not a hardcoded fallback).

- A Ruby fixture project at `tests/fixtures/test-gate-ruby/` is set up via `/dso:onboarding` during the sprint and its pre-commit gate runs `rspec` (or configured Ruby runner) via the same path; verified by transcript.
### State Lifecycle Owner Block (Probe-3 remediation)
| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |

| `commands.test_runner` (dso-config.conf) | `/dso:onboarding` writes per detected stack | **Stack-change UPDATE**: re-running `/dso:onboarding` after `stack` array changes rewrites this key for the new primary stack; multi-stack projects (per 188c) use `commands.test_runner.<stack>=...` namespaced variants | Pre-commit test gate; validate.sh | Removed only at project teardown OR explicit stack removal |
| `commands.test_file_runner` (with `{file}` placeholder) | Same | Same | Same (substituted at invocation) | Same |
| `commands.test_kill_grace_seconds` | Onboarding default | Operator edit | Test gate kill-grace timeout | Same |

The "stack migration" UPDATE flow named here (Python→Ruby example) is: operator runs `/dso:onboarding --refresh-stack` which detects the new stack, prompts before overwriting test-runner keys, and writes the new values. Closes the audit's UPDATE-undefined gap.
Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):
- The DSO repo's own `commands.test_runner` value is correct for Python and the pre-commit gate uses it.
- The Ruby fixture project's onboarding produced the Ruby runner value AND the gate uses it.
## Dependencies
None (first in the polyglot hardening sequence — blocks 01f5-28c1 T9 trigger and 3818-310d polyglot lint/format gates)
## Approach

Add commands.test_runner as a new config key read by the test gate pipeline. Onboarding detects the project stack and writes the appropriate default. All three gate scripts (record-test-status.sh, record-test-exemption.sh, reinstall-hooks.sh) are updated to read the config key rather than hardcode Python tool invocations.
## Research Findings

- Test runner conventions: pytest (Python, `python3 -m pytest`), RSpec (Ruby, `bundle exec rspec`), Jest (Node/JS/TS, `npx jest` preferred over `npm test` — `npm test` invokes project's test script which may not be Jest)
- Stack detection via existing detect-stack.sh is the canonical source — this epic's onboarding writes the stack-appropriate default using the same detection logic
- `pyproject.toml` hard-fail in reinstall-hooks.sh is legacy — hooks install cleanly without it; check replaced with stack-aware check (pyproject.toml OR Gemfile OR package.json present)
- Exit code conventions: pytest/RSpec/Jest all follow the same 0=pass / non-zero=fail contract; record-test-status.sh's existing centrality-aware tier mapping works for all three
- Zero new runtime dependencies — all three runners are stack-native; no DSO-managed install
- commands.test_runner pattern is the foundation for 3818-310d's commands.lint / commands.format / commands.format_check keys (same config-driven approach)
## Scenario Analysis

- Monorepo with both package.json and Gemfile at root (medium, detection): stack detection returns one winner via detect-stack.sh's existing precedence order; onboarding writes that stack's default; subdirectory-specific overrides are out of scope but documented as a known limitation in KNOWN-ISSUES.md

- `npx jest` vs `npm test` ambiguity in JS projects (medium, correctness): onboarding prefers `npx jest` (bypasses project `test` script which may not invoke Jest); documented default with user override path via manual config edit

- `bundle exec rspec` fails when Gemfile.lock is missing (medium, deployment): onboarding emits a [DSO WARN] with actionable guidance ("run `bundle install` before using test gate"); does not block onboarding completion

- record-test-status.sh on .py file in a Ruby-detected project (low, correctness): stack detection determines test runner; if project detects as Ruby, .py files trigger pytest fallback when python3 is available, otherwise skipped with [DSO WARN]; documented fallback behavior
- commands.test_runner absent at gate execution time (medium, regression): gate emits [DSO WARN] commands.test_runner not configured and skips; matches polyglot-lint-gates precedent (3818-310d)
- Test runner exit code convention differs across frameworks (low, correctness): all three runners follow 0=pass / non-zero=fail; confirmed via prior art; no special handling needed

- reinstall-hooks.sh removal of pyproject.toml check inadvertently breaks a Python-project invariant (medium, regression): check is replaced with stack-aware check — hooks require EITHER pyproject.toml (Python) OR Gemfile (Ruby) OR package.json (Node/JS/TS) present; missing ALL three emits an actionable error

## Context

The 2026-04-28 manual ruleset adjustments on this repo's GitHub Ruleset enabled (item #2) Require code scanning results with CodeQL — Security alerts: High or higher, Alerts: Errors and (item #3) Require code quality results — Severity: Errors. These rules require CI to emit code-scanning-API-compatible results (CodeQL SARIF for security; SARIF or equivalent for code quality) before they can be turned on without permanently blocking PRs. Until the CI emits these results, the rules cannot be enabled. Epic 4e55-a6ba (PR-merge mode + enforcement-strategy config) explicitly defers these two ruleset rules to this follow-on epic, with provision-ruleset.sh's knob set unimplemented for them. This epic adds the CodeQL job, the code-quality scanning + SARIF upload step, and extends provision-ruleset.sh with the require_codeql and require_code_quality knobs so the rules can be enabled on projects that opt in.
## Success Criteria
- A CodeQL job is added to .github/workflows/ci.yml that runs on every PR, scans the code, and uploads results to GitHub's code-scanning API.

- A code-quality job (or step) emits SARIF output from existing lint/static-analysis tooling (ruff for Python, actionlint for workflows, shellcheck for bash) and uploads via github/codeql-action/upload-sarif so the Require code quality results rule has data to gate against.
- provision-ruleset.sh extended with require_codeql (boolean) and require_code_quality (boolean) knobs that toggle those Ruleset rules; defaults to false on new projects.
- This project's GitHub Ruleset has Require CodeQL and Require code quality rules enabled (matching the 2026-04-28 manual adjustments) — verified in-session via gh api repos/.../rulesets.
## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation, 2026-05-16)
### Knob Lifecycle Owner Block (Probe-3 remediation)
| Knob | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |

| `require_codeql` (provision-ruleset.sh bool, default false) | provision-ruleset.sh applied per repo by `/dso:onboarding` security step OR operator | Operator edit; provision-ruleset.sh re-run after rule renames at GitHub side | provision-ruleset.sh ruleset-write payload; CI gate downstream | N/A — persistent per-repo config; flipped to false to suspend gating |
| `require_code_quality` (provision-ruleset.sh bool, default false) | Same | Same | Same | N/A — persistent |
Cross-repo CREATE owner: `/dso:onboarding` security step writes the knobs to `dso-config.conf` during project setup; the same step applies them via provision-ruleset.sh.
### External-dependency verification (Probe-6 remediation)
Before Phase I:
- GitHub Ruleset present: `gh api /repos/$OWNER/$REPO/rulesets --jq '[.[] | select(.name == "code-scanning-required")] | length'` returns ≥1.

content.text: ## Description

**What**: Implements the DESIGN.md addition flow end-to-end: ui-designer emits design_md_additions payload, preplanning orchestrator surfaces for user approval, accepted additions written to DESIGN.md.
**Why**: Token introductions must be deliberate design decisions via preplanning, not rubber-stamped commit-time accidents. The linter is enforcement-only and never adds tokens.
**Scope**:
- IN: dso:ui-designer payload emission, preplanning Phase H Step 7 approval flow, flock-serialized DESIGN.md write, decline path (design:tokens_pending tag), PREPLANNING_INTERACTIVE=false handling
- OUT: Contract document (draft-3), lint wrapper (draft-2)
## Done Definitions

- dso:ui-designer emits a design_md_additions payload conforming to plugins/dso/docs/contracts/design-md-additions-payload.md as a nullable field inside the existing UI_DESIGNER_PAYLOAD ← Satisfies: sc-2 (sc-2: "DESIGN.md addition flow via preplanning, never via the linter")
- The preplanning orchestrator surfaces the design_md_additions payload to the user as part of Phase H Step 7 approval when the payload is non-null ← Satisfies: sc-2
- On user approval, accepted additions are written to repo-root DESIGN.md via flock-serialized write before the sprint implementing the story begins ← Satisfies: sc-2
- On user decline, the orchestrator skips the DESIGN.md write, tags the story design:tokens_pending, and continues sprint dispatch ← Satisfies: sc-2
- In PREPLANNING_INTERACTIVE=false mode, the orchestrator emits an INTERACTIVITY_DEFERRED ticket comment instead of blocking for approval ← Satisfies: sc-2
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic
## Considerations
- [Concurrency] The flock-serialized write prevents race conditions when multiple preplanning sessions run concurrently on the same repo.
- [Idempotency] If the same token addition is approved twice (e.g., from two stories), the write should be idempotent — duplicate tokens should not be appended.
- [Linter separation] The linter (draft-2) is enforcement-only and never adds tokens; this story is the only path for token additions.

- [Completeness] SC-4 says migration script refuses to create DESIGN.md on greenfield projects without design-notes.md. But this story writes token additions to DESIGN.md. For greenfield projects, the preplanning flow may need to bootstrap an empty DESIGN.md if one does not exist and the project has no design-notes.md to migrate.
## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

## Description
**What**: Exports Figma design frames as PNG via REST API with rate-limit awareness, caching, and resolution normalization to match the comparison viewport.
**Why**: Provides the baseline design image that the perceptual diff compares against the implemented UI.
**Scope**:
- IN: GET /v1/images/:key with format=png, lastModified check before re-export, 3-5s delay between sequential requests, local PNG cache, resolution normalization to configured viewport
- OUT: Playwright screenshots (S2), perceptual diff scoring (S3)
## Done Definitions
- When this story is complete, Figma frames are exported as PNG via REST API with a lastModified check that skips re-export if the Figma file hasn't changed since last cache
← Satisfies: "checks lastModified before re-exporting"
- When this story is complete, sequential image export requests include a 3-5 second delay to stay within rate limits
← Satisfies: "rate-limit-aware client"

- When this story is complete, exported PNG dimensions match the configured viewport (design.figma_viewport, default 1440x900) via scale factor computation or post-export resize; output path convention: designs/{uuid}/validation/<frame_node_id>.png
← Satisfies: adversarial review finding on resolution contract + output naming
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic
## Considerations
- [Reliability] GET /v1/images/:key 429 after ~10 sequential requests — cache + lastModified check critical

- [Performance] Resolution normalization: Figma frames may be designed at arbitrary canvas sizes; exported PNG must match Playwright viewport for pixelmatch to work (pixelmatch requires identically-sized images)
- [Integration] Verified: GET /v1/images/:key supports format=png, scale parameter, returns temporary download URL
