## Context

DSO's ci-pr workflow mode currently has incoherent LLM review semantics for operators running /dso:sprint and /dso:debug-everything. Sprint Phase A (session-init, creates a long-lived session→main draft PR) opens the session PR correctly, but Phase F (per-story commit + merge) opens story PRs with base=main and auto-merges each one to main directly — orphaning the session draft PR and triggering full-PR llm-review re-reviews of code already cleared by per-story review on every story push. In a representative 5-story sprint, this produces ~3 redundant whole-PR re-reviews on already-approved hunks. /dso:debug-everything Phase F/G (per-tier and per-bug-batch sub-branches) reviews them via local /dso:review sub-agent dispatch, diverging from sprint's CI-driven flow.

This epic refactors both skills onto a unified architecture: when dso.workflow=ci-pr, all sub-branches (story/**, fix/**, bug-batch/**) open PRs against the session branch, gated by a Per-Branch LLM Review CI workflow under GitHub Rulesets (preferred over classic branch protection for session-* pattern scoping per Research Findings). A single session→main PR is the lone path to main; its required check is provenance verification (3-signal cross-check, pinned check-name) plus a narrow integration LLM review whose scope is un-provenanced commits ∪ files modified in ≥2 sub-branches.

Phase definitions: Sprint Phase A = session-init (create-sprint-draft-pr.sh); Sprint Phase F = post-story merge step (changes PR base to session); Debug Phase F = tier 0-1 auto-fix sub-branches; Debug Phase G = tier 2-7 fix-batch sub-branches.

Depends on 3b8b-d7e1-eeff-4796 (dso.workflow config consolidation). Supersedes 8ee4-c51c-c546-4d4e (cycle-tracking) and cafb-4b97-1703-41e3 (squash SHA-rewrite class). Coordinates with b575-ac1c-f720-4839 (cycle-end arbiter — both edit ci.yml llm-review) and 0cf2-42b5-8840-48a1 (sprint SKILL.md refactor — both edit Phase F) via named-step contracts. Reverse depends_on: af26-dd5a-df6d-4f81 (HARD-GATE enforcement) will be blocked by this epic.
## Success Criteria

1. Provenance integrity: every commit in main..session-HEAD on the session→main PR traces to a sub-branch PR whose Per-Branch LLM Review (matching pinned dso.review.check_name) returned SUCCESS, or is reported with its SHA and routed into the integration review's scope. Verified by a fixture sprint where (a) all commits are provenanced (verifier exits 0) and (b) a synthetic direct-to-session commit is injected (verifier exits non-zero, reports the SHA, and the injected commit appears in the integration scope's input file).

2. No re-review of per-branch-approved code: integration LLM review input contains zero hunks for files confined to a single sub-branch with passing review. Verified by inspecting the integration review's input on a fixture sprint where 3 stories touch disjoint files — the input contains zero matching paths for those files.

3. Cross-story integration coverage: integration review scope includes files modified by >=2 sub-branches in the current session. Verified by a fixture sprint where Story A and Story B both modify lib/helper.py — the integration review's input contains the cumulative diff for lib/helper.py.

4. Workflow + branch protection enforced end-to-end: sub-branch PRs base on session-branch; per-branch-review.yml fires for story/fix/bug-batch pushes; Rulesets on session-* reject direct pushes; Phase A preflight asserts (a) Ruleset exists and matches session-*, (b) pinned check name appears in required_status_checks.checks, (c) required_linear_history is false. Verified empirically: a representative sprint produces sub-branch PRs with the expected base; gh run list --workflow=per-branch-review.yml returns >=1 run per branch pattern; an attempted direct push to session is rejected with the expected branch-protection error; the preflight exits non-zero on missing or misconfigured Ruleset.

5. Skill convergence in ci-pr; local mode preserved byte-identical: sprint Phase F + debug Phase F/G in ci-pr mode both invoke per-branch-review.yml; their SKILL.md files reference no local /dso:review in ci-pr branches. Local mode byte-identical to a pre-epic baseline (commit-breadcrumbs.log + git log --pretty=format output diff). Deprecated path sprint-story-review.yml is renamed to per-branch-review.yml; all named consumer files updated: plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/runner.py, plugins/dso/skills/sprint/SKILL.md, tests/workflows/test-sprint-story-review.sh (renamed), tests/workflows/test-sprint-story-review-defenses.sh (renamed), tests/hooks/test-validate-review-output.sh, tests/scripts/test-ci-defense-pipeline.sh, tests/skills/dso_ci_review/test_dispatch_schema_correction.py, and docs/findings/sprint-resume-state.md. Verified by grep -rn 'sprint-story-review' returning zero matches outside explicit deprecation notes.

6. Superseded bugs closed with reproducers passing: bug 8ee4-c51c-c546-4d4e closed with DSO_REVIEW_CYCLE>=2 computed correctly on the session→main PR and prior defenses in TrackerDefenseStore suppressed in the integration review (reproducer: write a defense via defense_store_write, push a triggering commit, observe the cycle-2 review skipping the defended finding). Bug cafb-4b97-1703-41e3 closed with the new API-based provenance check accepting a squash-merged sub-branch's commits as provenanced (reproducer: create a sub-branch PR, squash-merge it into session, run the provenance verifier on a session→main PR including that squash commit — verifier exits 0).
## Operational Constraints

- Provenance retry/backoff: provenance verifier uses exponential backoff (initial 2s, doubled per retry, cap 60s) on gh api commits/<sha>/pulls returning 403/429. Per-walk budget ceiling of 200 API calls; on exhaustion, exit non-zero with BUDGET_EXHAUSTED marker. Per-session SHA→PR-number cache stored in artifact to avoid re-querying on re-runs.

- Ruleset provisioning ownership: one-time repo-admin setup of the session-* Ruleset is the documented prerequisite (instructions added to INSTALL.md and to /dso:onboarding for new projects). Phase A preflight (see SC4) detects missing or misconfigured Ruleset and fails fast with an actionable error message linking to setup docs. This epic does NOT mandate that DSO hold administration:write permission at runtime — operators retain control of branch protection administration.

- In-flight migration: when this epic ships, in-flight sprint sessions may have open story PRs targeting main. A one-time migration script (migrate-story-pr-bases.sh) detects these via gh pr list --search 'base:main head:story/', PATCHes their base to the session branch, then issues gh workflow run per-branch-review.yml --ref <head-branch> to re-trigger the required check. Run by operator before first new sprint after this epic merges.

- Exempt direct-push call sites (descoped from SC4's branch-protection rejection): plugins/dso/scripts/onboarding/github-bootstrap.sh:114 (git push origin HEAD:main) is a one-time repo-bootstrap operation that occurs before any session branch exists; Rulesets on session-* do not apply. Tests that push directly to main (test-record-review.sh, test-merge-to-main-portability.sh, test-merge-state.sh, test-merge-to-main-cleanliness.sh, test-claude-safe-post-merge-amend.sh) are test-infrastructure operations against ephemeral fixtures, exempt.
## Scenario Analysis
- Concurrent sub-branch merges race condition (high, runtime): snapshot session-HEAD SHA at job start.
- GitHub API rate limiting (high, runtime): exponential backoff + 200-call budget + SHA→PR cache.
- Custom merge-commit template omits PR number (high, runtime): signals 1+2 (API + check status) are the trusted pair; signal 3 corroborating only.
- In-flight PRs target main at deploy time (high, deployment): one-time migration script.
- Branch protection requires admin pre-setup (high, deployment): documented one-time setup + Phase A preflight.
- Workflow rename breaks required-check reference (high, deployment): pinned dso.review.check_name config.
- SESSION_BRANCH resolution failure (critical, configuration): 3-step fallback (draft PR headRefName → vars.SPRINT_SESSION_ID → fail-fast, never silent default to main).
- dso.workflow=ci-pr unset silent local-mode fallback (medium, configuration): orchestrator warns when .sprint-active or .debug-active is set but dso.workflow != ci-pr.
- Empty integration scope (medium, configuration): job exits 0 cleanly.
- Direct-push commits unmapped by GitHub API (high, assumption): fail-closed; un-provenanced commits route into integration review.
- Squash on session→main collapses history (medium, assumption): documented choice in INSTALL.md; default merge-commit.
- Check-name drift between workflow and Ruleset (high, assumption): pinned config + Phase A preflight.
## Research Findings
### External Integration: GitHub Branch Protection / Rulesets API
- Trigger condition name: External integration
- Query summary: programmatic branch protection configuration, required permissions, merge-style interactions, modern Rulesets alternative

- Source URLs: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/branches/branch-protection, https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/available-rules-for-rulesets, https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules

- Key insight: Classic protection (PUT /branches/{branch}/protection) and Rulesets (POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets) both require admin permissions. required_linear_history=true BLOCKS merge commits — must be false on session-* so merge-commit PR-number references survive. Rulesets (2023+) are the recommended path for dynamic per-sprint branches due to pattern-based scoping (e.g., session-*) and per-session toggleability.
### Migration: Sub-Branch PR Base Re-Targeting
- Trigger condition name: Migration / compatibility
- Query summary: PATCH API for changing open PR base, CI re-trigger semantics, working migration examples
- Source URLs: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/pulls, https://github.com/heroku/main-branch-switch/blob/main/retarget.sh, https://github.com/ethomson/retarget_prs

- Key insight: PATCH /pulls/{n} with a base field retargets cleanly; GitHub recomputes the diff but CI workflows are NOT auto-re-triggered. The migration script must explicitly issue gh workflow run (or workflow_dispatch) after PATCHing the base to re-trigger required checks. Working examples exist; not a capability gap.

Placeholder epic capturing what we currently know about Nava Strata's Layer 4 — the "Deployable Microservices" tier of the Strata stack (Layer 1 infra templates, Layer 2 app templates, Layer 3 SDK, Layer 4 microservices). Each Layer 4 service is shipped as its own `strata-template-*` repo containing both an infra module and an app template, installable independently via `platform-cli`. This epic is NOT yet brainstormed; it is a durable capture so the work can be picked up in a future `/dso:brainstorm` session without re-doing the research.
## Layer 4 Service Catalog (as of 2026-05-07)

- **DocumentAI** — AI-powered document classification and extraction. Pilot stage. Stack: FastAPI + AWS Bedrock Data Automation (BDA). Repo: `navapbc/strata-template-documentai-api`. AWS-only; intentionally NOT built on Strata SDK or existing Strata app templates. Naming open question: "IDP" collides with "Identity Provider".

- **Rules Engine** — Eligibility and business rules engine. Pilot stage. Stack: Catala (Apache 2.0) transpiled to Python, served via FastAPI. Repo: `navapbc/strata-template-rules-engine-catala`. Targets means-tested benefit programs (SNAP, Medicaid, WIC, paid leave). Deliberately lightweight; rules editable by non-engineers.

- **QC Preview ("Intelligent Case Review Surface")** — Sidecar quality-review app for SNAP Payment Error Rate. Concept stage. No repo yet. Tied to HR1 SNAP deadline 2026-09-30. Surfaces "Case Criteria" (Status, Confidence, Explanation, Source references) over external case data ingested via batch or API.

- **Payments Service** — Beam-acquisition-derived payments microservice. Concept stage. No repo yet. Multi-provider design (JPMorgan, USIO); scheduling, recipients, funding sources, transaction tracking. Beam disbursed $400M as payment-provider-of-record pre-acquisition.

Common pattern across all four: each Layer 4 service ships as a `<service>-infra-module` (Terraform) plus a `<service>-app-template` (FastAPI / Rails / Next.js as appropriate), installable via `platform-cli`.
## Open questions to resolve in future brainstorm
- Should Layer 4 land as one umbrella epic or as separate per-service epics? Each service is at a different stage and stack.
- Does the AWS-only scope of DocumentAI (BDA) rule out Strata projects on Azure infrastructure? Implication for project-detection logic.
- Where does the Beam-derived Payments service land in the platform-cli lifecycle once it has a repo? Today it has no `strata-template-*` repo.
- How should DSO surface the microservice catalog and install workflow during prototype scaffolding (Epic A) — a single "want any Layer 4 services?" prompt, or deferred to Day-N iteration?
- Catala is currently the only rules-engine language; does future support for OpenFisca or JSON-based engines change DSO's planning context for the Rules Engine?
- The four services span wildly different maturity (Pilot vs. Concept) and stacks; DSO's planning context likely needs per-service detection rather than a single "Layer 4 enabled" flag.
- What is the intersection with Epic B (Strata SDK)? E.g., does an app using DocumentAI also typically use the SDK, or are they orthogonal?
## References
- https://www.navapbc.com/strata
- Layer 4 Confluence briefs (provided 2026-05-07): PLAT-DocumentAI, PLAT-Strata Rules Engine, PLAT-QC Preview, PLAT-Payments Service
- `navapbc/strata` (umbrella repo)
- `navapbc/strata-template-documentai-api`
- `navapbc/strata-template-rules-engine-catala`
- `navapbc/oscer` (real Strata-based app; reference customer for DocumentAI work)
- Related abandoned: `navapbc/strata-sdk-mcp` (research-only, not a dependency)
## Status
This epic is captured for future brainstorming. Do NOT plan or implement until `/dso:brainstorm <epic-id>` has been run interactively. Tagged `scrutiny:pending`.

### Cross-epic boundary decision (2026-05-14): arbiter_ruling emission

Confirmed during Epic 4 (seat-oil-flank, da4e-4e9a-250b-4a8b) brainstorm:

- **Producer**: Epic 1 (swap-maple-flyby, b575-ac1c-f720-4839)'s `code-reviewer-arbiter` agent writes per-finding rulings to the defense store. No telemetry-emit.sh call inside the agent.
- **Emitter**: Epic 4 (seat-oil-flank, da4e-4e9a-250b-4a8b) ships a `dso-arbiter` adapter under `plugins/dso/scripts/telemetry-adapters/dso-arbiter.sh` that reads defense-store arbiter entries and emits canonical `arbiter_ruling` events via `telemetry-emit.sh` (Epic 2, colder-fin-exile, d2f9-ee1a-48ab-4bf6).
- **Linkage**: adapter uses `--link dso-llm:<cycle>:<finding_index>` to populate `finding_event_id`, matching the same cross-event linkage convention as `dso-resolver`.

Rationale: keeps Epic 1's explicit out-of-scope clause for telemetry adapters intact; preserves pattern consistency (all producers write artifacts, all emitters are deterministic adapters); avoids opus-tier prompt bloat and emit-step reliability risk inside the arbiter agent.

**Key decisions captured**:
1. Vendor: AWS (Lambda Function URL + S3 + DuckDB-for-read; no API Gateway, no Athena/Glue)
2. Region: us-east-1
3. Setup via idempotent AWS CLI shell scripts (NOT Terraform/CDK)

6. Write auth: anonymous Function URL + WAF rate-limit per-IP
7. Read auth: maintainer AWS credentials on S3
8. Retention: forward-only; lifecycle to Glacier IR after 180 days; never delete by default
9. Local-mode fallback: `|| true` (silent drop); no client-side buffering
10. Schema: 5 event types (review_finding, resolver_outcome, arbiter_ruling, tool_finding, review_cycle); UUIDv7 event_ids; 11 common fields + per-type
11. `telemetry-emit.sh` utility consolidates all per-adapter complexity — single seam

13. Reviewer schema extension: optional rule_id field (in scope, non-breaking)

**Spec revisions applied during remediation (critical architectural changes):**

- **WAF REMOVED**: AWS WAF cannot directly associate with Lambda Function URL (confirmed by AWS docs + AWS Compute blog). Architecture now uses Lambda **reserved-concurrency throttle** (default 10 concurrent executions) instead. Lambda Function URL keeps anonymous public POST; reserved concurrency bounds blast radius from abuse.
- **Glacier IR transition timing CORRECTED to 90 days**: matches Glacier IR's 90-day minimum storage duration. Previous spec said 180 days, which is the minimum for Glacier Deep Archive (different class).
- **Idempotency claim scoped**: `aws-deploy-handler.sh` always re-uploads Lambda code (always produces a new deployment timestamp); idempotency claim scoped to bucket + Lambda creation operations only, with documentation in the script header.
- Pre-flight IAM permission probes added to setup scripts (sts:GetCallerIdentity + dry-run create-role) to fail fast with clear missing-permission errors rather than partial-creation state.
- Flock-based concurrent-write protection added for event-id-map.json to prevent race under parallel adapter invocations.
- **Two-layer privacy enforcement**: adapter-side cited_excerpt strip + Lambda server-side defense-in-depth (replaces non-conforming cited_excerpt with null before S3 write).
- DuckDB listed as documented prerequisite + checked in aws-status.sh; date-range partitioning required for query-stats.sh to bound S3 scan latency.
- Empty `client_id` rejected as hard error (not default-to-self fallback).
- Privacy disclosure section added to telemetry-event-schema.md documenting the emit_excerpts data-sharing implication for opted-in host projects.
- 10 surviving red-team scenarios added under `## Scenario Analysis` with specific mitigations.

**Minor residual finding (acceptable; doesn't block pass threshold):**
- S3 bucket policy `NotPrincipal` pattern requires dual-ARN (role ARN + sts assumed-role ARN) for Lambda; documented as story-level implementation nuance for `aws-setup-bucket.sh` preplanning.

### Cross-epic boundary decision (2026-05-14): arbiter_ruling emission

Confirmed during Epic 4 (seat-oil-flank, da4e-4e9a-250b-4a8b) brainstorm:

- **Producer**: Epic 1 (swap-maple-flyby, b575-ac1c-f720-4839)'s `code-reviewer-arbiter` agent writes per-finding rulings to the defense store. No telemetry-emit.sh call inside the agent.

- **Linkage**: adapter uses `--link dso-llm:<cycle>:<finding_index>` to populate `finding_event_id`, matching the same cross-event linkage convention as `dso-resolver`.

Rationale: keeps Epic 1's explicit out-of-scope clause for telemetry adapters intact; preserves pattern consistency (all producers write artifacts, all emitters are deterministic adapters); avoids opus-tier prompt bloat and emit-step reliability risk inside the arbiter agent.

## Context

The DSO plugin emits telemetry events from code review pipelines but has no central data store — `classifier-telemetry.jsonl` and `review-event-schema.jsonl` exist as local-only files with no documented consumer. PR history is per-repo and not queryable across host projects. The umbrella `e7f3-2b45-8d7d-4c68` (grainy-speck-ball) requires a centralized telemetry pipeline supporting cross-reviewer comparison, downstream consumer epics (LAURA, replay-regression-harness, reporting), and zero-friction host-project participation.
This epic builds and deploys the **AWS-hosted, universal-endpoint** telemetry infrastructure plus the deterministic emit utility that downstream adapters consume.
## Scope
**In scope — AWS infrastructure (deployed via idempotent setup scripts using AWS CLI):**
- **Lambda Function URL** as the public POST endpoint (no API Gateway; built-in HTTPS)

- **Lambda function** (Python 3.13 runtime) — validates event JSON against the canonical schema, writes to S3 keyed `${client_id}/${YYYY-MM-DD}/${event_id}.jsonl`, returns 202 Accepted on success / 400 Bad Request on malformed

- **Lambda reserved-concurrency throttle** (default: 10 concurrent executions) — bounds blast radius from abuse / runaway loops. Lambda Function URL does not support direct WAFv2 association; reserved concurrency is the supported throttle mechanism.
- **S3 bucket** — append-only via per-event object writes (no true-append needed); per-client_id key prefix; public access blocked; bucket policy denying non-Lambda writes
- **IAM role for Lambda** — `s3:PutObject` on the bucket only (no read, no list, no delete; defense-in-depth)

- **S3 Lifecycle rule** — transition objects >90 days to **Glacier Instant Retrieval** (90-day minimum storage class). Provides cold-storage cost savings (~6×) while preserving millisecond retrieval for ad-hoc maintainer queries. Never delete by default.
- **CloudWatch log group** — Lambda execution logs at 7-day retention
- **AWS region**: `us-east-1`
**In scope — plugin-shipped CLI setup scripts** (under `plugins/dso/scripts/telemetry/`, idempotent, AWS CLI based):
- `aws-setup-bucket.sh` — creates S3 bucket + lifecycle rule (90d → Glacier IR) + bucket policy + public-access-block; re-runnable

- `aws-setup-lambda.sh` — creates Lambda + execution role + Function URL + reserved-concurrency configuration; re-runnable. **Pre-flight IAM permission check**: script verifies the operator has required IAM permissions (sts:GetCallerIdentity probe + dry-run create-role probe) BEFORE attempting any creation; exits with a clear error listing missing permissions rather than partial-creation state.

- `aws-deploy-handler.sh` — packages and updates Lambda handler code. **Pre-flight ordering check**: verifies the Lambda function exists before attempting update; if not, prints "Run aws-setup-lambda.sh first" and exits 1.
- `aws-status.sh` — reports endpoint URL, bucket name, lifecycle state, reserved-concurrency setting, last 24h event count
- `aws-teardown.sh` — clean uninstall; gated `--user-approved`
- Documented IAM permissions required for the operator running setup (in `plugins/dso/docs/telemetry/aws-setup.md`)
**In scope — `telemetry-emit.sh` utility** (deterministic adapter shim, no LLM cycles):
- Reads `telemetry.endpoint` + `telemetry.client_id` + `telemetry.emit_excerpts` from config (or `DSO_TELEMETRY_*` env vars)

- Generates UUIDv7 `event_id` via Python (`python3 -c "import uuid; print(uuid.uuid4())"` is the v1 implementation since UUIDv7 requires Python 3.13+; sufficient for our identifier needs); auto-populates all 11 common fields from environment (schema_version, event_type, client_id, tool_id, tool_version, timestamp, pr_number, commit_sha, cycle, language)

- Optional `--key <logical-id>` registers the event_id in `${ARTIFACTS_DIR}/event-id-map.json` for cross-event linkage. **Concurrent-write protection**: uses flock (or `mkdir`-based mutex fallback on systems without flock) to serialize event-id-map writes from parallel adapters.
- Optional `--link <key>` looks up event_id by logical-id, populates `finding_event_id` for resolver_outcome / arbiter_ruling events

- **Privacy enforcement with strict empty-string handling**: when `client_id == "dso-self"` AND `emit_excerpts` is unset/false, emit full cited_excerpt. When `client_id` is anything else (including empty string `""` treated as invalid input — error 400) AND `emit_excerpts != true`, strip cited_excerpt to null and emit `cited_excerpt_hash` only. Treat empty `client_id` as a hard error (exit 1 with clear message), not as a default-to-dso-self fallback.

- **Server-side defense-in-depth**: Lambda handler verifies the privacy invariant on every event — if `client_id != "dso-self"` and `cited_excerpt` is present, replace with null server-side before writing to S3. Two-layer enforcement protects against adapter-side bypass.
- Idempotency: maintains `${ARTIFACTS_DIR}/telemetry-submitted.log` keyed by event_id (and by `--key` when supplied); silently no-ops on duplicate
- Submission: curl POST with fail-open `|| true` semantics; logs warnings to stderr
- All adapters (Epic 4) consume this utility — single seam for endpoint logic
**In scope — canonical schema + minor upstream changes:**

- `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/telemetry-event-schema.md` — formal contract documenting 5 event types (`review_finding`, `resolver_outcome`, `arbiter_ruling`, `tool_finding`, `review_cycle`), schema_version=1, all common + per-type fields, defaults, **and the privacy disclosure**: a clearly-labeled section documenting that `telemetry.emit_excerpts=true` on the shared multi-tenant endpoint means verbatim code excerpts from the host project's PRs will be readable by the central-endpoint maintainer. Host project operators must affirmatively opt in to this data-sharing posture.
- Reviewer schema extension: add optional `rule_id` field to reviewer-findings.json in reviewer-base.md (non-breaking — existing findings without it still validate)

- Token-usage capture: tiny reviewer-dispatcher addition to write Anthropic API response `usage.input_tokens` + `usage.output_tokens` to `${ARTIFACTS_DIR}/review-cycle-usage.json` so the `review_cycle` emitter can populate `tokens_used` + `token_cost_usd`
**In scope — plugin config knobs (`dso-config.conf`):**
- `telemetry.endpoint` (default: ships pre-configured to the Joe-hosted Lambda Function URL)
- `telemetry.client_id` (default: `dso-self` for this repo; configurable per host project; empty string treated as hard error)
- `telemetry.emit_excerpts` (default: `false`; opt-in for verbatim sharing for non-dso-self clients; docs document the privacy implications)
**In scope — stats retrieval:**

- `plugins/dso/scripts/telemetry/query-stats.sh` — bash + AWS CLI + DuckDB; 5 validation subcommands: `roundtrip` (smoke test), `counts` (events per tool_id × event_type × day), `recent` (last N events), `missing` (clients silent for N days), `sizes` (bytes per client_id, cost monitoring). **Unknown-subcommand handling**: case-statement default branch prints usage to stderr and exits 1 (not 0).

- **DuckDB prerequisite**: setup docs list DuckDB CLI as required for queries (not auto-installed). Setup script `aws-status.sh` checks `command -v duckdb` and emits a clear install pointer if missing.

- **S3 scan latency mitigation**: query-stats.sh uses **client_id + date-range partitioning** in DuckDB glob patterns rather than full-bucket scans. Documented usage: `query-stats.sh counts --client-id=dso-self --days=7` runs against a 7-day prefix subset, not the entire bucket. Bounds object scan to recent partitions.
- `/dso:review-stats --source=central` skill flag — thin dispatcher to `query-stats.sh`
- Output is validation-grade only; full analytics/reporting deferred to `spiky-stand-chick` placeholder
**Operating model:**
- Joe-hosted AWS account for v1; universal endpoint URL shipped as the `telemetry.endpoint` default
- All DSO projects submit to the same endpoint (multi-tenant from day 1)
- Privacy: plugin-self emits full `cited_excerpt`; host projects emit `cited_excerpt_hash` only by default, can opt in via config (with disclosure)
- Write throttle: anonymous Function URL + Lambda reserved-concurrency cap (10 concurrent); no WAF (Lambda Function URLs don't support direct WAFv2 attachment)
- Read auth: maintainer AWS credentials on the S3 bucket
- Retention: forward-only; lifecycle to Glacier IR after 90 days; never delete by default
**Out of scope (delegated to sibling epics):**
- Telemetry adapters for individual tools (ruff, mypy, eslint, rubocop, etc.) — Epic `da4e-4e9a-250b-4a8b` (seat-oil-flank)
- `dso-llm` and `dso-resolver` emitter wiring into REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md and review-fix-dispatch.md — Epic `da4e-4e9a-250b-4a8b`
- External-reviewer comment ingest (CodeRabbit/Gitar/Copilot) — Epic `f27a-3c6a-1a4e-48ae` (turbid-maze-tread)
- Cycle-K arbiter consuming telemetry — Epic `b575-ac1c-f720-4839` (swap-maple-flyby); hard rule: arbiter reads from `gh api` only, never from this central store
- Full reporting/dashboard UI — placeholder epic `e8ac-6a65-62f6-47b8` (spiky-stand-chick)
- LAURA retrieval over defense corpus — placeholder epic `25b5-78e3-41b3-4ae9` (bland-bag-rind)
- Replay regression harness — placeholder epic `87b1-7fd0-edce-45d0` (balk-ozone-dip)
- Backfill of historical PR data (forward-only from deployment)
- Host-project deployments of their own AWS infrastructure (the design supports it; v1 ships only Joe-hosted)
- Detection of CloudFront-fronted WAF or alternative WAF strategies (rejected — Lambda reserved-concurrency is the v1 throttle)
## Approach

The S3 bucket layout is `s3://<bucket>/<client_id>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<event_id>.jsonl` — one event per object. DuckDB reads these JSONL objects directly with `read_json_auto('s3://<bucket>/<client_id>/<date-prefix>*/*.jsonl')` using narrow date-range partitioning to bound scan latency. No dedicated query service (Athena/Glue/OpenSearch) needed at v1's volume (~6k events/month plugin-self, ~50 MB/month at 100× host adoption with hash-only emissions; storage envelope re-evaluated if cited_excerpt sizes drive volume past 1 GB/month).

Setup scripts are idempotent: each script begins with AWS resource pre-checks (`aws iam get-role || aws iam create-role` pattern) PLUS pre-flight permission checks (sts:GetCallerIdentity + dry-run probes) to fail fast with a clear missing-permission error rather than partial-creation state. Re-running on an already-provisioned account is a no-op (with the caveat that `aws-deploy-handler.sh` always re-uploads Lambda code regardless of content — Lambda metadata shows a new deployment timestamp on every run; documented in the script header).

The `telemetry-emit.sh` utility is the **only** seam adapters cross. Adapter authors populate type-specific fields; the utility owns event_id generation, HTTP, schema versioning, privacy policy, dedup, concurrent-write protection (flock on event-id-map.json), and fail-open semantics. The Lambda handler enforces the same privacy invariant server-side as defense-in-depth.
Field feasibility was audited (2026-05-14). All schema fields are obtainable from CI + local environments without expensive computation. Two small upstream changes are scoped into this epic:
- Add optional `rule_id` to reviewer-findings.json (reviewer-base.md edit)
- Capture Anthropic API `usage.*` to `${ARTIFACTS_DIR}/review-cycle-usage.json`

## Scenario Analysis
Surviving red-team scenarios (blue-team filtered; 10 of 14 retained):

- **(`critical`, `configuration`) telemetry.emit_excerpts=true on shared multi-tenant endpoint exposes verbatim code**: addressed by SC4's two-layer privacy enforcement (adapter strip + server-side defense-in-depth) and SC6's explicit Privacy Disclosure documentation.

- **(`high`, `runtime`) DuckDB S3 scan latency grows unbounded as object count increases**: addressed by date-range partitioning in `query-stats.sh` (SC7). Long-term mitigation: if bucket exceeds ~1M objects, introduce monthly-archive consolidation.
- **(`high`, `runtime`) event-id-map.json race under parallel adapter invocations**: addressed by flock-based mutex in telemetry-emit.sh.
- **(`high`, `deployment`) First deployment fails silently on incomplete IAM**: addressed by pre-flight IAM permission probe in setup scripts (sts:GetCallerIdentity + dry-run create-role).

- **(`high`, `configuration`) telemetry.client_id empty string bypasses privacy enforcement**: addressed by treating empty client_id as a hard error (exit 1 with clear message), not a default fallback.
- **(`high`, `assumption`) DuckDB available in operator's environment**: addressed by listing DuckDB as a prerequisite in setup docs + aws-status.sh prerequisite check.

- **(`high`, `assumption`) anonymous write access to Lambda Function URL acceptable**: now mitigated by Lambda reserved-concurrency cap (default 10) bounding blast radius from abuse; server-side schema validation rejects malformed events; documented as accepted-tradeoff in setup docs.
- **(`medium`, `deployment`) aws-deploy-handler.sh run before aws-setup-lambda.sh**: addressed by pre-flight existence check in aws-deploy-handler.sh.
- **(`medium`, `assumption`) ~50 MB/month at 100× adoption is stable upper bound**: addressed by documenting re-evaluation trigger if cited_excerpt sizes drive volume past 1 GB/month.
- **(`medium`, `assumption`) UUIDv7 generation in standard bash**: addressed by using Python uuid module (UUIDv4 sufficient for our identifier needs; ordering not required at v1).

- 2 WAF-related scenarios — WAF removed from architecture
- Lambda cold start — accepted tradeoff with || true fail-open
- query-stats.sh missing-subcommand — addressed by SC7 explicit handling

None. This epic is foundational. Downstream epics consume its infrastructure: `swap-maple-flyby` (token-usage capture wiring for the arbiter), `turbid-maze-tread` (external-reviewer comment ingest emits to this endpoint), `seat-oil-flank` (adapter starter pack uses `telemetry-emit.sh`), `bland-bag-rind` / `balk-ozone-dip` / `spiky-stand-chick` (placeholders that consume the populated S3 bucket).

## Context

LLM test-writing sub-agents in this project (red-test-writer, sprint task-execution prompt, fix-bug RED phase) routinely produce tests that assert on internal method names, mock-invocation counts, or source-grep patterns rather than on observable system behavior. Research documents this failure mode: ~25% of LLM oracles are wrong-but-confident (Di Grazia et al. ASE 2025), 30-60% of LLM tests fail basic compile/execute floors (Yuan et al. 2024), and LLM tests show Assertion Roulette in 38-49% of class-level tests (Wang et al. 2024). The existing 5-rule behavioral-testing-standard.md describes correct principles but is too abstract to bind at generation time. This epic introduces a structured per-test intent-claim header that test-writers attach to every new or modified test, and extends the existing code-reviewer-test-quality agent with two review dimensions to enforce both assertion shape and articulation during code review. Pre-commit gating is deliberately out of scope — enforcement runs through the review overlay only, with iteration in the wild before any deterministic tooling is added.
## Success Criteria

- SC1: plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/behavioral-testing-standard.md gains Rule 6 — every NEW or MODIFIED test in the diff carries a fenced "## Test Intent" header above the test function with fields intent_id (SC|DoD|AC reference from parent ticket subtree, or "UNTRACKED — <one-line rationale>" permitted sentinel) and catches_regression_where (sentence-completion form: "this test turns RED if and only if [specific production-code change]"). Rule 6 includes canonical per-language header fixture examples covering Python (docstring with markdown fence inside), JavaScript/TypeScript (block comment with markdown fence inside), and bash (line-comment block with markdown fence inside). Legacy tests not modified in the diff are exempt.

- SC2: behavioral-testing-standard.md gains Rule 7 — when adding behavioral coverage for an intent_id already claimed by an existing test, add a sibling parameterized case or new sibling test function in the same test file. Do NOT append assertions to an existing test function. Do NOT create a duplicate test function claiming the same intent_id without an orthogonal scenario suffix. Each test function carries at most one "## Test Intent" header. behavioral-testing-standard.md is designated a safeguard file per CLAUDE.md rule 22 — sub-agents may not propose edits that weaken Rule 6 or 7 without explicit user approval.

- SC3: Three test-writing surfaces updated to reference Rules 6 and 7 in their generation guidance: plugins/dso/agents/red-test-writer.md, plugins/dso/skills/sprint/prompts/task-execution.md, and the fix-bug RED-phase prompt (concrete path under plugins/dso/skills/fix-bug/ resolved during implementation-plan). Synthetic verification: a dispatch of dso:red-test-writer against a fixture task containing one AC produces a test file whose header parses under the per-language syntax appendix and whose intent_id field exactly matches the fixture AC identifier; parse success is confirmed by an automated grep that finds the fenced "## Test Intent" block, the intent_id field, and the catches_regression_where field in the output.

- SC4: plugins/dso/docs/workflows/prompts/reviewer-delta-test-quality.md (the build source for the compiled plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-test-quality.md agent, regenerated via build-review-agents.sh) gains two new review dimensions. Tier 1 (assertion shape) emits a finding when a test assertion targets internal method names, private state, mock-invocation counts (e.g., mock.called_with), or source-grep patterns against source files; requires assertions to target observable outputs (return values, exit codes, file contents, side effects, emitted events). Tier 2 (articulation) emits a finding when (a) a new/modified test has missing or malformed header, (b) catches_regression_where is tautological, (c) the assertions do not exercise the intent named in intent_id (REQUIRED scaffold: reviewer first lists the observable artifact each assert measures, then lists what intent_id claims is measured, then flags if these two sets are disjoint), (d) catches_regression_where would not in fact cause the test to fail given the assertions present, (e) duplicate intent_id without orthogonal scenario suffix or sibling-case structure per Rule 7. Dimension carries an anti-sycophancy prime: "Identify the single most damaging flaw. If no flaw exists, state 'No findings' explicitly." The build pipeline regenerates code-reviewer-test-quality.md from this delta source as part of the implementation work.

- SC5: A /dso:review run against a synthetic diff containing (a) a new test with no header, (b) a new test asserting only on mock.called_with(...), (c) a new test whose intent_id claims SC-1 but whose only assertion is `assert True == True`, produces a reviewer-findings.json where the findings[] array includes at least one entry with dimension matching "Tier 1 (assertion shape)" or "Tier 2 (articulation)" AND whose source_path:source_line falls inside violations (a), (b), (c) respectively. The same findings[] array contains zero entries with those dimensions whose source_line falls inside any unmodified legacy test block in the same diff.
Each "5-rule" / "five rules" / "Rule 5" reference is updated to version-agnostic phrasing OR extended to enumerate Rules 6 and 7.
- SC7 (dogfood): The tests written for d566's own implementation carry valid Rule 6 headers. A /dso:review run on the d566 implementation PR emits zero Tier 1 or Tier 2 findings on those tests.

- SC8 (explicit descope): plugins/dso/hooks/pre-commit-test-quality-gate.sh and plugins/dso/hooks/semgrep-rules/test-anti-patterns.yaml are explicitly NOT extended by this epic. Rule 6 + Rule 7 enforcement is review-only via the dimensions added to code-reviewer-test-quality in SC4. If future evidence supports adding hook-level enforcement, a follow-on epic will scope it.
grep -rEni '5[-. ]?rule|five[-. ]?rules?|Rule[[:space:]]+5\b|behavioral[-. _]testing[-. _]standard'

Every match is triaged into one of three outcomes: (i) updated to version-agnostic phrasing or extended to reference Rules 6/7, (ii) explicitly descoped with a one-line rationale (e.g., "Rule 5 in this context refers to a different standard"), or (iii) already version-agnostic — no change required. The implementation PR description includes the full final grep output (count and list of matches) plus the triage disposition for each one (file path → outcome i/ii/iii with rationale where required). Pattern validation against the 14 consumers identified during brainstorm confirmed 100% coverage at brainstorm time; this SC ensures any consumer added between brainstorm and implementation is also caught.
## Approach

Inline rule additions to behavioral-testing-standard.md (Rule 6 + Rule 7 + per-language syntax appendix with canonical fixture examples). Prompt updates to three test-writing surfaces. Extension of reviewer-delta-test-quality.md (build source) — rebuild via build-review-agents.sh regenerates code-reviewer-test-quality.md. Pointer updates across the 10 named consumer files in SC6, plus structural sweep per SC9 to catch any unenumerated consumers. No new tooling, no new contracts, no new scripts.
## Scenario Analysis
- Fabricated tautological catches_regression_where (high/correctness): partially mitigated by Tier 2(b) and (d) reviewer checks; residual risk that the reviewer is itself LLM-judgment-based.
- intent_id collision across distinct scenarios sharing an abstract SC (high/correctness): partially mitigated by Rule 7 orthogonal-suffix requirement; "orthogonal" is reviewer judgment.

- Claim-vs-assertion contradiction degrades without manifest (critical/observability): partially mitigated by predicate-listing scaffold in Tier 2(c); semantic drift remains until 94ed-f55c manifest ships.
- Bash test header silent no-match in parser (high/runtime): partially mitigated by canonical per-language fixtures in SC1.
- LLM reviewer sycophancy on fluent headers (high/correctness): partially mitigated by anti-sycophancy prime; instructional primes are a known weak defense.
- Test rename orphans header (medium/configuration): unmitigated; deferred to 94ed/411b.
- Multiple tasks retroactively claim same test for different intent_ids (high/correctness): mitigated by one-header-per-function rule in SC2.
- Agent self-proposes Rule 6 relaxation (medium/configuration): mitigated by safeguard-file designation in SC2.
- Polyglot header embedding inconsistency (medium/runtime): partially mitigated by canonical fixtures.
## Research Findings

Three independent research dispatches during brainstorm surveyed academic literature, open-source tooling, and practitioner thought leaders on the question "at generation time, how do we know whether a candidate test would catch a real regression?" Convergent findings across all streams identified three signal tiers: Tier 1 (assertion shape — observable output vs internal name; cheap floor; 30–60% of LLM tests fail this per Yuan et al. 2024), Tier 2 (articulation — name the invariant and the plausible mutation; medium cost, LLM-friendly; cross-practitioner consensus from Khorikov, Beck, Bach/Bolton, Hughes/Wayne, Fowler), Tier 3 (empirical — mutant kill on the changed line; Meta TestGen-LLM 2025 mutation-guided pipeline; deferred to sibling epic 411b-a047). This epic implements Tiers 1 and 2 only.
## Dependencies

- a03c-d55e (Closure Checks schema migration) — required because intent_id under Rule 6 must reference end-state SC/DoD/AC, which a03c structurally separates from transitional Closure Checks via the new "## Closure Checks" template section and the updated verifiable-sc-check.md end-state-only rule. d566 owns the header schema; a03c's completion-verifier consumes Rule 6 headers for intent_id→test_artifact lookup. Sequential dependency, no conflict.

- 94ed-f55c (Plan-time intent allocation manifest) — required because Rule 6 intent_id field references manifest entries. d566 ships only after 94ed publishes the manifest schema and intent_id format.

- 7f42-e41f (suite growth metrics, sibling) — sequencing: d566 ships first; 7f42 builds on d566's header schema for its per-intent-item growth metrics. To avoid concurrent edits to behavioral-testing-standard.md, 7f42's brainstorm/implementation defers until d566 closes.
## Sibling Calibration Program
- 7f42-e41f: suite growth tracks behavioral coverage (Tier 1+2 metrics).
- 69e8-af39: feedback loop from production bugs and review findings into test-creation prompts.
- 411b-a047: mutation-testing infrastructure (Tier 3 empirical verification).
## Planning Intelligence Log
- Web research (Step 2 of scrutiny pipeline): not triggered — external research was performed at user request during Phase 1 dialogue, prior to Step 2 firing.
- Scenario analysis (Step 3): triggered (SCs ≥ 5); 12 red-team scenarios surfaced, 9 surviving after blue-team filter.

- Cross-epic scan (Step 2.25): triggered against a focused candidate set of 16 test/agent/review-related open epics. 1 ambiguity (a03c-d55e) resolved in Dependencies; 4 consideration signals on sibling/prereq epics; 1 benign signal on kudos.

- Bot-psychologist (Step 5): triggered (LLM-instruction signal: agent definitions + prompt templates). Findings folded into SC1, SC2, SC4 (catches_regression_where rename, UNTRACKED sentinel, predicate-listing scaffold, anti-sycophancy prime, sibling-case rule).

- Fidelity review (Step 4): Agent Clarity pass (5, 4), Value pass (4, 4), Scope (4, 4, 4, 3); consumer_completeness=3 finding structurally resolved by SC9 sweep. Reviewer anti-pattern incident filed as bug 270e-225f-6c72-4f0c.
- Scale context (Step 0): not applicable — development-time tool, per-test-author invocation.
- Session-signal override for complexity routing: success_criteria_count = 9 (≥ 7 threshold) AND scenario_survivor_count = 9 (close to 10 threshold) — routes to /dso:preplanning full mode.
## Closure Checks (added by /dso:preplanning Phase E)

- (sc-7 dogfood gate, escalated from the adversarial review) A /dso:review run on the d566 implementation PR emits zero Tier 1 (assertion shape) or Tier 2 (articulation) findings on the tests authored by this epic; the dso:completion-verifier confirms this gate before epic close.

## Context

DSO planning skills (brainstorm, preplanning, implementation-plan) evaluate features at the capability level but never surface operational-coordination requirements: the pattern where one script writes an artifact X while a separate file Y that references X is left stale in the same change. This produced the release.sh + marketplace.json desync that broke a real plugin release. This epic teaches planning to detect artifact-reference couplings and require atomic co-update, surfaced as an acceptance criterion before implementation, seeded by a registry bootstrapped from the codebase.

Terminology: "AC" = Acceptance Criterion (a human-readable task field). A "writer" is a file in a story's file-impact table with action create or modify whose output is consumed by a registered downstream reference. "touches" = a file appears in the story file-impact table with action create or modify.
## Success Criteria

- SC1: A new Category 8 "Operational Atomicity / Artifact-Reference Desync" is added to the red-team-reviewer story_review taxonomy and the taxonomy_category output enum gains the value operational_atomicity. During story-map review, for a story that touches a registered writer, the reviewer emits a finding whose AC names the paired referencing file and requires atomic same-commit update. Registry-backed findings are authoritative; LLM-inferred findings carry confidence: advisory and are suppressible via SC8. The registry is injected into the reviewer via the orchestrator dispatch arguments at the path in registry.antipattern_path. A Category 8 finding suppresses a parallel Category 6 finding for the same pair; rename/remove cases defer to Category 7.
Verify-intent: a preplanning run over a fixture story editing a registered writer emits a finding with taxonomy_category=operational_atomicity and an AC string naming the paired referencing file.

- SC2: ast-grep is reclassified from optional to required in the dependency phase of onboarding/SKILL.md and INSTALL.md; onboarding hard-exits non-zero with install remediation when ast-grep is absent, or when the only sg on PATH is the Linux shadow-utils setgid /usr/bin/sg. Detection uses an identity probe (parse sg --version; accept only if it identifies ast-grep at version >= 0.20), never a bare command -v sg. All DSO scripts invoke the long-form ast-grep binary.
Verify-intent: an onboarding run with ast-grep absent and a decoy setgid sg exits non-zero and the error output contains "ast-grep" plus a recommended install command.

- SC3: A new bootstrap migration script fans out sub-agents over chunked codebase slices, each running ast-grep to emit (file, normalized_path, role, line, snippet) tuples (map), joined by an equijoin on the realpath-normalized path (reduce). A pair is admitted only when all hold: exact realpath-normalized path, a recognized write idiom (shell > / >>, tee, sed -i, jq write-to-file, Python open(w)/Path.write_text, Node fs.writeFileSync, Ruby File.open(w)/File.write, Go os.WriteFile; vocabulary externally extensible via registry config), and writer and reference in different files. Ambiguous/inferred pairs are out of scope for the migration.

Verify-intent: bootstrap over a fixture repo emits output equal to a sorted newline-delimited "writer_realpath<TAB>reference_realpath" manifest exactly (no missing/extra); near-miss fixtures (same-file self-reference; cross-file read-only) are absent.

- SC4: implementation-plan/SKILL.md emits, for any task that adds, modifies, or removes a dso-config.conf key, a separate child sub-task (testing_mode GREEN) titled "Document <key> in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md" carrying a depends_on link to the parent task. This child sub-task supersedes the generic doc-router path for config keys (no duplicate documentation task).
Verify-intent: an implementation-plan run on a key-adding task yields that child sub-task whose depends_on points to the parent task id.

- SC5: The Category 8 consumption point reads the antipattern registry at registry.antipattern_path. Registry schema (this epic codes against this shape; clear-fairy may ship it, else a local fixture supplies it): a YAML file whose records are {file_class: glob, pattern: regex or ast-grep query, audit_task_template: string} plus a top-level schema_version. When present, a matching file_class injects a pre-emptive audit task from audit_task_template. When absent, clean no-op logging "registry absent"; when present-but-unparseable, clean no-op logging "registry unreadable" (distinct). Adaptation to clear-fairy's final schema is limited to updating registry.antipattern_path + schema_version; no migration code is owned here.
Verify-intent: registry absent -> completes, logs "registry absent"; corrupt fixture -> completes, logs "registry unreadable"; valid fixture -> injects the audit task.

- SC6: When a registered referencing file is not co-updatable in the same commit, classified by the union (git check-ignore | generated-path heuristic reusing is_generated_file() patterns | cross-repo URL in the reference | branch-protected via gh api, where a 404 is treated as not-protected and the branch-protection result is cached per-branch), the gate emits a deferred-coordination note recorded as a story consideration that preplanning/sprint consume by creating a follow-up coordination task, instead of an unachievable atomic-update AC. The note format contract is named in the preplanning/sprint acceptance criteria so the receiving behavior is testable.
Verify-intent: a generated-file fixture yields a deferred-coordination consideration and a follow-up task, not a hard atomic-update AC.
- SC7: A re-runnable registry-refresh command (sharing a normalize-and-sort library with the bootstrap; idempotent sort-dedup on write) detects writer/reference pairs added since the last run.
Verify-intent: a re-run on a fixture repo with one newly-added pair surfaces exactly that pair as an update candidate; a no-change re-run surfaces nothing.

- SC8: A config key review.atomicity_inference_enabled (default false; documented in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md) gates only the Category 8 LLM-inference pass; the deterministic registry pass always runs. The SC4 story is sequenced before the SC8 story so SC8's key documentation follows the G11-M2 pattern.
Verify-intent: with the key false, a planning run emits zero confidence: advisory findings but still emits registry-backed findings.
## Closure Checks
- The plugin-shipped seed registry contains the pairs release.sh<->marketplace.json, *.conf<->CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md, and plugin.json<->marketplace source ref.
- onboarding docs list ast-grep as required (minimum version >= 0.20) with install instructions (cargo/npm/brew) and document the /usr/bin/sg shadow-utils collision.
- red-team-reviewer.md taxonomy_category enum includes the value operational_atomicity.
- review.atomicity_inference_enabled and registry.antipattern_path are documented in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md.
- The shared normalize-and-sort registry library file exists and is sourced by both the bootstrap and refresh scripts.
## Dependencies

- clear-fairy / 7575-5a90 (depends_on) for the antipattern registry artifact consumed by SC5 only. All other SCs have no external dependency. The 85cb idempotent-task-semantics relationship was reviewed and overridden (our state-check ACs hold regardless of how idempotency is later formalized).
## Approach

Hybrid detection: a plugin-shipped seed registry of artifact-reference pairs (YAML) plus a project-local overlay, read deterministically by a new Category 8 pass in the red-team-reviewer at preplanning time, supplemented by an LLM inference pass for novel couplings (advisory, suppressible). Bootstrap migration uses ast-grep as a one-engine polyglot extractor (per-file tuple emit) plus an external equijoin on the realpath-normalized path (ast-grep matches within a file only). ast-grep is upgraded to a required onboarding dependency with shadow-utils /usr/bin/sg disambiguation. This converged with prior art: deterministic registry/declaration over inference for anything that gates (changesets fixed/linked, release-please extra-files, syncpack), one tree-sitter engine over per-language plugins, and inference confined to advisory triage. clear-fairy delivers the antipattern registry (G6-M2); this epic owns its consumption (G6-M3), the config-key/doc pairing (G11-M2), and the core atomicity check.
## Scenario Analysis
- setgid /usr/bin/sg shadows ast-grep so a bare guard runs the wrong binary (critical) - mitigated by SC2 identity probe + invoking ast-grep.
- Equijoin path normalization across sub-agents produces false/missed pairs (high) - mitigated by SC3 realpath normalization.
- Category 8 LLM-inference fires non-deterministically across runs (high) - mitigated by deterministic registry authority + SC8 toggle + advisory confidence.
- Bootstrap sub-agents truncate tuple lists at context limit with no error (high) - operational risk for preplanning.
- G6-M3 no-op when registry absent is indistinguishable from unreadable (medium) - mitigated by SC5 distinct diagnostics.
- Seed + overlay have no merge protocol; stale overlay shadows updated seed (high) - registry-lifecycle risk for preplanning.
- Onboarding block does not propagate to CI; CI silently skips the gate (high) - mitigated by a CI ast-grep precondition before planning jobs.
- Bootstrap is one-time; registry goes stale (high) - mitigated by SC7 refresh.
- Write-idiom set not configurable; project idioms produce no pairs (high) - mitigated by SC3 extensible vocabulary.
- No knob to disable Category 8 inference (medium) - mitigated by SC8.
- Equijoin assumes path stability; symlinks/aliases produce phantom/missed pairs (high) - mitigated by SC3 realpath resolution.
- Atomic-co-update AC is unachievable for generated/cross-repo/branch-protected files (high) - mitigated by SC6 deferred-coordination note.

## Context

The current `scripts/create-dso-app.sh` clones a hardcoded fork of Strata's NextJS template with DSO infrastructure baked into the fork's files. The fork is NextJS-only (precluding Strata SDK access, which is Rails-first) and detached from `platform-cli`'s install/upgrade lifecycle, so it drifts from upstream Strata over time. There's no way for a non-technical user to scaffold a Strata Rails+SDK+USWDS prototype with one command. This epic rewrites the installer to invoke `nava-platform app install` against upstream Strata templates (Rails default, pinned to v1.0.0), apply a DSO overlay, and deprecate the fork — using a phased script structure with extracted overlay engine and pre-implementation feasibility spike (already executed and recorded as a baseline at `tests/audits/A1-feasibility-spike-results.md`).
## In Scope

- Restructure `scripts/create-dso-app.sh` into six explicit phases: `parse-args` → `check-prereqs` → `invoke-platform-cli` → `apply-overlay` → `rails-sdk-add` → `emit-summary`. Each phase is a bash function; failures emit `[A1] phase=<name>` tagged errors and a "what to do next" hint.

- New shared script `plugins/dso/scripts/apply-host-overlay.sh` (the overlay engine): walks `plugins/dso/templates/host-project/`, applies `{{PROJECT_NAME}}` substitution per the existing installer convention, copies into target, leaves a one-line audit comment in dso-config.conf. Reusable beyond create-dso-app.sh.

- New in-plugin overlay tree `plugins/dso/templates/host-project/`: canonical DSO files (CLAUDE.md template, dso-config.conf, .pre-commit-config.yaml, project-understanding.md skeleton, design-notes.md skeleton, ARCH_ENFORCEMENT.md skeleton) with `{{PROJECT_NAME}}` placeholders matching the installer's substitution patterns.

- Ship `plugins/dso/scripts/lib/strata-config-defaults.conf` — shared canonical definition file mapping each Strata template variant to its `commands.*` values, Rails-Strata ARCH_ENFORCEMENT footguns, and Strata Posture section template. Single source of truth — sourced by A1's `apply-overlay` phase AND by A2's `prompts/strata/config-writes.md` + `arch-enforcement.md`. A1 MUST NOT independently define `commands.*` keys — sources from this file. A1 writes the FULL Posture section (not a skeleton) using install-time-known `_commit` and `_src_path`, so A2's onboarding-time idempotency check produces zero diffs.
- Tickets orphan-branch creation post-overlay; explicit `git push origin tickets` exit-code check; remote conflict surfaced with clear error and exit non-zero.

- CLI flags: `--app-name=<name>` (positional kept for back-compat plus added as flag), `--port=<num>` (default 3000), `--template=rails|nextjs|flask` (default rails), `--no-sdk` (skips Rails SDK gem add), `--no-overlay` (skips DSO overlay), `--auto-install-prereqs`, `--help`. Phase-tagged errors and recovery hints.

- Defensive guard against unknown Copier vars: at `check-prereqs`, parse upstream `copier.yml` at pinned commit hash (via `gh api`) and diff required-var list (name + type + accepted-values for enums) against hardcoded list in `plugins/dso/scripts/lib/strata-template-vars.sh` (where copier.yml is the source of truth and the hardcoded list is the script's coverage map). If any copier.yml-required var is NOT in the hardcoded list, fail fast with `[A1] copier.yml required var '<name>' not in --data list; update plugins/dso/scripts/lib/strata-template-vars.sh`. At `invoke-platform-cli`, hang detector (5s prompt-pattern + 60s no-output) as defense-in-depth.
- `nava-platform` install command pins to specific upstream tag/commit (per spike: v1.0.0 for `template-application-rails`); pinned ref documented in `strata-template-vars.sh`.

- Rails SDK gem-add (when `--template=rails` and not `--no-sdk`): single-line text-append of `gem "strata", github: "navapbc/strata-sdk-rails"` (gem name is `strata`, not `strata-sdk-rails`, per spike) to the generated `Gemfile`. Idempotent grep-before-append. No Ruby/bundler on host; user's first `make build` runs `bundle install` inside Docker.

- Project layout: `create-dso-app.sh my-prototype` flow creates `my-prototype/` as project root; runs `nava-platform app install --template-uri ... --version v1.0.0 --data app_name=app --data app_local_port=3000 . app` from inside `my-prototype/`. Result: `my-prototype/` is project root with DSO overlay (CLAUDE.md, dso-config.conf, ticket store dir, `.template-application-rails/app.yml`); `my-prototype/app/` is the Rails app. Canonical app subdirectory name: `app`.
- Overlay engine: collision-protection (refuses to overwrite by default; `--overlay-mode=skip|overwrite|merge` flag); binary-safety (text-extension whitelist + `file -b --mime` detection).

- Prereq install contract: OS matrix = macOS + Linux (Windows users directed to WSL2 via clear error). Package manager selection: macOS detects Homebrew (`brew install uv` if present, else `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh`); Linux uses official `curl` installer. After uv installer runs, unconditionally `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"`; verify with `command -v nava-platform`; fail fast if not found. Failure semantics: prereq install failure aborts (no warn-and-continue). `--auto-install-prereqs` skips interactive confirmation; if NOT passed AND prompt would be required AND no TTY available, abort with `[A1] phase=check-prereqs no TTY for prereq prompt; pass --auto-install-prereqs for unattended`.
- Docker pre-flight check: detect Docker; emit clear pre-flight error if absent (with link to Docker Desktop install page). Docker is NOT auto-installed.
- `--app-name` validation: regex `^[a-z0-9\-_]+$` at parse-args; reject invalid names with clear error before any installation work.

## Success Criteria

1. One-command Strata Rails+SDK+USWDS scaffold completes non-interactively. Non-technical user (Ruby NOT installed; uv NOT installed; Docker installed) runs `bash <(curl -fsSL .../create-dso-app.sh) my-prototype --auto-install-prereqs` and the script completes with exit zero and zero non-prerequisite interactive prompts. Result `my-prototype/` containing: (a) working Strata Rails app from upstream `template-application-rails@v1.0.0` (`make build` succeeds in Docker); (b) USWDS bundled (`@uswds/uswds@^3.7.1` in package.json); (c) `gem "strata", github: "navapbc/strata-sdk-rails"` present in Gemfile; (d) DSO overlay files with substituted PROJECT_NAME; (e) tickets orphan branch present + pushed if remote configured; (f) SDK functional check: post-build, `make rails-runner CMD='require "strata"; puts Strata::VERSION'` returns a non-empty version string. Additionally, the values written into `dso-config.conf`, `ARCH_ENFORCEMENT.md`, and `project-understanding.md`'s `## Strata Posture` section match what A2's `prompts/strata/*` sub-files would produce when run on the same scaffolded project state — verified by behavioral test asserting zero diffs in those three files. CLI flag variants produce documented outputs. `--template=nextjs` produces NextJS scaffold without SDK gem. `--template=flask` produces Flask scaffold without SDK gem. `--no-sdk` skips Gemfile append (verified by absence of gem line). `--no-overlay` produces clean upstream Strata scaffold without DSO overlay files. `--port=8080` propagates to upstream `app_local_port`. `--auto-install-prereqs` installs missing uv/nava-platform without prompting. Install-time test: simulated prompt-pattern in stderr → kill within 5s with same error class. No hung script in either path.

4. Overlay engine independently testable; collision-protected; binary-safe; idempotent. `apply-host-overlay.sh` invoked directly produces correct output; collision protection refuses overwrite by default; binary files (image/lock-file fixtures) NOT substituted; idempotent re-run (Gemfile dedup, no double-tickets-branch).

## Scenario Analysis

11 surviving scenarios (red/blue team filter) all addressed via In Scope mitigations: nava-platform interactive hang protection (input redirect + hang detector); platform-cli version pinning; overlay collision detection (refuse overwrite by default); Gemfile idempotency (grep before append); tickets push exit-code handling; binary file safety in overlay (text-extension whitelist + MIME detection); uv prereq detection + offered install; real-URL E2E test updated BEFORE fork archive (sequencing constraint); --app-name regex validation; defensive guard upgrade (parse copier.yml at pinned hash AND install-time prompt detection).
## Approach

Phased script structure with extracted overlay engine. Defensive guard via hardcoded required-var lists pinned to upstream commit hashes (with copier.yml as source of truth, hardcoded list as coverage map — fail fast on divergence). Container-first Rails SDK installation (no host Ruby). Fork archived via `gh repo archive --yes`. Behavioral test via existing `test-create-dso-app-real-url.sh` opt-in pattern.
## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation, 2026-05-18)
### Bypass Governance — --no-sdk / --no-overlay / --overlay-mode=overwrite (Probe-4 remediation)
These three flags bypass safety defaults (SDK gem add, DSO overlay, collision protection). The existing single-comment audit in dso-config.conf is upgraded to a structured governance pairing:

- **Audit log:** every invocation of create-dso-app.sh with any of the three flags writes a structured JSON line to `.dso/create-app-bypass.log` with `{timestamp, target_dir, flag, value, justification, operator_uid}`.

- **Required justification companion:** each flag MUST be accompanied by `--bypass-reason="..."` with non-empty content; create-dso-app.sh exits non-zero if a bypass flag is set without `--bypass-reason`. (Hard enforcement, not soft.)

- **Abuse-detection:** retro / debug-everything inspects `.dso/create-app-bypass.log` on every project entry; if the same operator+target_dir combination shows ≥3 bypass invocations within 30 days, surface a MUST-display warning ("bypass pattern detected; investigate") before allowing the next bypass invocation.

- **Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):** synthetic test invokes create-dso-app.sh with each of the three flags WITHOUT `--bypass-reason`; asserts non-zero exit + clear error. Then with `--bypass-reason="test"` succeeds; the log captures the entry.

### 1. Technical Environment
* **Plugin/Tool Versions:** dso v1.17.17
* **Context Scope:** worktree-20260522-142331, epic d2f9-ee1a-48ab-4bf6
* **Active Configs:** APPROACH_RESOLUTION=autonomous, SPRINT_MODE=ci-pr
### 2. Incident Overview
* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior
#### Expected Behavior

Per `plugins/dso/skills/implementation-plan/SKILL.md` Step 3, the `dso:task-decomposer` agent emits task drafts whose `Verify:` commands are robust enough to (a) pass plan review on cycle 1 in the typical case and (b) actually succeed at task execution time. Per Step 4, the plan reviewer perspectives (Task Design, Completeness) should catch fragile or incorrect `Verify:` commands before tasks land. The combined system should not require 2-3 review cycles per story to scrub out the same categories of AC defect.
#### Actual Behavior

Across three sequential story impl-plans in a single session (35ee, b386, d94e — all in epic d2f9-ee1a-48ab-4bf6), the task-decomposer produced ACs with the **same categories of defect** repeatedly. Each story required 2 or 3 plan-review cycles to surface and fix these defects. After cycle-pass on d94e, gap analysis still found 5 more AC defects to amend. The recurring categories are:
1. **Substring false positives in grep/awk patterns** — e.g., AC-9 on d94e: `'cycle' in section_text` substring-matches `'review_cycle'`, making the field-presence check trivially pass.
2. **Shell-expansion leakage in Verify command strings** — e.g., b386 task-1 AC-6: `grep -E 'PATH=.*:$PATH'` had `$PATH` expanded by the shell before grep saw it; needed `\$PATH`.

3. **Wrong invocation signature for cited helper scripts** — e.g., 35ee AC-7 cycle 1: passed `validate-review-output.sh "$FIXTURE"` (1 arg) when the script requires `validate-review-output.sh <prompt-id> <output-file>` (2 args, exit 2 on usage error).

4. **Fixture files chosen without validating they work for the AC's purpose** — e.g., 35ee AC-7 cycle 2: used `tests/fixtures/ci-review-corpus/post-loop-findings.json` to assert non-breaking validation, but that fixture fails `code-review-dispatch` validation for unrelated reasons (missing `summary`, `category`, `file`, `cited_excerpt`), so the AC could never pass regardless of the change under test.

5. **Conflicting ACs without a resolution AC** — e.g., b386 task-1 cycle 1: AC-1 ("Unit tests pass — Universal") conflicted with AC-5 ("Test fails RED in isolation") because the required `.test-index` RED-marker AC was missing — neither AC alone signaled the dependency.

6. **Missing prerequisite-state ACs** — e.g., b386 task-1 cycle 1: no AC to add `.test-index` RED marker for the new source, so the pre-commit test gate would block the commit even though all other ACs pointed at a correctly-authored test.

7. **grep patterns too narrow for natural authoring formats** — e.g., d94e AC-5 cycle 1: `'schema_version[[:space:]]*=?[[:space:]]*1'` matches bare prose but NOT `"schema_version": 1` (JSON), `schema_version: 1` (YAML), or `| schema_version | 1 |` (markdown table) — all valid documentation forms.

8. **Wrong assertion target — prose vs structured artifact** — e.g., d94e AC-9 cycle 1: checked field name presence in section TEXT (prose) when DD-2 requires presence in a JSON example block; a section that mentions the field in prose but omits it from the JSON example trivially passed.

9. **No cardinality guards** — e.g., d94e AC-9 cycle 1: "all 5 event types have worked examples" was never asserted as "exactly 5 sections exist"; a doc with fewer sections could pass if the present sections were valid.

10. **Stale or future-only sibling references** — e.g., b386 cycle 1: task description cited `verify-aws-account.sh` as a pattern reference, but that file is created by sibling story ac57 which had not yet been implemented; the existing real sibling is `verify-session-provenance.sh`.

11. **Fragile awk range delimiters** — e.g., d94e AC-12/13 cycle 1: `/^##[[:space:]]+[^P]/` as section-end pattern was a negation that broke for any `## ` section starting with a `P` (e.g., a hypothetical `## Performance` after `## Privacy Disclosure`); the robust form is `/^## /` as the next-section anchor.
### 3. Action History and Workarounds
* **Steps Taken:**
* Story 35ee impl-plan: 3 plan-review cycles required (cycles 1, 2 failed on AC-7 variants; cycle 3 restructured AC-7 to a construction-based check that passed).
* Story b386 impl-plan: 2 plan-review cycles required (cycle 1 surfaced RED-marker absence + regex bugs + sibling reference; cycle 2 passed).
* Story d94e impl-plan: 2 plan-review cycles required (cycle 1 surfaced AC-5 narrowness + AC-9 substring/prose/cardinality/per-type defects + AC-12/13 awk fragility; cycle 2 passed).

* After d94e cycle 2 passed plan review, gap analysis surfaced **5 additional** AC defect categories in the same task — confirming the issue is systemic and not caught even by the cycle-2-passing review.

* **Known Workarounds:** Run the plan-review loop to its 3-cycle limit per story, then file gap-analysis amendments after. This is the current de facto workaround but it (a) doubles or triples planning time per story, (b) consumes opus/sonnet budget on the review loop, and (c) when the 3-cycle limit is hit on a stubborn story (35ee), the orchestrator presents a still-broken plan to the user.
### 4. Chronological Rationalization
* Initial reasoning during 35ee cycle 1: the task-decomposer is opus-level and should produce shippable ACs first try. The 3 review cycles needed felt anomalous.

* During b386 cycle 1: same defect categories surfaced (regex shell expansion, sibling reference accuracy). The repetition across distinct stories signals a systemic generation issue, not a per-story bug.

* During d94e cycle 1: same categories AGAIN (grep narrowness, substring vs structured-artifact assertion, cardinality). At this point the pattern is clear: the task-decomposer is not running an internal "would this Verify command actually work?" sanity check.

* Post-d94e gap analysis returning 5 more amendments confirms that plan review (Step 4) and gap analysis (Step 6) overlap in scope but neither has explicit anti-patterns for Verify-command robustness.
### 5. Skills and Workflows
* **Active Workflow:** `/dso:sprint` Phase B → `/dso:implementation-plan` (Steps 3–6)
* **Skills/Agents Involved:**
- `dso:task-decomposer` (opus) — generates the ACs at Step 3
- `dso:code-reviewer-*` / plan-review perspectives (sonnet) — review the ACs at Step 4
- Gap analysis opus sub-agent — Step 6 surfaces remaining defects
* **Reference files implicated:**
- `plugins/dso/agents/task-decomposer.md`
- `plugins/dso/skills/implementation-plan/docs/reviewers/plan/task-design.md`
- `plugins/dso/skills/implementation-plan/docs/reviewers/plan/completeness.md`
- `plugins/dso/docs/ACCEPTANCE-CRITERIA-LIBRARY.md`
- `plugins/dso/skills/implementation-plan/prompts/gap-analysis.md`
### 7. Additional Details

**Remediation surface** (do NOT remediate the specific tickets 35ee/b386/d94e — those plans are already fixed in-cycle and shipped). Remediate the planning skills/agents so future stories do not produce these defects:
1. **task-decomposer prompt** (`plugins/dso/agents/task-decomposer.md`): add an explicit anti-pattern checklist for Verify commands, including:
- Substring false-positives (word-boundary vs substring matching; quote JSON keys when checking presence in JSON)
- Shell expansion in single-quoted heredocs vs double-quoted (escape `$PATH`, `$?`, etc.)
- Helper script invocation: cite expected argv signature; cross-reference the helper's `--help` or first-line usage comment
- Fixture selection: require that the chosen fixture is independently valid for the AC's purpose, not just convenient
- Cardinality guards: when a DD names a count ("all 5 event types"), the AC MUST assert that count
- Format tolerance: when checking a documented value in a `.md` file, accept JSON, YAML, prose, and pipe-table forms unless one is mandated
- Awk range delimiters: prefer positive `/^## /` next-section anchors over negation patterns
- Prerequisite ACs: when a downstream Universal AC depends on a project mechanism (e.g., RED markers), include the mechanism-setup AC explicitly

2. **Plan-review reviewer perspectives** (`plugins/dso/skills/implementation-plan/docs/reviewers/plan/task-design.md` and `completeness.md`): add a dedicated dimension or rubric item for Verify-command robustness. Specifically scrutinize each AC's command for the 11 defect categories above.

3. **Gap-analysis prompt** (`plugins/dso/skills/implementation-plan/prompts/gap-analysis.md`): add a category for AC-Verify defects so gap analysis catches what plan review missed, rather than rediscovering category-1 issues at gap-analysis time.
4. **AC library** (`plugins/dso/docs/ACCEPTANCE-CRITERIA-LIBRARY.md`): add a "Common Verify-Command Anti-Patterns" appendix referenced by the task-decomposer.

5. **Sanity-check step** (optional, larger change): an inline `mktemp + apply mock content + run Verify` smoke loop in task-decomposer before emitting tasks, catching shell-expansion and substring-false-positive cases at generation time.

**Acceptance for remediation**: after the fix lands, a representative doc-only story (similar in shape to 35ee/d94e) and a representative RED→GREEN script story (similar to b386) should both pass plan review on cycle 1 with no AC defects from the 11 categories above. A test suite simulating these stories against the task-decomposer (or a corpus snapshot of the kind of ACs it produces) would prove the remediation.
**Out-of-scope for this bug**: do not edit tasks 41b8/2607/da20/4830 or their ACs. Those are already cycle-passed and ship-ready.

content.text: Incorporate concrete, measurable UI/UX constraints into DSO's design review process as hard enforcement — not soft suggestions.
## Reference: ui-ux-pro-max-skill
### Interaction timing as enforced constraints (not guidelines)
ui-ux-pro-max-skill treats these as hard constraints checkable in code review:
- Animation durations: 150-300ms with platform-native easing
- Tap/click feedback latency: 80-150ms (ripple/opacity/elevation)
- Touch targets: 44×44pt minimum (Apple HIG) / 48×48dp minimum (Material Design)
- Micro-interactions: 150-300ms
- prefers-reduced-motion: mandatory, not optional
### No emoji as icons — enforced professional quality signal

The skill explicitly bans emoji as UI icons and requires professional SVG icon libraries (Heroicons, Lucide, Phosphor, USWDS icons). This is treated as a concrete, automatable code quality signal — not a style preference.
## What to Add to DSO Design Review
1. Add measurable interaction timing constraints to the design review checklist — reviewer should flag animations outside 150-300ms, missing tap feedback, and touch targets below platform minimums
2. Add an automated check for emoji used as icons in UI code (detectable via regex/AST)
3. Add prefers-reduced-motion support as a required review dimension
4. Make these constraints configurable per project via dso-config.conf (e.g., design.animation_max_ms=300, design.touch_target_min=44)
5. Integrate into the completion verifier for UI stories — verify timing and icon constraints are met before story closure

* **Scenario Type:** Sub-Agent Blocker (planning-model defect)
**Filed by d076 post-mortem analysis (`docs/findings/d076-postmortem-analysis.md`) — implementation deferred to a remediation sprint.**
#### Expected Behavior

When /dso:end-session runs and the closing session shows ≥N invocations of any bypass-hatch (DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=0, DSO_DEBUG_ACTIVE=0, --force-*, --override-*) in the session's audit logs or hook output, end-session must (a) emit an integrity-check warning surfacing the count and the bypass reasons, (b) file a follow-up bug ticket capturing the pattern (component = the area being bypassed; description = audit-log excerpt), and (c) include the warning in the session-close summary so the next orchestrator picks it up. The threshold N can be configured per project (e.g., `end_session.bypass_alert_threshold`); a sensible default is 3.
#### Actual Behavior

During the d076 sprint, DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=0 was invoked ~20 times to commit directly to the session worktree. End-session did not surface the count. The orchestrator wrote a Phase I session-close summary declaring the work shipped. The user only discovered the situation by inspecting PR #140 and asking "Evaluate carefully whether PR 140 followed a process that included LLM review of all code." Surveillance is necessary even when justification is required, because justification cannot detect pattern-of-abuse (justifying each individual instance vs. a systemic bypass behavior).
### 5. Skills and Workflows

Affected skill: end-session. Suggested implementation: a new check that globs /tmp/sprint-merge-only-bypass-*.log (and any other bypass-log path), counts entries against the session window, and fires the integrity-check workflow if the threshold is exceeded.
