## Context

DSO plugin users running orchestration skills (sprint, debug-everything, fix-bug) are constrained by a hard cap of 5 concurrent sub-agents — a blunt workaround for session usage limits that no longer applies now that billing is metered and process improvements (dependency graphs, file impact analysis) naturally bound parallelism. The cap forces unnecessary batching overhead (commit + push between batches) and slows sprint execution without preventing the actual risk: exhausting session usage quotas.

Architecture: All three orchestration skills delegate sub-agent dispatch through agent-batch-lifecycle.sh, the sole integration point. The OAuth endpoint returns five_hour.utilization and seven_day.utilization as floats (0.0-1.0). Null/missing fields are treated as 0% (fail-open).
## Success Criteria

1. A check-usage.sh script polls the Anthropic OAuth usage endpoint, caches results in a shared flock-protected file (~/.cache/claude/usage-cache.json, 5-min TTL, locked via separate usage-cache.lock file), and returns a throttle verdict as exit code: 0=unlimited, 1=throttled, 2=paused

2. When 5-hour utilization reaches 90% OR 7-day utilization reaches 95%, agent-batch-lifecycle.sh emits MAX_AGENTS: 1 and orchestration skills dispatch exactly 1 sub-agent per batch; subsequent batches proceed only after the prior agent returns

3. When 5-hour utilization reaches 95% OR 7-day utilization reaches 98%, agent-batch-lifecycle.sh emits MAX_AGENTS: 0 and orchestration skills skip sub-agent dispatch, writing a ticket comment with utilization percentages and reset time

4. An orchestration.max_agents config key in dso-config.conf caps the upper bound on concurrent sub-agents; when unset and verdict is unlimited, MAX_AGENTS: unlimited is emitted with no artificial ceiling — verified by test dispatching 10 agents without truncation
5. CLAUDE.md rule #4 no longer contains the phrase "5 sub-agents"; it references the orchestration.max_agents config key and the two throttle tiers — verified by grep returning no matches

6. An error-reactive fallback pattern-matches sub-agent result text for rate-limit keywords (rate.limit|usage.limit|quota.exceeded) and triggers throttling to 1 agent when matched — verified by test injecting error string and asserting throttle activates
7. Test asserts that with verdict unlimited and max_agents unset, a batch of 10 independent stories dispatches 10 concurrent sub-agents with no intervening commit/push steps
## Integration Details
- CI fallback: no credentials -> exit 0 (unlimited), USAGE_SOURCE: no-credentials
- Linux token: ~/.claude/.credentials.json -> claudeAiOauth.accessToken key path
- Portable locking: Python fcntl.flock (not flock(1) CLI)
- 429 stale-cache: use last known verdict (fail-closed toward throttled); cold-cache 429: exit 1 (throttled to 1)
- In-flight agents complete when throttle transitions mid-sprint
- Cache TTL floor: 60s minimum enforced regardless of config
- Cache dir: mkdir -p ~/.cache/claude/ before write
## Approach

agent-batch-lifecycle.sh is extended: its cmd_pre_check() calls check-usage.sh and emits MAX_AGENTS: unlimited|<N>|0 (replacing the current binary 5/1 output). check-usage.sh handles OAuth polling, caching, and CI fallback. An error-reactive wrapper in agent-batch-lifecycle.sh pattern-matches sub-agent result text for rate-limit errors as a secondary signal.
## Scenario Analysis
- flock on deleted cache file (high): Lock on separate lockfile + atomic rename for writes
- OAuth endpoint timeout (critical): curl --max-time 8 enforced
- Error-reactive false positives (medium): Match quota-specific keywords only, not generic HTTP 429
- Null API fields (high): Treat as 0% utilization (fail-open)
- Missing cache dir on first run (medium): mkdir -p before write
- CI runners have no credentials (high): Short-circuit to unlimited
- flock portability on macOS (high): Python fcntl.flock for portability
- Cache TTL of 0 (medium): Floor at 60s enforced
- Multiple OAuth tokens (high): Use claudeAiOauth.accessToken key path
- Immediate pause on first run (high): Log warning with reset time and suggest manual override
## Dependencies
- Coordinate with dso-0wi2 (config flags): ensure orchestration.max_agents follows config extension pattern
- Coordinate with 5df7-63ac (observability): this epic owns throttling only, not analytics/telemetry
- Coordinate with dso-9fgn (limit tool use): that epic constrains tools within agents; this constrains how many agents are dispatched
## Spike Recommendation

~2 days before implementation: (1) verify Linux credentials path yields valid OAuth token, (2) confirm endpoint response schema under 429 conditions, (3) validate Python fcntl.flock under concurrent access from two shell sessions
## Research Findings
### External Integration: Anthropic OAuth Usage Endpoint
- Trigger: External integration
- Query: OAuth usage endpoint behavior and rate limiting
- Sources: github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/31021, github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/31637
- Key insight: Endpoint rate-limits aggressively (~1 call/min, 429s persist for hours with no Retry-After header). 5-min cache TTL + flock prevents multi-session hammering.
### Prior Art: Usage-Aware Throttling
- Trigger: External integration
- Query: Claude Code plugins implementing usage monitoring
- Sources: github.com/mironmax/claudecode-plugins, github.com/aryansidbatte/nice-claude-status-bar, github.com/wntdev99/claude-code-server

- Key insight: mironmax uses PostToolUse hook with 60s cache and 95%/98% thresholds. wntdev99 uses TokenTracker + IntelligentThrottler at 85% warn / 90% pause. Our approach follows the mironmax pattern but with 5-min cache to avoid 429s.

- Bright-line conditions that fired: external integration, security/credentials
- Scenario analysis (Step 2.75): triggered

## Context

DSO plugin users running orchestration skills (sprint, debug-everything, fix-bug) dispatch multiple sub-agents per epic, but all sub-agents share the orchestrators working directory. This causes: (1) parallel agents risk file conflicts, (2) changes batch into large commits harder to review reliably, (3) review/test gates run on combined changes rather than individual units of work.

This is Epic A of a two-epic sequence. Epic A delivers the full vertical slice for worktree isolation with serial review. Epic B (separate ticket) scales to parallel review with Clash conflict prevention.
## Success Criteria

1. Orchestration skills dispatch implementation sub-agents with isolation: worktree, giving each agent its own working directory — verified by test asserting sub-agent git rev-parse --show-toplevel differs from orchestrators root

2. Worktree-isolation-guard updated from categorical deny to auth-file allowlist: orchestrator writes /tmp/worktree-isolation-authorized-<session-id> before dispatch, guard checks marker — verified by test showing authorized agents pass and unauthorized agents blocked

3. When implementation sub-agents return, orchestrator reviews and tests each worktree serially, running review/test sub-agents in that worktrees cwd (each worktree naturally gets its own ARTIFACTS_DIR via REPO_ROOT hash) — verified by review producing reviewer-findings.json in worktrees artifact dir

4. Each worktree that passes review produces its own commit in its worktree branch and merges into the session branch immediately (first-pass-first-merge by completion order) — verified by git log showing one commit per worktree with no combined batches

5. Merge conflicts detected at merge time are flagged — conflicting worktree queued for re-implementation or user escalation — verified by injected conflict test asserting ticket comment CONFLICT: worktree <id> blocked
6. A worktree.isolation_enabled config key in dso-config.conf enables/disables worktree isolation (default: true); when disabled, fallback to shared-directory mode — verified by config toggle
7. Worktree retention protocol: orchestrator retains worktree until merge complete; cleanup only after successful merge or explicit release
## Approach

Pattern B (orchestrator-controlled): Sub-agents dispatch with Claude Code native isolation: worktree and implement code changes only — no review, test, or commit in sub-agent. When agents return, orchestrator reviews and tests each worktree serially (one at a time), commits in the worktree branch, then merges into session branch. Auth-file allowlist pattern for the isolation guard: orchestrator writes temp marker, guard checks it.
## Spike Findings (verified in session)
- ARTIFACTS_DIR: naturally isolated per worktree because get_artifacts_dir() hashes REPO_ROOT, which differs per worktree. No code changes needed for artifact isolation.

- Diff hash: stable because review + commit both happen in the worktree (same HEAD). Merge commit into session branch triggers merge-state detection, and review gate skips merge commits (existing behavior). The hash mismatch concern is a non-issue.
- reviewer-findings.json: no race condition. Parallel worktrees write to different ARTIFACTS_DIRs automatically.

- Guard allowlist: auth-file approach is feasible. Guard receives full tool_input JSON. Orchestrator writes /tmp/worktree-isolation-authorized-<session-id> before dispatch; guard checks for marker file. Unforgeable by prompt injection.

- Dynamic dispatch: Claude Code isolation: worktree parameter is documented for Agent tool. The claude-code#26923 exit-code reliability concern is specific to exit code 2, not to the JSON permissionDecision mechanism the guard uses.
## Scenario Analysis
17 scenarios survived blue team filter (from 27 red team). Key resolutions:
- Clash non-propagation: deferred to Epic B (Clash not in Epic A scope)
- Sequential merge deadlock: serial review eliminates this in Epic A; Epic B adds timeout
- Branch base drift: review + commit in worktree before merge; standard git 3-way merge handles drift
- reviewer-findings.json race: naturally isolated per worktree via ARTIFACTS_DIR
- CI fallback: worktree.isolation_enabled config key
- Guard blocker: auth-file allowlist pattern
- Review gate hash mismatch: non-issue per spike findings
- Merge-state misidentification: merge commit correctly detected by existing merge-state.sh
- Test gate centrality: orchestrator writes test-gate-status in worktree before commit
- Version bump: merge-to-main runs once at session end, not per worktree
- Worktree cleanup before review: explicit retention protocol
- Ticket system access: sub-agents dont touch tickets (Pattern B); orchestrator owns all ticket ops
## Dependencies
- Depends on dso-t7af (Remove 5-sub-agent cap): can ship with existing cap retained; throttling epic unlocks full potential
- Coordinate with 4c54-4205 (Interface contracts for parallel agent coordination)
## Research Findings
### Claude Code Native Worktree Isolation
- Trigger: Novel architectural pattern
- Query: Claude Code isolation:worktree sub-agent behavior
- Sources: code.claude.com/docs/en/common-workflows, code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents

- Key insight: First-class support since v2.1.49. Framework handles creation, cwd injection, cleanup. Plugin files available in worktree (fresh checkout). Plugin hooks do NOT propagate to plugin sub-agents.
### Multi-Agent Worktree Patterns
- Trigger: Novel architectural pattern

## Context

DSO engineers planning sweeping/repetitive changes — function-signature sweeps across many call sites, import/API renames, framework upgrades, and schema/DB migrations — currently receive a plan that assumes smallest-atomic-task decomposition. The planner over-fragments the work or misses call sites and rollback safety, so missed sites and unsafe migrations surface during sprint execution instead of at plan time. This epic makes /dso:implementation-plan detect migration-style stories and plan them as an automated-sweep + manual-verification (plus rollback for DB) structure, and gives /dso:sprint a two-pass execution ordering. The planner runs both inside the DSO plugin and in consuming projects (Python/Alembic, Django, Rails, TypeScript), so detection is stack-generic.
## Success Criteria

- /dso:implementation-plan auto-classifies a story migration-class via two sub-classifiers: (a) sweep — one logical change repeats across call sites of the specifically targeted symbol/API (not surrounding boilerplate/imports/tests) above a configurable threshold (migration.call_site_threshold, with an explicit default when unset), detected via ast-grep; (b) db — the change touches schema/migration file patterns (migrations/, alembic/, db/migrate, *.migration.ts, schema.sql) regardless of call-site count. The classification and detection query are persisted as a durable migration-class marker in the plan header; classification proceeds without user confirmation. When sg is unavailable, an explicit migration-class:inconclusive marker is recorded (never silently false) and the planner does not crash.

- For each migration-class:sweep change, the dso:task-decomposer emits an automated-sweep task carrying an explicit transform descriptor (recipe rule or sg rewrite, distinct from the detection query), recipe-preferred with agent-sweep fallback, paired with a manual-verification task whose emitted done-definition requires BOTH completeness (re-run the detection query and assert zero remaining sites; un-automatable sites recorded as inline TODO(migration) markers and enumerated in an un_automatable_sites field) and semantic correctness (run the test gate over modified files — a zero detection count without a passing test gate is not complete).

- For migration-class:db changes, the plan always emits a paired rollback task and rollback-verification task; the rollback is classified safe-revert (additive) or compensating-forward (destructive — ambiguous defaults to compensating-forward and leads with a DATA LOSS RISK note); rollback-verification asserts the resulting schema state, not merely that the task ran. The rollback pair is authored in the same plan as the forward migration.

- The dso:task-decomposer emits a feature-flag rollout task only when the rollout:feature-flags-approved tag is present on the story or its parent epic (two-hop lookup via the ticket CLI). When present, it emits a flag-guarded cutover task plus a paired flag-removal cleanup task. When absent on both (including when no parent exists), no feature-flag task is emitted and the plan header records feature_flags:prohibited with reason — regardless of any feature-flag mention in the story text.

- /dso:sprint reads the persisted migration-class marker from the plan header (it does not recompute detection); for each (automated-sweep, manual-verification) pair it sets the verification task's depends_on to the sweep task and schedules the sweep in an earlier batch; absent the marker, standard ordering applies. The two-pass flow is documented in sprint/SKILL.md.

- A fixture at tests/implementation-plan/fixtures/migration-sweep/ (synthetic codebase, at least 5 call sites of a target signature, one intentionally omitted) demonstrates in-session that /dso:implementation-plan emits a migration-class marker and an automated-sweep/manual-verification pair, and that when the sweep leaves the omitted site, the verification completeness assertion exits non-zero and surfaces the missed site — while the pre-change planner (RED-phase committed baseline) produces no marker and no paired structure. Shown with captured tool output.
## Closure Checks
(none — all success criteria are verifiable within the closing sprint session)
## State Lifecycle
| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |

| migration-class marker (plan header) | /dso:implementation-plan detection | final once recorded | /dso:sprint two-pass ordering; dso:task-decomposer emission | discarded with the plan; not persisted past sprint close |

| rollout:feature-flags-approved tag | user / follow-on brainstorm capture (epic 094a-6057) | boolean presence | dso:task-decomposer feature-flag gate | user via ticket untag; else persists for epic lifetime |
## Dependencies

None blocking. The rollout:feature-flags-approved tag is produced upstream — brainstorm-side capture of that approval is a follow-on (relates_to 094a-6057, out of scope here); this epic reads the tag and defaults to prohibited (safe default). Reuses the existing recipe registry/adapters, plugins/dso/scripts/sprint/translate-recipe-to-llm-task.sh, ast-grep (sg), the ticket CLI, and depends_on — all verified present.
## Approach

Add a migration-class detection branch to implementation-plan's contextual-discovery step (dual sub-classifier: ast-grep repetition threshold on the targeted symbol for sweep; migration file-pattern match for db), persist a migration-class marker, and have the dso:task-decomposer emit automated-sweep + manual-verification pairs (and rollback + rollback-verification pairs for db), with /dso:sprint consuming the marker to order sweep before verification via depends_on. Prompt wording uses affirmative gates over prohibitions, an explicit config default, a conservative rollback default, an over-trigger guard (count only the targeted symbol), and a self-contained sprint instruction with an absent-marker fallback.
## Scenario Analysis
- Assumption (critical): rollback assumed invertible — destructive schema changes have no safe inverse; addressed by safe-revert/compensating-forward classification.

- Runtime (critical): ast-grep call-site count diverges from the true set of sites (dynamic dispatch, generated/vendored code); mitigated by the re-run-query assertion plus test gate, residual risk flagged for implementation-plan stories.
- Deployment (critical): forward migration applied before the rollback is authored; addressed by same-plan rollback authoring.
- Configuration (high): rollout tag set on the epic but read only on the story; addressed by the two-hop lookup.
- Configuration (high): sg present locally but absent in CI causing plan divergence; addressed by the persisted marker and sprint consuming (not recomputing) it.
- Assumption (high): detection pattern reused as the sweep pattern; addressed by the explicit transform descriptor.

- Recorded for implementation planning: recipe-engine version mismatch (silent no-op sweep), LLM-fallback non-determinism across parallel sweep agents, missing lock-timeout guard for production schema migrations, and call-site-threshold false-positives on large non-repetitive stories.

- /dso:implementation-plan skill — shared with 9ddd-117b, ab57-b534, 4001-7ad3, f7d5-59e4, dfa1-f9fd, 853a-c719, 94ed-f55c, c206-5acb, d63f-2c74, a8e8-0b23. Constraint: coordinate task-emission ordering, marker/comment namespaces, and authorship of the skill edits.

- Recipe system / translate-recipe-to-llm-task.sh — shared with c821-e995 (security recipes). Constraint: coordinate recipe registration/selection schema when multiple recipe-driven task types coexist.

- ast-grep / command resolution — shared with 986e-91c5 (fail-loud command policy), cf7b-86a9 (CI portability), w21-bsnz (remediation engine). Constraint: align the sg-absent degradation path with the command-resolution none sentinel.
- /dso:sprint ordering — shared with 0cf2-42b5, dso-8l5h, dso-94ya, e884-d0ad, 9679-695c. Constraint: preserve depends_on insertion points.
- Ticket CLI — shared with 1de7-50d4 (--reason to --resolution), 7510-0198 (--parent enforcement), 2007-26e6 (ID display). Constraint: emitted tasks must adopt current flags/format.
## Research Findings

- Migration or compatibility (completeness): re-run the same detection query post-sweep and assert empty; expect ~5% of sites to resist automation and mark them with TODO comments for the verifier. Sources: martinfowler.com/articles/codemods-api-refactoring.html; webflow.com/blog/codemods-and-large-scale-refactors-at-webflow. Shaped the SC2 verification definition.

- Migration or compatibility (rollback): down-migrations are dangerous for destructive changes — classify safe-revert vs compensating-forward; prefer expand-contract for multi-deploy. Sources: atlasgo.io/blog/2024/11/14/the-hard-truth-about-gitops-and-db-rollbacks; docs.gitlab.com/development/migration_style_guide. Shaped SC3.

content.text: ### 1. Technical Environment
* **code_version:** see git log
### 2. Incident Overview
* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior
#### Expected Behavior

Per the named-agent dispatch pattern documented in skills/sprint/SKILL.md and the using-dso memory: the orchestrator dispatches a named DSO agent (e.g., subagent_type: \"dso:story-decomposer\") directly. The fallback path (read agent file → pass content verbatim as prompt to a general-purpose agent) is triggered ONLY after a dispatch returns an \"Unknown agent\" error. The agent file must NOT be read prior to the dispatch attempt.
#### Actual Behavior

During /dso:sprint 3a03-b3f2-b34c-4e4f, before dispatching dso:story-decomposer, the orchestrator ran a Read tool call on agents/story-decomposer.md to build a fallback inline prompt — anticipating that the named dispatch might fail. This inverts the correct pattern.

Root cause (confirmed by orchestrator self-report): defensive over-preparation. The orchestrator prepared the fallback path before even attempting the primary dispatch, reasoning that the agent file might be needed if the named type was unrecognized. This is incorrect: the fallback path exists exclusively as recovery after failure, not as a preparation step.
**Consequences:**
1. Tokens wasted reading the agent file into orchestrator context on every dispatch, even when the named type succeeds.
2. Agent internals (prompt text) leaked into the orchestrator's context window, increasing compaction pressure.
3. Pattern is subtly wrong — the orchestrator is building infrastructure for a failure that hasn't happened yet.
#### Reproduction
1. Observe orchestrator dispatching any dso:* named agent during a sprint or preplanning run.
2. Check whether a Read tool call on the agent file appears BEFORE the Agent tool call.
3. If yes: bug is present.
### 3. Action History
* User caught the behavior mid-sprint and asked \"Why are you reading the agent prompts instead of dispatching the named agent?\"
* Orchestrator self-reported the root cause and corrected immediately.
* User requested a bug ticket so the pattern is documented and preventable.
### 5. Skills and Workflows
Affects: /dso:sprint (Phase E dispatch), /dso:preplanning (story decomposer, red-team, blue-team dispatch), any skill that dispatches named dso:* agents.

Fix: Add explicit rule to sprint SKILL.md and preplanning SKILL.md: \"Never read a named agent file before dispatch. Dispatch subagent_type: 'dso:<agent-name>' directly. Only fall back to reading the file if dispatch returns 'Unknown agent' error.\"

## Description
**What**: A shared shell script (confluence-fetch.sh) that handles URL fetching with Confluence authentication, file-based caching, and config-driven reference URL management.

**Why**: All subsequent integration stories (researcher sub-agent and citation injection) depend on a single, tested fetch-and-cache layer. Centralizing auth and cache logic prevents duplication and makes credential handling reviewable in one place.
**Scope**:

- IN: confluence-fetch.sh — fetches a given URL; detects whether it is a Confluence URL by exact domain match against confluence.base_url in dso-config.conf; uses CONFLUENCE_EMAIL+CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN env vars for Basic Auth on Confluence URLs; public URLs fetched without auth

- IN: Tiny Confluence link resolution — URLs matching /wiki/x/<base64> followed via `curl --location-trusted=false -L` (strips Authorization header on redirect to non-base_url domains) before page ID extraction

- IN: /tmp/dso-ref-cache/ directory with 1-hour mtime-based TTL; cached files stored with 0600 permissions; cache hit emits "[cache hit: <url>]" to stderr without making a network request; concurrent writes serialized via flock
- IN: Missing CONFLUENCE_EMAIL or CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN — Confluence URLs skipped with stderr warning; public URLs continue unaffected
- IN: Domain guard FAILS CLOSED — unset confluence.base_url rejects all Confluence-authenticated URLs (never all-accept); trailing-slash base_url normalized before domain comparison
- IN: Startup credential-placement check — rejects CONFLUENCE_EMAIL or CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN found in dso-config.conf with a security warning (credentials MUST be env vars)
- IN: dso-config.conf config keys: confluence.base_url, confluence.reference.url, confluence.reference.tags (per-URL; multiple entries supported)
- OUT: CQL search, citation injection, roadmap integration (those are separate stories)
## Done Definitions
- When this story is complete, confluence-fetch.sh fetches any URL passed to it; Confluence-domain URLs use Basic Auth via CONFLUENCE_EMAIL+CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN; public URLs require no credentials
← Satisfies: "Reference documents (Confluence-authenticated and public URLs) are fetched and stored in /tmp/dso-ref-cache/ with a 1-hour mtime-based TTL"

- When this story is complete, fetched content is cached in /tmp/dso-ref-cache/ with 0600 permissions; a second call within the 1-hour TTL window serves from disk and emits "[cache hit: <url>]" to stderr without a network request; concurrent writes to the same cache file are serialized via flock
← Satisfies: "Repeated calls within the cache window serve content from disk and emit a '[cache hit: <url>]' message to stderr without making any network request"
- When this story is complete, missing CONFLUENCE_EMAIL or CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN causes Confluence URLs to be skipped with a stderr warning; all other processing continues uninterrupted
← Satisfies: "When CONFLUENCE_EMAIL or CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN is not configured, Confluence-authenticated URLs are skipped with a stderr warning"

- When this story is complete, the domain guard FAILS CLOSED: unset confluence.base_url causes confluence-fetch.sh to reject all Confluence-authenticated URLs (never all-accept fallback); trailing-slash base_url is normalized at config read so domain comparison matches URLs without trailing slash
← Satisfies: SC6 (domain guard FAIL CLOSED behavior for unset base_url and trailing-slash normalization)

- When this story is complete, tiny Confluence links (/wiki/x/<base64>) are resolved by following `curl --location-trusted=false -L` redirects; Authorization header is stripped on any redirect to a non-base_url domain to prevent credential exfiltration via attacker-controlled tiny-link redirects
← Satisfies: SC6 (tiny-link handling with off-domain redirect protection)

- When this story is complete, startup credential-placement check rejects CONFLUENCE_EMAIL or CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN found in dso-config.conf with a clear security warning directing users to use environment variables; the script aborts with non-zero exit rather than proceeding with compromised credentials
← Satisfies: SC3 (credentials MUST be env vars; startup rejection on dso-config.conf placement)

- When this story is complete, reference URL list and per-URL topic tags are parseable from dso-config.conf (confluence.reference.url / confluence.reference.tags key pairs) without modifying plugin code
← Satisfies: "The reference URL list is configurable in dso-config.conf with per-URL topic tags; adding a new reference requires only a config change with no modification to plugin code"

- When this story is complete, unit tests are written and passing for all new or modified logic, including (i) unset base_url rejection, (ii) trailing-slash base_url normalization, (iii) off-base_url redirect during tiny-link resolution stripping Authorization, (iv) credential-in-dso-config.conf startup rejection
## Considerations

- [Security] curl error output may expose CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN in stderr — use --stderr /dev/null or token masking before the curl invocation to prevent token leakage in CI logs and session transcripts
- [Security] Domain guard FAILS CLOSED: unset confluence.base_url rejects all Confluence URLs (never all-accept) — prevents credential exfiltration when base_url is missing and credentials are set
- [Security] `curl --location-trusted=false -L` ensures Authorization header is stripped on off-domain redirects during tiny-link resolution
- [Reliability] /tmp write access unavailable on hardened CI runners — this is a known limitation; DSO_REF_CACHE_DIR override is out of scope for this story; document in KNOWN-ISSUES.md (Story F)

- [Reliability] Concurrent calls to confluence-fetch.sh may produce partially-written cache files — implement file locking (flock) or atomic write-to-temp-then-rename to prevent cache corruption under concurrent implementation-plan sessions
- [Maintainability] all URL fetching in dso:confluence-researcher and ref-library-loader.sh must call through confluence-fetch.sh — do not duplicate auth logic in either consumer

- [Integration] Verified: Basic Auth via curl -u email:token is confirmed working for Confluence Cloud REST API (atlassian-python-api, aashari/mcp-server-atlassian-confluence, coulibal/Confluence-Rest-API)
## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

- [Correctness] Match-none prevents 12-budget exhaustion on untagged URL references spamming every task
- [Security] Substring match must not allow regex injection — input is treated as literal substring

## Context

After Epics A1, A2, and B add the new ticket CLI subcommands and the FILE_IMPACT event type, four scripts still access .tickets-tracker/ directly and 290+ references across skills, workflows, agents, and CLAUDE.md still point to old script names or describe direct .tickets-tracker/ access patterns. Without enforcement, the boundary will erode as new scripts are written — a DSO plugin contributor who writes a new script has no guardrail today; they copy sprint-next-batch.sh patterns and inadvertently bypass the ticket API, creating audit and testability gaps. This epic gives that contributor a fast-fail pre-commit hook with an actionable error and a CLI replacement, so the correct path is also the easy path.
## Success Criteria

- Four scripts that currently access .tickets-tracker/ directly are refactored to use ticket CLI subcommands: sprint-next-batch.sh calls ticket next-batch (preserving full flag surface — flags, output format, and exit codes are identical so callers require no update); sprint-list-epics.sh calls ticket list-epics; purge-non-project-tickets.sh calls ticket purge-bridge; pre-commit-ticket-gate.sh calls ticket exists. All subprocess calls use the ticket dispatcher shim (.claude/scripts/dso ticket <subcommand>), consistent with check-shim-refs.sh enforcement. Each refactored script passes its existing test suite with no behavioral regression. Scripts that become thin wrappers retain their filename for shim compatibility and are added to the boundary hook allowlist with a comment citing this epic.

- A check-tickets-boundary.sh pre-commit hook is added to .pre-commit-config.yaml that exits non-zero when any staged non-ticket-system file contains: (a) a direct .tickets-tracker/ reference for ticket data access, or (b) a reference to an absorbed script by its original filename. The hook's closed allowlist contains exactly: ticket-system scripts (plugins/dso/scripts/ticket-*), .suggestions/ accessors (suggestion-record.sh, retro-gather.sh), .review-events/ accessors (emit-review-event.sh, review-stats.sh), exclusion-pattern scripts (capture-review-diff.sh, skip-review-check.sh, compute-diff-hash.sh), thin wrapper scripts from SC1, and legitimate structural documentation (files under plugins/dso/docs/ that describe the directory layout rather than access it — path-scoped exclusion). Adding to the allowlist requires a comment citing the tracking ticket.

- test-check-tickets-boundary.sh validates the hook with at minimum: (1) a synthetic violator exits non-zero with an actionable error naming the disallowed reference and the CLI replacement; (2) a staged change to each allowlist member (compute-diff-hash.sh, emit-review-event.sh, suggestion-record.sh, retro-gather.sh, capture-review-diff.sh, skip-review-check.sh) passes with exit 0, confirming the allowlist is not over-broad.
## Dependencies
- Epic A1 (2c28-e5b9 — Core Query Layer): mandatory — next-batch, list-descendants, list-epics, exists must exist before callers can be migrated and the boundary hook can enforce
- Epic A2 (4931-f639 — Validation & Classification Layer): mandatory — validate, classify, etc. must exist before the doc sweep can reference them
- Epic B (86c8-2d40 — File Impact): partial — file impact document references benefit from the sweep, but can be documented as "see Epic B" if B is not yet complete
## Approach

Three parallelizable work streams: (1) four refactor stories (independent of each other), (2) boundary hook + test, (3) document sweep. Stream 3 is gated on stream 2 reaching a stable hook definition, not on stream 1 completing. The boundary hook follows the check-plugin-self-ref.sh pattern: scan staged file content via git diff --cached, match against disallowed patterns, check against the closed allowlist. Downstream consumer map: sprint/SKILL.md (12 sprint-next-batch.sh call sites), debug-everything/prompts/batch-conflict-matrix.md (2 references with shim-exempt annotations — update to ticket next-batch), preplanning/SKILL.md (sprint-list-epics.sh reference), brainstorm/SKILL.md (sprint-list-epics.sh --max-children=0 call). Atomic-merge orchestration: land hook first, then B-E refactors + F doc sweep on a shared integration branch + single squash-merge to prevent live-session regressions.
## Research Findings

- Existing boundary pattern: `check-plugin-self-ref.sh` establishes the grep-based pre-commit boundary hook pattern (scan staged file content via git diff --cached; match disallowed patterns; check closed allowlist) — `check-tickets-boundary.sh` copies this pattern with a different allowlist

- Closed allowlist format: explicit enumeration file (distinct name from `review-gate-allowlist.conf` to avoid collision); each allowlist entry comment cites a tracking ticket for future audit; allowlist additions follow existing `plugin-boundary-allowlist.conf` convention
- Shim enforcement: `check-shim-refs.sh` enforces `.claude/scripts/dso <script>` invocation; refactored scripts must use this shim pattern when calling `ticket <subcommand>`

- 3-layer enforcement model: (a) pre-commit hook (this epic), (b) existing tool-use review-gate PreToolUse, (c) runtime shim enforcement — documented together in hook definition so contributors understand the whole picture
- Script count audit: 4 scripts access .tickets-tracker/ directly (confirmed by grep); 290+ doc references (confirmed via grep across skills/workflows/agents/CLAUDE.md)
## Scenario Analysis

- Doc sweep ships separately from refactors → live session invokes old script name → skill fails (high, deployment): atomic-merge orchestration requirement — all 3 streams ship in same commit batch via shared integration branch + single squash-merge; documented in SC3

- Allowlist too narrow rejects legitimate new ticket-system script (medium, friction): allowlist member addition requires ticket citation in the file's entry comment; documented escape valve; pattern matches existing plugin-boundary-allowlist.conf convention

- Allowlist too broad permits future .tickets-tracker/ access drift (medium, design): path-scoped exclusions (e.g., plugins/dso/docs/ files that describe the layout rather than access it) + exact script-name matches prevent glob-expansion drift
- Refactored thin wrapper drops a flag (high, correctness): each refactor story's done-def requires existing test suite to pass without modification + preserved flag enumeration documented in SC1

- Pre-commit hook takes too long on large diffs (medium, performance): grep-based scan on staged files only (not full repo); performance budget tracked against existing check-plugin-self-ref.sh baseline

- TICKET_TRACKER_OVERRIDE / CONF_OVERRIDE env vars break under thin wrapper (high, testing): `ticket exists` subcommand must honor these env vars; dceb-2566 story done-def explicitly tests env-var pass-through to injected tracker
- Purge-bridge introduces network dependency via thin wrapper (medium, regression): purge-bridge subcommand is LOCAL-ONLY by design; story d2c4-5515 done-def explicitly forbids network deps
### Planning Intelligence Log
- **Web research (Step 2.6)**: not triggered — bright-line none (boundary enforcement is internal pattern extension of check-plugin-self-ref.sh; no external integration)
- **Scenario analysis (Step 2.75)**: triggered
- Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 7
- **Practitioner-requested additional cycles**: none
- **Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0)**: not triggered
- **Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5)**: not triggered

- **LLM-instruction signal (Step 5)**: triggered — keyword: skill file modifications + hook behavioral logic (doc sweep across skills/workflows/agents/CLAUDE.md; new check-tickets-boundary.sh hook; ~290 reference updates)
- **Scale context (Step 0)**: small scale (default) — per-commit boundary check + bounded ~290 doc references; not volume-sensitive
## Closure Checks

- All document references in skills, workflows, agent definitions, and CLAUDE.md are updated: references to absorbed scripts use the new ticket <subcommand> syntax; references to direct .tickets-tracker/ access for ticket data are replaced with ticket CLI equivalents. No backward-compatibility shims. The document sweep ships in the same commit batch as the SC1 script refactors to prevent live session regressions in skills that invoke old script names directly. Verified by check-tickets-boundary.sh passing in CI with zero violations.

content.text: Create tests/scripts/test-analyze-test-gate-log.sh with RED tests for phantom mapping detection (SC2).
## Test Cases
- test_detects_phantom_python: audit log has source=foo.py method=fuzzy test=test_foo.py, but test_foo.py contains no import of foo — flagged as phantom
- test_passes_real_mapping_python: test_foo.py imports foo → not flagged
- test_detects_phantom_bash: test-bar.sh contains no source/call to bar.sh — flagged
- test_passes_real_mapping_bash: test-bar.sh sources bar.sh → not flagged
- test_empty_log_no_output: empty audit log → exit 0, no phantoms
- test_handles_renamed_files: log entry references deleted file → skipped (not flagged as phantom)
## Test Approach
Each test creates temp audit log fixtures and temp source/test files with controlled import relationships, then runs analyze-test-gate-log.sh and asserts exit code and stdout phantom reports.

**Out of scope.** New stacks/runners; architecture changes to the implementation-plan pipeline itself.

Add provenance tracking so every code change can be attributed to the skill, agent, and task that produced it.
## Reference: antigravity-awesome-skills Source Attribution

antigravity-awesome-skills (30k stars) maintains a source attribution ledger that tracks the origin of every skill: self (maintainer-authored), community (contributor PR), or upstream repo. This provenance tracking enables accountability across 1,340+ skills from many contributors.
DSO should apply the same principle at the code change level — not just tracking which skill exists, but which skill/agent/task produced each line of code in the host project.
## Problem
When a bug is discovered in code written by a sub-agent, there is no fast way to determine:
- Which skill orchestrated the work (sprint, fix-bug, debug-everything)
- Which sub-agent wrote the code (model tier, agent type)
- Which task ticket the code was implementing
- What checkpoint state the agent was in when it wrote the code
- Whether the code passed review, and what the review scores were

This information exists in git history and ticket comments but is scattered and expensive to reconstruct. A bug in a function requires searching git blame → commit message → ticket ID → ticket comments → checkpoint notes → review findings — across multiple systems.
## What to Track
For each commit produced by DSO workflows:
### In the Commit Message (Structured Trailer)
feat(auth): add login endpoint
Implements POST /api/auth/login with JWT token generation.
DSO-Skill: sprint
DSO-Agent: dso:code-reviewer-standard
DSO-Task: task-abc-1234
DSO-Story: story-def-5678
DSO-Epic: epic-ghi-9012
DSO-Model: sonnet
DSO-Review-Score: 4.2/5
### In the Telemetry Log (Detailed)
- Full agent dispatch context (prompt size, model, duration)
- Checkpoint progression (which checkpoints completed)
- Review findings summary (dimensions, scores, resolution attempts)
- Files read before editing (read_first compliance)
- Token usage for this task
## Integration Points
1. **Commit workflow** — automatically append DSO trailers to commit messages based on the active task/story/epic context
2. **Git blame enrichment** — a /dso:blame command that reads git blame + DSO trailers to show skill/agent/task attribution per line
3. **Bug investigation** — fix-bug should query DSO trailers on the blamed commit to understand the context in which the buggy code was written (which model, which review score, which skill)
4. **Retro analytics** — aggregate attribution data to identify which skills/agents/models produce the most bugs, highest review scores, or most rework
5. **Review context** — when reviewing code, the reviewer agent can see what produced the code under review (was it a haiku sub-agent? an opus architectural decision?)
## Design Considerations
- Trailers are git-native (recognized by git interpret-trailers) and don't pollute the human-readable commit message
- Keep trailers lightweight — IDs and scores only, not full descriptions
- Telemetry log has the detailed data; trailers are the index
- Must not break existing commit message conventions or Conventional Commits format
- Attribution should be opt-in via dso-config.conf (attribution.enabled=true) for projects that want it

## Reference Content Format Standard

Epic 0b7c-d811 (Embedded UI/UX Design Knowledge Base) establishes the canonical file format for static reference content stored within the DSO project. Any reference material fetched and cached by this epic's confluence-fetch.sh / ref-library-loader.sh infrastructure should conform to this format when persisted to disk as a reusable corpus entry.

**Format**: Markdown files with YAML frontmatter
**Schema** (per entry):
```yaml
---
id: <kebab-case-unique-id>
title: <human-readable title>
domain: [<domain-tags>]          # e.g., accessibility, navigation, forms
component: [<component-tags>]    # e.g., button, modal, data-table
action: [<action-tags>]          # e.g., validate, animate, focus-manage
compliance: [<compliance-tags>]  # e.g., wcag-2.2-aaa, section-508
severity: <critical|high|medium|low>
story_type: [<types>]            # e.g., feature, accessibility, ux
coverage: <sentence summary>
source: <URL or citation>
license: <license identifier>
---
### Summary
<~2-sentence brainstorm-level synopsis>

### Detail
<Full guidance for preplanning and design review>

### Implementation
<Concrete implementation checklist for sprint agents>
```

## Context

DSO agents running brainstorm and roadmap sessions operate without access to institutional knowledge in Confluence (architectural decisions, API contracts, compliance requirements, domain guides). Implementation plans cite generic guidance and miss org-specific constraints. This epic adds the Confluence integration foundation: a shared `confluence-fetch.sh` script with authenticated URL fetching and file-based caching, a `dso:confluence-researcher` sub-agent that surfaces CQL-derived search results during brainstorm Phase 1 and (opt-in) roadmap exploration, and the config schema for reference URL sources. Implementation-plan citation annotation and local-first corpus merging are delivered by a follow-on epic that consumes this epic's fetch infrastructure.

**Boundary with other reference-library epics**: Epic 0b7c-d811 (UI/UX design knowledge base) operates on a distinct static, shipped-with-plugin corpus at `plugins/dso/data/ui-reference/` retrieved via `dso ref-query` — it does not share `confluence-fetch.sh` or `/tmp/dso-ref-cache/` with this epic. The two systems serve different contracts (curated vs. dynamic org-specific). Epic e82e-3888 (live security API client) is unrelated — it targets vulnerability API integration, not reference document fetching.
## Success Criteria

- When /dso:brainstorm reaches the end of its Phase 1 understanding loop, a dso:confluence-researcher sub-agent is dispatched with the accumulated feature understanding as context; it derives CQL keywords automatically, searches all accessible Confluence spaces, and returns the top 5 most relevant page summaries ranked by Confluence's native CQL relevance score (configurable via `confluence.max_results` in dso-config.conf) — without the user providing any URLs.

- Reference documents (Confluence-authenticated and public URLs) are fetched via `confluence-fetch.sh` and stored in `/tmp/dso-ref-cache/` with a 1-hour mtime-based TTL and 0600 file permissions; repeated calls within the cache window serve content from disk and emit a `[cache hit: <url>]` message to stderr without making any network request; concurrent writes to the same cache file are serialized via `flock`.

- When CONFLUENCE_EMAIL or CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN environment variables are not configured, Confluence-authenticated URLs are skipped with a stderr warning and all other workflow steps continue uninterrupted. Credentials MUST be sourced from environment variables ONLY; credential detection at startup rejects credentials found in dso-config.conf with a security warning.

- When `confluence.roadmap_research_enabled=true` in dso-config.conf, /dso:roadmap dispatches dso:confluence-researcher at the start of its exploration phase using the roadmap theme as context; when the flag is absent or false, the step is skipped silently. Default: false (opt-in).

- When the CQL search returns zero results, the agent emits `[confluence-research: no results for query: <keywords>]`; when Confluence returns HTTP 400 (malformed query), the agent emits `[confluence-research: invalid query: <keywords>, error: 400]`; the session continues in both cases.

- confluence-fetch.sh domain guard FAILS CLOSED: unset `confluence.base_url` rejects all Confluence-authenticated URLs; trailing-slash base_url is normalized; tiny-link resolution via `curl --location-trusted=false -L` strips Authorization header on redirect to non-base_url domains. Integration test asserts the domain guard behavior for (i) unset base_url, (ii) trailing slash, (iii) off-base_url redirect during tiny-link resolution.

- An integration test suite at tests/integration/test-confluence-integration.sh validates using a local HTTP stub fixture on a dynamically-allocated port (no live Confluence required): (a) the researcher returns at least 1 of top 3 summaries containing a keyword from the seed topic; (b) confluence-fetch.sh serves cached content without network requests and emits `[cache hit: <url>]` to stderr for files within the 1-hour TTL; (c) credential-in-dso-config.conf placement triggers a startup rejection; (d) trailing-slash and missing base_url cases produce explicit error messages.
## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation, 2026-05-18)
### Self-use SC (Probe-1 remediation)

The e471 sprint exercises the dso:confluence-researcher sub-agent + brainstorm/roadmap Confluence integration on real content during sprint execution. At least one brainstorm or roadmap invocation during the sprint dispatches the confluence-researcher and ingests real (or fixture) Confluence content; the resulting planning artifact contains a citation to that Confluence page.
Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):
- Sprint transcript shows at least one Agent invocation of `dso:confluence-researcher` during a brainstorm or roadmap run.
- The produced planning artifact contains a citation to a Confluence URL OR ingested content blob; `grep -nE 'confluence\.|atlassian\.net/wiki' <planning-artifact>` returns ≥1.
- If real Confluence is unavailable, a fixture Confluence response (`tests/fixtures/confluence/`) is used and the same verification applies against the fixture URL.
### External-dependency verification (Probe-6 remediation)
Before Phase I:
| Resource | In-session verification | Expected |
| Confluence host reachable | `curl -sf -H "Authorization: Basic $(printf "$CONFLUENCE_EMAIL:$CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN" \| base64)" "$CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL/rest/api/space"` | 200 + JSON |
| `CONFLUENCE_EMAIL` env present | `test -n "$CONFLUENCE_EMAIL"` | Returns 0 |
| `CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN` env present | `test -n "$CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN"` | Returns 0 |
| Token has read scope | `curl -sf $CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL/rest/api/content/<known-page-id> -H "Authorization: Basic ..."` | 200 (read scope present) |

| Fixture fallback works | Synthetic test: unset CONFLUENCE_* env; verify confluence-researcher uses the `tests/fixtures/confluence/` fallback and emits an explicit "fixture-mode" notice | Test pass before sprint close |
Converts the audit's prose-only Confluence dependency into structured in-session checks with explicit fixture-fallback for sessions without live Confluence access.
## Dependencies
- ENV: Confluence Cloud or Data Center instance reachable from the agent's runtime — required for SCs 1, 2 (auth'd URLs only), 4, 5; other SCs function without Confluence (public URLs or no URLs).
- No blocking epic dependencies (purely additive).
- Follow-on coordination: "Implementation-plan citation annotation with local-first reference library merging" consumes `confluence-fetch.sh` infrastructure; that epic depends on this one.
- Future migration target: when `dso-soyt` (Incorporate Semantic Search & MCP) ships, the CQL sub-agent is adapted into an MCP tool — no blocking dependency.
## Approach

Single-phase sprint delivery. `confluence-fetch.sh` provides URL fetching, auth detection (exact-domain match against `confluence.base_url` with trailing-slash normalization; FAIL CLOSED on unset), Basic Auth via env vars, `curl --location-trusted=false -L` tiny-link resolution (strips Authorization on off-base_url redirect), 30s subprocess timeout, 1-hour mtime TTL cache at `/tmp/dso-ref-cache/` with 0600 perms and `flock` during writes. `dso:confluence-researcher` sub-agent derives CQL keywords from brainstorm/roadmap context, queries `/wiki/rest/api/search?cql=...`, returns top-5 page summaries. Sub-agent respects MAX_AGENTS cap from throttling; when credentials absent, dispatch is skipped entirely (not just fetch).
## Research Findings

Prior art for Confluence CQL integration is well-established: atlassian-api/atlassian-python-api (Python, cql() with _links.next pagination), aashari/mcp-server-atlassian-confluence (Node.js MCP server exposing CQL to AI systems — direct prior art for dso:confluence-researcher), sooperset/mcp-atlassian (Python MCP server), langchain-ai/langchain ConfluenceLoader (CQL with limit/max_pages/pagination), and coulibal/Confluence-Rest-API (bash curl approach). Hard 50-result CQL cap confirmed (atlassian-python-api issue #1127). Pagination via _links.next is required and tested across these implementations. Tiny-link resolution (curl -L redirect follow) is the correct approach per Atlassian community — but must strip Authorization on off-domain redirects via `--location-trusted=false` to prevent credential exfiltration.
## Scenario Analysis

- curl -L tiny-link resolution follows redirects to non-Confluence domains, bypassing domain guard (critical, runtime): Basic Auth credentials could be exfiltrated if curl sends Authorization headers across redirect chains; use `--location-trusted=false`.

- CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN stored in dso-config.conf instead of environment variable gets committed to git (critical, configuration): startup-time rejection required; pre-commit hook scan for credential patterns in dso-config.conf.

- Missing confluence.base_url config key causes confluence-fetch.sh to accept all domains, bypassing domain guard (critical, configuration): guard MUST fail closed — unset base_url rejects all Confluence URLs.
- dso ref-query subprocess hangs block entire ref-library-loader pipeline (high, runtime): 30s timeout with PID tracking (forwarded to follow-on epic).
- confluence.base_url set to URL with trailing slash causes exact-domain match to fail for all requests (high, configuration): trailing-slash normalization required at config read.
- First-run /tmp/dso-ref-cache/ creation fails in restricted CI environments (high, deployment): check mkdir exit code; fall back to configurable cache directory via `CACHE_DIR` env var.
- LLM relevance judgment called with 20-entry merged set exceeds context when excerpts are long (high, runtime): addressed in follow-on epic via 200-char truncation + concurrent-invocation cap 3.

- Dependency on 0b7c-d811 dso ref-query not enforced at install time, causing silent no-op (high, deployment): runtime `command -v dso ref-query` guard with stderr warning and URL-only fallback (follow-on epic).
- Cache directory race condition under concurrent sprint sub-agents (medium, runtime): `flock` around cache writes prevents truncated-read race.
- Merged result set silently drops corpus entries when URL fetch failures inflate the merge cap (medium, runtime): consistent budget accounting required (follow-on epic).
- CQL keyword auto-derivation produces empty or single-term queries that Confluence rejects with 400 (medium, runtime): distinct stderr signals for HTTP 400 vs. zero results.

- dso:confluence-researcher sub-agent dispatched in brainstorm Phase 1 before CONFLUENCE_EMAIL/CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN are documented in onboarding (medium, deployment): when credentials absent, dispatch is skipped entirely — not just fetch.
- Integration test HTTP stub fixture bound to a hardcoded port collides in parallel CI jobs (medium, deployment): dynamically-allocated port per test run.
- Cache files written during CI survive to subsequent runs via warmed /tmp, serving stale test fixtures (medium, deployment): tests use isolated CACHE_DIR override; CI pre-run cache cleanup.
- Two-variant citation format breaks downstream tooling that parses only the URL-sourced form (medium, configuration): documented in follow-on epic's consumer contract.
### Planning Intelligence Log
- **Web research (Step 2.6)**: triggered

- Bright-line conditions that fired: external integration (Confluence CQL API, atlassian-python-api, langchain ConfluenceLoader), security/authentication (Basic Auth with API token, credential handling, redirect-based credential exfiltration)
- **Scenario analysis (Step 2.75)**: triggered
- Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 15
- **Practitioner-requested additional cycles**: scenario analysis re-run 1 time (split from original e471-dda3 to focus on Phase 1 scope only)

- **Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0)**: triggered — depth: 0 (one follow-on epic created: "Implementation-plan citation annotation with local-first reference library merging"; full scrutiny pipeline ran on follow-on with right_sized 3→4 after YAGNI rationale)
- **Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5)**: not triggered
- **LLM-instruction signal (Step 5)**: triggered — keyword: agent definitions (new dso:confluence-researcher sub-agent; brainstorm/roadmap SKILL.md modifications)
- **Scale context (Step 0)**: small scale (default) — per-brainstorm/per-roadmap CQL query; not volume-sensitive
## Closure Checks

- dso-config.conf schema additions documented in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md: `confluence.base_url`, `confluence.max_results`, `confluence.roadmap_research_enabled`, multi-valued `confluence.reference.url` / `confluence.reference.tags` pairs. All keys additive; no changes to existing schema.

## What

Execute the phased rollout per epic 4047's plan, using Story 3's obligation tracking for the inherently validation-class DDs. Phase 0 (cap=0, no writes) → Phase 1 (5 passes, cap=10, 50 cumulative tickets) → Phase 2 (3 passes, cap=100, 350 cumulative) → Phase 3 (live-uncapped, scheduled cron resumed). At each phase advance, commit `.reconciler-phase-gate=<next-phase>` to the tickets branch.
## Why
The reconciler must be live-verified against the actual DIG Jira project (≈2,200 issues) before it can be considered functional. Each phase is a controlled-blast-radius experiment.
## Depends on
Stories 1, 2, and 3 of this epic MUST be merged to main BEFORE this story can start.
## Done Definitions (validation-class — each produces a Story-3 obligation ticket)

- **Phase 0 dispatch**: After committing `.reconciler-phase-gate=dry-run` to the tickets branch and dispatching workflow_dispatch `mode=dry-run`, `ticket list --tag=imported:reconciler-bootstrap` returns ZERO tickets AND the workflow run logs "OK: steady-state pass converged — N mutations" with N == differ-derived count (no apply). Tracked obligation: dispatch within 7 days of Stories 1+2 merge; closure evidence = manifest file path + ticket count = 0.

- **Phase 1 dispatch** (5 sub-obligations, one per pass): After committing `.reconciler-phase-gate=bootstrap-strict` and dispatching 5 sequential workflow_dispatch passes with `mode=bootstrap-strict`, the cumulative `ticket list --tag=imported:reconciler-bootstrap` count reaches exactly 50 (10 × 5). Per-pass asymmetric manifest contains the documented shape. Closure evidence per sub-obligation: pass URL + ticket-count delta + manifest path.

- **Phase 2 dispatch** (3 sub-obligations): After committing `.reconciler-phase-gate=bootstrap-throttle` and dispatching 3 passes with `mode=bootstrap-throttle`, cumulative count reaches exactly 350. 10% spot-check sample reviewed per pass (recorded as ticket comments). Closure evidence per sub-obligation: pass URL + spot-check review comment + manifest path.

- **Phase 3 enablement**: After committing `.reconciler-phase-gate=live` AND merging a PR that re-enables the scheduled cron in `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`, 5 consecutive cron-triggered passes each emit a manifest with ≤5 mutations (per epic 4047 SC10). Tracked obligation: monitor for 7 days post-enablement; closure evidence = 5 run URLs + per-run mutation counts.

- **Bridge-fsck label-only-orphan delta**: capture count BEFORE Phase 1 (expected 197) and AFTER Phase 2 (expected 0). Both counts recorded as comments on this story ticket. Closure evidence per side = stderr output of `bridge-fsck` invocation.

- **Round-trip idempotency per element class**: against throwaway DIG issues, exercise create/edit/delete for comments / labels (excluding dso-id) / links. For each operation: 3 consecutive passes produce exactly 1, 0, 0 mutations for that element. Evidence = pass-1/2/3 manifests for each operation. When an epic's deliverable IS the sprint or debug-everything orchestration architecture (CI workflows that fire during sprint, sprint Phase F changes, branch topology changes, merge-graph changes), brainstorm Step 2.x must ask: "Can this epic's sprint itself run on the architecture this epic delivers? The probe surfaces the central paradox of architectural epics: the sprint that builds the architecture is not bound by the architecture it builds, so the work can ship as a monolithic diff even when the deliverable is "per-story diffs."

## Context

After the bridge-cluster-202605 fix family (jade-cabin-tithe + pump-pup-lime + mud-karma-burst + 487d-ce11 + dc75-9b69 + fb8e-9022) lands, the bridge will be substantially more robust at NOT silently dropping events. But drift between local tickets and Jira will still accumulate over time when:
- Bridge runs partially succeed (BRIDGE_ALERT-tracked but not cursor-blocking once mud-karma-burst is fixed)
- Operators make direct Jira-side changes that don't go through the bridge
- External integrations (Linear, etc.) introduce indirect drift
The reconciliation done manually 2026-05-14/2026-05-15 (this session) ran:
1. `acli jira workitem search --jql 'project = DIG AND statusCategory != Done' --paginate --json`
2. Walk every event JSON on the `tickets` orphan branch to build local-id -> jira_key mapping
3. Compute set differences and field-mismatch lists
4. Surface drift classes (local-closed-jira-open, jira-open-no-local, field mismatches)
This worked but was a manual ad-hoc invocation. The drift is invisible until someone explicitly looks.
## Goal
Schedule the same reconciliation as a recurring CI check (daily or hourly) that:
1. Emits a structured BRIDGE_ALERT (or equivalent) whenever any drift class is non-empty
2. Posts a summary comment on a designated "bridge health" ticket so trends are visible
3. Categorizes drift by class:
- `local_closed_jira_open` (outbound STATUS failure pattern — was jade-cabin-tithe)
- `local_deleted_jira_open` (outbound DELETE failure pattern — surfaces mud-karma-burst-class failures)
- `jira_open_no_local` (inbound miss — was pump-pup-lime)
- `local_open_jira_closed` (this currently doesn't happen, but worth detecting)
- `field_mismatch` (title/type/status divergence on tickets open in both)
4. Provides a `--auto-fix` mode that auto-transitions safe classes (e.g., local-closed → Jira-Done) and offers a dry-run report for the rest
## Done Definitions
- When complete, a new GH Actions workflow runs the reconciliation on a cron schedule.
- When complete, drift counts are emitted as workflow output that operators can dashboard.
- When complete, non-zero drift triggers a notification on a tracked health ticket.
- When complete, the manual reconciliation done in this session is no longer needed for routine operations.
## Out of scope
- Fixing the bridge bugs themselves (covered by the cluster)
- Linear/external integration drift (separate concern)
- UI/dashboard work (workflow output and ticket comments are enough for v1)

## Evidence: 3-cycle non-converging llm-review loop on PR #89 (2026-05-11)

**Source session**: PR #89 in `navapbc/digital-service-orchestra` (this repo's own llm-review job, dogfooding). Head SHA `4a5d83088b` at escalation time.
**Diff under review**: ~350 LoC across 1 new bash script (pr-finalize-classify.sh), 1 new markdown doc (PR-FINALIZE-WORKFLOW.md), 1 SKILL.md edit (brainstorm), 1 commit pointer edit (merge-to-main-pr.sh).
**Result**: After 3 sequential push-and-review cycles applying the previous cycle's findings in good faith, the loop was halted by the `PR-FINALIZE-WORKFLOW.md` same-failure-3x rule. PR is open and unmerged at escalation.

### Per-cycle finding shape

**Cycle 1** — first review on initial diff. Mix:
- 1 critical: real shell-injection vulnerability (reviewer-supplied review-thread bodies shell-interpolated into a Python heredoc). Legitimate, fixed cleanly.
- 4 important: GraphQL input validation, fail-open error handling, unguarded JSON parsing, doc clarity. All legitimate; all fixed.
- 1 minor: completion-message API change framing. Defended without code edit.

**Cycle 2** — review of the cycle-1 fixes. Mix:
- 4 important: no test coverage for the new script; gh API contract not verified; PIL backend enforcement not visible in diff; branch precondition not enforced by classifier. Of these: test coverage is real-but-out-of-scope (filed as `ce4e-a135` P3 deferral); API contract and PIL enforcement are unverified-reference findings where the cited code does exist upstream of the diff (defended); branch precondition was legitimate, fixed.
- 2 minor: exit code semantics not documented; `/dso:resolve-conflicts` skill reference not verified. Verified to exist; exit code header added.

**Cycle 3** — review of cycle-2 fixes. New findings, NONE of which were present in cycles 1 or 2:
- 1 important: branch-precondition check (added in cycle 2) fail-opens when `git branch --show-current` errors or python json-parse fails, because the `[[ -n A && -n B && C ]]` short-circuits to true. Reachable only under simultaneous git corruption AND gh malformation, but a real defensive gap.
- 1 minor: thread-body truncation (600 chars) not documented in the workflow doc.

### Calibration signals visible in this session

1. **Non-convergence is the default behavior.** Each fix expands the diff with new prose/code; the reviewer evaluates the FULL diff each cycle and finds new surface in the new code. Without an explicit stopping rule (which the `PR-FINALIZE-WORKFLOW.md` same-failure-3x rule provides), the loop can continue indefinitely.

2. **Finding severity drifts down across cycles.** Cycle 1: 1 critical security + correctness foundation. Cycle 2: 4 important + 2 minor, mostly defensive and unverified-reference. Cycle 3: 1 important (narrow defensive) + 1 minor (doc gap). The severity-weighted value of each cycle decays sharply; the cost of one cycle (push, full CI re-run, full review, agent attention) does not.

3. **Severity inflation specifically observed**: at least 3 cycle-2 importants were really minors — "unverified API dependency" on `gh` JSON shapes is a maintainability concern, not an `important` correctness issue; "PIL backend enforcement not visible in diff" is a documentation completeness concern, not a correctness issue; "no test coverage" is a follow-on-work concern. All would have been more honestly graded as minor.

4. **Unverified-reference findings have an asymmetric cost.** The reviewer reports "I couldn't verify X exists" → the agent spends real cycles verifying X DOES exist → defense is logged but the next cycle re-discovers Y, Z, etc. The reviewer prompt could include a single instruction: "If you cannot verify a reference from the diff, mark the finding as `verification_needed` rather than `important` — do not block on it." That single change would have moved 4-5 of this session's findings out of the blocking severity bucket.

5. **Reviewer reasoning about its own fixes lacks recurrence-awareness.** Cycle 3's branch-precondition fail-open finding is reviewing the ADDITION from cycle 2 that addressed cycle 2's branch-precondition finding. The reviewer has no awareness that the line it's now critiquing exists BECAUSE of its own prior request — and that the previous version had no branch check at all. Treating new code added in response to review as evaluated identically to original code creates a structural "perfect-fix" expectation that human-authored code rarely meets.

### Suggested calibration adjustments (for brainstorm)

The cited counter-examples in this session, if added to a labeled corpus, would calibrate against the four patterns above:

- **Convergence floor**: after N cycles, automatically downgrade `important`-severity findings on diff-added-in-prior-cycles to `minor` unless they cite a NEW class of issue not seen in prior cycles. (Self-referential code is treated more leniently.)

- **Verification-needed severity**: when the reviewer cannot verify a reference from the diff alone, the finding becomes `verification_needed` (non-blocking) rather than `important`. Caller is responsible for the verification check.

- **Severity floor on documentation/maintainability**: any finding categorized as `maintainability`, `verification`, or `documentation` is capped at `minor` severity regardless of reviewer's first impulse.

- **Out-of-scope detection**: when a finding asks for test coverage of newly-added code that has no existing test scaffolding in the area, mark as `out_of_scope_for_pr` with severity `minor` and an automatic follow-on-ticket suggestion.

### Artifacts

- PR #89: https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/pull/89
- Defenses applied during cycles 2 and 3: see commit messages of `e0b3247a12` and `4a5d83088b`.
- Deferred follow-on: bug `ce4e-a135-70f6-4c1e` (test coverage for pr-finalize-classify.sh).
- Related bug for the design gap that triggered this PR: `9e06-e198-fb6f-4c39` (merge-to-main local-mode loop).

Filed as evidence for the labeled corpus this epic plans to build. The full per-cycle finding text is available in the GitHub Actions logs of PR #89's CI runs.

<!-- dso:reconciler-echo -->

F7b (cycle-over-cycle reviewer convergence) brainstormed 2026-05-12 — filed as two child stories under this umbrella:

- **1ef8-79c4-6195-4c98** (Story A, P1): Wire cited_lines through CI defense pipeline + proximity-matching suppression filter. Standalone, no upstream deps; replaces the description-prefix matcher in runner.py:369 with file+line proximity matching using the already-existing cited_lines schema field and ±5-line proximity rule (review-findings-schema.md:203).
- **0b1b-8177-db5e-4055** (Story B, P2, depends on A): Enforce relation+escape_rationale for cycle ≥ 2 NEW_INTRODUCED findings on unanchored files/lines. Defer-able if Story A telemetry shows 'new file in cycle ≥ 2' is rare.

**Empirical evidence driving the design** (PR #102 cycle 2 + PR #103 cycle 3 analyzed inline during brainstorm):
- ~70% of cycle ≥ 2 findings cite the same file as a cycle-1 finding, within ±5 lines. Several exact-line matches across both PRs.
- The actual cycle-2 DEFENSE_RECORDs posted by mirror-defenses-to-pr.sh on PR #103 contained only severity+description, no cited_lines — confirms the wiring gap is the primary failure mode, not LLM behavior alone.
- Cycle 2 also introduces findings on entirely new files (~30%); Story B addresses this case via the schema's already-designed relation taxonomy.

**Interaction with other RC-B work**:
- F6 (PR #106, merged) — orthogonal; reduces within-cycle severity inflation. Stacks cleanly.
- 677d-a6a0 (P0, in_progress, BLOCKING) — strengthens Story A when shipped (adds content-hash anchor via cited_excerpt). Story A intentionally does not depend on it.
- 4100-95a4 (verifier agent, P0) — loosely coupled. Verifier rulings could feed Story A's matcher as a secondary key but neither story depends on it.

**Story C deferred**: cited_excerpt content-hash anchor as a fortification on Story A. Should only be filed after 677d-a6a0 lands and CI begins emitting verified cited_excerpt content.

<!-- dso:reconciler-echo -->

## Additional decomposition inputs from RC-B gap analysis (2026-05-12)

Following the F7b brainstorm that filed stories 1ef8-79c4 (Story A) and 0b1b-8177 (Story B), three structural gaps in the convergence-failure problem space surfaced that aren't covered by either story and naturally belong under this umbrella for decomposition.

### Gap input 1: hard cap on review cycles

`review.max_resolution_attempts=3` caps resolution attempts per finding, not review cycles. Verified via grep: no `max_cycles` / `MAX_REVIEW_CYCLE` / `cycle.*limit` config or code anywhere under `plugins/dso/scripts`, `plugins/dso/docs`, `.claude/dso-config.conf`. `ci.yml` computes `DSO_REVIEW_CYCLE = PRIOR_CYCLES + 1` unboundedly.

Even with Story A (proximity matcher), Story B (relation enforcement), and Story C (cited_excerpt content-hash) all working, a PR with 1-2 genuine new findings per cycle never converges. PR #103 needed admin merge override after 3 cycles. There is no policy for 'at cycle K, defer remaining important-and-below to a follow-up ticket / escalate to user / hard-merge.' Suggested decomposition direction: a new `review.max_cycles` config knob (default 4) with a defer-to-follow-up-ticket fallthrough that creates a `review-followup` ticket containing the remaining unresolved findings and lets the current PR merge. Story-sized work under this epic.

### Gap input 2: zero-findings instruction missing from general reviewer prompts

Verified via grep: only `code-reviewer-security-red-team.md` carries an explicit 'zero findings is valid' instruction ('An empty findings array is a valid and expected output for most diffs. The quality of your review is measured by precision, not quantity.'). The generalist agents — `code-reviewer-light.md`, `code-reviewer-standard.md`, `code-reviewer-deep-correctness.md`, `code-reviewer-deep-hygiene.md`, `code-reviewer-deep-verification.md`, `code-reviewer-deep-arch.md` — do not carry this language. Without it, the model is implicitly incentivized to find something every cycle to 'earn its keep,' which is plausibly the structural cause of cycle-over-cycle drift that all of F7b is patching around. Suggested decomposition direction: a single small story to mirror the security-red-team instruction into `reviewer-base.md` and the generalist agent files. ~5 line edit per file. Cheapest available intervention on the convergence problem.

### Gap input 3: corpus / feedback-loop / model-regression test (this epic's description already mentions this)

The epic description already calls out 'tracking review outcomes per cycle, building a labeled corpus of past findings (true positive / false positive / severity-correct / inflated), tuning agent prompts and the rubric against that corpus, and adding a regression test that catches calibration drift.' Concrete decomposition inputs:

- **Telemetry already exists**: `classifier-telemetry.jsonl` (per `docs/contracts/classifier-telemetry.md`) and `review-gate-telemetry.jsonl` are append-only JSONL logs emitted on every review run. Per `classifier-telemetry.md:32`: 'Currently no automated consumer exists.' The gap is the consumer, not the producer.
- **Defense corpus already exists**: every PR with a non-trivial review writes `DEFENSE_RECORD` lines as PR comments via `mirror-defenses-to-pr.sh`. Mining these (severity + description + defense_text per defense) yields a labeled false-positive corpus 'for free' — each defense is a labeled 'this was a false positive or out-of-scope.' Adding cited_lines to the records (Story A) makes them keyable by code region.
- **Human escalation is also a label**: when `review.max_resolution_attempts` exhausts and escalates to the user, the escalation reason is a labeled 'this was either a true positive we couldn't fix or a false positive we couldn't defend.' Currently discarded.
- **Model-regression test corpus**: when Anthropic ships a new model or when prompts like F6 land, no automated test against a labeled-PR replay catches regression. Decomposition direction: assemble a fixture set from recent multi-cycle PRs (#100, #102, #103) with known true/false labels, run the reviewer prompt against each fixture diff after every prompt change, alert on regression.

Suggested decomposition: 2-3 stories — corpus assembly, telemetry consumer, regression test harness.

### Gaps already filed as separate stories (for reference)

- Story 1ef8-79c4 (P1): proximity matcher / Story A
- Story 0b1b-8177 (P2, depends on Story A): relation+escape_rationale / Story B
- Bug (filed alongside this comment) for cancel-in-progress cycle counting integrity — investigation-class, not decomposition material

### Gap routed elsewhere

- Defense-record tamper detection → commented on jira-dig-1673 (its namesake 'defense citations' makes it the natural home).
- Story A regression-masking design carve-out → commented on 1ef8-79c4.
- Story B review-side oscillation detection → commented on 0b1b-8177.

<!-- dso:reconciler-echo -->

UMBRELLA-COORDINATION (2026-05-13): F4 and F5 from the post-PR-#103 calibration analysis are now bundled and decomposed as epic 4100-95a4-07ce-41ab (sue-tribe-skid), tagged brainstorm:complete. F6 was shipped earlier in PR #106. F7b (cross-cycle convergence file+line fingerprint matcher) does not yet have its own epic — sue-tribe-skid will emit the fingerprint surface (per its SC10) so a future F7b epic has a stable matching anchor. Governance ADR docs/adr/0013-verifier-severity-authority.md (merged via PR #122) authorizes the verifier sub-agent's severity authority as a named exception to CLAUDE.md rule 11.

When this umbrella epic enters /dso:brainstorm, the open scope is approximately: (a) the fourth fix in the calibration bundle (F7b cross-cycle convergence) — currently no epic exists, candidate for either inclusion in this umbrella's decomposition or a sibling epic; (b) any further calibration work surfaced by post-shipment telemetry from sue-tribe-skid (verifier confirm/downgrade/drop counts, minor-finding-rate canary); (c) the verifier's interaction with the future Approach 4 minor-finding ticket gate (epic bb93-c474-d065-4d06, P1, depends_on sue-tribe-skid). Do NOT re-decompose F4+F5 (already done in sue-tribe-skid). Do NOT re-author the rule-11 exception (already in ADR 0013).

Follow-on bug filed during sue-tribe-skid brainstorm: e253-f62a-1527-4319 (jumpy-bolt-scythe, P2) — orchestrator owns cross-epic-scan setup pipeline; not blocking this brainstorm but may surface again at Step 2.25.

<!-- dso:reconciler-echo -->

## Research citation: Evidence-anchored severity (Rulers)

The umbrella's severity-calibration program implements the core contribution of "Rulers" (arxiv 2601.08654 — locked rubrics + evidence-anchored scoring with diff-span evidence per severity claim). The Rulers pattern is satisfied across three shipped/in-flight artifacts:
