Several bc7f-1a0d scenario-analysis survivors reference w21-bsnz shared infrastructure — recorded here for w21-bsnz implementation-plan consideration:
- Confidence YAML pattern_id collisions (risk of duplicate IDs or renamed threshold keys across w21-bsnz and bc7f-1a0d)

- T1 (assertion-less test): DETECTED on Python (AST 95%), JS/TS (ast-grep+grep 90%), Ruby (ast-grep+grep 90%)
- T3 (import-only file): DETECTED on Python (AST 99%), JS/TS (grep 95%), Ruby (grep 90%)
- C1 (unreachable branch): DETECTED on Python (AST 95%), JS/TS (grep 80%), Ruby (grep 75% — implicit returns complicate)
- C2 (unused variable): DETECTED on Python (AST 95%), JS/TS (grep 70%), Ruby (grep 65%)
- Jekyll: only docs patterns (D2, D4, D5) apply — confirmed bash-grep sufficient (90%)

SC3 VERDICT: ACHIEVABLE on all 4 stacks. No SC changes needed.

Key spike finding: Python AST module provides highest confidence across all patterns. The confidence mapping should include python-ast as an engine alongside semgrep/ast-grep/bash-grep. For Ruby, C1 confidence is lower due to implicit returns and guard clauses — implementation should consider routing Ruby C1 matches to blue-team rather than auto-remediation.

## Agent Definition Skeletons (created during brainstorm)

Two agent definition files were created during brainstorm with HARD-GATE behavioral constraints informed by bot-psychologist analysis and prior-art research across 17 open-source projects (Anthropic security review, GitHub Security Lab taskflows, SWE-agent, Sweep, PR-Agent, refactor-clean, and others).

### plugins/dso/agents/bloat-blue-team.md
Skeleton with 6 HARD-GATEs: confidence-blind (agent never sees static confidence scores — orchestrator retains them for routing/audit), asymmetric-error-policy (DISMISS when uncertain), needs-human-floor (80% definitive verdict rate), scope-anchoring (classify only the excerpt), confirm-requires-evidence (bloat_evidence field required for CONFIRM), plus a trusted-by-default enumeration (snapshot tests, env-gated flags, changelogs auto-DISMISS).

Input/output contracts defined. Pattern-specific guidance for P-T1, P-D3, P-C1 included with CONFIRM/DISMISS signals and common false-positive traps.

### plugins/dso/agents/bloat-resolver.md
Skeleton with 7 HARD-GATEs: finality-assumption (no mention of downstream review gate), cascade-check (search for callers before deletion), no-change-categorization (closed enum: CASCADE_RISK/INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT/PATTERN_UNCLEAR/STACK_UNCERTAINTY), green-baseline (verify tests pass before any deletion), dynamic-reference-check (search for import()/require()/string refs/decorator registration), self-review (re-read own patches — check imports, calls, re-exports, __all__, type annotations), scope-creep-prohibition (no refactoring while cleaning).

## Context

Developers running DSO on nava-platform projects experience friction from accumulated codebase bloat that prevention gates cannot address retroactively. Specifically: false test failures from change-detector tests slow CI and erode trust in the test suite; stale documentation sections generate noise in code review; and dead code (unreachable branches, unused variables) slows codebase comprehension for new contributors. This epic adds a /dso:remediate skill that safely prunes high-confidence bloat patterns and surfaces lower-confidence candidates through an opus blue-team filter before presenting them for human resolution. The observable improvement: after running /dso:remediate --all, the developer sees a structured summary of what was cleaned, flagged, or skipped — and the next CI run, code review, and onboarding session encounters less noise.

Pattern namespace: bright-line patterns use category prefixes (T, D, C) and are eligible for auto-remediation. Probabilistic patterns use the P- prefix (P-T1, P-D3, P-C1) and are always routed to the blue-team agent when in confidence range — never auto-remediated regardless of threshold.
## Success Criteria

SC1. A new skill /dso:remediate is added, invoked with one of four scoped flags: --tests, --docs, --code, or --all. Invocation without a flag prints usage and exits non-zero. A sub-agent guard runs at skill entry: if the Agent tool is unavailable, the skill returns an error message and exits without mutations. Before any mutation, the skill checks for staged changes (git diff --cached --quiet); if staged changes exist, it aborts with an error.

SC2. A static confidence mapping file (YAML) ships with the plugin at plugins/dso/config/remediate-confidence-map.yaml, declaring {pattern_id, engine} -> confidence_score for every pattern/engine combination. Each per-stack linter (ruff, eslint, rubocop) has its own engine entry. Two new dso-config.conf keys control routing: remediate.auto_threshold (default: 90) and remediate.blue_team_threshold (default: 60). At runtime, the skill detects installed engines via command -v, looks up the highest-confidence installed engine for each pattern, and routes: >= auto_threshold -> auto-remediate, >= blue_team_threshold -> route to blue-team agent, < blue_team_threshold -> skip with a note in the summary.
SC3. The skill detects and auto-remediates the following bright-line patterns when confidence meets the auto threshold:
- --tests: T1 (assertion-less test body — auto-delete the test function), T2 (exact-duplicate test — auto-delete the duplicate), T3 (import-only test file — auto-delete the file)

- --docs: D2 (broken internal links — annotate with TODO: fix or remove inline comment), D4 (duplicate headings — included in summary as flagged_for_review with file path), D5 (large unstructured file — included in summary as flagged_for_review with file path)

- --code: C1 (unreachable branch after unconditional return/raise/throw — auto-delete the dead block), C2 (unused local variable without suppression annotation — auto-delete), C3 (exact-duplicate function body — included in summary as flagged_for_review with both file paths)

For C2, auto-prune is suppressed if the line contains # noqa, # type: ignore, or # side-effect; such matches are flagged for human review instead. For C1 and C2, the skill delegates to per-stack linters when available, falling back to semgrep rules.

SC4. For probabilistic patterns where the best available engine's confidence falls between the two thresholds, the skill dispatches a dso:bloat-blue-team opus sub-agent. Engine selection follows the same rule as SC2: the highest-confidence installed engine determines the routing decision. The blue-team agent emits one of three verdicts per candidate: CONFIRM, DISMISS (with rationale), or NEEDS_HUMAN (with ambiguity note). DISMISS candidates are excluded from the user-facing report. CONFIRM and NEEDS_HUMAN candidates both proceed to SC5 resolution paths. NEEDS_HUMAN is counted as a distinct field in the SC6 summary. Probabilistic patterns: P-T1 (change-detector test), P-D3 (stale example referencing absent symbol), P-C1 (feature flag never toggled to true). If no installed engine covers a probabilistic pattern, it is skipped and recorded in skipped_pattern_ids.
SC5. After blue-team filtering, the skill presents the user with a choice of two resolution paths:

- Path A (manual): Displays a numbered list of CONFIRM and NEEDS_HUMAN candidates with file location, pattern ID, and blue-team note. User enters item numbers to remove (comma-separated), or presses Enter to skip all. Fixture tests simulate Path A by injecting a pre-set selection list via DSO_REMEDIATE_SELECT env var.

- Path B (auto-resolve): Dispatches a dso:bloat-resolver opus sub-agent that applies all CONFIRM candidates and emits NO_CHANGE: <reason> for any it declines. Changes from the resolver follow the normal commit workflow (COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md -> /dso:review), ensuring at least two independent agents review every change.

SC6. The skill emits a structured session-end summary written to $ARTIFACTS_DIR/remediate-summary-<timestamp>.json with schema: {"auto_remediated": 0, "blue_team_dismissed": 0, "blue_team_needs_human": 0, "skipped_below_threshold": 0, "skipped_pattern_ids": [], "flagged_for_review": 0, "user_resolved": 0, "resolver_applied": 0, "resolver_no_change": 0, "flags": ["--tests"]}

SC7. Validation is run against each nava-platform template (flask, nextjs, rails, jekyll-uswds) using synthetic test fixtures at tests/fixtures/remediate/<template>/. Each fixture includes a fixture-manifest.json declaring expected counts and file-level outcomes. Validation asserts: auto-remediated items -> target file/function absent and auto_remediated count matches; flagged items -> no mutation and flagged_for_review count matches; skipped items -> skipped_pattern_ids contains expected IDs. Each fixture also includes at least one valid-but-pattern-matching item (e.g., intentional golden-file test, changelog with duplicate headings) that must NOT be removed — the manifest declares these as expected_false_positive_safe and the test asserts they remain unmodified.
Out of scope: P-D4 (concept drift), P-D1 (orphaned sections), P-T2 (mock-heavy tests), P-C2 (redundant parameters). These are deferred to follow-on epic bc7f-1a0d.
## Scenario Analysis
- P-T1 golden-file false positives (critical): Intentional regression tests are structurally identical to change-detectors; the static confidence mapping cannot distinguish them by project context.
- P-C1 env-flag false positives (critical): Feature flags gated on environment variables are statically never true during analysis, matching every env-conditional flag.
- auto_threshold=0 bypass (critical): Setting threshold to 0 routes all matches to auto-prune, bypassing blue-team entirely.
- Unbounded resolver batch (important): 50+ auto-prune candidates in a single dispatch may exhaust agent context.
- Test coverage gap after deletion (important): Deleting the sole test covering a source file leaves an invisible coverage gap.
- Interrupted mid-batch state (important): No checkpoint/state file to resume from after SIGURG.
- Inverted thresholds dead zone (important): blue_team_threshold > auto_threshold creates undefined routing behavior.
- Missing config key (important): Absent threshold keys cause bash comparison failure and silent abort.
- Stack-detection mismatch (important): Monorepo stack detection may select wrong linter for confidence lookup.
## Prompt Alignment Findings
- Blue-team agent must form its verdict before consulting the engine confidence score to avoid anchoring
- Blue-team should default to DISMISS when uncertain — false CONFIRMs are amplified by the resolver; false DISMISSes are recoverable
- Resolver prompt must NOT mention the downstream review gate — prevents moral hazard
- Resolver must check for callers before deleting any function/class/export and emit NO_CHANGE with CASCADE_RISK when callers exist outside the candidate list
- Embed these as hard constraints in agent definition files during implementation
## Research Findings
### Code Bloat Remediation

- Polyglot Piranha (Uber, https://github.com/uber/piranha): Java/Kotlin/Swift/ObjC/JS/Go. Tree-sitter AST with cascading cleanup rules. Auto-remediates (210K lines deleted, 1611 PRs). Binary match/no-match — no confidence tiering. Excels at feature flag cascading cleanup.
- DCE-LLM (NAACL 2025, https://aclanthology.org/2025.naacl-long.501/): Hybrid CodeBERT triage + LLM judgment. 94%+ F1. Architecturally closest to our approach but requires fine-tuned models.
- Knip (https://github.com/webpro-nl/knip): JS/TS only. TypeScript type checker as ground truth. Highest-precision JS/TS dead code detector — candidate linter delegate for JS/TS stack.
- Semgrep autofix (https://semgrep.dev/docs/writing-rules/autofix): 20+ languages. Rule-based or LLM-assisted (https://choly.ca/post/semgrep-autofix-llm/). No native confidence tiering.
- Datadog: LLM false-positive filtering for static analysis (https://www.datadoghq.com/blog/using-llms-to-filter-out-false-positives/)
### Documentation Bloat Remediation
- lychee (https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee): Async Rust link checker. Fast, caching, .lycheeignore. Report only.
- markdownlint (https://github.com/DavidAnson/markdownlint): MD024 duplicate headings with siblings_only option (changelog-aware). Has auto-fix. More precise than bash-grep for D4.
- Doc Detective (https://github.com/doc-detective): Execution-based stale example detection (runs docs against live system). Complementary to LLM approach.
- Vale (https://github.com/errata-ai/vale): Prose style linter with YAML rules. Can approximate P-D3 with deprecated-term lists but brittle vs LLM approach.
### Test Bloat Remediation
- TSDetect (https://github.com/TestSmells/TSDetect): Java only. 20 test smells including assertion-less (Unknown Test). Report only.
- TestIQ (https://github.com/pydevtools/TestIQ): Python/pytest. Coverage-based duplicate detection. Higher FP rate than AST hashing.

- UTRefactor (FSE 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.16739): Java. LLM-based auto-refactoring of test smells (89% reduction). Closest to our blue-team filter but collapses detection and remediation into one pass.
- Mutation testing (PIT, mutmut): Ground truth for test redundancy but too slow for commit gates.
### Key Tradeoff Summary

No existing tool implements all three of our architectural pillars: per-pattern confidence mapping, tiered routing (auto/LLM/skip), and per-stack linter delegation. Implementation should consider: Knip as JS/TS linter delegate, markdownlint for D4 (siblings_only precision), Piranha's cascading pattern for resolver design.
## Dependencies

No blocking epic dependencies. The confidence mapping YAML (plugins/dso/config/remediate-confidence-map.yaml) is a deliverable artifact — its schema is a stable interface that follow-on epic bc7f-1a0d will consume. Two new dso-config.conf entries: remediate.auto_threshold, remediate.blue_team_threshold. Runtime tool availability handled by confidence mapping graceful degradation.
## Approach

Option A: Tiered Engine Selection. Ship a static confidence mapping YAML declaring {pattern_id, engine} -> confidence_score. At runtime, detect available engines via command -v, look up the highest-confidence available engine for each pattern, and route through three tiers using two global config thresholds. Detection engines: semgrep (declarative AST rules, polyglot), ast-grep (structural queries), bash-grep (textual fallback), plus delegation to per-stack linters (ruff, eslint, rubocop) where they already detect the pattern.
## Resolved Implementation Gaps
### Gap 1: Agent Contracts (resolved 2026-04-14)
**dso:bloat-blue-team input**: {candidates: [{candidate_id, pattern_id, file, line_range, excerpt, engine, confidence}]}
**dso:bloat-blue-team output**: {verdicts: [{candidate_id, verdict, rationale, rationale_basis}]}
- rationale required for DISMISS and NEEDS_HUMAN, optional for CONFIRM
- rationale_basis enum: excerpt_only | file_context | cross_file (required)
- Contract file: plugins/dso/docs/contracts/bloat-blue-team-payload.md
**dso:bloat-resolver input**: {confirmed_candidates: [{candidate_id, pattern_id, file, line_range, action}]}
- action enum: delete_function | delete_file | delete_block | annotate | flag
**dso:bloat-resolver output**: {applied: [{candidate_id, action_taken}], no_change: [{candidate_id, category, reason}]}
- no_change.category enum: CASCADE_RISK | INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT | PATTERN_UNCLEAR | STACK_UNCERTAINTY (required)
### Gap 2: Config Validation Behavior (resolved 2026-04-14)

Add to SC2: If either config key (remediate.auto_threshold, remediate.blue_team_threshold) is absent, non-numeric, or outside 1-100, log warning to stderr naming the invalid key and value, then use defaults (auto=90, blue_team=60) for the entire run. If blue_team_threshold >= auto_threshold after resolution, log warning (inverted thresholds) but proceed.
### Gap 3: Monorepo Multi-Stack Support (resolved 2026-04-14)

Add to SC2: At scan start, classify files in scope into language groups by extension. For each language group, select the highest-confidence installed engine. Extension-to-language mapping is a static lookup table shipped alongside the confidence mapping YAML. Unrecognized extensions scanned with bash-grep only.
### Gap 4: Prompt Engineering Constraints (resolved 2026-04-14)
Blue-team: form verdict before consulting confidence; default to DISMISS when uncertain; 80%+ definitive rate; declare rationale_basis.
Resolver: no mention of downstream review gate; check callers before deleting; categorize every NO_CHANGE.
### Gap 5: Feasibility Spike Results (resolved 2026-04-14)

SC3 ACHIEVABLE on all 4 stacks. Confidence ranges: Python python-ast 95, semgrep 85; JS/TS ast-grep 88; Ruby ast-grep 85; Markdown bash-grep 90. Ruby C1 lower confidence — consider routing to blue-team.

## Incident Overview
**Component:** plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/applier.py (_apply_batch drift detector)
**Condition:** Filtered reconciler pass with mixed inbound and outbound mutations on a fresh tickets-branch worktree
**Observed Result:** HeadDriftError raised mid-apply-loop even with d822 defer-bug-filing fix and try/finally remediation in place; bindings save() skipped, orphan Jira issues
## Reproduction
1. Run e2e_field_validation_probe.sh (DSO_FIELD_VALIDATION_PROBE=1)
2. Probe creates 10 local tickets, sets assignee on ticket 5, adds comment on ticket 8
3. Runs reconciler: `python -m dso_reconciler --mode bootstrap-throttle --filter-local-ids <ids>`
4. Reconciler fails with: `ERROR: reconcile_once raised: drift: 78392cd6→19da05f6`
5. All 10 bindings show 'unbound' afterwards; Jira issues DID get created (DIG-4711-4720) but bindings.json wasn't saved
## Expected Behavior

Filtered reconciler pass completes without drift error. The d822 fix (defer conflict bug-filing out of apply loop) was supposed to eliminate in-apply-loop commits to the tickets branch. PR #425 landed that fix, and the try/finally remediation ensures deferred filing runs even on exception paths.
## Actual Behavior
Drift still fires. Even though:
- d822 defer-fix is in main (PR #425 merged as commit 9cd7755888)
- Phase 1 of probe has zero inbound conflicts (all 10 mutations are outbound creates)
- _file_conflict_bug_ticket is NOT in the apply path for outbound creates
- The probe Phase 1 reconciler still hits drift
This means a DIFFERENT commit source exists during `_apply_batch` execution that we haven't identified yet.
## Suspected Root Causes

H1: `create_one` (applier.py:1462) writes identity markers via `client.add_label(jira_key, dso-id:local_id)` and `client.set_entity_property(jira_key, dso_local_id, local_id)`. These are Jira API calls, but if any retry or fallback path commits to the tickets branch, that would explain drift.

H2: The reconciler's legacy snapshot differ emits inbound_create mutations alongside the outbound_creates (because the Jira snapshot has issues that the differ thinks need local creation). `_apply_typed` dispatches inbound_create which calls `_write_event_file` to create local jira-* tickets. _write_event_file writes to .tickets-tracker/ filesystem but does NOT commit. So this shouldn't cause drift unless something else triggers a commit.
H3: The reconciler may be calling `acquire_pass_lock` or similar mid-pass. acquire_pass_lock commits to the tickets branch. If it's called inside apply()... unlikely but possible.
H4: There's a deferred-write or background-sync mechanism (binding_store.save? mapping.json write?) that commits during the pass.
H5: A git hook (post-write, post-event-file) commits automatically.
## Investigation steps

1. After a failed probe run, run `git -C $REPO_ROOT/.tickets-tracker log --oneline -20` to see which commits accumulated during the failed reconciler invocation. Compare to the drift SHAs in the error message to identify the offending commit's author/message.
2. Add temporary print statements around `concurrency.snapshot_head` calls inside `_apply_batch` to log when HEAD changes (and what was just being processed when it changed).
3. Audit ALL the calls inside `_apply_batch` that touch git or filesystem state. Specifically inspect: create_one, _audit_dso_id_label_writes, _persist_field_provenance, _write_pass_record.
## Key code paths
- plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/applier.py:2271-2278 (drift detector)

(b) CONFIRMED GAP: _apply_outbound_update (applier.py lines 258-314 on base branch) has _OUTBOUND_UPDATE_ALLOWLIST = frozenset({'summary','description','assignee','priority'}) — NO labels, NO comments. (c) changed_fields empty path: When a mutation only has label/comment changes, changed_fields={}, allowed={}, client.update_issue is NOT called, and the function returns ApplyResult with fields_pushed=[] and no warning — silent success. No non-empty guard existed on the base branch.

(d) CREATE path: create_one handles labels and comments indirectly — _mutation_to_batch_dict surfaces them in the batch dict, and create_one adds the dso-id label post-create. Standard user labels from the CREATE payload were NOT being added via add_label in create_one — they are threaded through the batch dict's labels key but create_one only calls add_label for dso-id. ## Incident Overview
**Component:** plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/applier.py (post-C2-fix outbound update dispatch path)
**Condition:** Local edits to bound tickets, reconciler runs without error, Jira unchanged
**Observed Result:** Outbound UPDATE matrix shows FAIL for title, description, priority, assignee, labels, comments — but reconciler reports OK and no exceptions
## Reproduction
`cd /Users/joeoakhart/digital-service-orchestra && DSO_FIELD_VALIDATION_PROBE=1 plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/e2e_field_validation_probe.sh`
Latest run: /tmp/field-probe-full-1779988610.log. Phase 1 PASSES (all 10 bindings confirmed, drift tolerance working). Phase 2 makes local edits then runs reconciler which logs:
`filter: 690 mutations computed, 10 match filter (10 local IDs, 10 target keys)` — no errors.
But Phase 2 verify reads Jira via get_issue_by_rest and sees:
- title: original (not 'UPDATED title')
- description: empty
- priority: Highest (not Low, expected 3→Low)
- assignee: Joe Oakhart (not unassigned)
- labels: only dso-id:*, no user labels
- comments: missing
## Expected Behavior
Local field edits propagate to Jira via the outbound UPDATE path. The C2 fix landed two coordinated changes that should make this work:
1. _mutation_to_batch_dict properly maps changed_fields → fields for UPDATE mutations
2. update_one propagates labels (add_label/remove_label) and comments (add_comment) alongside the scalar update
Both are present in the current applier.py (verified via grep: 16 occurrences of changed_fields/CREATE-branching, 3 occurrences of add_label/remove_label paths in update_one).
## Hypotheses

- H1: Outbound update mutations route through _apply_outbound_update (the typed leaf) which only pushes scalar fields via update_issue — bypasses the labels/comments propagation in update_one. The legacy batch path with update_one (where labels/comments DO propagate) isn't being reached.
- H2: The differ doesn't produce UPDATE mutations after the local edits. Possibly the local ticket state isn't reflecting the EDIT events (event-sourcing bug), or the differ compares stale snapshots.
- H3: ticket-CLI edit doesn't emit EDIT events for some field types.
- H4: ACLI calls succeed but silently no-op. get_issue_by_rest is reading stale state.
- H5: The mutations are produced and routed, but get filtered out by --filter-local-ids (filter target set mis-classified).
## Investigation goals
1. After a probe failure, examine the manifest at bridge_state/snapshots/<pass_id>.manifest.json — does it show update mutations with results indicating success? Or no update mutations at all?
2. Run `ticket show <id>` after Phase 2 edits to confirm local reducer captured the change. If priority shows 3, the local state is correct. If still 0, the EDIT didn't take effect locally.

3. Trace: for an outbound update typed Mutation, which dispatch arm runs — _apply_outbound_update (typed leaf, allowlist-filtered, no labels/comments) or update_one (legacy batch, labels/comments propagation)? Read apply() partitioning at lines 1995-2090.
4. If the typed leaf is the actual path: the C2 fix to update_one isn't reachable, and the typed leaf needs the same labels/comments-aware logic.
## Affected Files
- plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/applier.py — _apply_outbound_update (typed leaf), update_one (legacy batch), apply() partitioning
- plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/outbound_differ.py — verify UPDATE mutations are emitted
This bug blocks bidirectional sync verification beyond CREATE operations.

fix(outbound-differ): comment dedup fix committed — commit 23705b8f51 on branch audit/c2-leaf-gap-agent.

Root cause (DIG-5287 idempotency stall 27→18→18): _diff_comments in outbound_differ.py had two bugs that caused every local comment to be re-emitted as an 'add' on every reconciler pass:

1. Wrong snapshot key: the function read jira_issue.get('comments', []) but the Jira REST API stores comments at fields['comment']['comments'] (outer key is 'comment', not 'comments'). The fetcher writes the snapshot verbatim from the fields dict, so jira_issue['comment']['comments'] is the correct lookup. Because the key was always wrong, jira_bodies was always empty and all local comments were re-emitted unconditionally.

2. ADF body mismatch: Jira Cloud v3 returns comment bodies as ADF documents (nested dicts). Without adf_to_text() normalisation, the differ compared local plain-text bodies against ADF dicts and they never matched.

Fix: read jira_issue.get('comment', {}).get('comments', []) for the Jira comment list; apply _normalise_comment_body() on both sides (adf_to_text() for ADF documents, str() passthrough otherwise) and strip() whitespace before equality comparison. Body equality after normalisation → skip; otherwise emit 'add'.

Labels (via _diff_labels) already use set-diff and were idempotent; no label fix needed.

Tests: 5 new unit tests in test_outbound_differ_comment_dedup.py — all RED before fix, GREEN after. 21 pre-existing inbound-path baseline failures unchanged.

Compute-only diagnostic (driving both differs as reconcile.py does) shows the differ seam already implements local-wins correctly: on contention (local!=jira on a field) outbound EMITS the local value and inbound is SUPPRESSED (suppression_count=1); next pass (jira==local) yields 0 mutations. Convergence works at the differ level.

ROOT CAUSE of residual non-convergence (this ticket's idempotency-churn family): assignee shape asymmetry. The inbound differ extracted only displayName from Jira's assignee field and compared it against the local assignee string. Live Jira returns assignee as {accountId, displayName, emailAddress}; local stores the email form by default. Mismatch -> phantom inbound assignee mutation EVERY pass (the field never converges). Enumerated 6 contended fields (title/description/priority/assignee/labels/status): only assignee re-emitted at the converged state; the other 5 were already stable.

FIX: mirrored outbound_differ._assignee_matches into inbound_differ._diff_jira_vs_local. A Jira dict whose email/accountId/displayName matches the local string emits nothing; a genuine reassignment still emits (carries displayName).

Suite: 800 passed + 2 xfailed (the 1 failing test_e2e_dedup_pass is PRE-EXISTING/unrelated - FakeAcliClient lacks get_comments).

LIVE-VERIFIED against LLP-189 (real assignee shape): pre-fix 1 phantom assignee mutation {'assignee':'Joe Oakhart'}, post-fix 0. No throwaway tickets created (read-only live data used).

## Incident Overview

The reconciler's outbound apply path silently no-ops: filter-narrowed mutations are computed and the reconciler self-reports `OK: steady-state pass converged — 10 mutations`, but observed Jira state never changes. Phase 6 idempotency disproves the convergence claim — three consecutive no-op passes each compute 21 filter-matching mutations.

Manual single-ticket isolation test on DIG-4753 mid-session confirmed `update_one → client.update_issue` with `fields_pushed=['summary','description','priority']` DOES propagate to Jira and is readable back via `acli jira workitem search`. So Jira accepts our writes when the direct legacy path is called directly. The breakage is somewhere in the full reconciler dispatch chain on the e2e probe path — likely in OutboundMutation→typed Mutation conversion, in `_mutation_to_batch_dict` (CREATE+UPDATE branching recently changed in PR #437), or in `_apply_outbound_update`'s allowlist filter where `changed_fields = payload.get("changed_fields") or payload` could collapse to {} after key-stripping.
**code_version:** e9b3fcb9e1
**Observed evidence** (from /tmp/field-probe-final-1779994025.log, b6clq8b8s task):

- Phase 1 outbound CREATE: `Phase1.verify-description-multiline — got:` (empty); all 4 `Phase1.verify-label-*` FAIL — only auto-applied `dso-id:...` label present; `Phase1.verify-comment-outbound — comment not found`

- Phase 2 outbound UPDATE: every read-back returns pre-update value — `verify-title-updated got: ...baseline...`; `verify-priority-updated expected Low got: Highest`; `verify-assignee-unassigned got: Joe Oakhart`; `verify-comment-pushed second comment not found`
- Phase 6 idempotency-pass-{1,2,3} — expected 0 filtered mutations, got: 21
**Counter-evidence** (NOT a Jira / ACLI failure): mid-session single-ticket manual test on DIG-4753 confirmed outbound UPDATE via update_one works end-to-end.
**Hypotheses** (priority order):
1. `_mutation_to_batch_dict` UPDATE branch (applier.py, PR #437 change) drops/mangles `changed_fields` during OutboundMutation → typed Mutation conversion

2. `_apply_outbound_update` allowlist filter (applier.py:304-307) silently drops every field because `changed_fields` reaches it empty or wrong-shaped; `payload.get("changed_fields") or payload` fallback collapses to {} when CREATE-side keys are stripped
3. `reconcile.py` OutboundMutation→typed Mutation conversion drops `changed_fields` before applier sees it
4. Phase 1 CREATE failures hint at related/separate bug — labels/comments/multiline description not in CREATE payload at all
5. Apply path runs against wrong jira_key — 200s on a different issue, read-back of test issue sees no change
**Affected files**:
- plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/applier.py — _apply_outbound_update (258-314), _apply_batch, _mutation_to_batch_dict, _apply_outbound_create
- plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/reconcile.py — OutboundMutation → Mutation conversion, _mutation_matches_filter
- plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/outbound_differ.py — _diff_fields, _diff_labels, _diff_comments

**Reproduction**: requires JIRA_URL/JIRA_USER/JIRA_API_TOKEN + DSO_FIELD_VALIDATION_PROBE=1; run `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/e2e_field_validation_probe.sh` from /Users/joeoakhart/digital-service-orchestra. To localize, prefer manual reconciler invocation with --filter-local-ids <single-id> piping all stderr (probe's grep filter swallows diagnostics).

content.text: ### 1. Technical Environment
* **code_version:** 554882bf2bca71605681e53fdae768e284809af4
* **Affected paths:** plugins/dso/scripts/acli-integration.py (AcliClient.update_issue); plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/applier.py outbound update path
### 2. Incident Overview
* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior (defense-in-depth hardening)
#### Expected Behavior

Mature Jira clients (ankitpokhrel/jira-cli, andygrunwald/go-jira) pre-validate enum-bounded outbound mutations against API metadata client-side before issuing the mutation — Gap 8's `transition_issue_by_name` already does this for status by querying `/rest/api/3/issue/{key}/transitions`. The same pattern should apply to assignee changes via `/rest/api/3/user/assignable/search`: if the assignee string doesn't resolve to any assignable user for the issue, the reconciler should raise BEFORE the mutation is dispatched, not after ACLI silently no-ops.
#### Actual Behavior

Validation probe E confirmed `acli jira workitem assign --key DIG-3000 --assignee bogus@example.com --yes` returns exit=0 with `✗ Failure:` in stdout — same silent-failure shape as the broader Gap 5 bug 44de-3351-7e61-4714, but uniquely preventable client-side because assignable users are enum-bounded for a given project/issue.
### 3. Resolution

Add `AcliClient.validate_assignee_exists(assignee, *, issue_key=None, project_key=None) -> str` that GETs `/rest/api/3/user/assignable/search?query=<assignee>&issueKey=<key>` (or `project=<project>` for CREATE path), returns the matched accountId, raises `AssigneeNotFoundError` on no match. Hook into `update_issue` ahead of the ACLI edit dispatch when an `assignee` kwarg is present.

Out of scope: pre-validation for editable fields (summary/description/labels) — these are freeform and have no enum to validate against. Tracked separately in 44de-3351-7e61-4714 (Phase B REST-direct migration).

* **code_version:** e74a751bfe (origin/main HEAD before PR-4 worktree)
* **Skill:** plugins/dso/scripts/ticket (and underlying push retry logic)
* **Tickets worktree HEAD:** a1c0fcc761
## 2. Incident Overview
### Expected Behavior

ticket create writes the new ticket file to the orphan tickets branch, commits, and pushes to origin/tickets. On a push failure (rejected by remote), the retry loop should fetch + rebase/merge + retry until success — or fail loudly if the conflict is unresolvable.
### Actual Behavior
During a session-level audit on 2026-05-28, 5 consecutive ticket create invocations each emitted:
Warning: tickets branch push failed (merge conflict, attempt 1)
Created ticket SLUG (ID): TITLE
ID

The ticket was created locally (slug + ID returned) but the push failed silently with merge conflict at attempt 1. The "attempt 1" wording suggests a retry loop exists but it neither incremented to attempt 2 nor resolved the conflict.
Five ticket IDs filed:
- 34b2-5523-0be0-4945 (P0: check-skill-refs.sh)
- 3706-ae76-0b07-4dfe (P0: qualify-skill-refs.sh)
- a530-53cb-c966-4d46 (P0: check-test-isolation.sh)
- 3bda-755d-c938-4e62 (P2: fixture paths)
None of these appear when scanning the recent commits of origin/tickets (latest a1c0fcc761 DELETE 2026-05-29T01-20-41 release lock).
## 3. Action History
5 ticket create invocations sequentially via the ticket CLI. Each returned ticket ID locally; each printed the merge-conflict warning. No remediation attempted yet.
## 4. Root-Cause Hypotheses (informational)
1. Stale local tickets branch ref — push rejected as non-fast-forward, classified as merge conflict
2. Retry counter not incrementing — bug where counter resets every attempt, or only single attempt wired
3. Conflict-resolution path absent — retry only attempts push without pulling/rebasing first
4. Compaction lock interference — release-lock commit suggests compaction lock; push may race against compaction
5. Orphan-branch race — rapid commit churn; another writer (Jira bridge, cleanup, another session) racing the push
6. Push silently failing without ticket loss — local commit exists, but other sessions do not see the new tickets until push succeeds
## 5. Investigation Needed
1. WHY did the push fail (non-fast-forward / merge-conflict / auth / branch protection)
2. WHY did the retry loop not self-heal (attempt 1 only — never attempt 2)
3. WHERE are the 5 just-filed tickets (local-only or successfully synced after the fact)
4. WHAT cleanup is needed to restore consistency

content.text: ## Summary
plugins/dso/scripts/check-skill-refs.sh line 27 sets
REPO_ROOT=\"\$(cd \"\$SCRIPT_DIR/..\" && pwd)\"

When invoked on a host project via the shim (.claude/scripts/dso check-skill-refs.sh), \$SCRIPT_DIR is the plugin-cache scripts dir, so REPO_ROOT resolves to the plugin root (~/.claude/plugins/.../dso-dev/<ver>/), NOT the host repo. The script's CLAUDE.md skill-ref check at ~line 106 then silently inspects the plugin's CLAUDE.md instead of the host's. Result: host operators get a silent PASS even when their CLAUDE.md has unqualified /skill references that should be flagged.
## Reproduction
1. Install DSO plugin on a host project via marketplace.
2. Add an unqualified \`/skill xyz\` reference to host CLAUDE.md.
3. Run \`.claude/scripts/dso check-skill-refs.sh\`.
4. Observe: exits 0 (silent pass). Expected: non-zero exit citing the host reference.
## Fix
Replace line 27 with:
REPO_ROOT=\"\${PROJECT_ROOT:-\$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)}\"
Add a hard-error if REPO_ROOT is empty.
This mirrors check-rule-anchors.sh:48 and audit-skill-resolution.sh:25 (already host-portable).
## Discovered by
Opus audit subagent on 2026-05-28 during PR-4 host-portability review.
Reference: similar fix shipped in PR #442 for provision-ruleset.sh DEFAULT_BRANCH resolution.

content.text: ## Summary
plugins/dso/scripts/qualify-skill-refs.sh line 28 sets
REPO_ROOT=\"\$(cd \"\$SCRIPT_DIR/..\" && pwd)\"

This is the same construction as the check-skill-refs.sh sibling bug (34b2), but worse because qualify-skill-refs.sh is a MUTATOR — it rewrites /skill -> /dso:skill across host CLAUDE.md, docs, and skill files. On a host project invocation via the shim, REPO_ROOT resolves to the plugin cache root, so the script edits files in the plugin cache (violating rule:no-edit-plugin-cache from CLAUDE.md) and the host's actual files are never qualified.
## Reproduction
1. Install DSO plugin on a host project.
2. Host CLAUDE.md contains unqualified /skill references.
3. Run \`.claude/scripts/dso qualify-skill-refs.sh\`.
4. Observe: host files unchanged; plugin cache files modified (likely diff visible in plugin cache git status if user navigates there).
## Fix
Replace line 28 with:
REPO_ROOT=\"\${PROJECT_ROOT:-\$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)}\"
Hard-error on empty REPO_ROOT.
Also verify that all subsequent path constructions (skill enumeration vs scan targets) correctly distinguish \$_PLUGIN_ROOT (plugin-shipped resources) from \$REPO_ROOT (host files to mutate).
## Discovered by
Opus audit subagent on 2026-05-28 during PR-4 host-portability review.

## Root Cause Analysis (Five-Whys)

**WHY 1**: Three plugin scripts fail on host projects.
- inference-recall-replay.sh: exits with CORPUS_INSUFFICIENT (soft fail)
- preconditions-coverage-harness.sh: exits with 'ERROR: corpus file not found'
- dogfood-gov-copy.sh: exits with 'error: baseline artifact not found' (also broken in dev repo)

**WHY 2**: The scripts reference fixture paths that don't exist on host projects.
- inference-recall-replay.sh lines 13-14: INCIDENTS_FILE defaults to CWD-relative 'tests/fixtures/inference-incidents/incidents.jsonl'
- preconditions-coverage-harness.sh line 41: _DEFAULT_CORPUS=$_REPO_ROOT/tests/fixtures/818-corpus/sample-bugs.json
- dogfood-gov-copy.sh lines 32-33: BASELINE/IMPROVED = ${_PLUGIN_ROOT}/tests/fixtures/dogfood/ (wrong subdir -- plugins/dso/tests/ doesn't exist)

**WHY 3**: The fixtures live under tests/fixtures/ in the dev repo, which is NOT packaged into plugins/dso/ for distribution.

**WHY 4**: No one relocated the seed fixtures when the scripts were added (they were written assuming dev-repo context).

**WHY 5**: The plugin boundary allowlist governs only plugins/dso/ content -- tests/ content is not distributed.

## Empirical Evidence

- OBSERVED: dogfood-gov-copy.sh fails immediately in dev repo: 'error: baseline artifact not found: ${repo}/plugins/dso/tests/fixtures/dogfood/bad-copy-baseline.yaml' (plugins/dso/tests/ does NOT exist)
- OBSERVED: preconditions-coverage-harness.sh works from dev repo root but fails on a fake host (git init + run from host root): 'ERROR: corpus file not found: /tmp/fake-host.X/tests/fixtures/818-corpus/sample-bugs.json'
- OBSERVED: inference-recall-replay.sh fails on fake host with CORPUS_INSUFFICIENT (grep exit on missing file, silenced by || true)
- DOCUMENTED: plugin-boundary-allowlist.conf already covers plugins/dso/data/** -- no allowlist change required
- DOCUMENTED: retro SKILL.md line 316 has an existing skip condition for missing tests/fixtures/inference-incidents/ (partial mitigation)

## Root Cause Candidates

**RC1 (CONFIRMED, HIGH CONFIDENCE)**: Scripts were authored using dev-repo-relative paths but shipped as plugin artifacts. The seed fixture files need to be relocated to plugins/dso/data/fixtures/ so they are present in the distributed plugin cache.

**RC2 (CONFIRMED, dogfood-gov-copy.sh specifically)**: dogfood-gov-copy.sh incorrectly constructs its fixture path as _PLUGIN_ROOT/tests/fixtures/dogfood/ -- but plugins/dso/tests/ doesn't exist. This is a path-construction error that fails in the dev repo itself, not just on host projects.

## Fix Plan

**Scope** (Option A from ticket description -- relocate fixtures):

**New files to create** (copy from tests/fixtures/):
- plugins/dso/data/fixtures/inference-incidents/incidents.jsonl
- plugins/dso/data/fixtures/inference-incidents/holdout.txt
- plugins/dso/data/fixtures/818-corpus/sample-bugs.json
- plugins/dso/data/fixtures/dogfood/bad-copy-baseline.yaml
- plugins/dso/data/fixtures/dogfood/good-copy-improved.yaml

**Script changes** (update default paths to plugin-relative):
- plugins/dso/scripts/inference-recall-replay.sh line 13-14: change defaults to ${_PLUGIN_ROOT}/data/fixtures/inference-incidents/...
- plugins/dso/scripts/preconditions-coverage-harness.sh line 41: change _DEFAULT_CORPUS to $_PLUGIN_ROOT/data/fixtures/818-corpus/sample-bugs.json
- plugins/dso/scripts/dogfood-gov-copy.sh lines 32-33: change BASELINE/IMPROVED to ${_PLUGIN_ROOT}/data/fixtures/dogfood/...

**Skill/doc changes** (update hardcoded tests/fixtures paths):
- plugins/dso/skills/retro/SKILL.md lines 214,217,257,279,280,316: update inference-incidents paths to use ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/data/fixtures/inference-incidents/ (or relative _PLUGIN_ROOT variable)
- plugins/dso/docs/contracts/inference-recall-result.md lines 86-87: update invocation example

**Allowlist**: plugins/dso/data/** is already in plugin-boundary-allowlist.conf -- no change needed.

**Test changes**: The existing tests already pass --corpus or INCIDENTS_FILE overrides, so they don't rely on the broken defaults. A portability regression test should be added to confirm defaults work from a directory without tests/fixtures/.

## Complexity Assessment: MODERATE
- Multiple files (5 scripts/skills + 5 new fixture copies)
- Straightforward mechanical path relocation -- no logic changes
- One file (retro SKILL.md) is an LLM-behavioral file -- changes are path/variable updates only, not behavioral guidance

<!-- dso:reconciler-echo -->
## Summary

Several plugin scripts reference fixture or corpus paths that exist in the development repo's tests/ tree but DO NOT ship inside plugins/dso/ in the marketplace-distributed cache. On a host project running via the shim, the paths resolve to non-existent locations.
Affected scripts:
- inference-recall-replay.sh:13-14 — defaults to tests/fixtures/inference-incidents/...
- preconditions-coverage-harness.sh:41 — _DEFAULT_CORPUS=\$_REPO_ROOT/tests/fixtures/818-corpus/sample-bugs.json
- dogfood-gov-copy.sh:32 — BASELINE=\${_PLUGIN_ROOT}/tests/fixtures/dogfood/bad-copy-baseline.yaml
- check-test-isolation.sh:34 — RULES_DIR=\$REPO_ROOT/scripts/test-isolation-rules (relates to a530)

This issue is masked today by the broken REPO_ROOT=SCRIPT_DIR/.. pattern (separate bugs 34b2/3706/a530) which makes REPO_ROOT resolve to the plugin tree. Once those are fixed, missing-resource errors will surface.
## Fix options
A. Move fixtures into plugins/dso/data/fixtures/ (or plugins/dso/resources/) and update scripts to use \${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/data/fixtures/...
B. Tag the scripts as plugin-self-test-only and remove them from the shim allowlist (host can't invoke them).
(A) is preferable for any script that is genuinely useful on a host project; (B) for purely internal dogfooding tooling.
## Discovered by
Opus audit subagent on 2026-05-28 during PR-4 host-portability review.

FIX_APPLIED (worktree-20260528-165839):

- plugins/dso/scripts/ticket-lib.sh: `_scratch_atomic_write` default max_bytes 4096 -> 32768 (8x increase, mirrors the Jira issue-properties precedent cited in epic 1d8b's design notes).
- plugins/dso/docs/ticket-cli-reference.md, plugins/dso/docs/ticket-scratch-cli.md: doc references updated 4096 -> 32768.
- tests/scratch/test-scratch-lib.sh Test I, tests/scratch/test-scratch-set.sh Test 6: bumped payload size 5000 -> 33000 to test the new boundary. All 39+25 scratch tests pass.

Empirical post-fix probe (turbid-maze-tread sprint session):
  4000, 8000, 16000, 30000, 32000, 32700 bytes -> ok (exact round-trip)
  32750, 32800, 33000, 50000 bytes -> oversize error (limit=32768, actual=N)
Effective payload budget: 32710 bytes (~43-byte JSON envelope overhead).

ARCHITECTURAL CAVEAT (from 1d8b brainstorm rationale):
The scratch channel was originally designed as a *receipt channel* — small structured handoffs (token-counted to motivate the original sub-agent context-cost reduction) with a 'size cutover threshold above which call-sites continue using a filesystem path' (PR #356 design notes). The current bump preserves the bounded-disk-risk intent while unblocking COMPLEX-epic story-decomposition payloads that the original 4096-byte cap forced into cryptic compression.

The structurally clean follow-up (not done here) is to restore the original receipt-as-pointer pattern in agents/story-decomposer.md and skills/preplanning/SKILL.md Story Decomposition phase: write the full JSON to $ARTIFACTS_DIR/story-decomposition-<epic-id>.json and put only {ticket_id, key, artifact_path} in scratch. That removes the cap entirely as a concern. Filing as a follow-up consideration on this ticket; 32KB is the practical ceiling fix for now.

<!-- dso:reconciler-echo -->

FINAL_CEILING_DECISION (worktree-20260528-165839):

Re-bumped 32768 -> 98304 (96 KB) after historical sizing analysis (sonnet sub-agent, n=200 closed+archived epics, 1229 stories, 4307 tasks).

Distribution stats:
- Stories per epic: P50=5, P90=9, P95=13, P99=18, max=18
- Tasks per story: P50=3, P90=8, P95=10, P99=15, max=18
- 14% of closed epics are stubs (0 descendants)

Key calibration finding the original 1700-byte/draft + 150-byte/SC model missed: sc_coverage_plan writes sc_text VERBATIM. Average SC text is P50=283, P95=917, MAX=2590 chars (epic dbbc-cf67, 6 SCs averaging 2590 chars each). For an 18-story epic with 6 long SCs, projected payload reaches 55-83KB. 32KB would silently oversize-block preplanning on the worst-case historical epics.

Empirical projection of payload size for the historical max:
- Task-decomposer P99 × 1.3 = 35,750 bytes
- Story-decomposer P99 × 1.3 (SC-aware) = ~71,600 bytes
- Historical max × 1.1 headroom = ~91,200 bytes
- Chosen cap: 98,304 bytes (next 8KB boundary)

- tests/scratch/test-scratch-lib.sh Test I, tests/scratch/test-scratch-set.sh Test 6: 99000-byte oversize boundary
- All 64 scratch tests pass.

- 80000, 96000, 98000, 98260 bytes -> ok
- 98270, 99000, 200000 bytes -> oversize (limit=98304)

### 1. Technical Environment
* **code_version:** $_CODE_VER
* **Script:** plugins/dso/scripts/ticket-scratch.sh — `_scratch_atomic_write` function
### 2. Incident Overview
* **Scenario Type:** Sub-Agent Blocker
#### Expected Behavior

Per `agents/story-decomposer.md` and `skills/preplanning/SKILL.md` Story Decomposition phase, the sub-agent should produce a faithful set of vertical-slice drafts (typically 4–8 for a COMPLEX 10-SC epic) and write them via `ticket-scratch.sh set <ticket> <key> <json>`. The scratch store is documented as the canonical handoff mechanism between sub-agent and orchestrator (output contract returns only a 3-field receipt; payload size is bounded only by ticket comment limits ~500KB downstream).
#### Actual Behavior

While preplanning epic `turbid-maze-tread` (10 SCs, COMPLEX), the `dso:story-decomposer` sub-agent reported it could not persist a faithful 7-draft decomposition because `_scratch_atomic_write` enforces a hardcoded 4096-byte ceiling (with ~575 bytes of envelope overhead, leaving ~3520 bytes for the JSON value). The agent compressed to 3 drafts (831 byte_count receipt → 3484 byte_count payload retained) and recorded the forced compression in `decomposition_notes`:
['X-epic:gh_comment_id(b575);S3(d2f9).', 'LIVE:1,3,8,9,10.', '4KB:split A->{schema,clf,scan,parsers};B->{adapt,CI}.']

The note instructs downstream phases (Phase C/F) to split draft A into 4 stories and draft B into 2. This works as a degradation path but degrades preplanning output below the agent's actual capability and loses per-draft detail (verify_commands, considerations, DD precision) that would have been captured in the unconstrained drafts.
### 3. Action History
1. `/dso:sprint` selected epic turbid-maze-tread (COMPLEX, 10 SCs)
2. `/dso:preplanning` dispatched `dso:story-decomposer` (opus, via general-purpose fallback)
3. Agent computed 7 drafts but `ticket-scratch.sh set ...` rejected payloads > 4096 bytes
4. Agent compressed to 3 drafts + split-instruction note, wrote 3484-byte payload, returned receipt
5. Orchestrator retrieved 3-draft payload successfully
### 4. Chronological Rationalization

The 4096-byte ceiling in `_scratch_atomic_write` predates the story-decomposer integration. The decomposer's output contract was written assuming scratch could hold arbitrarily large JSON. The contract and the storage layer drifted: SKILL.md says \"write your full JSON output\" but the storage layer caps it. Either the contract should set a payload budget the agent honors, or the ceiling should be raised to comfortably accommodate typical 5–10-story decompositions (~10–30KB).
### 5. Skills and Workflows
* `plugins/dso/skills/preplanning/SKILL.md` — Story Decomposition phase output contract
* `plugins/dso/agents/story-decomposer.md` — agent definition
* `plugins/dso/scripts/ticket-scratch.sh` — `_scratch_atomic_write` (hardcoded `MAX_BYTES=4096` or similar)
* Consumers: `plugins/dso/scripts/receipt-parse.sh`, preplanning Story Decomposition § Parse Output
### 6. Logs
Receipt returned: `{\"ticket_id\": \"turbid-maze-tread\", \"key\": \"preplanning:step4:story-decomp-draft\", \"byte_count\": 3484}`
Retrieved payload: 3 drafts, 10 SC entries (all covered), decomposition_notes contains forced-compression marker `4KB:split A->{schema,clf,scan,parsers};B->{adapt,CI}.`
### Recommended Fix Direction

Raise the scratch payload ceiling (e.g., to 64KB or 256KB) — sufficient for typical opus sub-agent outputs without amplifying risk. Alternatively, document a per-key payload budget in `ticket-scratch.md` and have the story-decomposer (and other heavy producers) honor it explicitly. Either fix is acceptable; raising the ceiling is lower-risk and avoids forcing every producer to learn the contract.

content.text: ### 1. Technical Environment
* **code_version:** 554882bf2bca71605681e53fdae768e284809af4
* **acli version:** acli version 1.3.18-stable
* **Affected paths:** plugins/dso/scripts/acli-integration.py (AcliClient + module-level wrappers); applier.py outbound mutation dispatch
### 2. Incident Overview
* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior
#### Expected Behavior

ACLI mutation commands (`edit`, `transition`, `assign`, etc.) should signal failure to programmatic callers either via non-zero exit code OR via a parseable structured error. The reconciler's outbound apply path must NOT mark a mutation `applied` when the underlying Jira operation failed — doing so corrupts the binding-store invariant and prevents idempotent convergence (next pass computes the same diff but reports zero work).
#### Actual Behavior
Validation probe E (2026-05-28, this session) confirmed ACLI returns exit=0 on three distinct failure classes:
- `acli jira workitem edit --key DIG-99999 --summary test --yes` -> exit=0, stdout: `✗ Failure: Issue does not exist or you do not have permission to see it.`
- `acli jira workitem transition --key DIG-99999 --status BogusStatus --yes` -> exit=0, similar stdout
- `acli jira workitem assign --key DIG-3000 --assignee bogus@example.com --yes` -> exit=0, similar stdout
The reconciler's `_apply_outbound_update` / `_apply_batch` paths key off non-zero exit code from `_run_acli` to detect failure; ACLI's exit-code contract therefore causes silent divergence.
### 3. Action History
- Gap 5 surfaced during sprint of Jira-sync field-parity work.
- Gap 8 (bug 85a1) partially mitigated for `status` field by introducing `AcliClient.transition_issue_by_name` which talks REST directly via `_direct_rest_get` + `_direct_rest_post_raw`.
- This bug captures the residual gap for all other outbound mutation fields.
### 4. Investigation finding — ACLI does expose structured failure via `--json`
Adding `--json` to the same bogus calls returns:
\"results\": [{\"status\": \"FAILURE\", \"message\": \"Issue does not exist or you do not have permission to see it.\", \"id\": \"DIG-99999\"}],
\"totalCount\": 1,
\"successCount\": 0
Exit code still 0, but `successCount == 0` + `results[].status == \"FAILURE\"` give a clean detector.
### 5. Resolution options (three viable approaches)

1. **REST-direct migration** (preferred per mature-client convention). Extend `AcliClient._direct_rest_*` helpers to cover all outbound mutations (edit, assign, label, comment, etc.). HTTP status code = primary signal; structured `errorMessages[]` body = secondary detail. Retry only 429/503/ConnectionError with exponential backoff + jitter. Matches pycontribs/jira, ankitpokhrel/jira-cli, andygrunwald/go-jira convention. Removes the ACLI hybrid.

2. **ACLI `--json` parsing** (bridge). Add `--json` to every ACLI mutation call site in `AcliClient` and module wrappers; parse `successCount` / `results[].status`; raise on FAILURE. Smaller diff, retains ACLI's subprocess cost, depends on Atlassian preserving the JSON shape.
3. **Hybrid** — pre-validate enum-bounded ops client-side (transitions, assignees) so the bogus-input class is caught before ACLI runs; `--json` parsing on remaining calls.
### 6. Sources / Evidence
- Validation probe E results (this session, 2026-05-28).

- Research subagent findings (this session): pycontribs/jira resilientsession.py raise_on_error() + parse_errors(); ankitpokhrel/jira-cli api/client.go status-code discrimination; andygrunwald/go-jira cli.go; jira.js HttpException pattern.
- Atlassian ACLI troubleshooting page acknowledges OAuth/keychain failure modes that exit cleanly.
### Out of scope for this bug
- Phase A (assignee pre-validation via `/rest/api/3/user/assignable/search`) is being landed separately as defense-in-depth ahead of this fix.
- Bug 85a1 / b859 (the underlying Gap 8 + Phase 4 status outbound investigations).

## 2. Incident Overview
### Expected Behavior

The CI llm-review job's Strategy F (large-diff chunked/aggregated review) path should successfully dispatch multiple clusters to the LLM, collect per-cluster results, aggregate them, post findings, and exit with 0 (success) or 1 (real findings to address). Any infrastructure failure should exit with a distinct code (e.g. 4 per bug f148) rather than 1.
### Actual Behavior
On run 26614994184, the llm-review job hit a Python AttributeError in the Strategy F cluster aggregation path:
1. DECISION: DISPATCH (forced) — 3 unreviewed commit(s) on sub-agent branch
2. Diff: 42 files, 4403 lines, 191551 bytes
3. INFO: diff exceeds region-split threshold — activating Strategy F file-filter + chunked + aggregated review
4. INFO: dispatching 5 cluster(s) with cluster_concurrency=2
5. **ERROR: LLM call failed: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'**
6. Process completed with exit code 1.

Zero findings posted to the PR. The error message reaches stderr but no preview of the offending value is captured. The job exits 1 with the standard "review failed" semantics — same false-positive PR block as bug f148.
## 3. Action History and Workarounds
PR #446 was force-merged via admin override (same path as #432, #439) because zero findings existed.
## 4. Root-Cause Hypotheses (informational)

1. **Wrong-shape LLM response in Strategy F aggregator**: a per-cluster LLM call returned a string (e.g. an error envelope, refusal, or raw text) where the aggregator expected a dict with `.get()` callable. Likely site: cluster-result aggregation in `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/runner.py` Strategy F path.
2. **Provider adapter returned raw content unwrapped**: `providers/anthropic.py` or `dispatch.py` may have returned a string under failure conditions instead of raising or wrapping into a dict.

3. **Region-split + concurrent dispatch race**: 5 clusters at cluster_concurrency=2 may have produced a result list with a string error sentinel mixed with dicts; aggregator iterates without isinstance check.
4. **litellm response shape variation**: some response paths return `message.content` as str directly; others wrap in dict.
## 5. Relationship to Bug f148
Distinct surfaces:
- **f148**: `ValueError: LLM returned non-JSON response (length=275)` in primary single-cluster dispatch (`dispatch.py` chain)
- **THIS BUG**: `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'` in Strategy F multi-cluster aggregation (`runner.py` aggregator)

PR-A for f148 covers R1-R5 (PR HEAD SHA / fallback chain iteration / preview logging / rescue / parse) but does NOT directly address the Strategy F aggregator path. This bug needs its own fix even after PR-A merges.

## fix-bug:investigation (2026-06-03)

### STALENESS VERDICT: HOOK ALREADY IMPLEMENTED — ONE VIOLATION REMAINS

The bug-8229 prevention hook stack is fully in place. The ticket's requested deliverables already exist:

**Existing artifacts:**
- Hook: `.claude/hooks/pre-commit/check-script-dir-pattern.sh` (109 lines, references bug 8229 in header)
- Registration: `.pre-commit-config.yaml` id=`script-dir-pattern-check` (files: `^plugins/dso/.*\.sh$`, 10s timeout, via pre-commit-wrapper.sh)
- Test: `tests/scripts/test-check-script-dir-pattern.sh` (7 test cases, ALL PASS as of investigation date)

**Hook pattern:**
`^[[:space:]]*[^#]*REPO_ROOT[^#]*\$\{?SCRIPT_DIR\}?/\.\.`
Catches: `REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"`, `REPO_ROOT="${SCRIPT_DIR}/.."`, `: "${REPO_ROOT:=$SCRIPT_DIR/..}"`
Suppression: `# script-dir-pattern-ok: <rationale>` on same line as the assignment.

**Design decision: sibling (NOT extend check-plugin-self-ref.sh)**
One-concern-per-hook convention followed. check-plugin-self-ref.sh has zero bypass; check-script-dir-pattern.sh has a suppression mechanism for legitimately plugin-internal scripts. Correct separation.

**Registration:** pre-commit-config.yaml `script-dir-pattern-check` entry covers CI (CI runs pre-commit).

---

### CURRENT VIOLATIONS AUDIT

Full grep of `plugins/dso/scripts/` + `plugins/dso/hooks/` for hook pattern:

| File | Line | Content | Classification | Rationale |
|------|------|---------|----------------|-----------|
| `plugins/dso/scripts/validate.sh` | 96 | `REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"` | **NEEDS-FIX** | else-branch fallback when git fails; validate.sh then uses REPO_ROOT for all checks (cd, scan, config read). If invoked from plugin cache outside a git repo, REPO_ROOT silently = plugin cache root. No suppression marker. |

All other `SCRIPT_DIR/..` occurrences assign to `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`, `PLUGIN_ROOT`, `_PLUGIN_DIR`, `_plugin_dir` (plugin tree itself) — not caught by hook (correct scoping).

**validate.sh line 96 full context (lines 90-97):**
```bash
CALLER_GIT_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -n "$CALLER_GIT_ROOT" ]; then
    REPO_ROOT="$CALLER_GIT_ROOT"
else
    REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"   # ← VIOLATION
fi
```

**Canonical fix:**
```bash
else
    echo "ERROR: cannot resolve REPO_ROOT (not in a git repo and PROJECT_ROOT is unset)" >&2
    exit 1
fi
```
Or equivalently: `REPO_ROOT="${PROJECT_ROOT:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)}"` with an explicit error check.

---

### RED TEST PLAN (already implemented, all passing)

`tests/scripts/test-check-script-dir-pattern.sh` — 7 cases:
1. Anti-pattern in staged .sh under plugins/dso/ → hook exits 1 ✓

## Summary

The existing check-plugin-self-ref pre-commit hook catches literal \"plugins/dso\" path references in source files but MISSES the failure-mode-B blindspot: scripts that derive REPO_ROOT via BASH_SOURCE + \"cd ../..\". This pattern silently resolves to the plugin cache root on host projects, leading to silent passes (check scripts) or wrong-tree edits (mutator scripts).
Three critical instances were filed as separate P0 bugs (34b2, 3706, a530). A new lint hook would prevent recurrence.
## Proposed hook
Extend check-plugin-self-ref.sh (or add a sibling hook) that:
- Greps for assignments matching: REPO_ROOT=.*SCRIPT_DIR/\\.\\.
- Fails commit unless the file is on an allowlist (plugin-internal-only scripts that don't touch host artifacts).
- Suggests the canonical pattern:
REPO_ROOT=\"\${PROJECT_ROOT:-\$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)}\"
## Acceptance
- New hook runs in CI and pre-commit.

DIG-5002.summary: Add lint hook to catch REPO_ROOT=SCRIPT_DIR/.. pattern in plugin scripts

content.text: ## Summary
plugins/dso/scripts/check-test-isolation.sh line 31 uses
: \"\${REPO_ROOT:=\$(cd \"\$SCRIPT_DIR/..\" && pwd)}\"

The script is wired into host pre-commit chains (.pre-commit-config.yaml:134). On a host project, the shim resolves SCRIPT_DIR to the plugin cache, so REPO_ROOT defaults to the plugin root. The subsequent \`git diff --cached --name-only\` at line 56 then runs inside the plugin cache directory — either erroring (no git repo) or returning an empty diff. Net effect: silent pass; host's staged test files are never checked for isolation violations.
The := makes the env-override path acceptable (PROJECT_ROOT=… works), but the DEFAULT is wrong. Hosts that haven't set PROJECT_ROOT get the silent pass.
## Reproduction
1. Install DSO plugin on a host project, wire check-test-isolation.sh into pre-commit.
2. Stage a test file with a known isolation violation.
3. Commit. Observe: pre-commit reports PASS (false negative).
4. Verify the script ran inside the plugin cache: add `echo \"DEBUG: pwd=\$(pwd) REPO_ROOT=\$REPO_ROOT\" >&2` near line 56.
## Fix
Replace line 31 with:
REPO_ROOT=\"\${PROJECT_ROOT:-\$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)}\"
Hard-error on empty REPO_ROOT.

Also fix line 34 (RULES_DIR=\$REPO_ROOT/scripts/test-isolation-rules) which currently masks-as-working because REPO_ROOT resolves to plugin tree. The rules dir is a plugin-shipped resource; should be \${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/test-isolation-rules.

Opus audit subagent on 2026-05-28 during PR-4 host-portability review.

## Incident Overview

After landing Gap 8 (status outbound via REST POST /transitions) and Gap 1 (inbound comments + outbound marker), the e2e probe Phase 4 regressed. Probe transitions ticket 9 locally from `open` -> `in_progress` then runs the reconciler. Expected: Jira status reflects In Progress. Observed: Jira stays To Do AND the reconciler produces NO output matching `^(FILTERED|filter:|OK:|ERROR:)`. The probe's grep filter consequently sees nothing between 'Running reconciler' and the verify FAIL — the failure is INVISIBLE.

A prior probe run with Gap 8 alone (no Gap 1) showed status PASS. After Gap 1 sync, status fails silently. Either Gap 1 affected the apply path, or my Gap 8 transition_issue rewrite has an edge case the live workflow hits.
**code_version:** 717207a8e0 (session branch fix/c2-outbound-update-propagation, post-Gap1 sync)
## Evidence
`/tmp/field-probe-postgap1-1780016792.log` lines 135-145:
=== PHASE 4: Status outbound propagation ===
Running reconciler for status outbound test...
FAIL: Phase4.verify-status-outbound-in-progress — expected In Progress, got: To Do

NO reconciler output appears between 'Running reconciler...' and the verify FAIL. The probe's run_reconciler captures stdout+stderr via subshell; `run_filtered_reconciler` then `echo $reconciler_output | grep -E ^(FILTERED|filter|OK|ERROR):`. None of those tokens were present.
Phase 6 idempotency regressed from 18 -> 21/19/19 between the Gap-8-only run and this Gap-1 run — related signal that Gap 1 changes may have inadvertently affected the apply chain.
## Hypotheses (priority order)

1. transition_issue uses module-level shape: my rewrite at acli-integration.py:555-585 instantiates a fresh AcliClient inside transition_issue using env vars. If env vars are inconsistent at call time, this constructs a broken client. transition_issue_by_name then raises but the error is swallowed.

2. transition_issue_by_name raises RuntimeError, not JiraAPIError: _call_with_retry only catches JiraAPIError-class exceptions. RuntimeError propagates uncaught through update_one -> _apply_batch loop -> apply() -> reconcile_once -> __main__ broad except, which SHOULD print 'ERROR: reconcile_once raised:'. But no ERROR line in the log. So either it's being caught somewhere or the print is going to a buffer that gets dropped.

3. Mode-cap manifest renderer in apply() may swallow mid-batch exceptions: apply() has mode='bootstrap-throttle' branching that renders an asymmetric manifest. If the apply loop raises mid-iteration, the renderer might recover into a 'OK' return and the actual exception is consumed.
4. The new `getattr(im, 'comments', [])` in reconcile.py for Gap 1: if im is a SimpleNamespace without comments attr, returns []. Should be safe; rule out by inspection.
5. status mutation never reaches transition_issue_by_name: maybe Gap 4 assignee permissive match logic incorrectly suppressed the status entry too. _diff_fields rewriting must be checked.

6. Ticket 9's actual local status when Phase 4 runs is not what we expect. Phase 1 created with status open; nothing changed it before Phase 4. Probe does `ticket transition open in_progress`. But the local CLI might have a different in-flight value.

## 1. Technical Environment
* **code_version:** 195f93f76c (PR #442 HEAD on `fix-pr4-sub-pr-ruleset-patterns` branch at incident time)
* **CI run:** https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/actions/runs/26614385353/job/78428237761
* **Workflow file:** .github/workflows/ci.yml (llm-review job, line ~374-755)
## 2. Incident Overview
### Expected Behavior
The `llm-review` CI job should:
1. Dispatch the provenance-aware review (commit-scoped diff)
2. Send the diff to the configured reviewer agent (claude-opus-4-7)
3. Receive structured JSON findings
4. Post findings as PR review comments via the Reviews API
5. Report success/failure on the basis of CURRENT findings
When the LLM returns malformed output or the API fails, the job should fail with a SPECIFIC infrastructure-error class rather than surfacing stale findings from prior review cycles.
### Actual Behavior
On run 26614385353 (PR #442, HEAD 195f93f76c), the llm-review job hit a cascading infrastructure failure:
1. `DECISION: DISPATCH (forced) — 8 unreviewed commit(s) on sub-agent branch` (dispatcher correctly ran)
2. Diff: 26 files, 3075 lines, 143298 bytes (within cap of 100 files / 5MB)
3. `INFO: commit_sha changed (ec091b28f405 → 72334914eec9); resetting cycle_number from 2 to 1` (cycle counter reset detected)
4. `ERROR: LLM returned non-JSON response (length=275); cannot parse as findings.` (primary call to opus-4-7 failed)
5. `Fallback chain exhausted for agent code-reviewer-deep-verification (primary=claude-opus-4-7): LLM returned non-JSON response (length=275); cannot parse as findings.` (all fallbacks failed)
6. `WARNING: Reviews API failed (CalledProcessError); re-routing anchored findings to issue comments. gh stderr: 'gh: Unprocessable Entity (HTTP 422)'` (Reviews API rejected the post)
7. `ERROR: llm-review found blocking finding(s) — 4 important (see findings JSON above and 4 PR review comments for details)` (4 "blocking" findings reported)
The 4 "blocking findings" surfaced are stale from prior review cycles (timestamps 01:26 and 01:50 — well before the 02:48 failed call):
- `test-sync-sub-pr-ruleset.sh:7` (deleted file ref — both sync scripts; was fixed in commit 9f3f9b3877)
- `test-sync-sub-pr-ruleset.sh:159` (DEFAULT_BRANCH fallback test gap; was fixed in 51daebcd94 + 9f3f9b3877)
- `test-sync-sub-pr-ruleset.sh:206-210` (stub returns plain text; was fixed in 9f3f9b3877)
The system conflates a real LLM-infrastructure failure with a substantive review failure, blocking the PR on findings that have already been addressed in earlier commits.
## 3. Action History and Workarounds
* PR #442 has been through multiple cycles; each push triggers a re-review
* Earlier cycles (01:26, 01:50) flagged the findings noted above
* I addressed those findings in commits 51daebcd94 and 9f3f9b3877
* The 02:48 run hit the LLM infrastructure failure but still posted "blocking" findings
* No workaround attempted yet — running /dso:fix-bug to investigate
## 4. Root-Cause Hypotheses (informational, NOT prescriptive)

1. **Stale-findings surface on LLM-call failure**: When the LLM returns non-JSON and fallbacks exhaust, the runner reads a stale `findings.json` from a prior cycle's artifact cache and re-uses it as "current"
2. **LLM JSON-extraction missing**: The model may have returned valid JSON wrapped in markdown (```json ... ```) — the parser may be requiring raw JSON only
3. **Fallback chain not actually distinct**: All "fallback" models may share the same broken prompt → all return non-JSON for the same reason
4. **Reviews API 422**: Payload contains stale commit_id, or empty path/line in some comment, or PR is in a state that rejects reviews
5. **No infrastructure-error class**: The job exit handler treats LLM-error + 0-fresh-findings as "4 findings from before" rather than "LLM infrastructure unavailable"
## 5. Skills and Workflows
* Affected: every llm-review CI invocation on session→main PRs
* Related skills: /dso:review (host-side), the CI workflow ci.yml
* Cross-cutting: this defect causes false-positive PR blocks on infrastructure failures — operationally serious because it forces /dso:fp-recovery on what was actually a working PR
## 6. Logs
See the CI run logs at the URLs above. Key lines quoted in section 2.
## 7. Investigation Status
A background opus subagent (ID a56c220a8eba41c18) is currently investigating Q1-Q5 of the infrastructure failure surface. Its evidence will feed Phase C of fix-bug.

- `dso ticket deps f27a-3c6a-1a4e-48ae` reports children:[] (correctly excludes deleted) -- inconsistent with list-epics.
- `dso ticket list --parent=f27a-3c6a-1a4e-48ae --include-archived` returns the 7 deleted stories.

Downstream impact: sprint auto-resume (skills/sprint/prompts/auto-resume.md) and the Preplanning Gate (skills/sprint/SKILL.md Step 1) compute ALL via 'dso ticket list --parent=<id> --include-archived | grep -c \"ticket_id\"', which counts deleted children. With OPEN==0 and ALL>0, an epic whose entire decomposition was DELETED (not completed) wrongly satisfies the 'all children closed -> skip to validation / Phase G' branch instead of routing to re-decomposition. The completion-verifier would then run against 10 unmet success criteria.
### 5. Skills and Workflows
* Affected reference path `dso ticket deps` is already correct; the defect is in list-epics child_count and the include-archived child-enumeration used by the gate logic.

DIG-5013.summary: [reconciler/applier]: label add on bound ticket -> not propagated in either direction

content.text: ## Incident Overview

**What**: outbound_differ._EXCLUDED_PREFIXES = ('dso-id-', 'imported:') uses HYPHEN suffix 'dso-id-' but applier.py:637 writes the binding label as f'dso-id:{local_id}' with COLON. The prefix never matches, so the differ does NOT exclude the bridge-internal label from comparison. The differ then sees the label on Jira but not in local tags → emits a label-remove mutation for dso-id:<UUID>. The outbound audit guard (_audit_dso_id_label_writes for outbound_update path) blocks the unauthorized dso-id label write, aborting the entire outbound update mutation. Effect: NO outbound updates reach Jira for ANY bound ticket — labels, scalar fields, anything.
**Severity**: HIGH (every outbound update on a bound ticket blocked; entire outbound update channel silently broken).
## Reproduction

/tmp/labels-probe.sh T1 outbound add — local tag added, outbound pass runs, Jira does NOT receive the new label. (And the wider e2e probe matrix's Outbound UPDATE failures across all fields are likely the same root cause.)
## Suspected Fix

Change outbound_differ._EXCLUDED_PREFIXES tuple entry from 'dso-id-' to 'dso-id:'. Verify the applier and any other writers use the colon form consistently. Add a test that constructs a bound ticket with the dso-id:UUID label on Jira side and asserts no remove-label mutation is emitted by the differ.
## Discovered During
Investigation of bug 57b0-acfd-7cb1-4a3c (PR #453). Sub-agent traced the outbound symptom to this prefix mismatch while implementing the inbound labels fix.

DIG-5014.summary: [reconciler/outbound_differ]: dso-id label prefix mismatch -> outbound updates blocked on every bound ticket

content.text: ## Incident Overview

**What**: When a label is added locally and the reconciler runs (bidirectional, one pass), the inbound differ sees 'jira lacks X, local has X' and emits an inbound REMOVE label mutation for X. The applier then writes an EDIT with tags=<current minus X>, wiping the just-added local label. Outbound differ in the same pass also runs and pushes X to Jira, so the next pass's Jira will have X — but the inbound EDIT already cleared it locally.
**Severity**: HIGH — local tags lost on every label-add that triggers a bidirectional pass. Causes label drift on every outbound add.
## Reproduction
Run /tmp/labels-probe.sh. Observe:
- After T1: local 'after tag' has [labelprobe, ob-added]; outbound pass runs; T1 reports OB-ADD PASS (jira got ob-added).
- T2: 'local after untag: []' — local has NO tags. The pre-existing 'labelprobe-...' tag is also gone.
- This means T1's reconciler bidirectional pass cleared local tags, not the T2 untag command.
## Root Cause
inbound_differ does NOT consult the OUTBOUND-just-emitted mutation set. It sees:
- jira_labels = {dso-id:UUID, labelprobe} (pre-outbound snapshot)
- local_tags = {labelprobe, ob-added}
And concludes: jira lacks 'ob-added' → emit inbound REMOVE label mutation for 'ob-added'.
But OUTBOUND already in same pass emitted ADD 'ob-added' to jira. The inbound emission is WRONG — local just added it, didn't lose it from jira.
## Suspected Fix Approaches
1. **Two-phase sync**: run outbound first, refresh jira snapshot, then run inbound differ against fresh snapshot. Most correct but heaviest change.
2. **Cross-direction filter**: in compute_inbound_mutations, filter out labels that compute_outbound_mutations is concurrently adding (pass outbound mutation set as context).
3. **Last-write-wins by timestamp**: track when each side last changed each label; inbound only acts on labels jira changed after the binding's last-sync timestamp.
## Affected Files
- plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/inbound_differ.py (compute_inbound_mutations + _diff_labels_inbound)
- plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/reconcile.py (sync orchestration ordering)
## Related
- Bug bc8f-775e-9a34-44d1 fixed the REDUCER-FAILURE branch via Option A but didn't address the normal-path clearing (different code path).
- Bug 68a4 (PR #454 merged) fixed the dso-id label prefix issue.
- PR #453 (bc8f fix) merged Option A — addresses one failure mode only.
**code_version**: 30b86a25693e540bb6ab90c7eac808d97bf5df08

content.text:
## Approach re-analysis (2026-05-29)

**Option 2 (two-phase sync: inbound-first then refresh+outbound) is REJECTED — breaks local label removal.**

Scenario: local=[A, X], jira=[A, X, dso-id]. User removes X locally → local=[A].
- Inbound runs first against pre-pass snapshot: emits ADD X, applies → local=[A, X]
- Refresh: local=[A, X], jira=[A, X] → outbound emits nothing
- Net: X silently restored locally; user's removal undone.

The PR #457 local-wins suppression is load-bearing precisely because neither differ has a baseline. Reordering does not add information — it inverts which side wins by default.

**Only options 1 and 3 are correct fixes** (both add a baseline so differs can distinguish "local never had X" from "local had X and removed it"):

- **Option 1 — local-intent tracking**: outbound only emits REMOVE when there's a corresponding local TAG_REMOVE event. Requires consuming the event log in outbound_differ (larger surface).
- **Option 3 — binding-time baseline (RECOMMENDED)**: snapshot local tags at bind time, store on binding record. Outbound differ computes diff against (current_local - baseline) intent, suppressing spurious REMOVEs for labels local never had. Smaller schema delta than option 1; preserves local-wins semantics; no orchestration reorder needed.

Updated recommendation: **option 3**. Awaiting user approval before implementation.
