content.text: ### 2. Incident Overview
* **Scenario Type:** Sub-Agent Blocker / tooling
#### Expected Behavior
merge-to-main.sh --resume should reliably resume driving its OWN staged PR (work -> staged-* -> main two-channel) after an interrupted run.
#### Actual Behavior

When the initial merge-to-main.sh run is stopped before it checkpoints its state file (here: the run backgrounded into wait-for-pr.sh polling a conflicting PR, then was stopped), --resume loses the PR number. Its GitHub fallback then resolved the WRONG PR — a pre-existing legacy umbrella PR (worktree->main, #534) instead of its own staged PR (#542) — promoted #534 to ready and tried to drive it, which can never pass check-staged-head (only staged-* heads may merge to main). A later --resume emitted 'ERROR: could not resolve PR number for polling phase'. Net: the two-channel promotion could not be driven by the script and had to be hand-driven via PR-FINALIZE-WORKFLOW + manual staged-branch sub-PRs. Workaround exists (hand-drive) but is costly. Fix: persist the staged PR number durably at creation (before any timeout-prone wait) so --resume re-binds to the correct PR, and have the GitHub fallback filter to PRs whose head is the session branch AND base is the script's staged-* branch (never a base=main umbrella PR). Observed with dso-dev 1.17.102 during the waxen-sigma session.

The required check 'review-sub-pr' (ci.yml llm-review-sub-pr job) must actually RUN and PASS before a work->staged-* PR can merge. If its 'needs:' dependency (test-scripts / Script Tests) fails, review-sub-pr cannot run and the PR must stay BLOCKED.
#### Actual Behavior

PR #542 (worktree-20260601-183103 -> staged-fb60ad1b70e9-1780414095) auto-merged while review-sub-pr was SKIPPED. review-sub-pr 'needs: [changes, actionlint, shellcheck, lint-python, test-hooks, test-scripts]'; Script Tests FAILED (a broken doc-writer test), so review-sub-pr was skipped. GitHub treats a skipped required check as satisfied, so the auto-merge (queued by merge-to-main) fired — landing UNREVIEWED code carrying a failing Script Tests into staged-fb60. The broken test then blocked the downstream staged->main promotion (#548) and required a separate sub-PR (#547) to repair. Net: a required review was bypassed via skip-on-failed-dependency, and broken code entered the staged branch. Fix options: make review-sub-pr not 'needs:' the test jobs (so it runs independently and can post a real verdict / fail), or add a gate that treats 'skipped review-sub-pr' as non-passing for staged-* merges, or block auto-merge when any 'needs' dependency of a required check failed.

Across the waxen-sigma session each fix sub-PR re-triggered fresh reviews surfacing NEW false-positive / nitpick / stale findings with no convergence: e.g. a STALE 'line 99 word-split' finding posted after the fix already used a bash array; an FP 'git option injection' despite the 'git add --' separator; an FP 'output format change' that was a no-op (already space-joined); markdownlint MD040 + single-quote-escaping edge nits. Clearing required TWO separate /dso:fp-recovery opus passes (#550 and #548, each 0 critical/important/fragile). This is FP amplification across the two-channel boundary + cross-bot stacking, defeating the cycle cap. Related future work already noted in FP-RECOVERY-WORKFLOW.md: swap-maple-flyby (cycle-end arbiter) and side-pane-tithe (FP-rate measurement); this ticket tracks the specific two-channel double-review amplification.

## 2. Incident Overview
**Scenario Type:** User-flagged workflow defect (surfaced this session).
### Expected Behavior

Re-running `merge-to-main.sh` on a source branch that already has an open PR1 (source -> staged-*) should DETECT that open PR and iterate on it (re-push the head so review-sub-pr re-runs; advance to PR2 once PR1 merges), regardless of whether `--resume` was passed. The resumable state should be auto-detected.
### Actual Behavior

A bare re-invocation (no `--resume`) skips all existing-PR detection and mints a NEW staged-* ref (name embeds HEAD-sha + timestamp, always unique) + a NEW PR1 each time. Observed this session: #553 -> #554 -> #555, same source branch `fix/fp-recovery-guidance`, three different staged bases, three full CI re-runs. Documented prior art in the code comment at merge-to-main-pr.sh:2933 (#490/#492, same class).
### Root Cause (pre-investigation hypothesis)

The existing-open-PR detection (`gh pr list --head \$BRANCH --state open` at merge-to-main-pr.sh:2936) and the advance-to-PR2 logic (line 2893) are BOTH gated behind `if [[ \${_RESUME:-0} -eq 1 ]]`. Detection should run unconditionally; `--resume` should remain an optional fast-path, not a precondition.
### Constraints
- The version-bump phase (_phase_source_branch_version_bump) must not double-bump when reusing an existing PR1.
- Fail-safe: any gh/git uncertainty must default to the safe path (do not advance / do not reuse a wrong PR), preserving the existing `_resume_should_advance_to_staged` conservatism.
### Affected file
plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main-pr.sh (+ merge-helpers.sh state functions if relevant)

$ .claude/scripts/dso ticket list --parent=waxen-sigma --status=open
$ .claude/scripts/dso ticket list --parent=99f1-153c --status=open

The alias 'waxen-sigma' returns an empty array; the canonical ID returns the 11 tasks. Since Phase A sets primary_ticket_id to the user-selected value (the alias, when the user picks by number), --parent receives the alias and silently returns [].
ROOT CAUSE B — grep -c '"ticket_id"' undercounts single-line JSON:

The list CLI emits a single-line JSON array. auto-resume.md and the Preplanning Gate count children with `grep -c '"ticket_id"'`, which counts matching LINES (1), not occurrences. True occurrence count via `grep -o '"ticket_id"' | wc -l` is 11.
$ .claude/scripts/dso ticket list --parent=99f1-153c --status=open | grep -c '"ticket_id"'
$ .claude/scripts/dso ticket list --parent=99f1-153c --status=open | grep -o '"ticket_id"' | wc -l
$ .claude/scripts/dso ticket list --parent=99f1-153c --status=open | wc -l
Either defect alone breaks the count; with the alias they compound to [] -> 0.
### 3. Action History
1. /dso:sprint invoked with no arg; user selected epic #1 (waxen-sigma, in_progress).
2. Phase A routed to auto-resume.md; clause (b) ran ACTIVE=$({ list --parent=waxen-sigma --status=open; list --parent=waxen-sigma --status=in_progress; } | grep -c '"ticket_id"').
3. ACTIVE=0 reported despite 11 open task children confirmed via per-ticket `ticket show`.
### 5. Skills and Workflows
* skills/sprint/prompts/auto-resume.md clauses (b)/(c)
* skills/sprint/SKILL.md Preplanning Gate Step 1 (same grep -c pattern + OPEN/ALL counters)
* Both consume the line-based grep count; the Preplanning Gate ALSO uses it, so a non-resumed epic with 0 open / N closed could misroute too.
#### Impact

A resumed sprint with outstanding work silently skips to validation/closure instead of executing remaining tasks — high-impact correctness defect on the resume path. The operator only catches it by cross-checking per-ticket status manually (as happened here).

VERDICT: LIVE — bug confirmed unfixed as of HEAD bb39c4f334.

## Staleness Check
- Ticket created_at: 2026-06-02T18:21:01 UTC
- git log since then for auto-resume.md: zero commits touching the file
- grep for '.sprint-active' in auto-resume.md: NO MATCHES
- Bug is present and unpatched.

## Exact Location
File: plugins/dso/skills/sprint/prompts/auto-resume.md
Lines 55-57 (the Phase C routing):
  Line 55: '   5. After scan: if repo is clean, proceed to Phase C'
  Line 57: '   - Proceed to Phase C.'

The marker creation is absent at both Phase C entry points. The auto-resume path (section d) proceeds directly to Phase C without touching .sprint-active.

## Root Cause
Phase A of SKILL.md (line 157-158) creates the marker:
  touch "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.sprint-active"

Phase I (line 3110-3111) removes it:
  rm -f "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.sprint-active"

The auto-resume path (auto-resume.md) bypasses Phase A entirely and routes straight to Phase C. Since Phase I removes .sprint-active on graceful session close, a resumed sprint session starts without the marker → check-session-merge-only.sh hook is inactive → direct commits to session branch are ungated.

## Fix Approach
In plugins/dso/skills/sprint/prompts/auto-resume.md, add the touch command BEFORE 'Proceed to Phase C' in section (d). Exact insertion point: after line 55 ('After scan: if repo is clean, proceed to Phase C') and also after line 57 ('Proceed to Phase C.') — or consolidate into one block at the single final 'Proceed to Phase C.' on line 57.

Recommended: Add a labeled block just before 'Proceed to Phase C.' on line 57:

  ```bash
  # Re-create sprint-active marker (auto-resume path bypasses Phase A)
  touch "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.sprint-active"
  ```
  Then proceed to Phase C.

Mirror the exact command from SKILL.md line 158 verbatim: touch "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.sprint-active"

## RED Test Plan
Existing test (tests/hooks/test-sprint-skill-sprint-active-lifecycle.sh) only checks SKILL.md Phase A/I — does not cover auto-resume.md.

Recommended RED test (structural, execution-based):
  File: tests/hooks/test-sprint-auto-resume-sprint-active.sh
  Assert: auto-resume.md contains 'touch.*\.sprint-active' (grep -q)
  This will FAIL (RED) before the fix and PASS (GREEN) after.
  Pattern mirrors the existing lifecycle test Assertion 1.
  Non-behavioral rationale: auto-resume.md is LLM-executed skill prose, not a runnable script — structural grep is the correct behavioral-testing-standard approach for skill files per the 'structural skill test' category.

### 1. Technical Environment
* **code_version:** 4bf355cfdd0718adcc4fa04af021d14cefb2a675
* **Component:** plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/runner.py (findings parser); surfaced by the `review-sub-pr` CI job (.github/workflows/ci.yml) during the merge-to-main two-channel flow.
### 2. Incident Overview
* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior
#### Expected Behavior

The dso_ci_review runner should tolerate an LLM findings response that is valid JSON wrapped in Markdown code fences (e.g. a payload beginning with ```json and ending with ```), strip the fences, and parse the enclosed object. Here the enclosed object was `{"findings": [], "summary": "..."}` — i.e. zero findings — so the review should have reported a clean pass for that reviewer call. Bug f148-2cb6-8b7e-4cdd (closed; R1-R7 multi-PR fixes 67f75a2be6 / d8a7f93b58 / e1a8c8ca37 / 85bd8475af) was intended to make the runner robust to non-JSON / fallback-chain responses; fenced-JSON handling appears either uncovered by that work or regressed.
#### Actual Behavior
The runner emitted (verbatim from the CI job log):
ERROR: LLM returned non-JSON response (length=1187); cannot parse as findings.

ERROR [preview]: ```json
{
  "findings": [],
  "summary": "This diff updates documentation and test contracts for the dso plugin: ... No security vulnerabilities ... are present in the diff. ..."

The preview shows the LLM response WAS well-formed JSON (`{"findings": [], "summary": "..."}`) — it was simply enclosed in a ```json fenced code block. The parser treated the fenced payload as non-JSON and discarded it (including its empty `findings` array). A subsequent fallback path then produced blocking findings, ending with:
ERROR: llm-review found blocking finding(s) — 1 critical, 1 important (see findings JSON above and 2 PR review comments for details)

Net effect: a reviewer call that legitimately returned zero findings was discarded as a parse failure, and the `review-sub-pr` required check failed (1 critical + 1 important from the fallback path), blocking PR #557 and aborting the merge-to-main pipeline ("PR1 #557 reached terminal failure state — refusing to advance to PR2").
### 5. Skills and Workflows
* dso_ci_review runner (`runner.py`) findings-parse path
* `review-sub-pr` CI job (work→staged channel) in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
* `merge-to-main.sh` two-channel staged-release flow (PR1→PR2)
### 6. Logs / Evidence
* CI run: https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/actions/runs/26846036445/job/79167795371
* Related (closed) ticket: f148-2cb6-8b7e-4cdd — same family (non-JSON response handling); this fenced-valid-JSON case was not covered or has regressed.

* Reproduction is non-deterministic: depends on whether the review LLM wraps its JSON payload in Markdown code fences on a given call. The runner should deterministically strip a leading/trailing ```json ... ``` (and bare ``` ... ```) fence before JSON parsing.

The 1f5f fix must prevent the umbrella from being base=main (option ii — relocate the GitHubPRDefenseStore substrate / stop opening a base=main draft), OR scope check-staged-head to the actual promotion PR. FIX IMPLEMENTED + committed (bace2dc4ba): check-staged-head passes draft PRs (the umbrella is always a draft) so its failure no longer contaminates PR1's shared head SHA; ready_for_review added to triggers to close the draft->ready bypass. Enforcement intact (non-draft non-staged still blocks). Behavioral test 5/5. Combined with Fix C (resume fallback excludes base=main umbrella) in 78163b1407, all three 1f5f harms are now addressed. Landing on branch fix/merge-to-main-resume-hardening.

## 2. Incident Overview
**Scenario Type:** User-flagged process non-conformance.
### Expected Behavior

The session worktree should reach main only through the conforming promotion path (merge-to-main.sh: source -> staged-* PR1 with review-sub-pr, staged-* -> main PR2 with llm-review; or the MQ model under MQ-4). No standalone draft PR that proposes a direct session-worktree -> main merge should exist.
### Actual Behavior

sprint Phase A (ci-pr mode) calls create-sprint-draft-pr.sh, which runs `gh pr create --draft --base $_DEFAULT_BRANCH(main) --head $SESSION_BRANCH` (create-sprint-draft-pr.sh:113-116; also :46,:62). Its stated purpose is to be the GitHubPRDefenseStore substrate (a PR to attach per-story review defenses to), but as a base=main/head=session PR it (a) implies a direct session->main merge our process does not perform, (b) lingers alongside the staged-tier PRs that actually carry promotion, and (c) would bypass staged review if marked ready.

This overlaps MQ-4 (40f7-e831-b9e8-4158), which rewrites the promotion path to 'session->main direct' through the merge queue and retires the staged-*/PR1/PR2 tiers. Under MQ-4 a session->main PR becomes the REAL promotion PR (through the queue), which may SUBSUME this umbrella draft PR. plugins/dso/scripts/create-sprint-draft-pr.sh; plugins/dso/skills/sprint/SKILL.md (Phase A Draft PR Creation, ~line 175-192).

## VERDICT: CONFIRMED — same defect as abdf-8347-45f1-4ace (duplicate facets of one root cause)

### Duplicate/Facets Call
These are TWO FACETS of the SAME defect, not strict duplicates. 3349 (this ticket) was filed first (timestamp 1780430972) and describes the issue verbatim with a confirmed workaround. abdf (timestamp 1780444182) provides additional details including the git flow trace (steps 1-5), the exact error text, and the bypass escape hatch used. Recommend: fix against 3349 (primary), close abdf as duplicate with cross-reference.

### Exact Files and Lines

1. **plugins/dso/skills/sprint/prompts/per-worktree-review-commit.md** — Step 3.5 (lines 131-139): The offending copy instruction. Introduced in commit 29c8c6c8ad (chore: bump version to v1.17.23, 2026-05-23) as part of fix for bug e081-63c0. The step copies SESSION_ROOT/.sprint-active into WORKTREE_PATH/.sprint-active unconditionally before the Step 4 commit.

2. **plugins/dso/scripts/check-session-merge-only.sh** — lines 27-36: The primary checkout exemption. The hook exits 0 only when git-common-dir == git-dir (primary checkout). In a linked agent worktree, git-dir is .git/worktrees/agent-<hash>/... (not equal to git-common-dir), so the hook is ACTIVE. Lines 38-44 check for .sprint-active at REPO_ROOT of the worktree (which has now been populated by Step 3.5). Lines 99-103 reject the commit.

3. **plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/single-agent-integrate.md** — Step 7.5 (lines 221-231): Same copy pattern for single-agent callers. Same collision applies there.

### Root Cause

The e081-63c0 fix (PR #319, 2026-05-23) added .sprint-active propagation to agent sub-branch worktrees to satisfy check-sprint-trailer.sh's 4-cell enforcement matrix. However, check-session-merge-only.sh ALSO reads .sprint-active at REPO_ROOT and enforces merge-only on ALL linked worktrees (its 'primary checkout' exemption was added for merge-to-main.sh's version-bump case, not for agent sub-branch worktrees).

The two-tier design intent: agent sub-branch worktrees SHOULD commit directly (that is their purpose — the session worktree is merge-only, agent worktrees are commit targets). But check-session-merge-only.sh cannot distinguish 'session worktree (merge-only)' from 'agent sub-branch worktree (commit-allowed)' — both are linked worktrees from git's perspective.

The fix for e081-63c0 introduced a new invariant conflict: to enforce DSO-Story trailer (check-sprint-trailer.sh), .sprint-active MUST be present in the agent worktree. To not reject the per-task commit (check-session-merge-only.sh), .sprint-active MUST NOT be present in the agent worktree. These are mutually exclusive on the same agent worktree.

### Fix Approach (COPY SIDE — no safeguard edit required)

Preferred fix: modify Step 3.5 in per-worktree-review-commit.md to add a REMOVE step immediately after the Step 4 commit succeeds, so .sprint-active is cleaned up before the next git hook fires. Alternatively (and more robust): remove the copy entirely and instead pass sprint state to check-sprint-trailer.sh via an environment variable (DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=1) injected into the commit call, rather than relying on the filesystem marker.

The cleanest fix is: Step 3.5 should copy .sprint-active INTO the agent worktree ONLY for the duration of the check-sprint-trailer.sh gate, then remove it immediately after (before the git commit invocation runs the pre-commit hooks). But this is difficult because the copy is used by pre-commit hooks triggered BY the commit, not before it.

Better: keep the copy (Step 3.5) but add a Step 3.5b cleanup step that REMOVES .sprint-active from the agent worktree immediately after the Step 4 commit completes (whether the commit succeeds or fails). This ensures the marker is present for the commit hooks but does not persist.

Wait — the hooks fire during git commit, so the marker must be present at hook execution time. A pre/post approach won't work.

Correct fix: check-session-merge-only.sh needs to distinguish agent worktrees from the session worktree. This CAN be done on the COPY side: instead of copying .sprint-active (which trips check-session-merge-only.sh), propagate sprint state via DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE_CONTEXT=1 env var in the COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md invocation. check-sprint-trailer.sh would need to accept this env var as an alternative signal. This avoids modifying check-session-merge-only.sh (a safeguard file).

Alternatively: per-worktree-review-commit.md Step 3.5 could be updated to NOT copy .sprint-active and instead set DSO_SPRINT_TRAILER_REQUIRED=1 env var, while check-sprint-trailer.sh is updated to accept that env var as an equivalent to .sprint-active presence. check-sprint-trailer.sh is NOT a safeguard file (it is enforcement, but the rule:no-safeguard-edits list names pre-commit hooks and review-gate.sh, test-gate scripts — check-sprint-trailer.sh is not listed as a safeguard, only check-session-merge-only.sh qualifies as a session-safety safeguard under that rule).

**DOES THIS REQUIRE SAFEGUARD APPROVAL?**
check-session-merge-only.sh IS a safeguard file per rule:no-safeguard-edits. The preferred fix does NOT modify check-session-merge-only.sh. The fix modifies:
- per-worktree-review-commit.md (doc/prompt file — not a safeguard)
- single-agent-integrate.md (same)
- check-sprint-trailer.sh (hook, but not listed as a merge-only safeguard — it enforces trailer, not commit routing)

**This fix does NOT require safeguard approval.**

### Red Test Plan

Test file: tests/hooks/test-check-session-merge-only.sh (existing, add new test case)

New test (RED before fix):
- Name: test_agent_worktree_with_copied_sprint_active_accepts_non_merge_commit
- Setup: create main repo + linked worktree simulating agent-worktree (path containing /.claude/worktrees/agent-); touch .sprint-active in the linked worktree root; create a non-merge commit in the linked worktree
- After fix: assert exit 0 (commit accepted without bypass)
- Currently: assert exit 1 (confirms RED)

Alternatively, test the fix approach (env-var propagation path):
- New test file: tests/hooks/test-check-sprint-trailer-env-var.sh
- Setup: agent worktree without .sprint-active, but DSO_SPRINT_TRAILER_REQUIRED=1 env var set
- Assert: check-sprint-trailer.sh enforces trailer requirement (exit 1 when trailer absent)
- Assert: check-sprint-trailer.sh passes when trailer present

Existing test file for conventions: tests/hooks/test-check-session-merge-only.sh (see make_linked_worktree helper pattern, tests 1-14).

### Feasibility

HIGH feasibility. The fix is localized to:
1. per-worktree-review-commit.md Step 3.5 (remove the filesystem copy, replace with env-var approach)
2. single-agent-integrate.md Step 7.5 (same change)
3. check-sprint-trailer.sh (add env-var acceptance path as OR condition to .sprint-active check)

No safeguard file modification required. Tests follow existing patterns in test-check-session-merge-only.sh and test-check-sprint-trailer.sh.

content.text: ### 1. Technical Environment
* **code_version:** ed2792c71457a45e494bf6b2d44859f4163acd46
* **scripts:** plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main-pr.sh (_phase_staged_intermediate PR1 wait), plugins/dso/scripts/wait-for-pr.sh
* **workflow:** .github/workflows/check-staged-head.yml (on: pull_request: branches:[main])
* **context:** /dso:sprint waxen-sigma — merge-to-main after closing the Phase A draft PR
### 2. Incident Overview
* **Scenario Type:** Release-pipeline blocker (two-channel staged promotion)
#### Expected Behavior

Per merge-to-main-pr.sh design comments (lines 748-764): PR1 (source->staged-*) requires ONLY review-sub-pr (sub-PR ruleset); check-staged-head is a PR2 (staged-*->main) requirement (main ruleset). So PR1's wait must not be blocked by check-staged-head.
#### Actual Behavior
PR1 (worktree-20260602-122923 -> staged-*) is declared a terminal failure on 'check-staged-head':
"ERROR: PR1 #559 has failed required check(s): checks=check-staged-head"
Root cause chain:

1. sprint Phase A opened draft PR #556 (session -> main). check-staged-head.yml (on: pull_request branches:[main]) fired on PR #556 and FAILED (head 'worktree-*' != 'staged-*' pattern) — correct for a session->main PR, which should never exist in the two-channel model.

2. merge-to-main created the version-bump commit (ed2792c714) on the session branch WHILE #556 was still open, so check-staged-head ran on ed2792c714 and recorded a FAILED status permanently on that commit.
3. The user closed #556, but the recorded failed check-staged-head status on ed2792c714 persists.

4. merge-to-main PR1 (#558, then #559) reuses ed2792c714 as head. wait-for-pr.sh polls 'gh pr checks <pr>' which reports ALL checks on the head commit — including the stale failed check-staged-head — and exits non-zero. merge-to-main treats this as a PR1 terminal failure and refuses to advance to PR2.
#### Two contributing defects
(a) merge-to-main does not close/guard the Phase A draft session->main PR before creating the version-bump commit, allowing check-staged-head to contaminate the shared commit.
(b) wait-for-pr.sh / merge-to-main PR1 wait does not scope required checks to the PR1 set (review-sub-pr); it treats every reported check (incl. PR2-only check-staged-head) as blocking.
#### Suggested directions (not prescriptive)
- merge-to-main should close (or refuse to proceed with) an open session->main draft PR before the bump; OR create the bump commit only after that PR is closed.
- The PR1 wait should restrict to PR1's actually-required checks (review-sub-pr), ignoring statuses for checks not required by the staged-* ruleset.
### 5. Skills and Workflows

* Workaround that should work: rewrite the session head (reset to last work commit + let merge-to-main regenerate a fresh, uncontaminated version-bump commit) AFTER the draft PR is closed, so PR1's head has no check-staged-head status.

## Worktree-Isolation Investigation Detail (for later analysis)

Detected during internal dogfooding of /dso:sprint waxen-sigma. Two of eight isolation:worktree dispatches across two batches ran UN-isolated and wrote into the session worktree instead of an isolated agent worktree.

### Occurrences (2 of 8 dispatches)

|-------|------|-----------|---------|----------------------|
| L0 | b5fd-7682 | dso:red-test-writer | LEAKED | a3dd4ca9bba3376f5 |
| L0 | 5e96-ea32 | general-purpose | isolated OK | ac6b4f4e43f34ed5e |
| L0 | 55c7-f127 | dso:red-test-writer | isolated OK | a019f7c13d2d3e811 |
| L0 | 315a-77fb | general-purpose | isolated OK | a23215ee70e2bd8b6 |
| L1 | 3da3-a959 | general-purpose | LEAKED | a616dc9a6b2a2903d |
| L1 | 2298-45c0 | general-purpose | isolated OK | a7772b85366a07abe |
| L1 | 71bb-83b5 | general-purpose | isolated OK | aca7a4de7ed0a016f |

Transcript output files live under the session tasks dir:
/private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-joeoakhart-digital-service-orchestra-worktrees-worktree-20260602-122923/<run>/tasks/<agentId>.output

### Reliable diagnostic signal
The task-completion notification's <worktree> block presence/absence perfectly separated isolated from leaked dispatches:
- isolated (6): notification carried <worktree><worktreePath>.../agent-<id></worktreePath>...; an agent-<id> entry appeared in `git worktree list`.
- leaked (2): notification had NO <worktree> block; NO agent-<id> worktree was ever created; the sub-agent's own `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` resolved to the SESSION worktree; the agent's new file appeared staged in the session worktree (`git status --short`).

### What it is NOT
- NOT the prompt-path-leak failure mode (6b67-2aad / 1053-4ec3): dispatch prompts contained only SESSION_BRANCH (a branch name), SESSION_HEAD (a sha), and relative paths — no session-worktree absolute path. The agents correctly derived paths from their own `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; that simply resolved to the session worktree because no isolated worktree was allocated for that dispatch.
- NOT agent-type-specific: leaks hit both dso:red-test-writer (b5fd) and general-purpose (3da3).
- NOT reaping (907d): the worktree was never created in the first place (no agent-<id> ever in `git worktree list`), as opposed to created-then-removed.

### Conditions / hypotheses to test later
- Both leaks involved a single-new-file write; both occurred in batches dispatched as 3–4 parallel isolation:worktree Agent calls in one message. Hypothesis: a race / nondeterministic allocation failure in the harness worktree provisioning under parallel dispatch (since siblings in the same batch isolated fine, it is per-dispatch flaky, not batch-wide).
- Reproduction signal to capture next time: log whether the notification carries a <worktree> block; cross-check `git worktree list` immediately after dispatch.
- Harness: Claude Code desktop, isolation:"worktree". Capture exact harness version on recurrence.

### Recovery used (worked both times, no data loss)
Back up staged session changes to a patch -> `git stash` to clean the session tree -> `git worktree add agent-<task>-recovered -b worktree-agent-<task>-recovered <session-HEAD>` -> restore files + .test-index entry from the patch -> record-test-status -> commit (with DSO-Story trailer, WITHOUT copying .sprint-active) -> harvest-worktree.sh -> drop stash. Now 3 of 10 dispatches (b5fd, 3da3, 4268). All 3 leaks were single-file writes by general-purpose-family agents; siblings in each batch isolated fine -> per-dispatch flaky. agentId aee423cad188e9fd9; transcript in session tasks dir.

## Observed Pattern (full-sprint dataset: 11 dispatches)

| Batch | Dispatch mode | Size | Agents (type) | Leaked |
|-------|---------------|------|---------------|--------|
| 1 | PARALLEL (one message) | 4 | 315a(gp), 5e96(gp), 55c7(red-test-writer), b5fd(red-test-writer) | b5fd (4th) |
| 2 | PARALLEL (one message) | 3 | 2298(gp), 3da3(gp), 71bb(gp) | 3da3 (2nd) |
| 3 | PARALLEL (one message) | 2 | 4268(gp), 6f49(gp) | 4268 (1st) |
| 4 | SOLO (one agent) | 1 | ef64(gp) | none |
| 5 | SOLO (re-dispatch) | 1 | ef64(gp) | none |

### The pattern: concurrency, not agent type
- **Every parallel (same-message) batch leaked EXACTLY ONE agent** — 1 of 4, 1 of 3, 1 of 2. The "exactly one per batch regardless of batch size" signal strongly suggests a race in the harness's concurrent worktree provisioning where exactly one of the simultaneous allocations fails to materialize an isolated worktree (the agent then falls back to the session CWD).
- **Both SOLO dispatches isolated cleanly (0 leaks of 2).** No leak ever occurred when only one isolation:worktree agent was provisioned at a time.
- **No agent-type correlation:** red-test-writer leaked 1/2 and succeeded 1/2; general-purpose leaked 2/9 and succeeded 7/9. Both types both leaked and succeeded.
- **No dispatch-order correlation:** the leaked agent was the 4th, then the 2nd, then the 1st in its batch — not a fixed position.

### Conclusion
There IS an observable pattern: leaks correlate with **concurrent multi-agent dispatch in a single message**, not with agent type, model, or task. Solo dispatch was 100% reliable (2/2); every concurrent batch produced exactly one isolation failure (3/3 batches).

### Actionable mitigations to evaluate
1. Workaround available today: dispatch isolation:worktree agents ONE AT A TIME (solo) — eliminates the race at the cost of parallelism.
2. Or keep parallel dispatch + add the orchestrator-side post-dispatch verification already used here: check each completion notification for a <worktree> block and cross-check `git worktree list`; on a miss, recover via the RECOVERED_FROM_SESSION path. (3/3 leaks recovered with zero data loss this way.)
3. Upstream (Claude Code): the concurrent-provisioning path appears to have a one-loser race; capture harness version on next recurrence and file upstream with this dataset.

content.text: ## Description

**What**: Extend /dso:fix-bug Phase G to run after the 4911-c7ba bug-type classification step. On a bug closed with reason="Fixed: ...", a sonnet sub-agent evaluates extraction conditions (not caught by an existing test AND generalizable), performs mandatory pre-extraction redaction of credentials/tokens/keys/PII/internal IDs, requires non-vacuous scope_claim and falsification fields, writes the NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE comment + negative-example tag atomically, falls back to bug_type_slug=unclassified + retro-needs-classification tag when 4911 did not set a slug, logs a SKIP_RECORD comment on every skip, and validates intent_ids_if_applicable against 94ed manifest entries at write time.
**Why**: This is the capture half of the walking-skeleton loop — without it the corpus is never populated.
**Scope**:

- IN: Phase G prompt/logic edits; sonnet extraction evaluation; redaction step; scope_claim/falsification vacuity gate; atomic comment+tag write with rollback; unclassified fallback; SKIP_RECORD audit comment; intent_id write-time validation.
- OUT: retrieval (draft-3); graduation (draft-5/6); lifecycle reopening hook (draft-7).
## Done Definitions
- Phase G extraction executes only after the 4911-c7ba bug-type classification step has run, and reads the bug_type_<slug> tag that step sets ← Satisfies: sc-2

- On a closed-Fixed bug meeting extraction conditions (not caught by an existing test and generalizable pattern) the sonnet step produces a NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE comment whose missed_signal_summary describes what FAILED to be detected, and on a bug not meeting the conditions it produces a SKIP_RECORD comment with decision=skip and a one-sentence skip_reason ← Satisfies: sc-2

- Credentials, tokens, keys, PII, customer/user identifiers, and internal-only IDs are redacted from all NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE string fields before write; when redaction confidence is insufficient the extraction is skipped and a SKIP_RECORD comment with decision=skip and a one-sentence skip_reason is emitted ← Satisfies: sc-2

- When scope_claim or falsification is vacuous the extraction is skipped and a SKIP_RECORD comment with decision=skip and a one-sentence skip_reason is emitted, matching the SKIP_RECORD shape used by the conditions-not-met and redaction skip paths so every skip leaves an audit comment ← Satisfies: sc-2
- The NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE comment plus negative-example tag are applied as a single atomic unit that rolls back if either write fails ← Satisfies: sc-2

- When 4911 classification did not set bug_type_<slug>, the record uses bug_type_slug=unclassified and the ticket receives a retro-needs-classification tag; intent_ids_if_applicable values are validated against 94ed manifest entries at write time, with invalid values causing write failure or being dropped with a warning ← Satisfies: sc-2
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic ← Satisfies: sc-2
## Considerations

- [Dependency] EXTERNAL BLOCKER: SC2 ordering requires 4911-c7ba's bug-type classification step to set bug_type_<slug>; do not create an in-epic depends_on for 4911 — coordinate via the documented cross-epic dependency.
- [Dependency] EXTERNAL BLOCKER: intent_id validation reads 94ed-f55c manifest entries; the manifest schema is owned by 94ed.
- [Risk] Inverted-polarity: missed_signal_summary must describe what FAILED to be detected, NOT what the test checks — assert polarity explicitly in tests using the canonical contract example.
- [Privacy] Redaction is mandatory pre-write; a fixture bug carrying a token must result in redaction or a skip, never a leaked credential.

- [CrossStory] The NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE and SKIP_RECORD comments must carry a reliable creation timestamp so draft-5's since-last-retro watermark can compare its cursor against them when counting examples_extracted_since_last_retro and examples_skipped_count (SC9(l)); stamp the timestamp at write time on both comment kinds.
- [CrossEpic] 411b auto-created mutation-breach bugs flow through Phase G with no special handling per the epic cross-epic comment.

content.text: ## Description

**What**: Extend /dso:retro with a Graduation Phase where an opus sub-agent reads all negative-example bugs without a promoted-to-standard:* tag via a single CLI query and identifies candidates via (a) frequency floor (>=3 examples same bug_type_slug with distinct root-cause fingerprints, collapsing groups with >=80% missed_signal_summary similarity to one signal) and (b) cross-slug semantic match via a single falsifiable predicate naming a specific input state/code path AND expected observable outcome (theme-level labels rejected). Each candidate is surfaced with a 4-field draft rule, >=3 evidence_citations with quoted missed_signal_summary, and explicit provenance. A PRE-DRAFT validation checks existing behavioral-testing-standard.md rules and blocks surfacing on unresolved overlap. A SYCOPHANCY GATE on user acceptance requires a non-empty, non-restating answer to the distinct-coverage challenge before PR drafting, else marks the candidate challenged-rejected. Emits structured RETRO_TELEMETRY whose examples_extracted_since_last_retro and examples_skipped_count counters use a since-last-retro watermark.
**Why**: This is the promotion engine that turns accumulated examples into rule candidates.
**Scope**:

- IN: Graduation Phase logic; single CLI query; frequency-floor trigger + collapse; cross-slug falsifiable-predicate trigger; 4-field draft + evidence_citations + provenance; pre-draft conflict check; sycophancy gate; since-last-retro watermark; RETRO_TELEMETRY emission.
- OUT: the atomic PR-first graduation write + tagging (draft-6); the safeguard no-auto-commit assertion (draft-6); end-to-end fixtures (draft-8).
## Done Definitions
- The Graduation Phase reads all bugs tagged negative-example and lacking any promoted-to-standard:* tag via a single ticket-CLI query ← Satisfies: sc-5

- Frequency-floor candidates require >=3 examples sharing a bug_type_slug with distinct root-cause fingerprints, and a group whose examples are >=80% missed_signal_summary similar is collapsed to a single signal rather than counted as N ← Satisfies: sc-5

- Cross-slug candidates are surfaced only via a single falsifiable predicate naming a specific input state or code path and an expected observable outcome, and theme-level labels are not surfaced ← Satisfies: sc-5

- Each surfaced candidate carries a 4-field draft rule (rule_statement, rationale, anti_pattern_example, correct_pattern_example), at least 3 evidence_citations with quoted missed_signal_summary, and explicit provenance ← Satisfies: sc-5
- A candidate overlapping an existing behavioral-testing-standard.md rule is blocked from surfacing unless revised-as-modification or justified-as-distinct ← Satisfies: sc-5
- On user acceptance the sycophancy gate blocks PR drafting and marks the candidate challenged-rejected when the distinct-coverage answer is empty or merely restates the rule ← Satisfies: sc-5
- The Graduation Phase emits RETRO_TELEMETRY with the specified counter fields on completion ← Satisfies: sc-5

- The RETRO_TELEMETRY counters examples_extracted_since_last_retro and examples_skipped_count count only NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE and SKIP_RECORD comments whose creation timestamp is after the since-last-retro watermark, where the watermark is read from the prior RETRO_TELEMETRY artifact timestamp or a stored last-retro cursor ← Satisfies: sc-5
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic ← Satisfies: sc-5

- [Dependency] EXTERNAL BLOCKER: pre-draft conflict check reads behavioral-testing-standard.md structure established by a03c-d55e; slug grouping uses 4911-c7ba taxonomy.

- [Risk] Cross-slug over-clustering residual is opus self-assessment; the single-falsifiable-predicate constraint and sycophancy gate are the spec mitigations — assert both with THEME-only-rejection and empty-answer fixtures.

- [CrossStory] The RETRO_TELEMETRY counters examples_extracted_since_last_retro and examples_skipped_count (SC9(l)) count NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE and SKIP_RECORD comments produced by draft-2 Phase G. Establish a 'since last retro' watermark mechanism (read the prior RETRO_TELEMETRY artifact/comment timestamp, or a stored last-retro cursor) and count only comments created after it; rely on the creation timestamp draft-2 stamps on those comments.
- [CrossEpic] detected_by candidate-weighting signal lands with a34c-b345 observability epic; design the query so detected_by:<channel> filtering can be added without rework, but do not depend on it.

content.text: ## Description

**What**: Add a deterministic critic script to dso:story-decomposer that enforces three checks against the structured signals from draft-2: (a) each declared producer surface appears in the named producer story body and each consumer detection appears in the named consumer story body; (b) for every canonical_name with a corresponding plugins/dso/docs/contracts/<canonical_name>.md, the producer-side surface and consumer-side detection both match the contract doc's canonical_surface field; (c) cross-story edges are derived by matching consumes_signals.canonical_name against emits_signals.canonical_name. Each check emits a machine-distinguishable gate identifier on failure ("drift" for check (a), "canonical-anchor" for check (b), and the sc-4 post-pass emits "heuristic-undeclared-signal") rather than a single opaque critic-error, so downstream regression tests can assert which gate fired. On the f360-3a5b pre-fix fixture the critic emits the drift gate identifier and refuses to emit until surfaces are reconciled.
**Why**: This is the producer/consumer signaling-core enforcement that closes the original false-positive gap.
**Scope**:

- IN: the deterministic critic script; the three checks (a)/(b)/(c); a machine-distinguishable gate identifier per check (drift, canonical-anchor); the canonical_surface anchor against contract docs; cross-story edge derivation by canonical_name match; refuse-to-emit behavior keyed to the firing gate identifier; the f360-3a5b pre-fix fixture used to prove refusal.
- OUT: the heuristic zero-declaration post-pass (draft-5, which emits the heuristic-undeclared-signal identifier); the inline field schema (draft-2); preplanning fan-in (draft-4).
## Done Definitions

- Check (a) emits a critic failure tagged with the gate identifier "drift" when a declared producer surface is absent from the named producer story body or a consumer detection is absent from the named consumer story body ← Satisfies: sc-2

- Check (b) emits a critic failure tagged with the gate identifier "canonical-anchor" when a producer surface or consumer detection diverges from the canonical_surface field of the matching plugins/dso/docs/contracts/<canonical_name>.md ← Satisfies: sc-2
- Check (c) derives a cross-story edge by matching a consumes_signals.canonical_name to an emits_signals.canonical_name across the drafted stories ← Satisfies: sc-2

- Each of the three gates emits a distinct machine-readable gate identifier (drift, canonical-anchor, and the sc-4 post-pass heuristic-undeclared-signal) so a consumer can tell which gate fired without parsing prose ← Satisfies: sc-2
- Fed the f360-3a5b pre-fix fixture, the critic emits the drift gate identifier and the decomposer refuses to emit until the surfaces are reconciled ← Satisfies: sc-2

- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic, including one test per check, one asserting the three gate identifiers are pairwise distinct, and the f360 refusal case ← Satisfies: sc-2
## Considerations
- [Determinism] The critic is a deterministic script, not an LLM judgment; the original failure mode was prompt-directive enforcement that drifted.
- [Self-reference] The f360-3a5b pre-fix fixture must encode the producer copy-story / consumer copy:needed mismatch that the real f360 epic shipped with.
- [Coupling] Check (b) reads canonical_surface from draft-1's contract docs; if no contract doc exists for a canonical_name, check (b) is skipped for that name and only checks (a)/(c) apply.

- [Gate-identifiers] Each check emits a stable machine-distinguishable gate identifier (drift, canonical-anchor; the sc-4 post-pass emits heuristic-undeclared-signal) instead of a single opaque critic-error, so draft-6's distinct-gate regression assertion is mechanically verifiable. Treat these identifier strings as a contract draft-6 depends on; do not rename without updating the regression fixtures.
## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

**What**: Extend mutation-testing.yml with Ruby (mutant), JS/TS (Stryker --incremental), and Go (go-gremlins) parallel matrix jobs alongside the Python pilot; Flask is covered by the Python job.
**Why**: Delivers the polyglot informational-mode increment; completes the shippable Phase 1-2 release gate.
**Scope**:

- IN: per-stack tool install pinned to mutation.<stack>.tool_version with mutation.<stack>.fallback_versions chain; per-stack runtime cap via mutation.<stack>.timeout_seconds (Stryker 600, mutmut 900, mutant 1200, gremlins 900); partial-result emission with runtime_exceeded=true on timeout; matrix fail-fast false; ALL_STACKS_TIMEOUT prominent warning with no bug ticket and aggregate_kill_rate=null when every stack times out; aggregate job merges all stack findings into one PR comment; dso-config.conf default keys for the new stacks.
- OUT: calibration auto-surfacing; threshold enforcement; onboarding/setup integration.
## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, the workflow runs Ruby (mutant), JS/TS (Stryker --incremental), and Go (go-gremlins) as parallel matrix jobs with fail-fast false, each installing its tool at mutation.<stack>.tool_version with a mutation.<stack>.fallback_versions chain ← Satisfies: sc-3
- When this story is complete, a stack that exceeds mutation.<stack>.timeout_seconds emits a partial findings result with runtime_exceeded=true rather than failing the job ← Satisfies: sc-3

- When this story is complete, when every stack returns runtime_exceeded=true the PR comment surfaces an ALL_STACKS_TIMEOUT warning, aggregate_kill_rate is null, and no bug ticket is created ← Satisfies: sc-3
- When this story is complete, the aggregate job merges all stack findings into a single PR comment using the MUTATION_TESTING_FINDINGS_<pr-number> marker ← Satisfies: sc-3

- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic (per-stack timeout partial-result emission, ALL_STACKS_TIMEOUT aggregation, multi-stack merge) ← Satisfies: sc-3
## Considerations
- [Cost] Three additional matrix jobs multiply per-PR CI minutes; per-stack timeout caps and the concurrency group from draft-1 bound the worst case.
- [Correctness] Monorepo incremental-mode diff scoping is a documented limitation (mutmut on shared packages); do not attempt to mitigate within this story.

content.text: ## Description

**What**: Create the regression fixture family at plugins/dso/tests/fixtures/cross-skill-integration/ with exactly three variants, each mapped one-to-one onto a distinct named gate: tag-fork/ (producer emits copy-story, consumer detects copy:needed — the f360-3a5b shape; fires the drift gate, check (a)), contract-mismatch/ (a contract-doc-bearing variant: ships plugins/dso/docs/contracts/<canonical_name>.md whose canonical_surface mismatches the producer surface / consumer detection; fires the canonical-anchor gate, check (b)), and zero-declaration/ (producer touches tag-emit patterns but declares zero signals; fires the heuristic-undeclared-signal post-pass, sc-4). The prior surface-typo-coherence variant is repurposed into contract-mismatch because the typo variant shipped no contract doc and so could never reach check (b), leaving the canonical-anchor gate exercised by no fixture. Each variant fed through /dso:brainstorm -> /dso:preplanning independently fires exactly one of the three distinct gate identifiers. A dedicated regression test asserts the three pairings and fails on any collision or on the canonical-anchor gate going unfired.
**Why**: Without a regression family, the three gates from draft-3/draft-4/draft-5 can silently rot, and the canonical-anchor gate in particular was reachable by no fixture.
**Scope**:

- IN: exactly three fixture variants (tag-fork, contract-mismatch, zero-declaration) mapped one-to-one onto the three named gates; the contract doc shipped by the contract-mismatch variant; feeding each through brainstorm -> preplanning; the regression test asserting three distinct gate identifiers and failing on collision or on canonical-anchor going unfired.
- OUT: adding a fourth variant (the epic constrains the family to exactly three); the gates themselves (draft-3/draft-4/draft-5); the gate identifier strings (draft-3 owns them).
## Done Definitions
- The directory plugins/dso/tests/fixtures/cross-skill-integration/ contains exactly three variant subdirectories tag-fork, contract-mismatch, and zero-declaration ← Satisfies: sc-5
- The tag-fork variant fed through /dso:brainstorm then /dso:preplanning fires the drift gate identifier ← Satisfies: sc-5

- The contract-mismatch variant ships a contract doc whose canonical_surface mismatches its producer surface and consumer detection, and fed through brainstorm then preplanning it fires the canonical-anchor gate identifier ← Satisfies: sc-5
- The zero-declaration variant fed through brainstorm then preplanning fires the heuristic-undeclared-signal post-pass gate identifier ← Satisfies: sc-5

- The regression test asserts three distinct gate identifiers across the three fixtures and fails if any two fixtures fire the same gate or if the canonical-anchor gate is fired by none ← Satisfies: sc-5

- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic, including the three one-to-one fixture-gate assertions and the collision-detection assertion, run green via test-batched.sh ← Satisfies: sc-5
## Considerations

- [Distinct-gates] Each fixture maps one-to-one onto exactly one named gate: tag-fork -> drift, contract-mismatch -> canonical-anchor, zero-declaration -> heuristic-undeclared-signal. The regression test fails on any collision and on the canonical-anchor gate being fired by no fixture.

- [Variant-repurpose] The prior surface-typo-coherence variant is renamed and repurposed into contract-mismatch: it now ships a contract doc whose canonical_surface diverges from the producer surface and consumer detection, so check (b) is reachable. The typo variant could never reach check (b) because it shipped no contract doc (red-team / blue-team finding). The family stays at exactly three variants.

- [Coupling] This story depends on draft-3 (drift and canonical-anchor gate identifiers), draft-4 (fan-in gate), and draft-5 (heuristic-undeclared-signal post-pass) existing; the gate identifier strings asserted here are the contract draft-3 emits, so this test breaks if draft-3 renames an identifier.
- [Stability] Keep exactly three variants now per the epic's exactly-three constraint; the family is designed to grow in future post-mortems, not in this story.
## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

content.text: ## Description

**What**: Add threshold-mode enforcement: when mutation.calibration.completed=true and a stack's mutants_generated>0, compare its kill rate to mutation.threshold.<stack>.min_kill_rate; on breach auto-create a bug ticket with a structured 4-field blurb and content-hash dedup.
**Why**: Closes the feedback loop — surviving mutants become bug tickets that flow through /dso:fix-bug and 69e8 negative-example graduation (the steering-loop instance).
**Scope**:

- IN: gate on mutation.calibration.completed and per-stack mutants_generated>0; per-stack kill-rate vs min_kill_rate comparison; bug creation via .claude/scripts/dso ticket create bug pushing to the tickets orphan branch using the CI auth pattern; retry-with-backoff (3 attempts) and TICKET_CREATE_FAILED artifact + workflow annotation on final failure; 4-field blurb (CONTEXT/WHAT/THRESHOLD/NEXT_STEP, max 60 words total) where CONTEXT links to behavioral-testing-standard.md Tier-3 rationale and the 411b epic; content-hash dedup tag mutation-breach-<sha> where sha=hash(stack, source_file, mutant_locations); set detected_by:tests classification field and detected_by:tests tag (per a34c-b345 observability coordination).
- OUT: calibration surfacing (draft-3); onboarding/setup integration.
## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, the enforcement step runs only when mutation.calibration.completed is true and a stack's mutants_generated is greater than zero, and compares that stack's kill rate against mutation.threshold.<stack>.min_kill_rate ← Satisfies: sc-5

- When this story is complete, a kill-rate breach auto-creates a bug ticket via dso ticket create bug with retry-with-backoff over 3 attempts, writing a TICKET_CREATE_FAILED artifact plus a workflow annotation on final failure ← Satisfies: sc-5

- When this story is complete, the auto-created bug's CONTEXT field links to the behavioral-testing-standard.md Tier-3 rationale and the 411b epic, and the assembled CONTEXT/WHAT/THRESHOLD/NEXT_STEP blurb is at most 60 words total ← Satisfies: sc-5

- When this story is complete, the content-hash dedup tag mutation-breach-<sha> derives from (stack, source_file, mutant_locations) such that the same triple recurring across DISTINCT PRs produces the same tag and a single bug (no duplicate), while structurally-similar mutants in DIFFERENT source files produce different hashes and never collide into one bug ← Satisfies: sc-5

- When this story is complete, the auto-created bug includes a one-sentence WHAT field describing what mutation testing caught ← Validates Closure Check: "WHAT — one sentence on what mutation testing caught"

- When this story is complete, the auto-created bug includes a THRESHOLD field naming the specific threshold that fired plus the current kill rate ← Validates Closure Check: "THRESHOLD — specific threshold that fired plus current kill rate"

- When this story is complete, the auto-created bug includes a NEXT_STEP field instructing the investigating agent to investigate surviving mutants and not adjust the threshold ← Validates Closure Check: "NEXT_STEP — instructs investigating agent: investigate surviving mutants; do NOT adjust the threshold"

- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic (threshold gate, breach detection, retry/backoff, content-hash dedup, 4-field blurb assembly under 60 words) ← Satisfies: sc-5
## Considerations
- [Security] Bug-creation pushes to the tickets orphan branch using the same CI auth pattern as the Jira bridge / outbound checkpoint; do not introduce a new credential path.
- [Coordination] Per epic comments, set detected_by:tests classification and tag so a34c-b345's observability epic attributes mutation breaches to the tests channel.
- [Correctness] mutants_generated=0 must produce no bug ticket (PR touched only non-mutable code); ALL_STACKS_TIMEOUT must produce no bug ticket even in threshold mode.

- [Dedup-semantics] The content hash is over (stack, source_file, mutant_locations) only — never the PR number — so the same breach recurring across PRs collapses to one bug; source_file is part of the hash so similar mutants in different files cannot collide.

content.text: ## Description

**What**: Publish plugins/dso/docs/contracts/mutation-testing-findings.md (per-stack-result schema, aggregate-result schema with schema_version=1, unknown-field passthrough) and ship plugins/dso/workflows/mutation-testing.yml as a plugin template running a Python (mutmut) matrix job in calibration mode.
**Why**: This is the walking skeleton — the minimum end-to-end path proving the mutation-testing concept (contract -> CI run -> findings JSON -> PR comment) before polyglot expansion.
**Scope**:

- IN: findings contract markdown; mutation-testing.yml with pull_request trigger (types synchronize, opened; no branches filter; no pull_request_target; no push, per Operational Constraints Probe-2); concurrency group keyed to github.head_ref; skip-mutation-testing label opt-out; mutation.max_files_per_run (default 100) auto-skip with annotation; mutmut pinned to mutation.python.tool_version with mutation.python.fallback_versions chain and TOOL_INSTALL_FAILED annotation; incremental run over diffed Python files; findings JSON per contract; actions/upload-artifact telemetry; aggregate job upserting a PR comment with MUTATION_TESTING_FINDINGS_<pr-number> marker; GHA-summary-only fallback for fork PRs; scope-seal header block (SC8 in-workflow portion); dso-config.conf mutation.* default keys for Python; CLAUDE.md/contracts-index references are OUT (draft-8).
- OUT: Ruby/JS-TS/Go stacks; calibration auto-surfacing; threshold enforcement; onboarding/setup-script integration; standalone doc addenda.
## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, plugins/dso/docs/contracts/mutation-testing-findings.md exists and documents the per-stack-result schema, the aggregate-result schema with schema_version=1, and the unknown-field passthrough requirement ← Satisfies: sc-1
- When this story is complete, tooling that parses a findings JSON containing an unrecognized field re-emits that field unchanged in its output ← Satisfies: sc-1

- When this story is complete, plugins/dso/workflows/mutation-testing.yml triggers on pull_request types synchronize and opened with no branches filter, declares a concurrency group keyed to github.head_ref, contains no pull_request_target block, and contains no push block ← Satisfies: sc-2

- When this story is complete, a PR carrying the skip-mutation-testing label runs the workflow without executing the mutmut job and a PR whose mutable-file count exceeds mutation.max_files_per_run auto-skips with an annotation ← Satisfies: sc-2

- When this story is complete, the Python job installs mutmut at mutation.python.tool_version, falls back through mutation.python.fallback_versions on install failure, emits TOOL_INSTALL_FAILED on final failure, runs incremental mutation over diffed Python files, writes findings JSON per the contract, uploads it as a workflow artifact, and the aggregate job upserts a PR comment marked MUTATION_TESTING_FINDINGS_<pr-number> with a GHA-summary-only fallback ← Satisfies: sc-2
- When this story is complete, the mutation-testing.yml header contains the verbatim SCOPE-SEALED bash-out-of-scope block referencing the 411b epic and listing the supported stacks ← Satisfies: sc-8

- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic (findings-JSON emission, passthrough preservation, max_files_per_run skip-check, fallback-version chain) ← Satisfies: sc-2

- [Reliability] The aggregate PR-comment marker MUTATION_TESTING_FINDINGS_<pr-number> must be distinct from llm-review's marker so no comment-write race is possible.

- [Observability] Per EXTERNAL FRAMING (silent-sensor caution): mutants_generated is a distinct field; zero indicates the PR touched only non-mutable code and must not be conflated with a perfect kill rate.

content.text: ## Description

Why: the GraphQL mutation needs elevated workflow permissions that existing CI jobs do not grant, and the audit requires these be verified live. Scope IN: the CI job + permissions block, required-checks.txt registration, job ordering after llm-review, the SC10 six-check verification contract, the startup permission probe. Scope OUT: the resolution adapter logic itself (draft-5); the dogfooding run (draft-8).

- ci.yml declares a telemetry-collect job whose permissions block grants contents: write and pull-requests: write, runs after llm-review, and is registered in .github/required-checks.txt in the same change ← Satisfies: sc-10

- The repo workflow-permission default is write OR the job-level permissions cover the required scope, and a live resolveReviewThread mutation against a test thread on a sprint PR returns a non-error response (token can resolve threads) ← Satisfies: sc-10
- The pr_comments.bot_authors allowlist in .claude/dso-config.conf is populated with a non-empty list including the integrated bots ← Satisfies: sc-10

- An integration test exercises the telemetry-collect job's startup permission probe in a configuration-isolated environment (HOME set to an empty directory, no global git config, no pre-set environment variables) and the probe hard-errors on insufficient scope and passes on sufficient scope ← Satisfies: sc-10

- [Deployment] The job MUST be added to required-checks.txt in the same change as the workflow edit to avoid breaking branch-protection required-status-checks.

- Injecting a malformed bot-comment fixture causes the parser to exit 0 and write WARN: to stderr; CI stays green ← Satisfies: sc-6

**What**: Verify the per-language dynamic-import fail-open behavior of intent-header-source-check.sh for Python, JavaScript, and Ruby.

**Why**: Dynamic imports defeat static source-symbol matching; treating them as header_source_mismatch would produce false positives that erode trust in the signal. Fail-open with a warn keeps the check honest.

## VERDICT: LIVE — triggered when merge-to-main-pr.sh is invoked directly (bypass dispatcher) with MERGE_STRATEGY unset; OR when _state_init is re-invoked inside _phase_staged_intermediate or the PR2 advance block with MERGE_STRATEGY not exported into the sub-shell environment.

## ROOT CAUSE

Three  call sites in merge-to-main-pr.sh; all three are vulnerable if MERGE_STRATEGY is missing from the environment at call time:

1. **Line 2891** (top-level init): merge-to-main.sh dispatcher sets MERGE_STRATEGY and exports it (line 106). On the normal dispatcher path this is correct. HOWEVER: when merge-to-main-pr.sh is invoked DIRECTLY (not via dispatcher), MERGE_STRATEGY is derived at lines 70-78 but only within an `if [[ -z ... ]]` block that runs when MERGE_STRATEGY is absent. Crucially, after derivation, MERGE_STRATEGY is NOT exported — it remains a local shell var. When _state_init is called at line 2891, _state_init runs python3 via env passthrough. The python3 snippet at merge-helpers.sh:138 reads `os.environ.get('MERGE_STRATEGY', 'direct')`. If MERGE_STRATEGY is not exported to the environment when python3 is spawned, it defaults to 'direct' — even though the bash var is 'pr'.

2. **Line 2930** (PR2 advance block): BRANCH is mutated to the staged branch name. _state_init is called to create a new staged-branch-keyed state file. At this point, if MERGE_STRATEGY was not exported, the skeleton written for the staged branch also gets merge_strategy='direct'. This is the state file --resume will check on the NEXT invocation — the PR2 invocation.

3. **Line 1024** (_phase_staged_intermediate): Same risk. BRANCH is mutated to staged branch; _state_init is called; MERGE_STRATEGY must be in the exported environment.

## PRECISE FIELD-NAME BUG (corroborating the ticket's secondary note)

merge-helpers.sh line 138 writes a key named 'merge_strategy' (snake_case). merge-to-main.sh lines 82-88 read the key 'merge_strategy' (consistent). The two-field confusion in the ticket ('strategy' and 'merge_strategy') was a symptom of manual patching — the code only writes and reads 'merge_strategy'. There is NO second 'strategy' field written by any code path. The ticket's observation that patching 'strategy' alone did not fix the check is because 'strategy' is not the field being read at line 86 of the dispatcher.

## EXACT FILE + LINES

- **State write (bug site)**: plugins/dso/hooks/lib/merge-helpers.sh line 138 — `os.environ.get('MERGE_STRATEGY', 'direct')` — defaults to 'direct' when MERGE_STRATEGY env var absent
- **--resume check that aborts**: plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main.sh lines 82-101 — reads 'merge_strategy' from state JSON; rejects when != MERGE_STRATEGY (which IS correctly set by dispatcher)
- **Root cause**: merge-to-main-pr.sh lines 70-81 sets MERGE_STRATEGY as a bash local but does NOT export it, so when called directly the value is invisible to python3 spawned by _state_init

## TRIGGER CONDITIONS (precise)

- **Path 1** (CONFIRMED LIVE): merge-to-main-pr.sh called directly (not via merge-to-main.sh dispatcher). MERGE_STRATEGY is derived at line 70-78 but not exported. _state_init at line 2891 writes merge_strategy='direct'. Subsequent --resume via dispatcher correctly resolves MERGE_STRATEGY='pr', reads merge_strategy='direct' from state, fires cross-strategy abort.
- **Path 2** (CONDITIONAL): merge-to-main.sh dispatcher calls merge-to-main-pr.sh with MERGE_STRATEGY='pr' exported. Line 2891 _state_init correctly writes merge_strategy='pr'. THEN _phase_staged_intermediate (line 1024) or PR2 advance block (line 2930) calls _state_init again with BRANCH changed to staged-*. If MERGE_STRATEGY is still exported (it is, as inherited from the dispatcher), the re-init writes merge_strategy='pr' correctly. This path is NOT broken when using the dispatcher — consistent with the report that chunk 8 --resume worked correctly.
- **Path 1 is the live failure mode**: direct invocation of merge-to-main-pr.sh (without going through merge-to-main.sh dispatcher).

## FIX APPROACH

Single-line fix in merge-to-main-pr.sh: after MERGE_STRATEGY is set at line 75 or 77, add `export MERGE_STRATEGY` immediately after (or inline: `export MERGE_STRATEGY='pr'` and `export MERGE_STRATEGY='direct'`). This ensures python3 env passthrough in _state_init sees the correct value regardless of invocation path.

File: plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main-pr.sh
Change: line 75 → `export MERGE_STRATEGY='pr'`; line 77 → `export MERGE_STRATEGY='direct'`
(Or add `export MERGE_STRATEGY` after line 78 / before line 81.)

## RED TEST PLAN

**Test file**: tests/scripts/test-merge-to-main-dispatcher.sh (add new test after test 8)

**Test name**: test_state_init_writes_merge_strategy_pr_on_direct_invocation

**Scenario**: Source merge-helpers.sh. Set BRANCH to a unique name. Do NOT export MERGE_STRATEGY. Within a subshell, set (but do not export) MERGE_STRATEGY=pr, then call _state_init. Read merge_strategy from the written state file. Assert it equals 'pr' not 'direct'.

**Why RED before fix**: _state_init's python3 reads from os.environ, which only sees exported vars. Without the fix, MERGE_STRATEGY='pr' (non-exported bash var) is invisible to python3. The test will read 'direct' and FAIL.

**Why GREEN after fix**: With `export MERGE_STRATEGY` added, the value is in the environment. python3 reads 'pr'. Test PASSES.

**Alternate complementary test**: A full dispatcher integration test:

1. **Line 2891** (top-level init): merge-to-main.sh dispatcher sets MERGE_STRATEGY and exports it (line 106). On the normal dispatcher path this is correct. The python3 snippet at merge-helpers.sh:138 reads `os.environ.get('MERGE_STRATEGY', 'direct')`. 2. **Line 2930** (PR2 advance block): BRANCH is mutated to the staged branch name. _state_init is called to create a new staged-branch-keyed state file. At this point, if MERGE_STRATEGY was not exported, the skeleton written for the staged branch also gets merge_strategy='direct'. This is the state file --resume will check on the NEXT invocation — the PR2 invocation.

3. **Line 1024** (_phase_staged_intermediate): Same risk. BRANCH is mutated to staged branch; _state_init is called; MERGE_STRATEGY must be in the exported environment.

merge-helpers.sh line 138 writes a key named 'merge_strategy' (snake_case). merge-to-main.sh lines 82-88 read the key 'merge_strategy' (consistent). ## 2. Incident Overview
**Scenario Type:** Sub-Agent/tooling blocker (hit live landing the resume-hardening bundle).
### Expected Behavior

A merge-to-main run under dso.workflow=ci-pr (MERGE_STRATEGY=pr) should persist merge_strategy=pr in its state file, so a later --resume passes the cross-strategy check (merge-to-main.sh:81-101) and advances to PR2.
### Actual Behavior

The state file written by a ci-pr (pr-strategy) run recorded merge_strategy=direct (observed: /tmp/merge-to-main-state-fix-merge-to-main-resume-hardening.json had merge_strategy='direct' with staged_branch correctly set and strategy='pr'). On --resume the cross-strategy guard at merge-to-main.sh:95-96 read merge_strategy='direct' != config 'pr' and aborted: 'cross-strategy mismatch: state file was written with strategy=direct, but current config resolves to strategy=pr'. The only documented recovery is to delete the state file (which loses staged_branch -> --resume can't advance) or flip dso.workflow. Manual recovery required hand-patching merge_strategy=pr into the /tmp state JSON.

Secondary: there appear to be TWO strategy fields in the state JSON ('strategy' and 'merge_strategy'); the cross-strategy check reads 'merge_strategy' (line 86) while other code writes 'strategy' — a field-name inconsistency. Patching 'strategy' alone did NOT clear the check.
### Affected files
plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main.sh:81-101 (cross-strategy guard); plugins/dso/hooks/lib/merge-helpers.sh (state field writers); whatever writes merge_strategy.
### Impact
Every two-tier ci-pr --resume is at risk of a spurious cross-strategy abort if merge_strategy is mis-recorded as direct, blocking PR2 creation after PR1 merges.

**What**: Implement a PreToolUse hook that reads the active (skill, phase) from durable session state, looks up the forbidden set in the registry (draft-1), and blocks an in-flight tool call when its tool/action class is forbidden for that phase, emitting a structured error directing the agent to complete the prerequisite phase work or surface to the user for an override.

**Why**: This is the enforcement spine of the epic — it converts documented HARD-GATEs into tool-use-time blocks. It also carries the false-positive invariant: happy-path tool calls must pass through unblocked.
**Scope**:

- IN: Reading active phase from durable session state, registry lookup, block decision, structured block error message, pass-through for non-forbidden calls, the fixture where an Edit during brainstorm Phase 1 is blocked, and a happy-path trace test covering brainstorm, sprint, fix-bug, and implementation-plan flows that asserts no spurious blocks.
- OUT: Registry enumeration (draft-1); the override CLI and audit trail (draft-3).
## Done Definitions
- An agent attempting Edit during brainstorm Phase 1 is blocked by the hook, with a structured error naming the active (skill, phase) and the forbidden tool ← Satisfies: sc-1
- A tool call whose tool/action class is not forbidden for the active phase passes through the hook without a block ← Satisfies: sc-1

- When this story is complete, the hook derives the active (skill, phase) by reading the same durable session-state artifact the brainstorm/sprint/fix-bug/implementation-plan skills already write for resume rather than a hook-private phase store, verified by a test that drives the hook from a skill-written phase artifact ← Satisfies: sc-1

- A happy-path end-to-end trace for each of brainstorm, sprint, fix-bug, and implementation-plan runs with the hook active and produces no spurious blocks ← Validates Closure Check: "Zero false positives on representative session-level traces of brainstorm, sprint, fix-bug, and implementation-plan flows (each runs a happy-path session end-to-end with the new hook active and produces no spurious blocks)."
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic, including the phase-state read, the block decision, and the pass-through path ← Satisfies: sc-1
## Considerations
- [Reliability] The false-positive trace test is the cc-1 guard; a single spurious block on any of the four happy-path flows fails the story.
- [Convention] The hook .sh file sets the executable bit (chmod +x) on creation; non-executable hooks are silently skipped by the gate.

- [Consistency] The hook reads the skills' own durable resume artifact for active (skill, phase); a hook-private phase store would drift from the skills' resume state and produce spurious or missed blocks.

**Why**: The hook (draft-2) cannot decide whether to block a tool call without a data source mapping each phase to its forbidden tool/action set. This registry is the walking-skeleton data layer that the hook reads.
**Scope**:

- IN: Reading the four SKILL.md files, identifying each HARD-GATE forbidden-action statement, encoding it as a (skill, phase, forbidden-tool-or-action) tuple, writing the registry file, and a loader function that returns the forbidden set for a given (skill, phase).
- OUT: The hook that consumes the registry (draft-2); the override CLI (draft-3); any runtime tool interception.
## Done Definitions

- The registry file contains a (skill, phase, forbidden-tool-or-action) tuple for each forbidden-action HARD-GATE found in the brainstorm, sprint, fix-bug, and implementation-plan SKILL.md files ← Satisfies: sc-2
- A loader function returns the forbidden tool/action set for a given (skill, phase) pair and returns an empty set for a pair with no forbidden actions ← Satisfies: sc-2
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic, including the loader function and registry parsing ← Satisfies: sc-2
## Considerations
- [Maintainability] The registry must stay in sync with the SKILL.md HARD-GATEs; encode the source skill and phase so drift is auditable.
- [Convention] Any new .sh file created for the loader sets the executable bit (chmod +x) on creation per project convention.

- [External-blocker] Phase-state shape is informed by sibling-epic infra (d076-d35e, 750c-6033) get_artifacts_dir() worktree resolution and session-state tracking; this story encodes the registry only and does not depend on an in-epic story for that infra.

content.text: ## Description

**What**: Publish plugins/dso/docs/contracts/intent-allocation-manifest.md (contract_version=1) defining the per-entry schema and the validator acceptance rule, and ship plugins/dso/scripts/intent-id-mint.sh that mints stable slug-format intent_ids deterministically.

**Why**: This is the walking-skeleton spine. Every emit/read/validate slice and every downstream consumer (d566, 411b, 7f42, 69e8) references this single contract and intent_id format; without it the rest of the epic has nothing to align to.
**Scope**:

- IN: the contract markdown (per-entry schema: intent_id, owner_ticket, test_artifact{path,kind}, deferred, lightweight, shared_infra, confidence, rationale; manifest-level contract_version=1; unknown-field passthrough requirement; validator acceptance rule); the intent-id-mint.sh helper deriving the slug from {epic_id_prefix, item_index, first_5_words_kebab_case} per the `[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+){2,5}` regex; documentation of the additive 7f42 fields (source_files, deferred_test) as forward-compatible optional entries.
- OUT: any stage emitter wiring (sc-2/3/4); read/validate tooling (sc-5/6); the a03c hook (sc-7).
## Done Definitions

- intent-allocation-manifest.md exists at plugins/dso/docs/contracts/ and documents every per-entry field (intent_id, owner_ticket, test_artifact.path, test_artifact.kind, deferred, lightweight, shared_infra, confidence, rationale) plus manifest-level contract_version=1 ← Satisfies: sc-1

- The contract states the validator acceptance rule verbatim: an entry is valid when intent_id matches the slug regex, owner_ticket resolves to a ticket in the epic subtree (or shared_infra is set), and test_artifact kind/path pairing holds ← Satisfies: sc-1

- intent-id-mint.sh emits a slug matching `[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+){2,5}` derived from {epic_id_prefix, item_index, first_5_words_kebab_case}, and re-running it with the same inputs returns the identical slug ← Satisfies: sc-1
- intent-id-mint.sh emits distinct slugs for two items whose first five words differ, confirming the id is not ordinal-derived ← Satisfies: sc-1
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic in intent-id-mint.sh, including the stability and determinism cases ← Satisfies: sc-1
## Considerations

- [Stability] intent_id MUST be stable across re-runs: the same DoD/item inputs mint the identical slug so a re-decomposition never re-mints a different id for the same item. This is the load-bearing invariant for all downstream merge logic.
- [Forward-compat] The contract must mandate unknown-field passthrough so the additive 7f42 fields (source_files, deferred_test) and any future consumer fields survive read/merge round-trips.
- [Shell hygiene] intent-id-mint.sh is a new .sh file; set the executable bit (chmod +x) on creation or the test gate silently skips it.
- [Scope] The 7f42 additive-field request (ticket comment) is documented here as optional schema, not implemented as behavior; downstream consumers add their own population logic.

## Description

**What**: Add a migration-class detection step to /dso:implementation-plan's contextual discovery that classifies a story as sweep (targeted-symbol call-site repetition above a configurable threshold), db (schema/migration file patterns), or inconclusive, and persists a structured migration-class marker in the plan header.
**Why**: The marker is the spine the rest of the epic consumes — task-pair emission (sibling stories), sprint two-pass ordering, and the E2E fixture all bind to it.
**Scope**:
- IN: detection query over call sites; dual sub-classifier (sweep/db); configurable threshold; persisted marker with explicit schema; sg-unavailable degradation.
- OUT: emitting the migration task pairs (separate stories); sprint scheduling.
## Done Definitions
- When run against a story whose targeted symbol repeats at or above the threshold, the plan header records a migration-class:sweep marker
← Satisfies: sc-1  (sc-1: migration-class detection + persisted marker)

- When run against a story touching schema/migration file patterns (migrations/, alembic/, db/migrate, *.migration.ts, schema.sql), the plan header records a migration-class:db marker regardless of call-site count
← Satisfies: sc-1
- Call-site counting tallies only the specifically targeted symbol or API and excludes surrounding boilerplate, imports, and test files
← Satisfies: sc-1

- The sweep repetition threshold is read from config key migration.call_site_threshold with a documented default, and a test overriding the config moves a borderline target across the classification boundary
← Satisfies: sc-1
- The persisted marker includes the detection query string, and a test asserts the query is retrievable from the marker after persistence
← Satisfies: sc-1
- Classification persists the marker without emitting a user-confirmation prompt, asserted by a non-interactive test
← Satisfies: sc-1
- When sg is unavailable the plan header records an explicit migration-class:inconclusive marker (never silently false) and the planner does not crash
← Satisfies: sc-1
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

Define the marker schema explicitly here — fields: migration-class value (sweep|db|inconclusive), detection query, threshold used, target symbol — so consumers bind to a stable shape.
- [Performance] ast-grep call-site counting on large consuming-project codebases — consider scope/timeout behavior.
