content.text: ## Description

What: New plugins/dso/scripts/pr-destructive-action.sh <pr-number> <action> [args...] that internally invokes pr-owned-by-session.sh, then on exit 0 executes 'gh pr <action> [args...]', and on exit 1/2/3 emits structured stderr with the case identifier and exits non-zero (fail-closed). Why: Per the bot-psychologist R2 lesson, enforcement must be structural — a single permitted path that internalizes the check, not a 'remember to check first' composition. Scope IN: the internal-check-then-act control flow; fail-closed behavior on all non-own cases; a shell unit test covering all 4 internal-check outcomes end-to-end; the two-session integration test (session A stamps + acts succeeds; session B refused exit 1 on close/merge/comment; stripped-trailer exit 2). Scope OUT: the PreToolUse hook (draft-5); call-site migration (draft-7).
## Done Definitions

- pr-destructive-action.sh internally invokes pr-owned-by-session.sh and executes 'gh pr <action> [args...]' only when that check exits 0; on exit 1/2/3 it emits structured stderr with the case identifier and exits non-zero (fail-closed) ← Satisfies: sc-3
- A shell unit test covers all four internal-check outcomes (own/foreign/absent/api_error) end-to-end through the wrapper ← Satisfies: sc-3

- A two-session integration test: session A (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=session-A-uuid) creates a trailer-stamped synthetic PR and successfully acts on it; session B (session-B-uuid) is refused (exit 1, structured stderr) on close, merge, and comment; a PR with a stripped trailer returns exit 2 (absent) ← Validates Closure Check: "Two-session integration test: simulate session A with CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=session-A-uuid creating a synthetic PR (trailer stamped); switch to CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=session-B-uuid and attempt close/merge/comment via pr-destructive-action.sh — all three refused (exit 1, structured stderr). Positive case (session A acts on its own PR) succeeds. Edge case (PR with stripped trailer) returns exit 2 absent — included in the same test."
## Considerations
- [Structural] R2 lesson: the wrapper must INTERNALIZE the check (single permitted path), never delegate the check-then-act ordering to a caller's discipline.
- [Concurrency] Same-session concurrent destructive actions are intended-permitted (0777-0f3d); an advisory lock is explicitly deferred per the epic HIGH scenario.

- [Isolation] The two-session integration test must run in a configuration-isolated environment (empty HOME, no pre-set CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID inherited from the developer machine) so CI-runner behavior is validated, not the developer's ambient session.
## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

content.text: ## Description

What: Restructure the existing Step 3 classification in respond-to-pr-comments as a two-phase prompt — Phase A author-classification (per comment, using user_type + user_login) emitting author_class in {human, dso-llm, bot:<reviewer_id>, bot:other} plus a routing action, with a per-comment-iteration STOP directive co-located with Phase B's trigger; Phase B is the existing accept/defend/defer classifier, gated to run only when author_class==human. Extend pr-comment-response.sh's normalized JSON (backward-compatible additive fields) to include user_type and user_login per comment as the canonical Phase A discriminator. Why: bots post uncoordinated review noise and dso-llm replies are already mirrored; routing them into the human gate increments the cycle counter and produces churn. Scope IN: Phase A/B restructure with co-located per-comment STOP; the canonical user.type=="Bot" discriminator with the explicit negative directive (do NOT infer bot status from [bot] login suffix); pr-comment-response.sh user_type/user_login schema extension; the 9-fixture author-classifier integration test under tests/fixtures/bot-comments/ asserting the 5 routing outcomes. Scope OUT: the out-of-band telemetry adapter and parsers (separate stories); thread auto-resolution.
## Done Definitions

This is the first hook end-to-end and proves the full pattern (detection + baseline + diagnostics + suppression + fixture + dogfood) before replication.
**Why**: SIGPIPE-under-pipefail is the highest-volume and growing class (~63 files, up from 42); blocking new instances stops growth while the shrink-only baseline lets the backlog through.

- OUT: remediation of the ~63 existing violations; the other three hooks; the shared library functions (consumed from draft-1).

content.text: ## Description

What: New defense-store-to-thread-resolve.sh adapter that polls the defense store once for new entries since the last cursor (cold-start seeds cursor to defense-store HEAD and emits cursor_initialized; historical entries not processed), and for each new entry with defense_type in {dropped_by_arbiter, deferred_to_followup, defended_accepted} that carries a github_comment_id, resolves the matching review thread via a single (non-batched) gh api graphql resolveReviewThread mutation; thread-ID resolution maps comment ID to pullRequest.reviewThreads.nodes[].comments.nodes[].id (cached per PR per session); per-call uses || true with INFO log on 4xx (already-resolved / merged / force-push-orphaned); startup permission probe hard-errors on insufficient scope. Records without github_comment_id are skipped with INFO. The same trigger covers both arbiter rulings (sc-3) and our own llm reviewer's accepted defenses (sc-4). Why: closes both the bot-thread-noise gap and the pre-existing dso-llm accepted-defense gap via one uniform mechanism. Scope IN: the adapter, cursor polling + cold-start, thread-ID resolution + per-PR cache, non-batched mutation with || true, graceful skip on missing field, the mocked-gh auto-resolve test asserting mutation called with correct threadId and that the permission probe runs. Scope OUT: the CI job wiring + permissions block (draft-9); the defense schema field (draft-4).
## Done Definitions

- For each defense-store entry with defense_type in {dropped_by_arbiter, deferred_to_followup, defended_accepted} carrying a github_comment_id, the adapter dispatches a resolveReviewThread GraphQL mutation against the matched threadId within 60 seconds; the mocked-gh test asserts the mutation is called with the correct threadId and the startup permission probe runs ← Satisfies: sc-3

- A defended_accepted entry produced by our own llm reviewer (no arbiter involvement) is auto-resolved by the same trigger, proving the uniform mechanism fixes the pre-existing dso-llm gap ← Satisfies: sc-4
- A defense record without github_comment_id is skipped with an INFO: defense has no github_comment_id; skipping thread resolution log and no mutation is dispatched ← Satisfies: sc-3

- On first run with no cursor, the adapter seeds the cursor to defense-store HEAD, emits a cursor_initialized marker, and processes zero historical entries; on a 4xx mutation response the adapter logs INFO and continues ← Satisfies: sc-3
## Considerations
- [Reliability] Non-batched single-threaded mutations with || true per call; hard-error only on the startup permission probe so misconfiguration is visible while transient 4xx are absorbed.
- [Cold-start] First-deploy cursor seeding to HEAD prevents a burst of resolution attempts against already-merged/deleted PRs.

- [Trigger-surface-reconciliation] Specify which defense store the defense-store-to-thread-resolve.sh adapter polls — TrackerDefenseStore (local) or GitHubPRDefenseStore (CI) — and confirm the producing writer (dso-llm resolver per draft-10, and the b575 arbiter) targets that SAME store for the runtime context where resolution runs. A single-store cursor poll that reads a store no producer writes to in that context means sc-4 never fires in CI. State the store choice per context (local vs CI) explicitly.

VERDICT: LIVE (bug is present at HEAD c8f1700a74)

---

## 1. STALENESS CHECK

Files checked:
- plugins/dso/agents/story-decomposer.md — latest commit: c8f1700a74 (intent fidelity pipeline Phase 2). The DELTA OUTPUT MODE block was added at commit 26d7eb9b04 and has not been patched to add a DD-superset preservation constraint. LIVE.
- plugins/dso/skills/preplanning/prompts/phase-e-adversarial-review.md — latest commit: c8f1700a74 (same). Step 4 'Consume the delta only' instruction added; no orchestrator-side merge/superset-check added. LIVE.
- plugins/dso/skills/shared/workflows/remediation-loop-protocol.md — latest commit: c6586808a3. Contains Schema Preservation sub-sections for approach-proposer and task-decomposer, but NOT for story-decomposer. LIVE — the gap is confirmed open.

The contract file referenced by the phase-e prompt ('docs/contracts/remediation-context-payload.md') does NOT EXIST on disk. That forward reference is a dead link.

---

## 2. ROOT CAUSE

The defect is in BOTH locations — producer prompt and orchestrator consume step — operating together:

### A. Producer prompt (story-decomposer.md DELTA OUTPUT MODE) — PRIMARY ROOT CAUSE

The DELTA OUTPUT MODE section (lines 94–123 of story-decomposer.md) instructs the agent to:
- Step 3: 'Collect all target_story_id values from remediation_context.findings. Emit only story_drafts whose target_story_id appears in that set.'
- It says to emit the 'full updated draft for each' targeted story.

The critical missing constraint: there is NO instruction to treat the prior DD list as a floor (superset invariant). The agent is told to re-derive DDs for the targeted stories from the epic context + findings — which causes a fresh reasoning pass that regenerates DDs from scratch rather than adding to the existing ones. The only input constraint is 'Emit only stories whose target_story_id appears in the passed target_story_ids list.'

By contrast, approach-proposer and task-decomposer have explicit Schema Preservation sub-sections in remediation-loop-protocol.md (rules: 'preserved top-level keys verbatim when not named in any finding', 'preserve-by-omission rule', etc.). story-decomposer has NO such sub-section — that is the architectural gap.

### B. Orchestrator consume step (phase-e-adversarial-review.md Step 4 #5) — SECONDARY ROOT CAUSE (insufficient applier)

Step 4 #5 says: 'Consume the delta only. After the sub-agent returns, parse the DELTA OUTPUT block and apply only the new/modified stories.'

'Apply only the new/modified stories' — this instruction performs a wholesale replacement of the prior drafts for each target_story_id in DECOMP_JSON. There is no merge instruction: 'for each story in the delta, merge the new done_definitions onto the prior story's done_definitions, retaining all prior DDs that are not the subject of a finding.'

The orchestrator has DECOMP_JSON in session memory (loaded from scratch at Phase D Step 4) and could trivially merge; but the prompt gives no such instruction. ### 1. Technical Environment
* **Skill/agent:** dso:story-decomposer (opus) invoked in DELTA OUTPUT mode by /dso:preplanning Phase E Step 4 (remediation re-dispatch)
* **Contract:** plugins/dso/skills/preplanning/SKILL.md Phase E Step 4 ("Consume the delta only"); docs/contracts/remediation-context-payload.md
### 2. Incident Overview
* **Scenario Type:** Sub-Agent Blocker (faulty sub-agent output)
#### Expected Behavior

In DELTA OUTPUT mode the producer is supposed to APPLY the blue-team-accepted findings to the named target stories and emit the FULL updated draft for each, preserving every field and done-definition not touched by a finding. Per Phase E Step 4 the orchestrator is instructed to "Consume the delta only" and "apply only the new/modified stories" — i.e., the returned delta drafts are meant to be authoritative replacements that retain all prior coverage plus the additions.
#### Actual Behavior

When re-dispatched for target_story_ids [draft-1, draft-2, draft-5, draft-6] on epic dso-uvyl, the producer added the requested findings but REWROTE each target story's done_definitions from scratch and silently dropped original DDs that were not the subject of any finding:

* draft-2 (was fully_covered; the only accepted finding was add_consideration): its three substantive sc-2 DDs were replaced with weaker generic ones — lost "transform descriptor distinct from the detection query", lost the manual-verification "re-run detection query + un_automatable_sites enumeration" DD, and lost the "test gate over modified files (zero re-count alone insufficient)" DD.

* draft-5: lost the "reads marker, does not recompute" DD (demoted to a consideration), the "absent marker -> standard ordering" DD, the "sprint/SKILL.md documents two-pass flow" DD, and the TDD unit-test DD.
* draft-6: lost the core sc-6 DDs — the "completeness assertion exits non-zero on the omitted site" DD and the "RED-phase baseline produces no marker/pair" DD — and the TDD unit-test DD.

* draft-1: merged the db-marker and sg-unavailable behaviors into a single compound DD and dropped the "call-site counting excludes boilerplate/imports/tests" over-trigger-guard DD and the TDD unit-test DD.

Consuming this delta wholesale (as Phase E Step 4 instructs) would have removed verified Success-Criterion coverage and would have been caught only later by the Phase H SC-contradiction / spec-fidelity checks (or not at all). The orchestrator worked around it by merging the accepted additions onto the original DDs instead of consuming the delta.
### 3. Action History
1. /dso:preplanning dso-uvyl -> story-decomposer produced 6 drafts (full coverage).
2. Phase E red team (opus) raised 6 findings; blue team (sonnet) accepted all 6.
3. Phase E Step 4 re-dispatched story-decomposer in DELTA OUTPUT mode with target_story_ids [draft-1, draft-2, draft-5, draft-6].
4. Returned delta drafts contained the requested additions but with rewritten DD lists missing original coverage (see §2).
### 4. Chronological Rationalization

The DELTA prompt asks the producer to "emit the FULL updated draft" per target story. A code-generation model re-deriving the full DD list from the title/description tends to regenerate rather than diff, so DDs not referenced by a finding are silently lost. The contract has no machine assertion that the delta is a superset of the prior story's DDs, so the loss is invisible at the consume step.
### 5. Skills and Workflows
* Producer: plugins/dso/agents/story-decomposer.md (DELTA OUTPUT mode)
* Caller: plugins/dso/skills/preplanning/SKILL.md Phase E Step 4 ("Consume the delta only")

* Suggested guardrail (not a fix mandate): have the orchestrator diff delta DDs against the pre-remediation drafts and reject/merge when the delta is not a superset; OR instruct the producer to emit additive deltas (new/changed DDs only) rather than full rewrites; OR add a producer-side assertion that every prior DD id is present in the returned draft.
### 6. Logs
* Pre-remediation drafts: scratch key preplanning:step4:story-decomp-draft (now cleared) — 6 drafts, byte_count 28319.
* Adversarial review artifact: adversarial-review-dso-uvyl.json (6 findings, 6 accepted).
* Remediation sub-agent: agentId a09cc22216c81c2a0 (DELTA OUTPUT return block).

**What**: Add a synthetic end-to-end test exercising three scenarios across the emit/read/validate/verifier path: (a) HAPPY PATH — brainstorm 3-SC epic, preplanning extends and reassigns (deferred=false), impl-plan extends, read.sh returns zero _conflicts, validate.sh returns zero orphan_intent and zero lightweight_pending; (b) PARALLEL-SPRINT DUPLICATE-DETECTION — two dispatches register a test_artifact against the same intent_id, validate.sh surfaces unresolved_ambiguity AND a dedup warning fires (d566 integration or a synthetic stand-in); (c) ORPHAN-DETECTION — 1-SC epic with --lightweight preplanning and no impl-plan stage yields lightweight=true/deferred=true, validate.sh surfaces lightweight_pending, and completion-verifier produces a non-empty Intent Allocation Findings section naming the SC.
**Why**: Proves the stages compose end to end and protects the loop against regression.
**Scope**:
- IN: the three-scenario synthetic e2e test and its fixtures.
- OUT: changes to the stage emitters, read, validate, hook, or assistant (consumed, not modified).
## Done Definitions

- The happy-path scenario drives brainstorm, preplanning, and implementation-plan emitters and asserts read.sh returns zero _conflicts and validate.sh returns zero orphan_intent and zero lightweight_pending ← Satisfies: sc-10
- The parallel-sprint scenario registers two test_artifact entries against the same intent_id and asserts both validate.sh surfaces unresolved_ambiguity and a dedup warning fires ← Satisfies: sc-10

- The orphan-detection scenario runs --lightweight preplanning on a 1-SC epic with no implementation-plan stage and asserts lightweight=true with deferred=true, validate.sh surfaces lightweight_pending, and the completion-verifier output names the unresolved SC in a non-empty Intent Allocation Findings section ← Satisfies: sc-10

- The synthetic end-to-end test runs in a configuration-isolated environment (HOME set to an empty directory, no pre-existing worktrees, no global git config, no pre-set environment variables) and the test passes ← Satisfies: sc-10
## Considerations
- [Live-verified] SC10 asserts runtime end-to-end behavior across multiple stages, so it runs in a configuration-isolated environment rather than inheriting the developer's runtime.
- [Dedup stand-in] The d566 test-quality reviewer may not be shipped; scenario (b) uses a synthetic stand-in invocation for the dedup warning while still requiring both signals to fire.

content.text: ## Description

**What**: Publish plugins/dso/docs/contracts/intent-coverage-findings.md with an embedded jsonschema (contract_version=1) defining the seven finding types and their severities, and implement plugins/dso/scripts/intent-coverage-check.sh implementing the (a) manifest-claim breadth check.

**Why**: This is the walking skeleton for the epic: it establishes the finding-record shape every consumer validates against, and the first check that produces the headline signal 'intent with no test'.
**Scope**:

- IN: intent-coverage-findings.md contract doc; the jsonschema artifact; the seven finding types (intent_with_no_test, test_artifact_missing_on_disk, test_artifact_fails, header_source_mismatch, dynamic_import_inconclusive, source_files_unresolved, file_impact_likely_stale) with severities; contract_version=1; intent-coverage-check.sh reading the 94ed manifest via intent-allocation-read.sh; per end-state intent_id steps (i) entry presence, (ii) realpath normalization then on-disk existence, (iii) test pass/fail; pre-commit-mode flag that runs only steps (i)+(ii); --output-file flag for ARG_MAX-safe findings output; exit codes 0/1/2.
- OUT: the header-vs-source check (sc-3); the consumers (sc-4); the e2e fixture suite (sc-5); per-language dynamic-import detection (sc-6).
## Done Definitions
- plugins/dso/docs/contracts/intent-coverage-findings.md is published and its embedded jsonschema validates against the JSON Schema draft-07 meta-schema ← Satisfies: sc-1
- The schema enumerates all seven finding types and carries contract_version=1; a findings document emitted by intent-coverage-check.sh validates against the schema ← Satisfies: sc-1

- intent-coverage-check.sh reads the 94ed manifest via intent-allocation-read.sh and, for an end-state intent_id whose test_artifact path is absent on disk, emits test_artifact_missing_on_disk; for an intent_id with no manifest entry it emits intent_with_no_test ← Satisfies: sc-2

- intent-coverage-check.sh in pre-commit mode runs only entry-presence and on-disk-existence checks (no test execution), writes findings via --output-file, and returns exit code 0 with no findings / 1 with warn-only findings / 2 with a block-mode finding ← Satisfies: sc-2

- When this story is complete, intent-coverage-check.sh in full (non-pre-commit) mode runs step (iii) test execution and, for an end-state intent_id whose registered test_artifact exists on disk but fails when run, emits the test_artifact_fails finding (block-mode) and returns exit code 2; the finding is suppressed when the manifest entry sets deferred_test:true ← Satisfies: sc-2
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic ← Satisfies: sc-2
## Considerations

- [Dependency] External blocker 94ed-f55c-51f5-45f6 (manifest schema): intent-coverage-check.sh reads the 94ed manifest via intent-allocation-read.sh; cross-epic dependency, not an in-epic story dependency.
- [Dependency] External blocker a03c-d55e-1393-4f27 (Closure Checks schema cleavage): findings reference end-state SC/DoD/AC items separated from Closure Checks by a03c's schema.
- [Build] intent-coverage-check.sh is a new .sh file and must have its executable bit set per CLAUDE.md.
- [Reliability] test_artifact.path resolution normalizes via realpath before the on-disk existence test to avoid symlink false negatives.

content.text: ## Description

**What**: Ship plugins/dso/scripts/intent-allocation-read.sh <epic-id> that walks the epic subtree, reads all INTENT_ALLOCATION_<STAGE>: comments, and merges by stable intent_id using stage precedence (brainstorm < preplanning < implementation-plan), most-recent-timestamp within stage, and comment-UUID lexical order as the same-timestamp tiebreaker. Surfaces a _conflicts array for equal-stage duplicates and interleaved-stage anomalies, and preserves unknown fields.
**Why**: This is the read half of the walking skeleton; without a deterministic merge, every consumer and the validator would see raw, conflicting comment streams.
**Scope**:
- IN: subtree walk; stage-precedence merge; timestamp and UUID tiebreakers; _conflicts array (equal-stage duplicates + interleaved-stage anomalies); unknown-field passthrough.
- OUT: finding classification (sc-6); a03c hook (sc-7).
## Done Definitions
- intent-allocation-read.sh <epic-id> walks the epic subtree and returns one merged entry per stable intent_id across all INTENT_ALLOCATION_<STAGE>: comments ← Satisfies: sc-5
- When the same intent_id appears at brainstorm and preplanning stages, the merged entry reflects the preplanning value, confirming stage precedence ← Satisfies: sc-5
- When two same-stage comments share a timestamp, the merge selects the entry whose comment UUID sorts first, producing identical output across repeated runs ← Satisfies: sc-5
- The _conflicts array lists equal-stage duplicates and interleaved-stage anomalies such as an implementation-plan timestamp predating a later preplanning write ← Satisfies: sc-5
- Unknown entry fields present in input comments appear unchanged in the merged output, and unit tests written and passing cover all merge, tiebreaker, and passthrough logic ← Satisfies: sc-5
## Considerations
- [Determinism] The comment-UUID lexical tiebreaker is the only defense against equal-timestamp non-determinism; it must be applied before output is emitted.
- [Clock-skew] Interleaved-stage anomalies from worktree clock skew are surfaced in _conflicts, not silently resolved.
- [Shell hygiene] intent-allocation-read.sh is a new .sh file; set the executable bit on creation.
## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

content.text: ## Description

What: End-to-end dogfooding slice. Select an organic f27a sprint story PR that accumulates bot review comments, run the full pipeline (bot-comment-scan + arbiter ruling + defense-store-to-thread-resolve) against it, and capture before/after thread state, documenting a Dogfooding evidence subsection (PR number, before/after thread counts) in sprint closure notes before sprint Phase I. The synthetic-PR fallback (inject fixtures via the adapter against a synthetic test PR) is used ONLY if no organic sprint PR accumulates bot comments, and the fallback MUST be explicitly justified in closure notes. Why: SC8/SC9 require a proven engineer-visible behavior change, not just unit-level coverage. Scope IN: pipeline run against the chosen PR, before/after thread-state capture via gh CLI, the Dogfooding evidence closure-notes subsection, the synthetic fallback path with justification requirement. Scope OUT: the underlying adapters/parsers (draft-2/3/5); CI permission verification (draft-9).
## Done Definitions

- The full pipeline is run end-to-end against a target PR; before the run N bot-comment threads are open and after the run all threads with DROP/DEFER/ACCEPT rulings are resolved (before/after counts captured) ← Satisfies: sc-8

- At least one organic f27a sprint story PR (not synthetic) is the dogfooding target with >=1 Bot-authored review and zero unresolved review threads after the run; if the synthetic fallback is used instead it is explicitly justified in the closure notes ← Satisfies: sc-9
- The sprint closure notes contain a Dogfooding evidence subsection recording the PR number, before/after thread counts, and (if synthetic fallback used) the justification ← Satisfies: sc-8, sc-9

- An integration test exercises the synthetic-PR fallback (inject fixtures via the adapter then resolve) in a configuration-isolated environment (HOME set to an empty directory, no pre-existing worktrees, no global git config, no pre-set environment variables) and the test passes, proving the dogfooding path is sprint-executable regardless of PR availability ← Satisfies: sc-8, sc-9
- >=1 defense record on the dogfooding PR carries a non-null github_comment_id (SC10 check-6) ← Satisfies: sc-10, sc-9

- [Self-use] SC9 hardens SC8 to require an ORGANIC sprint PR; the synthetic path is a justified fallback only when no organic sprint PR accumulates bot comments (e.g., bot offline).

content.text: ## Description

What: Extend the defense record shape in plugins/dso/docs/contracts/review-defenses.md and both defense-store writers (TrackerDefenseStore / GitHubPRDefenseStore) to include an OPTIONAL additive github_comment_id field, coordinated cross-epic with b575-ac1c-f720-4839 (swap-maple-flyby) whose arbiter writes defense entries. Existing/legacy records without the field remain valid. Why: the auto-resolve mechanism (draft-5) needs a comment-ID anchor and the current 11-field record shape has none. Scope IN: the contract doc update, the optional field on both defense-store writer paths, schema-compat tests proving legacy records still validate. Scope OUT: the thread-resolution mutation itself (draft-5); the arbiter's ruling logic (lives in b575).
## Done Definitions

- A defense record written with a github_comment_id round-trips through the defense store and exposes the field to readers; the field is documented in plugins/dso/docs/contracts/review-defenses.md as optional and additive ← Satisfies: sc-3
- A legacy defense record without github_comment_id still validates and is readable (non-breaking additive change) ← Satisfies: sc-3
- Both defense-store writers (tracker-backed and GitHub-PR-backed) accept and persist github_comment_id when supplied ← Satisfies: sc-3
## Considerations

- [Cross-epic] This is a coordination requirement with b575-ac1c-f720-4839; the field must be additive/non-breaking so b575's arbiter writes and legacy records coexist. Coordinate the field name and type (github_comment_id, integer) with that epic's implementation sprint.
- [Contract] review-defenses.md is the source-of-truth contract; update it in the same change as the writer extension.

- [Cross-epic-field-lock] Lock the github_comment_id field name AND type with b575-ac1c-f720-4839 before implementation: confirm whether the stored id is the GitHub REST databaseId (integer) or the GraphQL node id (string). The defense-store dedup path and draft-5's resolveReviewThread thread-matching query MUST consume the same form — a REST-integer write paired with a GraphQL-node-id thread-match silently yields no matching thread (no-op resolution). Document the chosen form in review-defenses.md.

**What**: Wire /dso:preplanning to emit an INTENT_ALLOCATION_PREPLANNING: JSON ticket comment on the parent epic (temp-file write). For each story DoD mint a stable intent_id; when reassigning an epic SC to a story, preserve the existing intent_id and set deferred=false. Under --lightweight, still emit the comment and set lightweight=true on unreassigned items (deferred stays true).
**Why**: Carries allocation from epic-level seeds into story-level ownership and introduces the lightweight-placeholder distinction the validator relies on.
**Scope**:
- IN: preplanning emitter; intent_id preservation on reassignment; deferred=false on reassignment; --lightweight lightweight=true behavior on unreassigned items.
- OUT: brainstorm emitter (sc-2); impl-plan emitter (sc-4); validate finding types (sc-6); assistant dispatch (sc-8).
## Done Definitions
- A /dso:preplanning run posts one INTENT_ALLOCATION_PREPLANNING: comment on the parent epic with one entry per story DoD, each carrying a slug-regex intent_id ← Satisfies: sc-3
- When a story DoD reassigns an epic SC, the emitted entry reuses that SC's existing intent_id and sets deferred=false ← Satisfies: sc-3
- A --lightweight run emits the comment and marks each unreassigned item lightweight=true with deferred=true, distinguishing it from a genuine orphan ← Satisfies: sc-3

- When this story is complete, the INTENT_ALLOCATION_PREPLANNING comment is written through ticket-comment-from-file.sh via a temp file rather than an inline argument, so large epics do not hit ARG_MAX ← Satisfies: sc-3

content.text: ## Description

**What**: Build plugins/dso/hooks/lib/static-defense-lib.sh providing four reusable primitives: (1) staged-.sh enumeration over diff-filter A/C/M/R/T, (2) count-based shrink-only baseline load and diff (reject when post-commit count exceeds recorded baseline; reject removing a baseline entry without removing its source violation), (3) suppression-annotation parsing for `# antipattern-ok: <reason>` and `# bash4-only:` requiring a non-empty non-whitespace token, and (4) diagnostic formatting emitting offending line, remediation string, and originating-ticket citation. The library resolves its own paths via BASH_SOURCE -> readlink -f, never via CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT.

**Why**: All four hooks are thin wrappers over this library; proving enumeration completeness (sc-7) and bash-3.2 self-compatibility (sc-8) here once avoids divergence and re-implementation across hooks.
**Scope**:
- IN: the shared library file; its enumeration, baseline, suppression, and diagnostic functions; a fixture suite exercising those functions; a bash-3.2-constrained test for the library.
- OUT: the four concrete detection hooks; .pre-commit-config.yaml registration; the known-antipatterns.yaml registry.
## Done Definitions

- static-defense-lib.sh enumerates staged .sh files for git diff-filter classes added, copied, modified, and renamed/mode-changed, and a renamed file carrying a violation appears in the enumerated set ← Satisfies: sc-7

- static-defense-lib.sh loads a per-hook count-based baseline and reports a violation only when the staged-content count exceeds the recorded baseline; a commit that removes a baseline entry while its source violation remains is reported as a rejected grow operation ← Satisfies: sc-2
- static-defense-lib.sh parses `# antipattern-ok: <reason>` and `# bash4-only:` annotations and treats an empty or whitespace-only justification token as a rejected suppression ← Satisfies: sc-5
- static-defense-lib.sh formats a per-file diagnostic that contains the offending line text, the remediation string, and the originating-ticket citation ← Satisfies: sc-3
- static-defense-lib.sh executes under a bash-3.2-constrained interpreter with no declare -A or nameref usage, verified by a bash-3.2 test that passes ← Satisfies: sc-8
- unit tests (fixture-based) are written and passing for all new enumeration, baseline, suppression, and diagnostic logic in static-defense-lib.sh ← Satisfies: sc-6
## Considerations

- [Hermeticity] The library MUST resolve its own path and baseline locations via the BASH_SOURCE -> readlink -f idiom used by check-tickets-boundary.sh, never via CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, so it works under the pre-commit framework symlinked temp-path chain and in CI where CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is unset.
- [Compatibility] static-defense-lib.sh must not itself ship the bash-4-only antipattern (declare -A, namerefs) that check-known-antipatterns.sh is meant to flag.
- [Build] static-defense-lib.sh and any new .sh fixtures/tests must have the executable bit set (CLAUDE.md always:chmod-x-new-sh).
- [Baseline-format] The library owns one consistent baseline format (count-based) to avoid integer-vs-file-keyed-map ambiguity across hooks.

content.text: ## Description

**What**: Add a user-invoked `dso forbidden-action-override --reason="..."` command that grants a one-shot, audited override for the next blocked forbidden-action tool call, mirroring the sibling epic's dso commit-override audit-trail pattern. The agent cannot self-authorize; the override respects dso-fbky autonomous mode.
**Why**: A load-bearing block needs a sanctioned escape valve so a user can deliberately proceed past a HARD-GATE, with an audit record, without disabling the hook.
**Scope**:
- IN: The override CLI command, one-shot consumption semantics, an audit record capturing reason and timestamp, rejection of agent self-invocation, and dso-fbky autonomous-mode handling.
- OUT: The hook itself (draft-2); the registry (draft-1); abuse-detection surfacing at sprint Phase I or end-session closure.
## Done Definitions

- A user-invoked dso forbidden-action-override --reason="..." grants a single override that the next forbidden-action block consumes, after which a subsequent forbidden call is blocked again ← Satisfies: sc-3
- Each override writes an audit record capturing the supplied reason and a timestamp ← Satisfies: sc-3
- An override invocation that lacks a user context (agent self-authorization) is rejected and writes no override grant ← Satisfies: sc-3

- When this story is complete, under dso-fbky autonomous mode the override path follows the sibling epic's pattern and is not silently self-granted to the agent, verified by a test exercising the autonomous-mode path ← Satisfies: sc-3
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic, including one-shot consumption, audit-record write, and self-authorization rejection ← Satisfies: sc-3
## Considerations
- [Security] The override must reject agent self-authorization; only a user-invoked context grants it.
- [Security] Under dso-fbky autonomous mode the override is not self-granted to the agent; the autonomous-mode path mirrors the sibling epic's pattern.

- [External-blocker] Reuses the sibling-epic (d076-d35e, 750c-6033) dso commit-override audit-trail pattern and get_artifacts_dir() resolution; no in-epic depends_on is created for that outside infra.
- [Convention] Any new .sh file for the override command sets the executable bit (chmod +x) on creation.

content.text: ## Description

What: New PreToolUse hook plugins/dso/hooks/check-pr-destructive-action.sh that parses the Bash tool command string and blocks any invocation containing 'gh pr (close|merge|edit|comment)' that does not also contain 'pr-destructive-action.sh'; plus the CLAUDE.md 'Never Do These' rule 25 in negative-directive form documenting the prohibition, the exit-code contract (0/1/2/3), and the rationale (session ownership; see fe66-f05b). Why: This hook is the load-bearing enforcement that makes the negative directive structural. Scope IN: the hook with its command-string parse-and-block logic; a hook integration test asserting the block fires on direct 'gh pr close N' and does NOT fire on 'pr-destructive-action.sh N close'; the CLAUDE.md rule-25 text. Scope OUT: the wrapper itself (draft-4); SKILL.md call-site rewrites (draft-7).
## Done Definitions

- check-pr-destructive-action.sh blocks a Bash command containing 'gh pr (close|merge|edit|comment)' that does not also contain 'pr-destructive-action.sh', and allows commands that route through the wrapper ← Satisfies: sc-4
- A hook integration test asserts the block fires on a direct 'gh pr close N' invocation and does NOT fire on a 'pr-destructive-action.sh N close' invocation ← Satisfies: sc-4

- CLAUDE.md 'Never Do These' rule 25 states the negative directive (never invoke gh pr destructive directly; use pr-destructive-action.sh as the only permitted path; blocked by check-pr-destructive-action.sh), documents the 0/1/2/3 exit-code contract, and cites the session-ownership rationale (fe66-f05b) ← Satisfies: sc-4

- The hook does NOT allow a Bash command that merely CONTAINS the literal string pr-destructive-action.sh while still reaching a raw destructive gh pr (close|merge|edit|comment): the hook verifies the destructive gh pr token is actually the wrapper-invoked form, not a co-located, compound-separated, or quoted/heredoc/comment mention. Negative-adversarial fixtures — (a) co-location bypass 'echo pr-destructive-action.sh && gh pr close 5', (b) compound-statement separation ('pr-destructive-action.sh ...; gh pr merge 7'), (c) heredoc/comment mention of pr-destructive-action.sh preceding a raw gh pr edit — are all BLOCKED, while a genuine 'pr-destructive-action.sh 5 close' is ALLOWED ← Satisfies: sc-4
## Considerations

- [LoadBearing] This hook is the structural enforcement; the SKILL.md negative directives (draft-7) are documentation, not enforcement — the hook must fire regardless of whether SKILL.md text is followed.
- [Parsing] The command-string parser must handle compound commands (pipes, &&, subshells) so a destructive gh pr buried in a compound invocation is still blocked.
- [Doc-test] The CLAUDE.md rule-25 DD is verified by behavioral content assertion (regex on required tokens), not by diffing the file.

- [Adversarial] sc-4 structural premise: a substring-presence allow-check is defeatable. The allow-condition must establish that the destructive gh pr token is the argument of an actual pr-destructive-action.sh invocation (the wrapper-invoked form) — not that the wrapper name appears anywhere in the command string. Treat co-location, compound separation (&&, ;, |, subshells), and quoted/heredoc/comment mentions as bypasses to block.
## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

### 1. Technical Environment

* **Component:** plugins/dso/skills/debug-everything/SKILL.md (Bug-Fix Mode Execution) + plugins/dso/skills/debug-everything/prompts/dispatch-fix-batch.md (Sub-Branch Chunking / Per-chunk PR + integration)
* **Config:** dso.workflow=ci-pr
### 2. Incident Overview
* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior
#### Expected Behavior

Under `dso.workflow=ci-pr`, debug-everything Bug-Fix Mode is documented to chunk the open-bug list into sub-branches of at most 5 bugs each (`bug-batch/<debug-session-id>/bug-fix-batch-<K>`), open a PR per chunk against `SESSION_BRANCH`, await CI, and merge per chunk. See SKILL.md Bug-Fix Mode Execution step 2 ("Chunking" / "Per-chunk PR + integration (ci-pr mode)") and dispatch-fix-batch.md (shared chunking + per-sub-branch CI loop). The per-chunk (<=5-bug) sub-branch-PR cadence is the documented review-granularity contract for ci-pr mode.
#### Actual Behavior

During an autonomous ci-pr bug-fix session driven from the debug-everything two-batch pipeline (investigation batch -> fix batch), the orchestrator applied fixes correctly but committed every fix to a single accumulation branch and created NO per-chunk sub-branch PRs. The documented per-chunk (<=5-bug) sub-branch-PR process was not followed for the first batch of fixes. No gate, hook, pre-commit check, or invariant detected or prevented the deviation — the orchestrator silently bypassed the ci-pr chunk-PR cadence with no machine-readable trace that the contract was skipped.

This is the same class of process-conformance drift as the previously-diagnosed two-batch-collapse (guard jira-dig-1662; bot-psychologist root cause: #16 Instruction Locality + #17 Pink Elephant): the chunk-PR requirement lives in SKILL.md step 2 / dispatch-fix-batch.md but is not made salient or enforced at the moment the orchestrator decides where to commit fixes, so a "consolidate into one branch/PR" shortcut is reachable without any guard firing.
### 5. Skills and Workflows
* debug-everything Bug-Fix Mode (ci-pr) — Sub-Branch Chunking + Per-chunk PR + integration
* dispatch-fix-batch.md — shared chunking + per-sub-branch CI loop
* merge-to-main.sh two-channel staged flow
### 6. Suggested Direction (non-binding)

Two complementary mitigations consistent with the bot-psychologist findings: (a) co-locate an affirmative, salient "for each <=5-bug chunk: open a sub-branch PR" directive at the actual commit/dispatch decision site in SKILL.md (Instruction Locality fix); and (b) add a post-hoc / pre-merge detector that flags when a ci-pr bug-fix session produced > 5 fix commits on a single branch with zero `bug-batch/.../bug-fix-batch-*` sub-branch PRs (machine-readable trace of the bypass). Note: the bypass can be a legitimate operator choice (e.g., to avoid per-PR FP-amplification) — the gap is the absence of enforcement OR an explicit, recorded acknowledgement, not that consolidation is always wrong.

content.text: ## Description
**What**: Implement plugins/dso/scripts/intent-header-source-check.sh implementing the (a+) header-vs-source import check.
**Why**: Catches tests that claim an intent in their header but do not reference the intent's source files — a tautology-prone but cheap second signal that complements manifest-claim breadth.
**Scope**:

- IN: applies only to test files carrying an intent-claim header per d566 Rule 6 (header-less files skipped); per file: extract intent_id; resolve source_files via the manifest entry's source_files field, else the parent ticket's file_impact array, else emit source_files_unresolved (warn, fail-open, skip the check for that intent); when file_impact is used, additionally check disk presence and emit file_impact_likely_stale (warn) for missing entries while still matching against surviving entries; parse the test file with sg (ast-grep); emit header_source_mismatch when the test references no source_files entry; --output-file ARG_MAX-safe findings output; validate emitted findings against the sc-1 schema.
- OUT: per-language dynamic-import fail-open detection (sc-6); manifest-claim breadth check (sc-2); multi-surface wiring (sc-4); e2e fixtures (sc-5).
## Done Definitions

- intent-header-source-check.sh skips test files without an intent-claim header and, for a headered test file whose content references no source_files entry, emits header_source_mismatch validating against the sc-1 schema ← Satisfies: sc-3
- When an intent has no manifest source_files field and an empty parent file_impact, the script emits source_files_unresolved (warn) and skips the (a+) check for that intent ← Satisfies: sc-3

- When source_files are resolved from file_impact and a referenced path is absent on disk, the script emits file_impact_likely_stale (warn) and still matches against the surviving file_impact entries ← Satisfies: sc-3
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic ← Satisfies: sc-3

- [Dependency] External blocker d566-afa6-1aa3-4293 (Rule 6 intent-claim header): the script parses the header format d566 defines; cross-epic dependency.
- [Dependency] External blocker 94ed-f55c-51f5-45f6: source_files resolution prefers the manifest entry's source_files field.
- [Build] intent-header-source-check.sh is a new .sh file and must have its executable bit set per CLAUDE.md.

**What**: Ship plugins/dso/config/known-antipatterns.yaml as an append-only registry with a documented versioned schema (id, pattern, target languages/dirs, remediation, citation), document it in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md, and implement plugins/dso/hooks/check-known-antipatterns.sh as a thin wrapper over static-defense-lib.sh that reads the registry via a single pinned parser (python3 or yq, parser choice independent of yq v3-vs-v4 syntax), blocks staged content matching any registry entry (seeded with the declare -A bash-4-only class), enforces the append-only contract (reject removal or mutation of an existing entry), ships its per-hook baseline, and registers in .pre-commit-config.yaml between shellcheck and pre-commit-review-gate.

**Why**: The registry is the data-driven extension point consumed by downstream epics (99f1-153c, d63f-2c74, a47f-b451); it must publish a stable versioned schema and tolerate the empty-registry case before those consumers run.
**Scope**:

- IN: the registry file and its versioned schema, the CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md documentation, the hook, the append-only mechanical guard, the pinned-parser choice, the initial baseline, the .pre-commit-config.yaml entry, and the fixture + end-to-end test.
- OUT: populating the registry beyond the seed entry (owned by 99f1-153c); downstream consumer wiring.
## Done Definitions
- check-known-antipatterns.sh blocks a commit when staged content matches a registry entry (seed: declare -A in a bash-3.2-target script) read from known-antipatterns.yaml ← Satisfies: sc-1

- known-antipatterns.yaml ships as an append-only registry with a documented versioned schema carrying id, pattern, target languages/dirs, remediation, and citation fields, documented in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md, and a commit that removes or mutates an existing registry entry is rejected ← Satisfies: sc-4
- check-known-antipatterns.sh reads its per-hook count-based baseline so captured existing violations do not block while a new instance beyond the baseline is blocked ← Satisfies: sc-2
- check-known-antipatterns.sh emits a per-file diagnostic naming the offending line, the remediation string, and the registry-entry citation ← Satisfies: sc-3

content.text: ## Description

What: New plugins/dso/scripts/backfill-pr-session-trailers.sh that lists all currently-open PRs and, for each PR whose author matches the local 'gh api /user --jq .login', prompts the operator to (a) stamp this user's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID as the trailer retroactively or (b) skip; logs each decision; is idempotent (skips PRs that already have a trailer); is never automatic and never claims ownership for a session that is not the owner. Plus operator dogfooding: the 53ef sprint operator runs the backfill against their own open PRs in-session before Phase I and captures the decision log as a ticket comment on the epic; if zero un-trailered PRs exist, the script is run against a synthetic fixture and the fixture-mode log is captured instead. Why: Pre-existing PRs lack the trailer (epic HIGH scenario) and need a manual, safe migration path; the dogfooding artifact is the load-bearing Probe-6 operator-verification half. Scope IN: the backfill script; the in-session dogfooding run + decision-log ticket comment. Scope OUT: automatic backfill (explicitly prohibited).
## Done Definitions

- backfill-pr-session-trailers.sh exists with the executable bit set, lists open PRs, restricts stamping to PRs authored by the local 'gh api /user --jq .login', prompts per PR (stamp or skip), logs each decision, and is idempotent (skips PRs that already carry a Session-Id trailer) ← Validates Closure Check: "Pre-existing un-trailered PRs migration: a one-shot script plugins/dso/scripts/backfill-pr-session-trailers.sh lists all currently-open PRs and, for each PR whose author matches the local \"gh api /user --jq .login\", prompts the operator to either (a) stamp this user's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID as the trailer retroactively or (b) skip. Script logs each decision; idempotent (skips PRs that already have a trailer). The migration is operator-driven, never automatic, never claims ownership for a session not actually the owner."

- The backfill never stamps a PR not authored by the local user and never runs without an operator prompt, verified by a test that asserts a foreign-authored PR is skipped without prompting to stamp ← Validates Closure Check: "Pre-existing un-trailered PRs migration: a one-shot script plugins/dso/scripts/backfill-pr-session-trailers.sh lists all currently-open PRs and, for each PR whose author matches the local \"gh api /user --jq .login\", prompts the operator to either (a) stamp this user's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID as the trailer retroactively or (b) skip. Script logs each decision; idempotent (skips PRs that already have a trailer). The migration is operator-driven, never automatic, never claims ownership for a session not actually the owner."

- The 53ef sprint operator runs the backfill in-session before Phase I (against own open PRs, or a synthetic fixture if none) and the decision log is captured as a ticket comment on epic 53ef-d6fd-5ca5-4d62 ← Validates Closure Check: "SC (Probe-6 remediation, architecture-vs-evidence audit 2026-05-16): In-session runtime + operator-action verification. Before the 53ef sprint can be marked complete, the two runtime/operator dependencies are verified in-session: (a) CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID runtime-contract checks and (b) operator-driven backfill dogfooding sub-bullets, captured as ticket comments on this epic."
## Considerations
- [Safety] Owner-only is a hard invariant: the script must never stamp a PR whose author differs from the local gh user, even if the operator instructs it to — it must refuse, not prompt.
- [Idempotency] Re-running on an already-trailered PR must skip (no second trailer), so re-invocation validates rather than corrupts.
- [Dogfooding] The fixture-mode fallback (zero un-trailered PRs at sprint time) must still produce a captured log so the Probe-6 operator-verification artifact always exists.

- [Ownership-semantics] Backfill stamps the operator's CURRENT CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID onto a previously-untrailered PR; that session differs from the PR's creating session, so the backfilled PR reads own ONLY while the operator stays in that same session and foreign in the next session. Document that backfill confers ownership on the BACKFILLING session, not the creating session. Confirm (with a test) that a second backfill run in a different session SKIPS the now-trailered PR via the idempotency guard — it must NOT overwrite the first backfilled trailer with the second session's id.

**Why**: Completes the validate half of the walking skeleton and supplies the finding vocabulary the a03c hook (sc-7) and the e2e test (sc-10) consume.
**Scope**:

- IN: the six finding-type classifiers; --summary-mode; exit-code semantics (pending_intent/lightweight_pending classification per spec — pending_intent informational, lightweight_pending actionable).
- OUT: read/merge logic (sc-5, consumed here); a03c hook wiring (sc-7).
## Done Definitions

- intent-allocation-validate.sh <epic-id> classifies merged-manifest findings into the six types orphan_intent, unresolved_ambiguity, stale_entry, pending_intent, lightweight_pending, and cross_epic_reference ← Satisfies: sc-6

- An intent_id seeded in a comment but with no resolved entry after merge is reported as orphan_intent, and a lightweight=true item is reported as lightweight_pending distinct from orphan_intent ← Satisfies: sc-6
- --summary-mode groups findings by type with count-only output ← Satisfies: sc-6
- The script exits 0 when only informational pending_intent findings exist and exits non-zero with the finding count when actionable findings are present ← Satisfies: sc-6
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic, covering each of the six finding types and both exit-code paths ← Satisfies: sc-6
## Considerations

- [Classification] pending_intent (deferred=true) is informational and non-blocking; lightweight_pending (lightweight=true) is actionable. Conflating them re-creates the orphan-vs-placeholder ambiguity this finding type exists to remove.
- [Cross-epic] cross_epic_reference fires only when owner_ticket resolves outside the subtree AND shared_infra is unset.
- [Shell hygiene] intent-allocation-validate.sh is a new .sh file; set the executable bit on creation.

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

## fix-bug:investigation

### VERDICT: LIVE — bug is reproducible on every new worktree

**Staleness check:** The script has been modified since the ticket was created. Most recent relevant commit: `00e5410867` (fix: require PIL body fields, not just heading). The bug being investigated is NOT fixed by those commits — the marker-gate mechanism described below has been present since the initial implementation but fails specifically in the worktree lifecycle context.

---

### ROOT CAUSE (exact)

**File:** `plugins/dso/scripts/ticket-migrate-brainstorm-tags.sh`
**Lines 71-74** (marker check):
```bash
_MARKER_FILE="$_TARGET/.claude/.brainstorm-tag-migration-v2"
if [ -f "$_MARKER_FILE" ]; then
    exit 0
fi
```
**Lines 289-293** (marker write):
```bash
if [ "$_DRYRUN" = "0" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$_MARKER_FILE")"
    touch "$_MARKER_FILE"
fi
```

The marker IS present in the code. It IS checked before running. However:

**The marker file `.claude/.brainstorm-tag-migration-v2` is gitignored** (line 66 of `.gitignore`: `.claude/.brainstorm-tag-migration-*`).

Each new worktree is a fresh checkout. The marker file written in one worktree does NOT exist in any other worktree. When `/dso:brainstorm` or `/dso:preplanning` runs in a NEW worktree that has never executed the migration, the marker is absent, the gate falls through, the Python scan runs on the live ticket store, finds the epic has a PIL but no `brainstorm:complete` tag (it was deliberately removed), and re-applies it.

**Verified:** The incident worktree `worktree-20260602-141613` has NO `.claude/.brainstorm-tag-migration-v2`. The current worktree also has NO marker. Only 2 of the 17+ existing worktrees have the marker file — the rest would all trigger a re-migration on next skill invocation.

**Secondary defect (tag-derivation logic ignores untag):**
`scan_ticket()` in the Python block (lines 132-200) correctly reads events in sorted (timestamp) order and applies the LAST `data.fields.tags` value from an EDIT event as the authoritative tag list. This means the `_tag_remove` EDIT event written by `ticket untag` (which sets `data.fields.tags = []`) IS correctly picked up — `brainstorm:complete` correctly shows as absent in `latest_tags`. The guard at lines 233-234 (`if 'brainstorm:complete' in tags: continue`) would catch it IF the tag were still present.

So: the tag-derivation logic is NOT the root cause. The Python correctly sees the post-untag state (empty tags). The bug is purely the per-worktree marker file not existing in fresh worktrees, causing the migration to run again when it finds `pil=True` and `brainstorm:complete not in tags`.

**There is no check in the Python scan for whether the tag was previously removed by a human.** The migration's decision rule is: `if epic has PIL AND brainstorm:complete not in current_tags → add tag`. It cannot distinguish between "tag was never applied" (first migration run) vs. "tag was deliberately removed after migration". A ticket that has a PIL and a prior removal EDIT event is treated identically to a ticket that was never migrated.

---

### FIX APPROACH

**Targeted — small change, two options:**

**Option A (preferred): Move marker to the tickets branch (repo-shared, not per-worktree)**
Instead of writing the marker to `.claude/.brainstorm-tag-migration-v2` (gitignored, per-worktree), write it to the tickets tracker itself (the orphan `tickets` branch). Sibling scripts use `$_TRACKER_DIR/.migrations/` for this (e.g., `ticket-migrate-schema-hardening.sh` line 135: `_MARKER_FILE="$_TRACKER_DIR/.migrations/schema-hardening.done"`). Writing to the tracker branch means the marker persists across all worktrees since they all share the same `tickets` branch. Single-line path change in the marker logic.

**Option B (belt-and-suspenders): Check event history for prior removal**
In the Python scan's per-ticket decision loop (lines 224-250), before writing the EDIT event, check whether the ticket's event log contains a post-initial-migration EDIT that set `tags` to a list NOT including `brainstorm:complete` (i.e., an explicit removal). If such an event exists AND the tag is currently absent, skip without tagging. This ensures that even if the marker is missing (e.g., fresh worktree), a deliberately-removed tag is never re-applied.

**Option A is the right primary fix** because the root cause is the gitignored per-worktree marker file, not the tag-derivation logic. Option B is complementary but adds complexity for a scenario that Option A already prevents. Implementing only Option A addresses the contract: "marker-gated; no-op once migrated."

**Implementation scope:** 2-line change — update `_MARKER_FILE` path from `$_TARGET/.claude/.brainstorm-tag-migration-v2` to `$_TRACKER_DIR/.migrations/brainstorm-tag-migration-v2` and add the `mkdir -p` before the `touch`. The existing marker-check and marker-write logic is otherwise correct.

Note: the tracker's `.migrations/` directory is not gitignored (it's committed to the `tickets` orphan branch directly), so the marker will be visible in all worktrees once committed. However, need to verify the `git -C $_TRACKER_DIR add + commit` pattern is used for writing the marker (not a bare file write), consistent with how other tracker operations work.

---

### RED TEST PLAN

**Execution-based, isolated ticket-store fixture** (same pattern as existing Tests 2-16 in `tests/scripts/test-ticket-migrate-brainstorm-tags.sh`):

**New Test 17:** `test_untag_then_remigrate_does_not_retag`

Fixture steps (using existing `_make_test_repo` + `_write_event` helpers):
1. Create fresh test repo with epic that has a PIL and initial tags = []
2. Run migration → expect tag applied, marker written to `$TRACKER_DIR/.migrations/brainstorm-tag-migration-v2`
3. Run `ticket untag <id> brainstorm:complete` → confirm tags = []
4. **Delete the OLD marker file path** (`.claude/.brainstorm-tag-migration-v2`) to simulate a fresh worktree (the new fix stores the marker in the tracker, but the old path must be absent to confirm the test exercises the correct path)
5. Re-run migration
6. Assert: `brainstorm:complete` tag is NOT re-applied (new marker at tracker path blocks the re-run)
7. Assert: EDIT event count for the ticket has not increased since step 3

**RED condition:** test fails on current code because (a) current marker is gitignored per-worktree, (b) re-running after deleting the marker file re-applies the tag.
**GREEN condition:** after fix, marker is written to `$TRACKER_DIR/.migrations/`, survives the simulated fresh-worktree scenario, re-run is a no-op.

---

### FEASIBILITY: yes — small, targeted change (2-3 lines)

The fix is Option A: change `_MARKER_FILE` from `.claude/.brainstorm-tag-migration-v2` to `$_TRACKER_DIR/.migrations/brainstorm-tag-migration-v2` and add a `git -C "$_TRACKER_DIR" add` + `git -C "$_TRACKER_DIR" commit` after the `touch` so the marker persists on the tickets branch. The existing marker-gate and marker-write structure at lines 71-74 and 289-293 remains intact.

### 1. Technical Environment
* **Plugin/Tool Versions:** dso-dev 1.17.106
* **Context Scope:** worktree-20260602-141613; ticket store on orphan `tickets` branch
* **Component path:** plugins/dso/scripts/ticket-migrate-brainstorm-tags.sh
### 2. Incident Overview
* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior
#### Expected Behavior

The brainstorm/preplanning SKILL.md "Migration Check" sections describe their migration scripts as "marker-gated; no-op once migrated, never blocks the skill." Per that contract, a migration that has already been applied must be a no-op on subsequent invocations and must NOT re-apply a tag that has since been deliberately removed.
#### Actual Behavior

During `/dso:brainstorm af26-dd5a-df6d-4f81`, the pre-flight migration step ran `bash ticket-migrate-brainstorm-tags.sh`. Immediately prior, `brainstorm:complete` had been removed from af26 via `ticket untag` (tags confirmed `[]`). The migration then emitted:
[tickets 28490eb816] migration: add brainstorm:complete tag to af26-dd5a-df6d-4f81
1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)

A subsequent `ticket show af26-dd5a-df6d-4f81` reported `tags: ['brainstorm:complete']` — the deliberately-removed tag was re-applied by the migration. The migration re-ran and mutated the ticket on a fresh skill invocation rather than acting as a no-op.
### 3. Action History and Workarounds
* **Steps Taken:**
* `.claude/scripts/dso ticket untag af26-dd5a-df6d-4f81 brainstorm:complete` (tags -> `[]`, confirmed via ticket show)
* `/dso:brainstorm af26-dd5a-df6d-4f81` -> pre-flight ran `bash ticket-migrate-brainstorm-tags.sh`
* `.claude/scripts/dso ticket show af26-dd5a-df6d-4f81` -> tags back to `['brainstorm:complete']`
* **Raw Results:**
* Migration commit line: `migration: add brainstorm:complete tag to af26-dd5a-df6d-4f81  1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)`
* **Known Workarounds:** None durable. Manual `ticket untag` is overwritten on the next brainstorm/preplanning invocation.
### 5. Skills and Workflows
* **Active Workflow:** `/dso:brainstorm` Migration Check (also invoked by `/dso:preplanning` Migration Check)
* **Skills Invoked:** dso:brainstorm, dso:preplanning
### 7. Additional Details

* Historical corroboration: af26 carries a 2026-05-18 "Tag Integrity Correction" comment that removed the same `brainstorm:complete` tag for the same reason (the epic is a self-declared stub awaiting genuine brainstorm). The tag has since reappeared, consistent with this migration re-applying it on each invocation.

* Impact: the non-idempotent re-tag causes a stub epic to falsely satisfy the `/dso:preplanning` scrutiny gate, which keys on `brainstorm:complete` presence. Reproduction frequency: every brainstorm/preplanning invocation while the migration marker condition holds.

content.text: ## Description

**What**: Extend plugins/dso/docs/workflows/prompts/reviewer-delta-test-quality.md (the build source) with a Tier 1 (assertion shape) dimension and a Tier 2 (articulation) dimension, including the REQUIRED predicate-listing scaffold and the anti-sycophancy prime, then regenerate the compiled plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-test-quality.md via build-review-agents.sh. Also assert the explicit descope: pre-commit-test-quality-gate.sh and semgrep-rules/test-anti-patterns.yaml are NOT extended.
**Why**: The reviewer dimensions are the sole enforcement path for Rules 6/7 (review-only, no hooks). They consume the Rule 6 header schema.
**Scope**:

- IN: Tier 1 dimension (flag assertions on internal method names, private state, mock-invocation counts, source-grep patterns; require observable-output assertions); Tier 2 dimension cases (a) missing/malformed header, (b) tautological catches_regression_where, (c) predicate-listing scaffold for claim-vs-assertion disjointness, (d) catches_regression_where would not actually fail the test, (e) duplicate intent_id without orthogonal suffix; anti-sycophancy prime; build-review-agents.sh regeneration of the compiled agent; negative assertion that the two hook/semgrep files remain unextended.
- OUT: The synthetic-diff review validation run (draft-4); rule text in behavioral-testing-standard.md (draft-1).
## Done Definitions

- reviewer-delta-test-quality.md contains a Tier 1 (assertion shape) dimension that flags assertions targeting internal method names, private state, mock-invocation counts, or source-grep patterns and requires assertions on observable outputs ← Satisfies: sc-4
- reviewer-delta-test-quality.md contains a Tier 2 (articulation) dimension covering all five cases a through e, the predicate-listing scaffold, and the anti-sycophancy prime text ← Satisfies: sc-4
- running build-review-agents.sh regenerates code-reviewer-test-quality.md so the compiled agent contains the Tier 1 and Tier 2 dimension text ← Satisfies: sc-4
- pre-commit-test-quality-gate.sh and semgrep-rules/test-anti-patterns.yaml contain no Rule 6 or Rule 7 enforcement logic, confirming review-only enforcement ← Satisfies: sc-8
- unit tests written and passing assert the Tier 1 and Tier 2 dimensions are present in the regenerated compiled agent ← Satisfies: sc-4
## Considerations

- [Correctness] Tier 2(c) predicate-listing scaffold and the anti-sycophancy prime are weak defenses against LLM reviewer sycophancy on fluent headers; this is accepted residual risk per the epic Scenario Analysis.
- [Build] The compiled agent must be regenerated from the delta source via build-review-agents.sh; do not hand-edit the compiled code-reviewer-test-quality.md.
- [Descope] sc-8 is a negative constraint; the DD asserts absence of enforcement logic in the two named files rather than presence of a feature.
## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

content.text: ## Description

**What**: Build the walking-skeleton path: a shared normalize-and-sort registry library, a plugin-shipped seed registry of artifact-reference pairs, and a bootstrap migration script that fans out ast-grep over chunked codebase slices (map) and equijoins per-file tuples on the realpath-normalized path (reduce) to emit admitted writer/reference pairs.
**Why**: Without a deterministic discovered registry there is nothing for the Category 8 reviewer pass or the refresh command to consume; this is the minimal 'pairs discovered into a registry' spine.
**Scope**:

- IN: shared normalize-and-sort library file sourced by the bootstrap; seed registry YAML shipping the three named pairs; bootstrap map/reduce script using long-form ast-grep; write-idiom vocabulary (shell >/>>, tee, sed -i, jq write, Python open(w)/Path.write_text, Node fs.writeFileSync, Ruby File.open(w)/File.write, Go os.WriteFile) externally extensible via registry config; admission rule (exact realpath match + recognized write idiom + writer and reference in different files).
- OUT: refresh command (draft-3); reviewer consumption (draft-5); ambiguous/inferred pairs.
## Done Definitions

- The plugin-shipped seed registry contains the pair release.sh paired with marketplace.json ← Validates Closure Check: "The plugin-shipped seed registry contains the pairs release.sh<->marketplace.json, *.conf<->CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md, and plugin.json<->marketplace source ref."

- The plugin-shipped seed registry contains the pair *.conf paired with CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md and the pair plugin.json paired with the marketplace source ref ← Validates Closure Check: "The plugin-shipped seed registry contains the pairs release.sh<->marketplace.json, *.conf<->CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md, and plugin.json<->marketplace source ref."

- The shared normalize-and-sort registry library file exists and the bootstrap script sources it ← Validates Closure Check: "The shared normalize-and-sort registry library file exists and is sourced by both the bootstrap and refresh scripts."

- Running the bootstrap over a fixture repo emits output byte-equal to a sorted newline-delimited writer_realpath<TAB>reference_realpath manifest with no missing or extra rows; near-miss fixtures (same-file self-reference; cross-file read-only) are absent from the output ← Satisfies: sc-3

**Why**: This is the same artifact-desync pattern that motivated the epic (release.sh + marketplace.json); a config key and its reference doc must update together.
**Scope**:

- IN: add/modify/remove key detection in implementation-plan/SKILL.md; child sub-task emission with depends_on to the parent; suppression of the duplicate generic doc-router documentation task for config keys.
- OUT: the inference-gate config key itself (draft-6); reviewer Category 8 pass.
## Done Definitions

- An implementation-plan run on a task that adds a dso-config.conf key yields a child sub-task titled Document <key> in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md whose depends_on points to the parent task id ← Satisfies: sc-4
- An implementation-plan run on a task that modifies or removes a dso-config.conf key yields the same paired documentation child sub-task ← Satisfies: sc-4
- For a config-key task the generic doc-router documentation task is not emitted, so no duplicate documentation task exists ← Satisfies: sc-4
- The emitted child sub-task carries testing_mode GREEN ← Satisfies: sc-4
## Considerations
- [Sequencing] This story is sequenced before the inference-gate story (draft-6) so SC8's key documentation follows the established config-key/doc pairing pattern.
- [Coordination] CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md is edited at story-run time across many config-adding epics; coordinate key namespacing rather than locking the file at epic-merge time.

## VERDICT: CONFIRMED — same defect as 3349-8532-1183-4fc1 (duplicate facets of one root cause)

### Duplicate/Facets Call
These are TWO FACETS of the SAME defect. 3349-8532-1183-4fc1 (filed earlier, timestamp 1780430972) is the primary ticket: it describes the issue verbatim, identifies both conflicting hooks, and includes the confirmed workaround (skip Step 3.5). This ticket (abdf, timestamp 1780444182) provides the step-by-step action trace (fe8d-e8d7 sprint, steps 1-5), the exact error output, and documents the bypass escape hatch used. Both describe the same invariant conflict in the same files.

**Recommendation: fix against 3349-8532-1183-4fc1 (primary). Close abdf-8347-45f1-4ace as duplicate after the fix lands, cross-referencing 3349.**

### Exact Files and Lines

1. **plugins/dso/skills/sprint/prompts/per-worktree-review-commit.md** — Step 3.5 (lines 131-139):
   Introduced in commit 29c8c6c8ad (chore: bump version to v1.17.23, 2026-05-23) as part of bug e081-63c0 fix (PR #319).
   The step copies SESSION_ROOT/.sprint-active into WORKTREE_PATH/.sprint-active so check-sprint-trailer.sh sees the marker in the agent worktree. This is the COPY SIDE of the collision.

2. **plugins/dso/scripts/check-session-merge-only.sh** — lines 27-36 (primary checkout exemption), lines 38-44 (.sprint-active detection), lines 99-103 (rejection).
   The hook exempts only the primary checkout (git-common-dir == git-dir). All linked worktrees — including agent sub-branch worktrees — are subject to enforcement. Once .sprint-active is copied into the agent worktree root by Step 3.5, _sprint_active=1 and any non-merge commit is rejected with exit 1. This is a SAFEGUARD FILE (rule:no-safeguard-edits).

3. **plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/single-agent-integrate.md** — Step 7.5 (lines 221-231):
   Same copy pattern for single-agent callers. Same collision applies.

4. **plugins/dso/scripts/check-sprint-trailer.sh** — lines 12-19 (4-cell matrix):
   Gates trailer enforcement on .sprint-active at REPO_ROOT of the worktree. This is what requires .sprint-active to be present in the agent worktree. check-sprint-trailer.sh is NOT listed as a safeguard file (rule:no-safeguard-edits lists pre-commit hooks and review-gate.sh — check-sprint-trailer.sh is a commit-msg hook enforcing trailer correctness, distinct from session routing safety).

### Root Cause

The e081-63c0 fix introduced a new invariant conflict: both check-sprint-trailer.sh and check-session-merge-only.sh key on the same .sprint-active filesystem marker, but require OPPOSITE behavior for agent sub-branch worktrees:
- check-sprint-trailer.sh: REQUIRES .sprint-active in the agent worktree to enforce DSO-Story trailer
- check-session-merge-only.sh: REJECTS non-merge commits in ANY linked worktree where .sprint-active is present

The primary checkout exemption in check-session-merge-only.sh (added for bug 6e96-61bf) only covers the main repo. It does not cover agent sub-branch worktrees, which are the legitimate commit targets in the two-tier sprint design. No mechanism exists to distinguish 'session worktree' from 'agent sub-branch worktree' in check-session-merge-only.sh — both are linked worktrees with different git-dir paths under .git/worktrees/.

### Fix Approach (COPY SIDE — no safeguard edit required)

Fix location: per-worktree-review-commit.md Step 3.5 and single-agent-integrate.md Step 7.5 (the COPY side), plus check-sprint-trailer.sh (add env-var acceptance).

Approach: Replace filesystem .sprint-active copy with an env-var signal passed to COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md. Add DSO_SPRINT_TRAILER_REQUIRED=1 to the environment when invoking the commit in Step 4, and update check-sprint-trailer.sh to treat DSO_SPRINT_TRAILER_REQUIRED=1 OR .sprint-active presence as triggering enforcement. Remove Step 3.5's filesystem copy entirely.

This is a COPY-SIDE fix. No modification to check-session-merge-only.sh (the safeguard) is needed.

**SAFEGUARD APPROVAL REQUIRED? No.** The fix touches:
- per-worktree-review-commit.md (prompt doc)
- single-agent-integrate.md (prompt doc)
- check-sprint-trailer.sh (commit-msg hook — NOT the merge-only safeguard)

### Red Test Plan

**Primary test addition:** tests/hooks/test-check-session-merge-only.sh — add:
- test_agent_worktree_with_copied_sprint_active_accepts_non_merge_commit: create linked worktree, touch .sprint-active, attempt non-merge commit -> currently exit 1 (RED); after fix (no copy), exit 0

**New test for env-var path:** tests/hooks/test-check-sprint-trailer.sh (existing) or new test-check-sprint-trailer-env-var.sh:
- Assert: with DSO_SPRINT_TRAILER_REQUIRED=1 + dso.workflow=ci-pr + no .sprint-active file, trailer enforcement activates (exit 1 when trailer absent)
- Assert: with DSO_SPRINT_TRAILER_REQUIRED=1 + dso.workflow=ci-pr + trailer present, exits 0

Test conventions: follow make_linked_worktree helper in tests/hooks/test-check-session-merge-only.sh.

### Feasibility

HIGH. Three-file change:
1. per-worktree-review-commit.md: remove Step 3.5 cp command, replace with env-var export for Step 4 commit call
2. single-agent-integrate.md: same (Step 7.5)
3. check-sprint-trailer.sh: add || [[ "" == "1" ]] to the 4-cell matrix check

No safeguard file modification. Well-isolated. Existing test infrastructure covers all adjacent cases.

### 1. Technical Environment
* **Mode:** dso.workflow=ci-pr, worktree-isolation (default), .sprint-active present
* **Hooks involved:** plugins/dso/scripts/check-session-merge-only.sh, plugins/dso/scripts/check-sprint-trailer.sh
* **Skill docs involved:** plugins/dso/skills/sprint/prompts/per-worktree-review-commit.md (Step 3.5 and Step 4)
### 2. Incident Overview
* **Scenario Type:** Sub-Agent Blocker / Workflow tooling defect (surfaced during /dso:sprint on epic dso-uvyl, story 7913-abe2-de0e-45e3, task fe8d-e8d7-ae3a-4a1a)
#### Expected Behavior

Per per-worktree-review-commit.md Step 4, the orchestrator executes COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md in the agent worktree context and the per-task commit lands on the worktree-agent-* branch (later harvested via merge into the session branch). The agent worktree IS the "sub-branch worktree" that CLAUDE.md rule:no-session-direct-commit wants work routed through, so its commit should be accepted without disabling any safety hook.
#### Actual Behavior

Step 3.5 of per-worktree-review-commit.md copies .sprint-active from the session root into the agent worktree (intended so check-sprint-trailer.sh enforces the DSO-Story trailer; fix for bug e081-63c0). check-session-merge-only.sh keys off the same .sprint-active file and only exempts the PRIMARY checkout (it returns exit 0 when git-common-dir == git-dir). An agent worktree is a LINKED worktree (git-dir under .git/worktrees/agent-...), so the hook is active there and rejects the non-merge per-task commit:
Session Worktree Merge-Only Check (10s timeout)..................................Failed
ERROR: Direct commit to session worktree rejected (sprint-active mode).
Commits must go through a story worktree and be merged into the session branch.

The only way to land the per-task commit is the DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=0 + DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE_BYPASS_REASON escape hatch, which logs a bypass and disables the merge-only protection for what is actually the sanctioned per-task flow. per-worktree-review-commit.md Step 4 does not document this collision or the required bypass, so the canonical flow as written cannot commit. This affects every per-task commit in sprint worktree-isolation mode while .sprint-active is present.
### 3. Action History
1. Phase E dispatched task fe8d to an isolated worktree (worktree-agent-a74a00d12126b07fa).
2. Phase F Step 3.5 copied .sprint-active into the agent worktree.
3. Phase F Step 4 ran COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md (ci-pr: validation/review skipped) and attempted git commit on the worktree-agent branch.
4. check-session-merge-only.sh returned exit 1; commit blocked (branch tip unchanged).
5. Re-committed with DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=0 + bypass reason AND an explicit DSO-Story: trailer; commit succeeded (tip 35ef53d), all hooks passed.
### 5. Skills and Workflows
* per-worktree-review-commit.md Step 3.5 (copy .sprint-active) and Step 4 (commit) are mutually inconsistent with check-session-merge-only.sh for linked agent worktrees.
#### Suggested direction (non-binding)

check-session-merge-only.sh should additionally exempt legitimate agent worktrees (e.g. current branch matching worktree-agent-*) so per-task commits land without the bypass, while still blocking direct commits on the actual session branch. Alternatively, per-worktree-review-commit.md Step 4 should document the required DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=0 bypass for the agent-worktree commit. Resolution should reconcile the e081-63c0 trailer-enforcement intent with the merge-only protection without forcing the escape hatch on the happy path.
